home_pitcher_note: While Detroit's other starters have something to prove after last season, Verlander's 18 wins in 2007 vaulted him into baseball's elite at age 25 and helped earn him his first career Opening Day assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Meche did an outstanding job in last year's opener, defeating the Red Sox. Now he gets the honor again at Detroit, where he'll face a hostile crowd and a very hostile lineup. He's 4-1 lifetime in nine games at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers insists his arm feels fine this spring coming off of a frustrating 2007 season in which he lost nearly three months to a torn blood vessel in his shoulder and another month to elbow soreness. He debated retirement in the offseason but chose to come back for a 20th Major League season.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister, obtained from the Mets, had a superb rookie season once he got rolling last year. After going 0-3, he had a 12-4 gallop from June 1 to Sept. 2 and was in the AL Rookie of the Year running until a late slump. In Spring Training, Bannister tried to pace himself and condition himself to be strong in the stretch. He pitches to contact and is a fly-ball pitcher. Last year he was 2-1 with a 2.55 ERA against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: With cold weather expected all week in Detroit, it's hard to tell how much the Royals will see Bonderman's revamped changeup as opposed to fastballs boring in on chilly hands. Nonetheless, the offspeed pitch is expected to be a factor this season.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, Greinke started and finished the season in the rotation with a successful bullpen stay sandwiched between. His future seems to be as a starter, which he was in 2004 when he was a prized rookie (3.97 ERA) and in 2005, when he struggled (17 losses). Greinke spent 2006 rehabbing, mostly in Double-A, but is back on his game. He can throw a hot fastball, a mean slider and has fine control.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson has yet to lose his first outing of the season since breaking camp with the Tigers in 2004, including victories at home in his last two season debuts. That should give him some momentum going up against the White Sox, with whom he has had a rocky relationship in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Contreras ultimately could hold the key to his team's 2008 level of success. The big right-hander holds the franchise record with 17 straight winning decisions, a streak which ended in July 2006, but since the All-Star break, 2006, his 26 losses are the most in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Willis will make his American League debut under the spotlight of a home crowd and a FOX network regional broadcast, starting what he hopes is a rebound campaign following season highs in losses and ERA in his final season for Florida last year. He pitched through command issues in Spring Training, but the mid-90s velocity on his fastball gives the Tigers reason for encouragement.
His last time out, Verlander allowed four earned runs on four hits in six innings in his first Opening Day start. He gave up just one hit through five, but struggled with location in his last inning.
away_pitcher_note: It was an uncharacteristically short and disastrous start for the left-hander on Monday in Cleveland, as he made his sixth Opening Day start in seven years. Buehrle cruised through the first inning unscathed, only to allow seven runs on seven hits before he could record the third out of the second. Buehrle did throw 30 of his 48 pitches for strikes, but according to catcher A.J. Pierzynski, threw the ball too hard and lost some of his movement. Buehrle has five days before his next start, wrapping up this six-game road trip to start the season Sunday night in Detroit. Buehrle has a lifetime 12-8 record against Detroit and a 6-5 record at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka gets the honor of pitching the Fenway Park opener. This, after pitching on Opening Day for the Sox in Tokyo and then getting the ball at Oakland in the home opener for the Athletics. Matsuzaka was brilliant in his last start, limiting the A?s to two hits and a run while walking none and striking out nine over 6 2/3 innings. This time around, he goes against the heavy-hitting Tigers. Matsuzaka?s only career complete game to date came last year against Detroit, when he fired a gem at Fenway on May 14.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers looked sharp in his first outing this season but took the loss after receiving no run support. After missing almost three months last season due to injury, Rogers started the 2008 campaign allowing two earned runs on five hits in six innings. Now he looks to spoil Boston's home opener in his 26th career start against the Red Sox. He has a 11-7 record and 4.18 ERA vs. Boston in his career. Fenway Park is one of five current Major League ballparks in which Rogers has a losing record (5-6).

home_pitcher_note: For the first time this season, Lester faces someone besides the Oakland Athletics. Lester was brilliant in his last start, firing 6 2/3 shutout innings. This marks the lefty's Fenway debut in 2008. In 14 career outings at Fenway, Lester is 5-1 with a 4.60 ERA. This marks his first career start against the Tigers. Lester has a career record of 12-3. He has 29 Major League appearances under his belt, 28 of which have been starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman made his first start this season despite coming down with an illness that sent him home early the day before. He allowed four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings to suffer the Tigers' third straight defeat to open the season. He didn't experience his usual first-inning troubles, but gave up two home runs and struggled in his last three innings. During his five-year career, he has made just one start against Boston. He is making his first career start at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield's first start of the year went a lot better than his pitching line would indicate. The 41-year-old knuckleballer threw five shutout innings against the Blue Jays before running into trouble in the sixth. He surrendered a leadoff home run to Toronto left fielder Matt Stairs and later allowed RBI singles to Lyle Overbay and Aaron Hill. Wakefield finished the night with three earned runs over six frames while striking out four and walking three. Wakefield is 13-10 with a 4.50 ERA in 32 career outings against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start after a strong spring, Robertson allowed five earned runs on seven hits, struck out five and walked two in five innings. He left with the game tied at 5, giving him a no-decision on the day. He looked good at some times, and at other times would leave pitches up for the White Sox to drive. Robertson has a 2-3 record against the Red Sox in his career with a 6.42 ERA. At Fenway Park, he has gone 1-2 with an ERA at 7.56.

home_pitcher_note: Although the White Sox did not lose the game, it was not exactly the start to the 2008 season sought out by Contreras. It was especially true after Contreras'  dismal 2007 showing. The right-hander had trouble finding the strike zone, walking four in five-plus innings and throwing just 56 of his 92 pitches for strikes. Contreras yielded four earned runs on 10 hits, striking out two, but also losing his rhythm early on in the game. He faces the Tigers once again, this time on six days rest following Thursday's rainout.
away_pitcher_note: Willis put up an interesting line in his first start for his new team. He allowed three earned runs on just one hit and had a no-hitter through five innings, But he issued seven walks, retaining his control problems from Spring Training. He will make his second career start at U.S. Cellular Field. He left in the second inning with arm troubles in his only other start there.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander became the first White Sox starter to pick up a victory during the team's initial run through the starting five, allowing three runs on three hits over six innings. Floyd was touched up by Brandon Inge's two-run home run in the fourth, but he only walked two and gave up five other hits. He exited after just 87 pitches, raising his record to 2-0 over his past three appearances at Comerica Park, with an extra day off in between starts. Floyd gets the call again against the Tigers, with this effort coming in Chicago, where Floyd has a career mark of 0-3 with a 6.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander allowed a career-high nine nuns in his last start, a 13-2 loss to the White Sox on Sunday night, although four of the runs were unearned. He was sharp at times, but struggled with his command in his last two innings. He also allowed a home run to Nick Swisher on his second pitch of the game.

home_pitcher_note: Much like Mark Buehrle, Vazquez bounced back nicely in his second start of 2008 after a rough debut performance in Cleveland. The right-hander struck out eight and walked just one over seven innings, allowing three runs on seven hits. He had a defeat turned into victory courtesy of Joe Crede's seventh-inning grand slam. Vazquez faces his third different American League Central opponent in three starts, carrying a 4-4 record with a 4.73 ERA lifetime against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers battled his command much more in his second outing of the season after a quality start in his first, but he gave his struggling team a chance at a victory in both circumstances. Nevertheless, he's 0-2 after two starts in a season for the first time since 1995. He struggled in two starts on Chicago's south side last season after allowing just two earned runs over 20 innings there in 2006, but the difference was partly due to the difference in his health.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman became the first Tigers pitcher to earn a victory with his five-plus innings of work on Wednesday at Boston, recovering from a pair of early runs to keep the mighty Red Sox lineup relatively in check. He continued to show progression with his offspeed pitch, using it liberally and early to try to get Boston's power hitters off their timing. That could come in handy against a Twins lineup that has put up big innings against him over the years.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn continued to turn heads in his second Major League start. He gave up just two runs on seven hits over five innings against the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field. With a dominating fastball and cutter, Blackburn has had success by mixing in his offspeed pitches more frequently. He now must try to carry that same plan into his first career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: A struggling slider and inconsistent location has left Robertson unable to eat innings like he usually does. He threw 107 pitches over 5 1/3 innings in his last start Thursday at Boston, on the way to a combined 212 pitches from Tigers pitchers on the night, despite Robertson's command of the inside part of the plate the first time through the Red Sox order. He was stingy against the Twins last season, going 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: On a chilly night in Chicago, Baker was able to be effective, although not brilliant, against the White Sox. Baker pitched five innings and allowed three runs, all of which came on solo home runs. Baker�s few mistakes came on balls up in the zone, and the pitcher admitted that weather was a factor in his miscues. His next test will come in Detroit at Comerica Park, where the right-hander is 1-1 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: In a big contract season, the 2007 Cy Young Award winner has endured one of his career's toughest stretches to open the season. Struggling greatly with his command, Sabathia has yet to win, pitching poorly in each of his three starts. Whether the pressure is getting to Sabathia cannot be said so early, but his 3 2/3 innings Friday against the A's was his shortest stint in nearly two years. Lifetime against the Tigers, Sabathia is 13-8 with a 4.30 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be recalled from Triple-A Toledo to make his second Major League start. He'll take the place of Dontrelle Willis, who went on the 15-day disabled list with a hyperextended right knee. The 26-year-old Venezuelan, won each of his first two starts this season at Triple-A Toledo, allowing three runs on seven hits over 12 innings with 11 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona followed up a pair of outstanding starts with a startlingly wild loss against Oakland Saturday night. Blaming faulty mechanics, Carmona walked a career-high eight hitters while allowing three runs over just 3 1/3 innings. No Cleveland starter in 15 years had walked as many hitters in a game. Carmona says his arm was getting away from his body, which led to an inconsistent delivery. The team hopes the 24-year-old right-hander will be able to correct his delivery during his bullpen session between starts. In eight career outings against Detroit, Carmona is 3-2 with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This was not where Verlander expected his stats to be three starts into this season, but to some extent, he has pitched better than his record. He allowed a run on two hits over his first seven innings last Saturday at the White Sox before he lost his command in the eighth inning. He ended up being charged with six runs over 7 2/3 innings as his winless streak stretched to three starts, the second-longest of his career.

home_pitcher_note: The Blue Jays recalled Purcey from Triple-A Syracuse on Thursday and he's scheduled to make his Major League debut with a start against the Tigers on Friday. The left-hander is making a spot start for right-hander A.J. Burnett, who is being held back until Sunday after he made a relief appearance in Wednesday's 14-inning marathon against Texas. This season at Triple-A, the 25-year-old Purcey has gone 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers' 0-3 record to start a season is the first for him since 1991. After throwing a quality start in his season debut on April 2, he has struggled with his command in back-to-back outings, the more recent being a loss at Chicago in which he allowed four runs on seven hits with four walks in four-plus innings. He has a stellar 3.32 ERA to go with a 6-4 record for his career at the Rogers Centre.

home_pitcher_note: McGowan picked up a tough loss against the Orioles on Monday, surrendering three runs on 10 hits over six innings. It was the second quality start of the season for the right-hander, but McGowan has only received eight runs of support through three starts. In the defeat, McGowan struck out five and walked one, giving him 16 strikeouts vs. seven walks over 17 innings this season. In his career against the Tigers, McGowan is 1-2 with a 9.95 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: A few bad pitches and poor defense behind him led to a mediocre outing for Bonderman on Monday. Arguably Detroit's best starter thus far, Bonderman allowed seven runs -- four earned -- on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings.  His defense made three errors. He is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA against the Blue Jays in his career. At Rogers Centre, he is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett struggled late on Sunday against the Rangers, leaving after 5 2/3 innings having allowed four runs, all earned, on seven hits with two walks and three strikeouts. The right-hander made a rare relief outing in the 14th inning on Wednesday -- Burnett's first stint out of the bullpen since 2004 -- and he allowed two runs on three hits in one inning and took the loss. Lifetime against the Tigers, Burnett is 1-1 with a 9.88 ERA in three games, all starts.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson left his last start on Tuesday with tighness in his left lat after allowing four earned runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. The team said he will be evaluated by team trainers on Wednesday. Manager Jim Leyland said after the game that trainers told him Robertson should not miss a start. In his career against the Blue Jays, the left-hander has a 3-2 record and 4.46 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum continued his impressive early-season run in his latest outing, in which he earned a win over the Orioles on the road on Tuesday. The 26-year-old right-hander yielded two runs on four hits, including a pair of solo home runs, with four strikeouts and three walks over 6 2/3 innings. For the season, Marcum has compiled 20 strikeouts over 20 2/3 innings. In his career against the Tigers, Marcum is 0-0 with a 7.36 ERA in three relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga joined Detroit's rotation in place of injured Dontrelle Willis and took his game to a struggling Indians lineup in his first Tigers start. By pounding the lower part of the strike zone and moving ahead in the count, the 26-year-old Venezuelan recovered from a first-inning home run to retire the next 17 batters in order before tiring in the seventh. It added up to his first Major League victory.

home_pitcher_note: Until this season, the Tigers had never lost more than two of Verlander's starts in a row. Now, his outings have accounted for four of Detroit's losses, the latest a resounding defeat Thursday at Cleveland in which Verlander battled his command from the start and never quite found it. His fastball control has run off and on this season, and without it, the power aspect of his game is much less effective. The good news for Verlander is that a much more invited foe awaits in Texas, against which he owns a 3-1 record and 2.49 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his fifth start and his fourth start on the road. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in his first three starts away from Arlington. He was 2-7 with an 8.04 ERA on the road last year. Opponents are hitting .292 off him so far this year but just .192 with runners in scoring position. He is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in four career starts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers picked up his first victory of the season with an impressive performance against the Blue Jays in his last start. The veteran left-hander allowed just three hits over 6 2/3 innings. His only real struggles came during the bottom of the fifth inning when he started battling some control problems. He is 6-3 with a 3.80 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the year on the disabled list with a blister on the middle finger of his right hand, Mendoza allowed seven runs in three-plus innings against the Red Sox. He is a power sinker ball pitcher but he needs to complement that with a better breaking ball and/or changeup. In eight Major League appearances over the past two seasons, left-handed hitters are batting .346 and right-handers are hitting .205.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman struggled with his control during his last outing against the Blue Jays. He issued six walks and required 108 pitches to get through five innings of work. His most dangerous inning came in the bottom of the second. After allowing a leadoff single to open the frame, Bonderman issued three consecutive walks but was able to escape with just two earned runs after inducing a key double play. Bonderman is 2-1 with a 4.83 ERA in five career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers wanted to give Jennings two days of extra rest but decided they couldn't do that because of their overworked bullpen. So Jennings pitches on his normal four days of rest. Scott Feldman was recalled from Double-A Frisco but will be in the bullpen. The Rangers were going to start him but were concerned about not having a long reliever behind him. So Feldman will be in long relief behind Jennings.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson was cruising during his last start against the Blue Jays until he ran into trouble during the fourth inning. The biggest blow came off the bat off 5-foot-7 David Eckstein. The Toronto shortstop took a 1-1 four-seam fastball and hit it over the wall in left for his first home run of the season. Robertson escaped the four-run inning but was finished after five. He allowed five runs on eight hits while striking out five en route to his second loss of the season. Robertson is 0-4 with an 8.91 ERA in seven career starts against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Santana, returning to 2006 form when he won 16 games, is coming off one of the finest efforts of his career on Saturday at home against the Mariners. Across eight innings, he yielded three hits and no walks, striking out eight. An Adrian Beltre homer was the only blemish as Santana maintained his mid-90s heater to the finish, striking out the last two men he faced. He is 2-2 with a 5.82 career ERA in four outings against the Tigers. At Comerica Park, he�s 0-2 with a 15.26 ERA, having gotten knocked around in his only start in Detroit last season (eight earned runs on seven hits, including two homers, in 3 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: By winning each of his first two starts as a fill-in for injured Dontrelle Willis, Galarraga owns the statistical oddity of taking the team lead in wins, even though the rest of the rotation has been unchanged since the season began. For Galarraga, it's about throwing strikes and getting ahead in counts while opposing teams try to figure out his game. He has scattered just four hits over 12 innings with four walks and 10 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Moseley will make it his focus to get deeper in the game after not getting past the fifth inning in three of his four starts, the exception being a six-inning effort against the Indians. He's been a pitch or two away from getting out of trouble, and manager Mike Scioscia thinks he has been better than his record suggests. The plan is to keep him in the rotation until John Lackey returns, presumably in mid-May. Moseley is 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA in four career appearances against the Tigers, and he hasn't allowed a run in three innings at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander's winless skid ended Tuesday with six innings of one-run ball against the Rangers, but the real improvement was in the quality of his pitches. A slight tweak to raise his arm angle helped bring more consistent velocity to his fastball and sharper downward movement to his breaking ball. He has never beaten the Angels in his career despite scattering just three runs over 13 innings in two career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver needed 105 pitches to make it through five innings against the highly selective Red Sox on Tuesday night at Fenway Park, letting a 5-1 lead get away as he yielded five earned runs on 10 hits. Weaver actually felt stronger, with more zip on his fastball, after making an adjustment between starts in his delivery to acquire more balance. He was throwing 93-94 mph consistently and struck out four without walking a hitter. He is 1-1 with a 14.14 ERA in two career outings against the Tigers; he has not faced them at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes pitched just two innings in his start on April 24 at Chicago before a 51-minute rain delay knocked him out of the game. The good news for Hughes was that they were scoreless frames, as he allowed one hit and faced the minimum after getting a double play to end the second. Hughes still has not recorded a victory as he makes his sixth start of the campaign, facing the Tigers for the second time in his career. Detroit touched him for five runs in six innings last Aug. 26.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers struggled early and often in his last start vs. the Rangers. The 42-year-old lasted just 3 1/3 innings, allowing six earned runs on nine hits and left with the bases loaded after walking in a run. He had trouble with his control, throwing only 44 of his 73 pitches for strikes and walking three batters. Rogers looks to rebound against the Yankees, whom he pitched for from 1996-97. But he has struggled against his old club, going 5-7 with a 6.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte's last start came unhinged in a troublesome fifth inning in which Cleveland scored four times. Pettitte recorded the first two outs easily, but then allowed two singles as his arm strength evaporated, then surrendered back-to-back homers to Jhonny Peralta and Franklin Gutierrez.  Pettitte, who walked three and struck out three, noted that he was battling the after-effects of the flu bug that has circulated through the Yankees' clubhouse for weeks. Pettitte beat the Tigers on Aug. 1 at Yankee Stadium, hurling eight innings of one-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman had control problems for the second straight start last time out against the Rangers. He allowed two runs on two hits but walked seven. Bonderman has struggled against the Yankees, going 2-6 in nine starts with a 5.58 ERA. The right-hander owns a 1-3 record at Yankee Stadium. He has especially had problems against outfielder Johnny Damon, who has hit .438 (14-for-32) against him.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy ran into trouble in a three-run second inning on Saturday at Cleveland, issuing a bases-loaded walk, a sacrifice fly and a bloop RBI single. He got back on track to throw five innings of three-run ball, which encouraged manager Joe Girardi. Looking to overcome a winless start to his season, Kennedy allowed seven hits, but none after Travis Hafner's bloop, finishing at 105 pitches after five innings, walking one and striking out three. After the game, Kennedy waffled between saying he was happy with the outing and not real upset about it, the second inning still sticking with him. The Yankees viewed the start as progress, even though Kennedy has allowed three runs or more in four of his five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: For a normally strong starter off to the worst opening month of his career, Robertson showed progress in his last start against an Angels team that normally can hurt him. A four-run fourth inning, paced by a Vladimir Guerrero two-run homer, proved to be his downfall, but he lasted seven innings while throwing just 89 pitches. A similar start in a more favorable matchup could give him a better chance in New York.

home_pitcher_note: The leader of the Twins' starting staff couldn't help the team to save its taxed bullpen in his last start. Hernandez gave up seven earned runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Rangers to pick up his first loss of the season. It was also the first time Hernandez had been unable to pitch at least six innings in a start for the Twins. One other sign of concern is the fact that the right-hander has already shown a penchant for giving up the long ball, allowing a total of six in his last three starts. Next up for Hernandez will be his first start of the year against the Tigers at the Metrodome.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga had another strong outing in his third start after being recalled from Triple-A two weeks ago, this time against an impressive Angels offense. He no-hit them through 5 2/3 innings before Vladimir Guerrero wrecked it with a triple. Galarraga could not get out of the seventh, finishing with three runs allowed -- one earned --  on three hits and two walks. In his three Major League starts this season, he has allowed three earned runs on seven hits in 18 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baker saw his streak of 12 straight starts in which he held opponents to three runs or less come to an end against the Rangers. Baker allowed five runs over 4 1/3 innings before leaving with a mild groin strain. It's unclear whether that injury might affect his next start, but the pitcher will get an extra day of rest due to the team's number of off-days. Baker's next start would come against the Tigers. The right-hander gave up three runs over seven innings in his lone start vs. Detroit this year.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his first win of the season, Verlander looked sharp through three innings against the Angels, but he ran into trouble in the next three. He allowed one run each in the fourth and fifth, before allowing four in the sixth that knocked him out of the game. Verlander, which many pundits picked to win this year's American League Cy Young award, is off the worst start of his three-year career. He faces Minnesota for the first time this season. Verlander is 3-3 with a 4.00 ERA in six career starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander got back to what he does best in his latest start against the Sox and that's use his curveball to offset a strong fastball. It helped Bonser to limit his number of walks, issuing just one over seven innings, and he struck out a season-high eight. Bonser said his biting curve was the best he's had all season. Bonser will now face the Tigers in the three-game series finale. In two career starts against Detroit, Bonser is 2-0 with 3.75 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers earned his first victory at Yankee Stadium in 11 years on Tuesday by holding the Bronx Bombers to two runs over six innings despite walking the bases loaded in the third. He'll try to even his record on the season by continuing his success at the Metrodome, where he's 15-7 with a 3.90 ERA for his career but has only pitched once since joining the Tigers three years ago. He won all three of his starts against the Twins in 2006 but missed them during his injury-shortened 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman has some momentum going in his favor following a victory at Yankee Stadium, where he loaded the bases three batters into the game and went on to toss 7 2/3 innings of two-run ball. It was one of the strongest performances of the season from a Tigers starter not named Armando Galarraga, and it showcased what Bonderman can do if he stays aggressive and claims the inside part of the plate against left-handed hitters. If he can do the same against David Ortiz and Boston's feared lineup, he'll give himself a shot to get over the .500 mark.
away_pitcher_note: Dating back to Sept. 22, 2007, the Red Sox have won Matsuzaka's last eight starts. Matsuzaka earned a no-decision in his last start, but was in top form, limiting the Blue Jays to two hits and no runs over seven innings. Matsuzaka turned in a strong performance against the Tigers on April 8, firing 6 2/3 shutout innings, and is limiting opponents to a .164 average.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson rebounded from a winless April with a victory Thursday night at Yankee Stadium, something that seemed unlikely after a Bobby Abreu home run put him down three runs three batters into his outing. He recovered to retire nine straight batters and give his offense a chance to get him a lead. If he can command his fastball-slider combination, he'll have a chance to build on that.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer took a tough-luck loss in his last start, giving up three runs over seven innings against the Blue Jays. However, it marked only the third time in Wakefield's career he started a game without getting at least one strikeout. Wakefield is 13-10 lifetime against the Tigers with a 4.50 ERA. At Comerica Park, he is 2-3 with a 5.08 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga picked up his first Major League loss in his last start Friday at Minnesota with two earned runs and two unearned tallies over six innings. The aggressiveness that has helped him attack opponents remained, but his command was off enough to allow a run-scoring wild pitch and a bases-loaded walk to haunt him. He'll need to recapture that control to contain a Red Sox lineup known for working pitchers into quick exits and bad pitching lines.
away_pitcher_note: The righty has been on a roll, going 2-1 with a 1.40 ERA in his last three starts. This will be Buchholz's first career appearance against the Tigers. Buchholz has allowed three earned runs or less in six of his seven starts this season. Opponents are hitting .238 against him.

home_pitcher_note: The struggles continued into May for Verlander in his last start, but with four runs allowed over seven innings, he gave Detroit a chance at a victory had they mustered any offense against the Twins. The bright side was in his stuff, from sustained mid-90s velocity on his fastball to a tight breaking ball that dropped late. If he can take that into his outing against the Red Sox, a little Tigers offense might be enough for him to earn a victory. He tossed 7 2/3 innings of two-run ball against Boston with seven strikeouts in their lone meeting last year.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett got a lot of help from his friends -- both offensively and defensively -- in winning his last start, over Tampa Bay. The Red Sox made several nifty defensive plays behind their ace, including Manny Ramirez throwing Carlos Pena out at the plate with a run that would have made it 5-4 in the fourth inning. Beckett settled down after that as his teammates matched their season high with 12 runs in the win. Beckett is 1-2 in three starts on the road this year, yielding nine earned runs in 19 2/3 innings away from home, striking out 24 in those three starts. He is 0-1 with a 7.50 ERA in his only lifetime start against Detroit, that loss coming at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers retired the first 11 Twins he faced in order Sunday at the Metrodome before Minnesota began chipping away at what had been a six-run lead. He arguably should have finished his afternoon with seven innings and three runs allowed, but a two-out error in the seventh extended the inning for the Twins' go-ahead rally. Rogers allowed two runs on six hits in six innings to the Yankees last week in the Bronx.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees have strongly hinted that Igawa will be the choice to be promoted from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre to start against the Tigers, taking the place of the demoted Ian Kennedy. GM Brian Cashman reasoned that Rasner and Igawa are pitching the best at Triple-A, and after an up-and-down spring, this would be Igawa's first big league start of '08. The Japanese import had a shaky first season in the Majors and started this season 3-3 with a 3.86 ERA in seven starts at Triple-A. Igawa did not face the Tigers in the 14 big league appearances (12 starts) he made last year, and was 0-2 with a 5.76 ERA in five starts away from Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Bonderman was that his slider was more consistent as an out pitch in his last start against Boston. The bad news was he yielded a pair of two-run homers that sank his fortunes in defeat. He needed 113 pitches to last six innings, but he was much more efficient in his previous start against the Yankees. If he can keep that up in the rematch, he could continue his pattern of alternating wins and losses so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rasner was called up from Triple-A Scranton to make his first 2008 start in the Majors in a game against Seattle on Sunday. He gave up two runs on two hits in the first inning, and then settled in to pitch five scoreless innings, during which he gave up only three hits. With youngsters Phil Hughes, who is injured, and Ian Kennedy, who is working out his pitching problems in Triple-A, not around, Rasner has a great chance to stick with the team and said he intends to take advantage of it. He didn't walk a batter on Sunday and yielded only six in 31 innings at Scranton.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke just keeps grinding along. He won his first three starts, then he took a loss and two no-decisions despite pitching well in his next three. But he got his fourth victory on Wednesday night in a blowout over the Angels. He cruised through seven innings, giving up five hits and three runs and notched eight strikeouts. His ERA was second in the American League only to Cliff Lee's 0.81 mark for the Tribe. Greinke's first win this season came over the Tigers, and he is 7-3 against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson doesn't have a quality start in seven outings so far this year, and he has been inefficient with his pitches in his last two outings. Still, if he can repeat the last five innings of his victory over the Yankees from May 1, he'd be pretty happy, considering he gave up a three-run home run to Bobby Abreu three batters into his outing that night.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar had another strong outing last Thursday night, going seven innings in a 4-1 loss to the Orioles. Manager Trey Hillman didn't think he was as sharp as in his previous outing and he often fell behind in the count. The rookie walked just two but, sure enough, both runners scored and he floated a high changeup that Nick Markakis smashed for a three-run homer. Even so, Hochevar hasn't seemed overmatched in his four starts since being recalled from Omaha. He's at his best when he attacks with his sinking fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Not since the Tigers' 119-loss season of 2003 has a Detroit starting pitcher gotten off to as bad a start, record-wise, as Verlander, who gave up a three-run rally on singles in his last start against Boston before Kevin Youkilis took him deep for a two-run homer to put the game away. Manager Jim Leyland says it's execution, not stuff or velocity, that's hurting Verlander right now, and Verlander will spend his time between starts trying to fix a mechanical flaw he and pitching coach Chuck Hernandez spotted. If he's going to start a turnaround, there's nowhere better than Kansas City, where he's 3-0 with a 1.33 ERA in four career starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a promising seven-inning shutout performance at Cleveland, Meche hit a bump at home against the Orioles last Friday night. His curveball, which had revived sharpness against the Tribe, got "loopy" against the O's. They whacked two home runs and scored five runs in Meche's five innings. There has to be some concern about his ERA, 6.31 after eight starts, and the eight homers he's given up in 45 2/3 innings. Last season, he had a 3.67 ERA and surrendered just 22 homers in 216 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers pitched well in his second start against the Yankees this season. He threw six solid innings against his old club, allowing two earned runs on nine hits and two walks, while striking three. He gave up a solo home run to Jason Giambi in the second inning, but did not surrender another run until reliever Zach Miner allowed an inherited runner to score in the seventh. In the second game of the season, Rogers took the loss against the Royals after giving up two runs on five hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well in his start last, Friday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, but Ted Lilly was just a little better. Haren allowed just two runs on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander cruised through the first four innings and struck out the first two in the fifth. He then gave up a double to Mark DeRosa and walked Reed Johnson intentionally to bring up Lilly, who stroked a fastball into center to score a run. Alfonso Soriano followed with an RBI double. In his start prior to that, Haren didn't get a decision in a matchup with New York's Johan Santana.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman's first-inning troubles continued in his last start. He struck out the Yankees' Johnny Damon to start the game, but then served up a home run to Derek Jeter. Two hits and two walks later, another run scored. Bonderman lasted just four innings, giving up five earned runs on six hits and four walks. He faced the Royals in the third game of the season and lasted 6 1/3 innings, giving up four earned runs on eight hits, two of which were home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer was impressive in his last start against the Cubs, though he did not get a win as the bullpen was unable to hold the lead. Scherzer has made three big league appearances, two as a starter. In his Major League debut on April 29, he set the baseball world buzzing when he retired all 13 batters he faced in relief of Edgar Gonzalez. Scherzer, who was the team's No. 1 pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, struck out seven and his electric fastball reached 98 mph at times during the dominating performance. The D-backs put Scherzer in the rotation in place of Gonzalez and he struggled a bit in his first start against the Phillies as he allowed five runs (two earned) on seven hits over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga took a no-decision in his last start against the Red Sox, giving up five earned runs on seven hits, while striking out six in 5 1/3 innings. He struggled against Kevin Youkilis, as the red-hot first baseman cranked two home runs off him. After winning his first two starts against Cleveland and Toronto, Galarraga has two no-decisions and a loss in his last three starts. He makes his first career start against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson has won his last two starts to give him 287 for his career. In his last outing, he wasn't particularly sharp, as he allowed four runs over five innings to the Rockies at Chase Field. He also hit a ball off the wall in the second but stumbled over first base and had to hold with a single. In his start prior to that, Johnson picked up the win despite allowing four runs on five hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson turned in his first quality start of the season Tuesday at Kansas City, scattering two runs over seven innings, but ended up with no decision in his duel with Zack Greinke. Nonetheless, the performance offered some hope that the left-hander is getting closer to his aggressive pitching self. He gave up 10 hits in the outing, but limited the scoring damage to a Jose Guillen two-run double while not walking anyone.

home_pitcher_note: Other than a mid-90s fastball that hasn't hit the upper 90s, Verlander looks a little more like his old form with each passing start. Still, the Tigers' offensive struggles in his outings have left him in the AL lead for losses, the most recent loss occurring despite holding Kansas City to two runs over six-plus innings on Wednesday. Detroit has scored two runs or fewer in seven of Verlander's nine starts. He has won all four of his starts against Seattle during his career -- three times last year alone -- to go with a 2.63 ERA over 27 1/3 innings. But then, he had never lost to the Royals before this year, either.
away_pitcher_note: Silva allowed two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings and got a no-decision in his last start against the Rangers as he continues to be a consistent member of the Seattle rotation. Silva did have to leave the game with mild lower back stiffness in the seventh inning, but he said after the game that he will be able to make his next start. Since the Mariners are skipping Jarrod Washburn in the rotation, Silva will go Tuesday at home against Detroit. Silva has been lights out at Safeco Field. He is 5-2 with a 3.20 ERA for eight career starts at his new home ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: After three consecutive quality starts helped him even his record following three straight losses to open the season, Rogers had one of his worst starts as a Tiger on Thursday at Kansas City. Royals hitters sat on his breaking ball and sent out 11 hits over his four innings of work, resulting in seven runs and a jump of more than three-quarters of a run to his ERA. He has a loss and a no-decision in two outings against Seattle in a Detroit uniform, allowing nine earned runs over 12 innings in the process.
away_pitcher_note: It has been six days since the veteran left-hander had his first career save with a scoreless inning of relief agains the Rangers in Arlington. He faced four batter and retired three of them to walk off the mound to high-fives and handshakes. His last start didn't go nearly as well as he wobbled during a 38-pitch second inning against the White Sox and suffered his fifth loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman enjoyed one of his stronger outings of the season, but an Arizona seventh-inning comeback left it for naught. He allowed a lone run over his first six innings before back-to-back walks leading off the seventh set up an Arizona comeback and left him with a no-decision. Nonetheless, it was just his second quality start in nine outings this season. He had all sorts of trouble against the Mariners last season, allowing 14 runs over 14 1/3 innings to bump his career ERA versus Seattle to 5.01.
away_pitcher_note: Early game blues continue to haunt the veteran right-hander who been nowhere near as effective as a year ago when he led the team in wins with 16. He surrendered five runs in the first three innings, including three in the first inning, in a loss to the Padres in his last outing. He has walked 15 batters in his last 20 innings, which has kept him in trouble and hikes his pitch count. Batista has pitched in the seventh inning twice in his eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: With Dontrelle Willis heading to the bullpen for now, Galarraga remains in Detroit's rotation, where his ability to throw strikes and avoid serious damage has allow the Tigers to win five of his six starts. Four of those outings have been quality starts, tying him with Kenny Rogers for the team lead. One of those, however, was his only loss of the season, to the Twins on May 2 at the Metrodome, where two of his four runs allowed were unearned in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander appeared to make more progress in his latest start, despite picking up his fourth straight loss. Slowey allowed just three runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings to the Rockies in his first Interleague start at Coors Field. It was a bit of a laborious outing though for Slowey, as he threw 109 pitches in that time. The pitcher said his goal in his next start will be to make more pitches down in the zone. He'll get to test that in Detroit when he faces the Tigers for the first time this season. Slowey is 1-0 with a 6.00 ERA in one career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced and didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning in his latest outing Sunday at Arizona. A two-run fifth and two more in the sixth, however, sent him to defeat and continued the roughest start to a season in his big-league career.
away_pitcher_note: Bonser gave up more than one home run in a start for the first time this season, allowing two solo shots to the Rangers over his 6 1/3 innings Monday. Bonser delivered his sixth quality start of the season only allowing three earned runs in the outing. He ran into some late trouble against the Rangers which forced him out of the  game in the seventh. Bonser got back on track by rectifying a problem from earlier this season of overthrowing the ball. The right-hander had five strikeouts and did not issue a walk. Bonser will next take the mound Saturday at Comerica Park in the middle of a three-game set against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander made one of his best starts in his baffling year against the Mariners on Tuesday. He gave up a single and a home run in the first inning, but he allowed only two hits over the next five frames. He gave the Mariners a steady helping of offspeed pitches, which helped him post a season-high seven strikeouts. Verlander faced Minnesota once this season, a loss that saw him allow four earned runs on seven hits in seven innings. For his career, he has a 3-4 record and 4.19 ERA in seven starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins struck out three and didn't walk a batter in 6 1/3 strong innings Tuesday during an 11-4 victory over Texas. It was Perkins' third consecutive quality start. The lefty sailed through six scoreless innings before getting into trouble in the seventh by throwing up in the zone. Perkins was deceptive throughout, primarily relying on his changeup as an out pitch but effectively mixing the rest of his repertoire. He has been solid since being recalled from the minors after not making the team out of Spring Training. Next up for Perkins is a road start at Detroit on Sunday which will cap a three-game series.

home_pitcher_note: Garland put 10 runners on base in six innings in Toronto on Wednesday night, but only three scored -- and that made him a winner in vintage Garland style. Tough under pressure, he made pitches when he needed them, using his defense to make plays. He had only one strikeout against two walks, yielding eight hits. He seems to be settling into a nice groove. He's 13-6 in 24 career outings against the Tigers with a 4.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers followed his rough start last week by allowing four runs on eight hits (two home runs) and three walks in 5 1/3 innings. Rogers didn't start in the three-game series with the Angels earlier this season and didn't face them last year, either. In 2006, he went 1-1 against them with a 1.29 ERA. For his career against the Angels, the 43-year-old has a 17-15 record and 4.07 ERA in 44 starts.

home_pitcher_note: After claiming wins in six of his first seven starts, Santana has leveled off, going winless with two losses and a no-decision his past three starts. He's still throwing in the mid-90s with a quality slider and changeup, but the results haven't been the same: 13 earned runs in 17 2/3 innings (6.62 ERA) in those last three outings. He was touched for nine hits and four earned runs in six innings by the Blue Jays on Thursday, striking out seven to give him 57 Ks in 66 2/3 innings. He beat the Tigers on April 25 in Detroit, yielding three earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman worked in and out of trouble all afternoon against the Mariners to notch his third win his last time out. He had a runner on third in the first and third innings, and then loaded the bases with none out in the fifth, but escaped with only two earned runs. Bonderman had his share of troubles against the Angels last year, going 1-1 in three starts, but with an 8.27 ERA. Two of those starts were at Angel Stadium, where he had a 16.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Two outs away from his first career complete game and shutout in Chicago Friday night, Saunders gave way to Francisco Rodriguez, who held the lead but not the shutout. In a weakened condition while fighting sinus congestion, Saunders held the White Sox to three hits and an earned run in 8 1/3 innings, walking three and striking out four in yet another All-Star caliber performance. Thirteen of his outs came on the ground, his two-seam fastball having great effect. Saunders has a 2.84 ERA with no record in two career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga's hot hand was cooled by the Twins in his last start. He gave up five runs on seven hits and five walks to earn his second loss of the season, both against Minnesota. Galarraga faced the Angels earlier this season in a 6-4 win on April 26 at Comerica Park. He earned a no-decision after allowing three runs in six innings and carried a no-hitter for 5 2/3 innings, his only career start against them.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander makes his fifth start of the month still looking for his first win in May. He has lost four straight starts, taking much of the glitter off his 3-0 start with the Mariners, who signed him to a four-year, $48 million contract during the offseason. Silva is a battler, though, and is determined to get on a roll. As a pitch-to-contact pitcher, he needs the defense to be at the top of its game when he pitches.
away_pitcher_note: After going his first seven outings without a quality start, Robertson has two of them in his past three games, the latest a victory over the Twins during which he pitched 6 1/3 innings of three-run ball. Considering the Tigers scored 19 runs for him, he had plenty of reason to be aggressive against Minnesota hitters, but the low hit and walk totals were both encouraging. Robertson was miserable against the Mariners last year, allowing a combined 10 earned runs on 17 hits over 9 1/3 innings with seven walks and 13 strikeouts. Both outings were at home; Robertson hasn't pitched at Safeco Field since tossing seven scoreless innings on April 22, 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had terrific stuff for seven innings Monday against Boston. Even manager John McLaren said it was the best he'd seen him pitch all season. He allowed just two hits and one run through seven, then gave up four runs on five hits in the eighth in a 5-3 loss. For the most part, Hernandez can't seem to put an entire game together. Either he stays too long with his fastball or his late-game sequencing is off. He is 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA in four career starts against Detroit. He beat the Tigers twice last season.
away_pitcher_note: How feast or famine is the Tigers offense? While Kenny Rogers is averaging an AL-best 7.18 runs of support per nine innings as the pitcher of record, and Armando Galarraga is averaging 6.75, Verlander is stuck near the bottom at 3.44. He had only one run of support in his last outing Sunday against the Twins, spoiling his second straight strong outing. Not only did he throw seven innings of one-run ball, he hit 99 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun. That's the strongest sign yet that Verlander is getting his usual stuff back. If so, that's further bad news for the Mariners, whom he held to one run over six innings with seven strikeouts last Tuesday in Detroit for a victory. He has won all five of his outings against Seattle over his career, including two at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Batista held the Red Sox to two hits over five scoreless innings last Tuesday night when, with one out and none on in the sixth inning, an easy ground ball to shortstop Yuniesky Betancourt was mishandled, opening the door to an eventual game-tying, three-run home run by Manny Ramirez. Batista departed after seven innings and did not get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman has quality starts in his last three outings, but one win and a pair of no-decisions to show for it. He took a four-hit shutout into the eighth inning Tuesday against the Angels before back-to-back singles set up his departure. Both runners scored, taking him out of line for a victory. The good news for Bonderman is that a flip in the rotation allows him to pitch close to home in Washington state. He has quality starts and victories in his last two outings at Safeco Field, one in each of the last two seasons.

home_pitcher_note: In his sixth start of the season, his fourth since being reinstated from the disabled list May 11, Harden completed seven innings for just the second time this year, scattering five hits with no walks and five strikeouts while allowing just one run. He was part of a pitching dual against Toronto's Roy Halladay, though, and watched the A's suffer a 2-1 loss. It was his third career start in which he did not surrender a walk. Harden did not face Detroit last year, but is 3-1 with a 3.70 ERA in his career against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers pushed Rogers back a day so that he could pitch at McAfee Coliseum, where he's 25-4 over a 20-year career that included two years with the A's. He's coming off of his best performance of the season, even though it earned him no decision in the Tigers' 1-0, 12-inning loss to the Angels last Monday. Beyond his seven scoreless innings, he racked up 13 groundouts and showed he can still command a game when he commands the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: After pitching the best game of his career with a one-run complete game in his previous start, Eveland tossed his worst against the Blue Jays in allowing seven runs on 11 hits with two walks and three strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings -- his shortest outing of the season. With the loss, his ERA went from 2.90 to 3.66. Eveland will look to get back to form against a Detroit team he's never faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling to find innings for Willis pitching out of the bullpen, manager Jim Leyland decided to slot six starters into a five-man rotation by working Willis in a piggy-back role with Armando Galarraga, the guy who replaced him. Willis will get the start, his first since he hyperextended his right knee on April 11. Galarraga, whose 8 1/3 innings his last time out marked the longest start by a Tiger this season, will then follow Willis in relief. It's an unusual move usually seen only in the Minor Leagues, but it's the one way Leyland could work Willis back into rotation without removing another deserving candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer continues to thrive as a starter. He allowed just two runs in six innings against the Rangers in a 3-1 loss on Friday. It was fourth time in nine starts that Duchscherer has gone at least six innings. Even more impressive, the former reliever has allowed two earned runs or fewer in seven of his nine starts. He has not allowed more than three earned runs in a start. He has never walked more than two batters in 205 career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson battled through flu-like symptoms in his last outing Friday at Seattle to last 5 2/3 innings, long enough to earn a win after the Tigers gave him a seven-run lead before he took the mound for his first pitch. He has alternated quality and non-quality starts over his last five starts, and after allowing four Mariners runs -- two of them on Adrian Beltre home runs -- he's due for a more effective outing. Problem is, he's 0-3 with a 6.12 in four regular-season starts at Oakland, though he was successful there in the 2006 ALCS.

home_pitcher_note: See that loss total? The Tigers have scored two runs or fewer in seven of those defeats, giving him a run support average of 3.12 runs per nine innings as the pitcher of record -- fourth-lowest among qualified AL starters. The other problem, of course, is his pitching, and Felix Hernandez purely outpitched Verlander in his last start. With four runs allowed over seven innings, one of them on a botched squeeze bunt attempt that became a steal of home, Verlander saw his three-game streak of quality starts come to an end. He's 3-6 with a 7.03 ERA in 10 career starts against the Indians, but 2-1 when facing them at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd gave up a home run to Jose Guillen against the Royals on Sunday and never recovered. He lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up all six runs in a loss. Mark Grudzielanek, who hadn't homered since last year, hit a two-run shot off him. Byrd lamented the fact that he struggled so much when his team really needed a series win. In his last three starts, Byrd has now given up 14 home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers is now back in his customary spot between Justin Verlander and Jeremy Bonderman, giving the Tigers a finesse left-hander between their two power right-handers for the weekend series against the Indians. It also allows Rogers to pitch on his normal four days' rest after tossing quality starts in his last two outings. He pitched into eighth inning Monday at Oakland for the first time since the 2006 World Series, allowing two runs but keeping Detroit in the game. Rogers owns a 17-16 career record against Cleveland with a 5.12 ERA, but he's 4-2 against the Indians since joining the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe it was the Texas heat or just the hot Texas bats that got to him, but Laffey had his first rough outing of the season Monday against the Rangers. In five innings of work, he gave up eight runs on 11 hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He served up two home runs, including a game-tying grand slam. In his first six starts, Laffey had shown an ability to consistently work himself out of trouble by getting double-play balls, but he didn't have as much success keeping the ball down in this one. He has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will return to the rotation after pitching three innings of relief in an unconventional piggyback start last Tuesday at Oakland. He walked two batters and allowed a three-run home run before retiring the last seven batters he faced. His return to the Tigers rotation gives him a rematch against the team he beat for his first Major League victory April 16 at Jacobs Field. He held the Tribe to a hit and two runs with six strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings that night, starting him on the roll that has made him stick on the Tigers staff.
away_pitcher_note: With Jake Westbrook back on the disabled list with elbow inflammation, the Indians will once again have to dip into their starting depth to round out the rotation. Sowers has made two spot starts for the Tribe this season, and now he'll get his first chance at a more sustained stay in '08. Through 10 starts at Triple-A Buffalo, Sowers had a 4-3 record and 2.08 ERA that ranked fourth in the International League. Sowers struck out 43 batters and walked just 17 in 60 2/3 innings. Sowers is 1-1 with a 6.30 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers and has never pitched in Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Willis makes his first full start since coming off the disabled list with a hyperextended right knee. He started a game in Oakland last Tuesday, but piggybacked the start with Armando Galarraga. Willis threw four innings, giving up no runs, two hits and five walks, and Galarraga relieved him. Willis is 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA in two career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: The hitting-friendly conditions at Rangers Ballpark did not work in Lee's favor in his last start Wednesday in Texas, when he gave up six runs on nine hits in five innings but won thanks to an outpouring of offensive support. In general, though, Lee hasn't been nearly as dominant of late as he was in the first six weeks of the season, when he was putting up downright historic numbers. He's allowed 16 earned runs over his last four starts, yet he's won his last three in a row. He'll be in more pitching-friendly conditions Monday, when he faces the Tigers for the first time this season. Lee is 3-6 with a 5.23 ERA in 14 career starts against the Tigers and 1-1 with a 3.53 ERA in six starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Though Robertson has split wins and losses over his last four outings, he owns a 6.00 ERA in that span along with 11 walks over 24 innings as he struggles to find his command. He gave up five runs on eight hits over 6 1/3 innings at Oakland in his last outing, using up 109 pitches in the process. His only start against the White Sox this year came in the season's first week, when Chicago scored five runs in as many innings.
away_pitcher_note: Contreras has thrown six straight quality starts and is 4-0 in that span. He threw seven strong innings in his last start against Kansas City, surrendering just four hits and one run. His first two starts of the season came against Detroit, and those two games represent a majority of his struggles this year. He's 0-1 against the Tigers this season, having allowed eight earned runs in 11 2/3 innings. He walked seven batters in those two games, though, and his command has significantly improved since, issuing just 10 walks in his last six starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: While Verlander continues to put up decent to good outings over the past month, his run support continues to wane. A three-run fourth inning doomed him in his last start against Cleveland, though he went on to last seven innings with five hits and eight strikeouts. A rematch with the White Sox provides little solace considering his 1-6 career record versus Chicago, including back-to-back losses over the first two weeks of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez allowed an uncharacteristic two home runs in his last start against the Twins, lasting just 5 1/3 innings and giving up four earned runs on Friday. It was good enough to get the win, though, something manager Ozzie Guillen praised him for after the game. He's faced Detroit once this year, shutting them down over seven innings. He allowed five hits, walked nobody and struck out nine to pick up his second win of the season. Surprisingly, Detroit is the only team Vazquez has shut out this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers put together his third straight quality start his last time out. He went seven innings for the third consecutive start, giving up three runs, one earned, on five hits. He wiggled out of two-on jams throughout the afternoon, but the former Gold Glove winner's throwing error in the sixth inning helped the third run home. Rogers has given up just three earned runs in his last three starts. He faced Chicago in April and had one of his worst outings of the season, surrendering seven runs in four innings in the Tigers' 11-0 loss at U.S. Cellular Field. This start, however, comes at Comerica Park, where Rogers is 2-1 in five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle had one of his best outings of the season Saturday against the Twins. He went eight innings, which matched a season high, and allowed just one run. He issued only one walk and struck out four. It was his first win since May 17, when he beat the Giants in San Francisco. Detroit was the second team Buehrle faced this season and he picked up his first win against them, allowing two runs -- one earned -- in seven innings. It's been an up-and-down season for Buehrle, but he's also been a victim of bad luck; his offense only averaged 3.72 runs of support for him before last Saturday's 11-run offensive explosion.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga just missed his second straight quality start against the Indians. He gave up two earned runs on four hits over 5 2/3 innings to earn his first career win at Comerica Park. He had his slider working, and when he does, he can be quite impressive. The Tigers, meanwhile, improved to 7-2 when he starts. Galarraga has never faced the Dodgers, but he did perform well in his only Interleague start. He held the Diamondbacks to two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's a homecoming for Michigan native Derek Lowe, who also is coming off a wild win over the Cubs. The Dodgers were losing when Lowe left the game, even though he had taken a no-hitter into the fifth inning. But a rare five-run rally against Carlos Zambrano gave Lowe a second consecutive win and fourth consecutive quality start. Lowe is 7-1 with a 1.82 ERA lifetime against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Though the Tigers still haven't formally announced their starter, manager Jim Leyland said it's 90-percent likely they'll give Bonine his first chance in the Majors. A former Minor League Rule 5 draft pick, Bonine has quietly worked his way up the Tigers farm system, capped with a 9-2 record this season at Triple-A Toledo. Not a power thrower, he has succeeded by becoming a ground-ball control pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Penny pitched well for the second straight outing Sunday against the Cubs, yielding three runs on six hits in six innings. He also struck out five and walked three. Penny has not won since May 2, a span of seven starts, but he's pitched much better in his last two, both of which have been quality starts in which his opponent has shut down the Dodgers' offense. Before that, he had compiled a 9.43 ERA in his previous five outings.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson earned his third quality start of the season in his last start against the hot White Sox. He went 6 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on eight hits, while walking two and striking out four. He had solid command, especially of his slider, as 53 of his 87 pitches went for strikes. He surrendered a solo home run to Jim Thome in the second inning, but didn't have many other jams until he left the game with the bases loaded in the seventh. Robertson has only one career start against the Dodgers, in which he gave up four runs on five hits in five innings and earned a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was better against the Padres, getting into the sixth inning with only one run scoring while he was on the mound and a second that scored on a reliever's wild pitch. Still, he had occasional bouts of wildness that served mainly to run up his pitch count and hasten his exit. He's truly advanced for a 20-year-old, but he'll need to quickly improve on the 13 walks in 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum was typically effective in his last outing, blanking Colorado for seven innings while striking out nine. As if for emphasis, Lincecum ended five innings with strikeouts, often by coaxing the Rockies to flail at his curveball. He has made 15 consecutive quality starts dating back to 2007 and owns a four-decision winning streak, his second of the season. When Lincecum works at least six innings, he's 13-4 with a 2.46 ERA in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Almost a year to the day after his no-hitter, Verlander tossed his first complete game since then with a four-hit performance over the White Sox, a team that has generally roughed up the young right-hander over his brief career. He needed just 101 pitches to do it, efficiently earning first-pitch popups by spotting his fastball. The Tigers are hoping it's the trigger for another June roll just in time for them to make up some ground from their slow start. It's also just in time for Interleague Play, in which Verlander is 7-0 in seven career starts with a 1.99 ERA and 48 strikeouts over 49 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez isn't the Giants' biggest winner -- that distinction belongs to Tim Lincecum -- but they've been most successful when he pitches, compiling an 11-3 mark when he starts. In last Thursday's series finale at Colorado, Sanchez won his fourth consecutive decision despite allowing seven runs and nine hits. He became the first Giants starter to record a victory while allowing at least that many runs since May 21, 2000, when Russ Ortiz surrendered 10 runs in a 16-10 win at Milwaukee. Nevertheless, Sanchez has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 11 of his 14 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers had his longest outing of the season against the White Sox his last time out. He lasted eight innings, giving up one earned run on four hits. The 43-year-old has pitched at least seven innings in each of his past four starts. He had some of his best command of the season, throwing strikes on 67 of his 96 pitches. Rogers has had six starts against the Giants in his 19-year career, the last one occurring in 2001. In those starts, he has allowed a combined 27 runs on 43 hits in 37 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zito walked more batters (four) than he struck out (three) in his last start, allowing four runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Athletics, his former team. He was one pitch away from a quality start, but walked in a run on a 3-2 count in the sixth inning before being pulled. He allowed three runs in a three-hit, one-walk third inning, and lasted less than six for the ninth time this season. After facing just six batters in the fourth and fifth innings, Zito began losing steam and elevating his pitches in the sixth frame.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga gave up no runs on three hits in his last start, though two hits came after the ball hit him in the foot and skewed into foul ground for infield singles. After the second one drilled his foot in the sixth inning, the team's trainer ran out to the mound to check Galarraga. He sat on the infield grass, holding his right lower leg in pain at one point, but he collected himself and finished the outing. The Tigers improved to 8-2 in games he starts. Galarraga has never faced the Giants in his short career. However, he has two impressive outings this season in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux had, well, an un-Maddux-like outing in his last start, against the Indians in Cleveland. He uncorked his first wild pitch of the season, hit his first batter of the season and made a rare throwing error in taking a loss. Maddux allowed two earned runs but threw away a comebacker for only his 13th error since 2000, which led to a three-run home run later in the inning when he hung a changeup to Ben Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Bonine made his Major League debut against the Dodgers on a FOX regional television broadcast. The right-hander, who was tied for the International League lead in wins, gave up six earned runs on 10 hits and no walks in 5 1/3 innings. He exited with a 10-6 lead and to a standing ovation from Tigers fans. Bonine backed up his reputation as a controlled strike-thrower, with 53 of his 77 pitches thrown for for strikes. He didn't walk a batter. No surprise, because he walked only 14 in 74 1/3 innings at Triple-A Toledo. Bonine didn't give up many hard hits, but did surrender a home run. He makes the first road start against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard to figure out Baek, who is still getting his feet wet in the National League after joining the Padres from Seattle last month. Baek allowed three runs in the first inning of his last start at Cleveland on June 14 on two hits and two walks. What happened after that? Baek retired 20 of the final 21 hitters he faced, including the last 16 consecutive hitters in earning a no-decision. Baek threw 110 pitches, so it's safe to say he's stretched out now after he pitched in relief with Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson had some of his best control this season in his last start. He needed only 66 pitches to get through six innings, with 45 of them going for strikes. He did not reach double-digit balls until the fourth. Robertson allowed no runs in an outing for the first time this season. He also recorded his second straight quality start and fourth of the year. Despite starting his career in the National League, the left-hander has never faced San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf told reporters after his last start in New York on June 17 that "I was awful today. I can count on one hand the number of pitches that I executed today." Wolf, who was coming off a blissful run during which he allowed two or fewer runs in his previous five starts, allowed three home runs, two to Jason Giambi. Wolf struggled with his fastball command early. There have been starts this season when the left-hander's stuff and command have improved as the game has progressed. But not in his last start. "When you can't throw your fastball where you want, it's going to be a tough day," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander gets one more chance to swing the bat this year in Interleague Play, but his bigger focus will be to rack up a win for his trouble. His tough luck Monday at San Francisco was less about run support than it was about a blown lead in the late innings after his six innings with two earned runs and seven strikeouts allowed him to leave with a 4-3 lead. He had won all seven of his Interleague starts before then, a tribute as much to his torrid pitching over the last two summers as the National League's struggles to actually hit him.

home_pitcher_note: It took five solid starts, but Rogers finally has a winning record after losing his first three outings this season. He has allowed just four earned runs on 25 hits over 36 innings in those last five starts, the latest being seven innings of one-run ball against the Giants last Tuesday. In the process, the command that marked his 17-win season in 2006 has made a comeback. He'll need to pound the strike zone carefully against a Cardinals lineup that ranks fifth in the Majors in on-base percentage and actually fares better in that regard against left-handers, despite hitting 10 points lower against them than versus right-handers.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has been rolling lately, and the formula is very simple. Throw strikes, and keep it in the ballpark. He's gone four straight starts without allowing a home run, and three straight without a walk. As a result, the right-hander has a 1.95 ERA in May. That's despite a couple of starts in the inhospitable environments of Minute Maid Park and Great American Ball Park. Now he gets another kind of challenge, pitching to a potent lineup that includes a designated hitter.

home_pitcher_note: The early-season phenomenon that Galarraga seemed to be upon his April callup keeps rolling, and he's quietly building a case for a spot on the American League All-Star pitching staff. Another victory against a quality club like the Cardinals would obviously further bolster his case. Not only has the former Rangers farmhand won his last three starts, but he hasn't allowed an earned run over 13 innings in his last two outings. He has allowed just 47 hits over 71 1/3 innings this season, which translates to a mere .184 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: No starter in the NL is hotter than Lohse, who is 6-0 with a 2.09 ERA over his past seven starts. Lohse has delivered desperately needed stability to a rotation reeling from injuries, and has done a huge part to keep the Cardinals in contention while they do without Adam Wainwright. He's throwing strikes (seven walks in seven starts) and letting his defense work, and it's going extremely well.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers maneuvered their rotation for their homestand so that Robertson could start on his normal rest. The way he's been winning, it's hard to blame them. Robertson has won his last three starts, tying a career-best winning streak he set in 2004, his first full Major League season. The latest came Saturday at San Diego, where he gave up five runs on seven hits over six innings but somehow avoided further damage to let his offense pick him up for the victory. He's 6-3 for his career in Interleague Play, including one victory over the Cardinals last year at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: This one is written in pencil, rather than ink, but it appears that Wellemeyer will get the start in the series finale in Detroit. He had been absolutely exceptional until coming down with some elbow soreness, and the injury resulted in an extremely rocky last start. A fairly intensive bullpen session told Wellemeyer that he's coming along well, though, and he expects to get the ball. If he's not ready, the assignment would probably fall to rookie Mitchell Boggs.

home_pitcher_note: Bonine earned no decision for his trouble in his second Major League start last Friday at San Diego, but with seven innings of two-run ball, he had a better performance than the win he recorded in his debut. He has an even ratio of ground balls to fly balls, but he has taken advantage of the defense behind him to throw strikes and mix pitches. His knuckleball remains an X-factor in future starts, should he need it.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had been pitching well, without run support or wins, for a month and a half. He was finally rewarded Saturday night, when he used his fastball and slider as out pitches and mixed in good off-speed stuff while holding the Mets to two hits over eight innings in a win at Coors field on Saturday night. Jimenez, who earned his first win since April 8, has a 1.35 ERA over his last 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: All the early-season speculation over whether Verlander was pitching hurt has been put to rest by his arsenal of stuff over his past few outings. He had a season-high 10 strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings last Sunday at San Diego despite lacking a feel for his offspeed pitch. He hit 98 mph several times on the PETCO Park radar gun. He has dominated Interleague Play over his three full big league seasons, going 8-0 in nine regular-season starts against the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Old problems returned in Francis' last start, a loss at Kansas City on Monday. For one, he gave up four runs in the first inning. He had curbed that season-long problem in his two previous starts. Francis also struggled with the command of his fastball, and that's why manager Clint Hurdle thought he struggled. For the game, Francis lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs. In his last three starts, Francis is 1-1 and has given up 12 runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers had allowed just four earned runs over 36 innings in his previous five starts before the Cardinals charged him for five runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings, handing Rogers his first loss since May 15 and his first Interleague defeat since he joined the Tigers three years ago.
