He had allowed a lone run over his first 4 2/3 innings before a Brian Barton homer sent him laboring to finish the fifth before three hits chased him in the sixth. He'll try to start a new winning streak against a Rockies lineup that hits about 10 points against left-handers compared with right-handers this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Reynolds had no secondary pitches working but fount a way to last seven innings and hold the Mets to three runs in a 3-1 loss at Coors Field. It was a step forward to Reynolds, who adjusted by relying on his sinking fastball and showing just enough of a curveball to keep hitters honest. He is not a strikeout pitcher, but he has six against one walk in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins had to work to get through five innings against the Padres, despite giving up only three runs. The left-hander threw a total of 91 pitches in that span, scattering six hits while walking two and striking out two. A strong night defensively behind Perkins aided the pitcher, who will next face the Tigers at the Metrodome. Perkins won his only other start against Detroit earlier this season, allowing just one run on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga gave up five runs over 4 2/3 innings, including three solo home runs, on Wednesday against the Cardinals before a rain delay knocked him out of the game. Now he'll get back to American League competition with his third matchup against the Twins this year. Both of his previous meetings with Minnesota have been losses, with seven earned runs allowed on 13 hits and seven walks over 12 innings. He had won three consecutive starts before the Cardinals roughed him up.

home_pitcher_note: Some early troubles plagued Baker in his last start as he gave up three runs over his first three innings to the Padres. But while it wasn't the prettiest of outings, Baker managed to settle down to hold them to just those three runs on six hits over six innings. The Twins are still hoping to see Baker's pitch counts go down, as he threw 101 over that span. Next up for Baker will be his third start of the year against Detroit.  He is 0-0, having allowed just four runs over 10 innings in the first two starts. He's had success at the Metrodome this season, going 2-0 with a 2.28 ERA in five starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson, one of the Tigers' most consistent pitchers during their recent hot streak, allowed no earned runs for the second time in three starts on Thursday, though he wiggled out of trouble all afternoon. He allowed a season-high 11 hits in 6 1/3 innings, but stranded 10 runners (four in scoring position) with the help of key strikeouts and double plays. He kept the ball down, which translated into 11 of his 14 outs coming on the ground. In two starts against the Twins this season, he has allowed seven runs on 13 hits in 12 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn struggled to keep the ball in the ballpark during his last start against the Brewers. In his 4 2/3 innings, the right-hander gave up a total of six runs -- all coming on four homers. Blackburn didn't issue a walk in the start but the sinkerball pitcher needs to keep the ball down in the zone more than he did in his last start to be successful. Next up will be his second start of the season against Detroit. Blackburn gave up four runs over 5 2/3 innings in that start at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Bonine threw eight innings of one-run ball in his third Major League start Friday against the Rockies. While keeping Colorado hitless through four innings, he threw plenty of strikes down in the zone, which translated into 17 of his 22 outs coming via ground balls. The right-hander stayed true to his reputation as a strike-thrower, tossing 69 of his 99 pitches over the plate. All three of his starts occurred during Interleague Play, but now Bonine will get his first taste of an American League lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Precision was the name of the game for Silva in his last start as 62 of the 87 pitches he threw the Padres were strikes, which ended a career-high nine-game losing streak for the right-hander. He had not won a game since April 17, a stretch of 12 starts. He pitched ahead in the count and kept the ball down, two things he must do to be successful. He won?t strike out a lot of batters -- he fanned two Padres -- and stresses putting the ball in play early in the count. It worked perfectly against the Padres, and now he tries to do it against the Tigers, a team that has given him trouble this season, with 14 earned runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies came into Verlander's last start hoping to make him work, and they executed the game plan. Verlander left after 5 2/3 innings with a pitch count of 118. He had only one quick inning and averaged 22 pitches in the other five frames. He earned the no-decision and allowed two earned runs or fewer for the fourth straight start. Verlander has made two starts this season against the Mariners, which came 11 days apart in late May. In those outings, he gave up a combined five earned runs on 12 hits in 13 innings. Jose Vidro has hit .563 (6-for-19) with two doubles against Verlander.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander returned to the Mariners' rotation last Sunday after missing more than a week because of back spasms, and he threw 94 pitches over 5 2/3 innings against the Padres. He was in control of the game until the sixth, when he walked the bases loaded and surrendered his only run. The lefty has now pitched into the sixth inning eight times in 14 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers didn't have his best stuff in his last start, but he kept the Tigers in the game long enough for them to pull out a win. He also displayed some fancy defense, snaring a rocket line drive by Matt Holliday and making a nice stretch while covering first base to get a double play. The 43-year-old allowed three runs in the second inning but limited the damage and retired the final seven batters he faced. Rogers faced the Mariners once this season and earned the win after allowing four runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey put up his second effective start in a row on Monday, giving up two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings while striking out three. He couldn't pick up the win, thanks to an even better performance by Toronto's Roy Halladay. Of the nine hits Dickey gave up, eight were singles, and he mentioned afterward that some of the batted balls seemed to find holes. There has also been warmer weather in Seattle lately, which Dickey said can help his knuckleball move.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga is coming off an underwhelming start against Minnesota in which he went six innings, allowing nine hits and three earned runs while striking out three. He received a no-decision. The Tigers beat the Twins 5-4, however, improving the club's record in Galarraga's starts to 11-3. Galarraga's next start will come at Seattle. He has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith got his first Major League start on Tuesday and experienced mixed results. He sailed past the first three innings, but then gave up three earned runs before exiting with two outs in the fourth. The 62 pitches and 3 2/3 innings were both season-highs, and it will be interesting to see how the Australian responds to a second consecutive start with Felix Hernandez on the disabled list. He has communicated that he would like to be a starter eventually.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson had a rough outing Tuesday against the Twins, going four innings while allowing six earned runs on 11 hits in a 6-4 Tigers loss. The start comes following a stretch where he had allowed no earned runs in two of his last three starts. Robertson's next start comes against the Mariners. Robertson went 5 2/3 innings while surrendering four earned runs on four hits in a 7-4 victory over Seattle on May 30.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Jim Leyland used Monday's off-day to move up Verlander in the rotation and keep him on track to pitch every fifth day. Verlander has picked up his game since the opening month, but he has struggled with rapidly rising pitch counts and long innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The first start in the post-CC Sabathia era goes to Sowers. He might have better velocity on his fastball than a year ago, but the hard truth is that Sowers is much more like the guy who couldn't hold onto his big league job in '07 than the guy who dominated as a rookie in the second half of '06. His command has been out of whack -? never moreso than in his last outing against the White Sox on Monday. Sowers lasted just three innings in that loss, giving up eight runs on six hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He gave up a three-run homer to Jim Thome and a grand slam to Nick Swisher.

home_pitcher_note: Bonine was pushed back a day from his original rotation spot, which was slated to fall on Tuesday. That makes this his final start before the All-Star break. He'll still have the same opponent, facing an Indians club that has struggled offensively this year. That could provide the opportunity for Bonine to get back into quality pitching if he can attack the strike zone on the corners rather than the middle of the plate, which was his downfall his last time out at Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd has had a very inconsistent season, but one constant has been his penchant for dishing out the home-run ball. He might fare a little better in the pitching-friendly confines of Comerica Park. He had a strong outing there on June 6, when he held the Tigers to a pair of runs on four hits over seven innings for his 100th career victory, but he nonetheless gave up a pair of homers in that start.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Rogers out of his last outing Friday at Seattle was that he used a cutter effectively against right-handed hitters, something he hasn't done a lot with that kind of pitch. However, it couldn't help him through a pitching duel with Erik Bedard and the Mariners bullpen. He gave up a tape-measure solo homer to Raul Ibanez, a left-handed hitter, but stayed in the game until the Mariners wore him down in the eighth for two more runs, giving him four over 7 2/3 innings and returning his record to .500. Rogers gave up three earned runs on six hits with six strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings May 4 at the Metrodome in his only outing against the Twins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey saw his streak of 16 consecutive scoreless innings come to an end in the second inning of his last start against the Indians. The right-hander allowed five runs in the inning on three hits and two walks. But following a three-run homer by Grady Sizemore, Slowey recovered to retire 14 of his next 15 batters. Slowey's ability to bounce back speaks volumes to how far he's come this season in his first full year as a starter. Next up for Slowey will be his second start of the season in Detroit. He pitched six scoreless innings, allowing just four hits, in a win there on May 23.

home_pitcher_note: Though Galarraga battled command of his fastball for most of his last outing Thursday at Seattle, he tossed five scoreless innings before Jeff Clement's solo homer put some damage on his ledger in the sixth. He left with a lead that eventually slipped away, but his third straight no-decision nonetheless extended his unbeaten streak to eight consecutive starts since his last defeat May 28. One of those no-decisions came two starts ago against the Twins at Minnesota on June 30, when he gave up three earned runs and one unearned tally on nine hits over six innings. He lost twice to the Twins in May.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins is fresh off a start where he outdueled All-Star Cliff Lee of the Indians. The Twins lefty went seven innings, surrendering three earned runs on seven hits and one walk. The Twins prevailed, 4-3, while Perkins secured his fifth win. Perkins will next take on the Tigers. Perkins is 1-0 against Detroit in two 2008 starts, going a total of 14 innings and allowing only three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Just when Robertson seemed doomed to a summer of high pitch counts and quick hooks, the sixth-year veteran turned in arguably his best start in two years. He ended up with no decision Sunday at Seattle, but his nine innings of work with a lone run allowed on four hits essentially won the game for Detroit by allowing the Tigers' bullpen to outlast its Mariners counterpart. Any similar effort against the Twins would be a big boost for a Tigers club looking to close out the season's first half strong.
away_pitcher_note: Baker continued to impress against potent lineups as he held the Red Sox scoreless over seven innings at Fenway Park. The right-hander allowed just five hits, walking two and striking out seven while throwing 94 pitches. The heat and humidity in Boston seemed to wear Baker down a bit late in his outing, but he still managed to produce yet another quality start. He'll face the Tigers for the fourth time this season in his final start before the All-Star break. He's 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in those three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander yielded two runs on two hits in the first inning of his last start, but followed with six hitless frames. Only one batter reached in that span on a walk. In his last four starts, the righty has looked every bit the ace most predicted before this season. He won three of those starts, allowing eight earned runs in 24 innings. He has not lost since June 6. Verlander can help end the Tigers' pre-All Star schedule on a positive note. In two starts this season against Minnesota, he's 0-1 with a 3.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn more than made up for his rough relief outing at Fenway last season, when he gave up four runs in an inning. In his return to the famed ballpark, Blackburn pitched 6 2/3 innings and allowed just two runs on six hits to the Red Sox. Blackburn even retired a stretch of 10 straight batters during the outing. The right-hander has continued to make adjustments in each one of his starts and he'll have to do so again when he faces the Tigers for the third time this season. He is 1-0 with a 2.24 ERA in those first two starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Olson went 3-0 with a 4.28 ERA at home and 3-4 with a 6.81 mark on the road before the All-Star break, but he pitched to a 12.81 ERA in his first two July outings. Baltimore has watched Olson carefully and the southpaw has been knocked out before end of the sixth inning in 10 of his first 14 starts. Olson went 1-3 with a 7.79 ERA last season.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers gets the call to begin the second half. He finished the first half earning a no-decision against the Twins after allowing three runs on nine hits in seven innings. Since June 2, Rogers has been one of Detroit's most consistent starters, allowing an average of 2.3 earned runs in 10 starts. He beings the second half facing Baltimore, a team against which Rogers has a 10-9 record and 4.67 ERA in 28 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie entered the All-Star break tied for the league lead in quality starts (14), a statistic that serves as a better bellwether for how he's pitched than his record. The right-hander has completed seven innings in nine of his first 20 starts and has allowed three earned runs or less 15 times. Guthrie is 2-3 with a 3.51 ERA at home and 3-4 with a 3.47 mark on the road.
away_pitcher_note: After being recalled from Triple-A in mid-April, Galarraga comes into the second half as the Tigers' wins leader despite having only 15 starts. However, he has struggled a bit of late. He doesn't have a win in his last four starts. Two of those starts came against Minnesota, his Achilles' heel this season. His control has wavered a bit of late, as well. A consistent strike-thrower, Galarraga has walked almost three batters per game in his last three starts. The rookie has never faced Baltimore in his short career.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera has cut down his walks in a major way this season and appears to be on pace to throw 200 innings for the second consecutive season. The right-hander led the league in walks in each of the last two seasons, but he's had five starts this year in which he didn't walk a single batter. Cabrera has thrown two complete games this season.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson has alternated strong and troublesome starts coming into the second half. He allowed no earned runs against the Cardinals on June 26, then six against the Twins in his next start. He yielded one run in nine innings against the Mariners, but five in his last start against the Twins. If that pattern continues, Robertson should have a strong outing against the Orioles. Helping that argument is his career numbers against Baltimore: 4-1 and a 3.05 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burres has lost just once in his last 10 outings, a statistic that even he attributes to a hyperactive offense behind him. The southpaw has been highly erratic at times but became the first Oriole to register seven victories in his last start before the break. Burres has gone 4-2 with a 6.02 ERA at home and 3-3 with a 4.01 mark on the road this season.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling early this season, Verlander looks like the pitcher everyone expected. He battled through a 38-pitch fourth inning to allow two runs on four hits in seven innings, while striking out eight in his last start. He has allowed two runs or fewer in his last six starts dating back to June 11. In two career starts against Baltimore, he has allowed 10 combined hits and three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar pitched what he considered his best game on July 11 when he beat the Mariners, 3-1, a five-hit, no-walk performance. The rookie considered the game a breakthrough because "a light" came on and he trusted his stuff, pitched aggressively in the strike zone, worked both sides of the plate effectively and moved the ball around. In a departure from his results with his sinker, though, he had more fly-ball outs (nine) than ground-ball outs (eight). He also had four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Miner wasn't in the Tigers' plans to become a starter again, but after Eddie Bonine struggled in his last two starts, team officials decided to make him the latest to try to shore up the fifth spot in Detroit's rotation. He held down the job for much of the summer of 2006 after Mike Maroth underwent surgery, and his performance helped the Tigers go on a summer tear to make the postseason. A similar performance this year would be a blessing for Detroit and its search for pitching help.

home_pitcher_note: Davies has been without a victory since June 17 when he got through his fourth start with a 3-0 mark. He's made five starts since then with one loss and four no-decisions. His last outing, on July 13 against the Mariners, resulted in seven innings with three runs on six hits. Davies is making good progress in avoiding his big bugaboo, walks. He's had just four in his last three starts and 16 2/3 innings. Davies faced the Tigers twice last season; he was 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers started off the season's second half with a display in damage control, allowing 11 hits over six innings but limiting the Orioles to four runs. That allowed the Tigers to pull ahead in the late innings for a comeback victory, improving his career record to 6-7 when he gives up 11 or more hits in a game. However, he owns two losses in as many meetings with the Royals this season, allowing nine runs over 10 innings in the process.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was clipped for seven runs and 11 hits in just three-plus innings against the White Sox last Friday night. He even walked three batters and hit another. It was his shortest outing in what has been a very successful season. Manager Trey Hillman thought Greinke, who stayed mostly with his fastball, waited too long to go to his secondary pitches. The White Sox sent 11 batters to the plate in the first inning. Greinke beat the Tigers, 4-1, on April 3 and had a no-decision despite pitching well in a May 13 victory.
away_pitcher_note: The good news for Galarraga is that he returned to pounding the strike zone in his last outing, Friday at Baltimore, where he threw strikes with 71 of his 104 pitches. The downside for him is that the Orioles hit him for three home runs, including Melvin Mora's go-ahead two-run homer. Galarraga went to his slider a lot rather than spotting all three pitches for strikes and seemed to pay for it with his second straight loss after going unbeaten in nine consecutive starts. He has not faced the Royals this season.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson took the mound last Saturday at Baltimore with a six-run lead, but it was gone by the end of the third. So was Robertson, whom the Orioles hit around for seven runs on eight hits -- six of them singles -- over 2 1/3 innings. He has battled high hit totals in four of his last five starts, the exception being nine innings of one-run ball July 6 at Seattle. He's keeping the ball on the ground, but they aren't resulting in the outs that he needs. Robertson has split his two starts against the White Sox this season, including 6 1/3 innings of three-run ball to beat them on June 10 in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a quality start against the Royals, Floyd picked up his second loss in a row Saturday night at U.S. Cellular Field. He gave up three runs in the sixth, but only one was earned. Ross Gload hit a hard grounder toward Joe Crede that bounced off his glove and continued rolling into left field. The error led to John Buck's home run the next at-bat and the White Sox never recovered. Floyd walked three more batters in the game, too, having now issued at least three free passes in each of his past three starts. Floyd faced Detroit in back-to-back starts to open the season. He gave up a combined three runs in 13 1/3 innings to pick up his first two wins.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander has ascended from the depths of a 2-9 record in early June to now sit within a victory of .500. Not only has he gone 6-0 with a 2.30 ERA over his past eight starts, but he has given up two runs or fewer in each of those outings. He fell an out shy of a complete game last Sunday at Baltimore, allowing a run on three hits while throwing 105 pitches in sweltering heat. He's 1-2 against the White Sox this season and 2-6 against them in his career, but he started this run of his with a complete-game four-hitter against Chicago on June 11.
away_pitcher_note: Danks was uncharacteristically off his game Sunday against the Royals. The left-hander lasted just four innings, surrendering four runs on nine hits and two walks. It was the first time he gave up more then four runs since allowing seven on April 9 against Minnesota. His offense bailed him out of the loss. He hasn't been handed a loss since May 24. He'll try to get back on track against Detroit, perhaps helped by the fact that the Tigers have yet to see Danks this year. He was 0-1 with a 5.71 ERA in three starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: As Jim Leyland said, Miner was just what the doctor ordered. The Tigers needed a No. 5 starter, and Miner filled in the role perfectly Monday. In his first start since early 2007, he pitched six scoreless innings. Miner's control had improved greatly since his last relief outing, as he mixed mainly fastballs and changeups. Leyland wants Miner to improve his breaking ball if he wants to stick in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez literally made one mistake over seven innings during Monday's contest against the Rangers, but that mistake ended up costing him a chance at victory. Vazquez's 2-0 offering to Josh Hamilton with two outs in the third was deposited over the center field fence for a three-run home run, giving Texas all the runs it would need in a 6-1 victory. Vazquez fanned 10, producing his 36th career double-digit strikeout effort, and he also allowed four hits and walked two. Vazquez has lost three straight decisions and has not won since June 17. He has a 1-1 record with a 3.46 ERA against Detroit this season, with a 0-1 record at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd's fourth win was a long time coming. He was winless in six starts from June 11 to July 9, but he finally got in the win column against the Angels on July 21, allowing just one run on nine hits with two walks and five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. Byrd ran into some trouble with baserunners but never gave up the big hit, and he had some success with his changeup against left-handed batters, who have given him fits all season. Byrd is 1-0 with a 3.46 ERA in two starts against the Tigers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers was on track to seven, maybe eight innings in his last start, against the Royals. Rain changed that. A long delay meant that Rogers had to leave after just six innings, albeit a good six. He gave up just one run and four hits. If not for Mark Grudzielanek's three hits, Rogers would've had a one-hitter. After the game, Rogers said he feels better now than he did a month or two ago. His numbers reflect that: his ERA has gone from 6.66 on May 21 to 4.48.

home_pitcher_note: The benefactor of Aaron Laffey's demotion to Triple-A Buffalo, Ginter will get his third start of what could be a full rest of the season with the Indians. Ginter has certainly earned his spot in the Tribe rotation, tossing 11 innings and allowing just three runs. His stuff isn't the greatest and he's not going to blow opponents away, but he's had a knack of dodging trouble, which is all Eric Wedge can ask for at this point of the season. He has been fairly successful against one of his former teams, albeit in relief appearances. Lifetime against the Tigers, the 30-year-old righty has a 1.80 ERA over 10 innings of work in five appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga pitched six perfect innings against Kansas City last Wednesday and still thought he had thrown better before. He talked about his 8 1/3-inning performance against Anaheim in late May as his best of the season. Maybe so, but Galarraga sure was good. He gave up just one run and three hits in seven innings, while striking out a career-high seven. It was also his first win since June 18 against San Francisco. In his last three starts, Galarraga has given up a combined seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lee became the Majors' first 14-game winner with another outstanding effort against the Twins on Friday night. Working ahead and pounding the zone all night, he gave up just two runs on six hits with no walks and 10 strikeouts in eight innings. Lee has now won three straight starts, and he's given up two runs or less in eight of his last nine outings. He only seems to get stronger as his amazing 2008 season progresses. He gave up two runs on six hits with two walks and five strikeouts in five innings in a win over the Tigers on June 9.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson exited his last start to a standing ovation from a sellout Comerica Park of 44,000-plus. He started quick, throwing just 14 pitches in the first two inning, and finished his six innings allowing three runs on five hits. He encountered a pair of jams, but each time he ended the threat by retiring American League home run leader Carlos Quentin. The left-hander departed with a 4-1 lead in the seventh after back-to-back singles, which the bullpen allowed to score. Nonetheless, Robertson rebounded nicely from a rough outing at Baltimore. He faces the Indians for the first time this season. In his career, Robertson is 2-5 with a 4.74 ERA against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: The only thing Carmona can take away from his first start back from the disabled list was that he didn't go back on the DL. Carmona was out of control from the start and never got settled in a shellacking at the hands of the Twins on Saturday. Carmona lasted 2 1/3 innings, allowing nine runs on seven hits in an atrocious welcome back to the big leagues. Luckily, Carmona will have two things working in his favor Thursday. It will be daytime and he will be facing the Tigers. Carmona is 11-4 lifetime when the lights are off and is  4-2 with a 3.05 ERA all-time against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander had one of the shortest outings of his career his last time out. He lasted only four innings, allowing seven runs on nine hits to give him double-digit losses for the first time. It also marked the first time Verlander went just four innings since Aug. 22 against the Indians. The star righty's impressive stretch came to an end. He yielded more than three earned runs in a start for the first time since May 31. He had allowed two earned runs or fewer in his last eight starts. In his last two starts against the Tribe, Verlander has given up a combined five earned runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir was sharp on Saturday against the Royals, just not as sharp as he had been recently. He lasted just five innings, giving up two runs and picking up the no-decision. An hour long rain delay struck in the middle of his outing, possibly causing some problems. Kazmir's previous outing was one of his best. He threw seven scoreless innings with nine strikeouts. Recently, Kazmir said the key to his recent success was relaxing more on the mound and not over-analyzing every decision.
away_pitcher_note: Miner's transition from the bullpen to the rotation took another positive step in his last start. After shutting out the Royals over six inning his first time out on Monday, Miner held the AL Central-leading White Sox to two runs on five hits in six innings Sunday. He did not walk a batter, tossing 61 of his 92 pitches for strikes. He also didn't overthrow, as he has shown a tendency to do in relief appearances, and his sinking fastball registered in the 89-91 mph range. In his two starts this season, he has allowed eight hits and one walk in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine expressed disappointment at the offense's lack of fire power and with good reason. In his last start, a loss to Kansas City, he got one run of support. Before that, he also got one. Against the Royals, he did well for the first six innings, allowing three runs. Then in the seventh, he allowed two runners on base before exiting the game. Reliever Al Reyes came in and gave up a three-run homer. Sonnanstine finished with 6 2/3 innings, allowing five runs.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers is 9-4 with a 3.10 ERA in his career against the Rays, but just 1-4 with a 5.04 ERA at Tropicana Field, where he hasn't won since 2001 and hasn't pitched at all since 2006. He returns to find an obviously much-improved Rays team that probably won't make his task any easier. The Gambler has alternated quality and non-quality starts over his past six outings, most recently a Monday loss at Cleveland that sank on an unlikely Asbdrubal Cabrera two-run homer on what ended up being a cut changeup, a pitch Rogers had neither invented nor intended.

home_pitcher_note: Shields took his seventh loss of the season Monday night against Toronto despite the fact he made his 15th quality start of the season by allowing three earned runs in 7 1/3 innings while walking none. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus-fastball and curve, and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Just when you think the American League has finally figured out Detroit's rotation savior, the rookie right-hander shows he can win without his best stuff. He allowed three runs over 5 1/3 innings on Tuesday at Cleveland but limited the damage enough to avoid cleanup work for the bullpen and take advantage of a Detroit offensive onslaught for a victory. He has won his past two starts to take the lead in wins among Tigers pitchers, and he'll try to get into double digits against a Rays team that has never seen him.

home_pitcher_note: After going winless in three straight starts, two of which were losses, Floyd righted the ship personally and for his team during an 8-1 shellacking of the Twins Wednesday at the Metrodome. Floyd allowed one run on four hits over 7 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking one, while throwing 68 of his 101 pitches for strikes. The right-hander's performance helped put an end to the White Sox three-game losing streak and kept the team in first place. Floyd has a 2-0 record with a 2.79 ERA over three starts against Detroit this season. The right-hander also has a 7-2 mark with a 2.49 ERA in 11 starts at U.S. Cellular Field. He has a 3-0 lifetime record against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The spectacled lefty lasted just three innings Wednesday at Cleveland, the second time in his past three starts where he hasn't made it past the third. Robertson was tattooed for eight runs on nine hits in a losing effort against the Tribe. Both home runs he allowed -- a solo shot from Ben Francisco and a three-run homer by Grady Sizemore -- came with two outs. When Curtis Granderson muffed a Kelly Shoppach double in the third, Robertson failed to minimize the damage, allowing two more runs on two more doubles. Robertson has made three starts against the White Sox this season, going 1-0 with a 5.71 ERA. Lifetime, he has made 19 starts against Chicago, splitting with a 6-6 record and 5.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Danks still has not suffered a loss since May 24 but he picked up his second no-decision in three second-half starts on Thursday at the Metrodome and his 10th no-decision of the season. The left-hander was cruising along through four innings, before Justin Morneau touched him up for a three-run blast in the fifth. Danks exited after six innings and one batter in the seventh, allowing four runs on eight hits. He struck out four and walked two. Danks has a 1-0 record this season against Detroit and has a 3-3 mark with a 4.04 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field. Danks has a career record of 1-1 against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander took the loss on Thursday night after a strong start went awry. The right-hander's pitch selection was a major frustration for manager Jim Leyland who called the fifth inning "disastrous" and was visibly upset about a walk to Cleveland's No. 9 batter Asdrubal Cabrera, which was followed by a three-run homer from Grady Sizemore. Despite nine strikeouts, Verlander surrendered six runs off five hits in 5 2/3 innings. He has not fared well against the White Sox previously this season -- going 1-3 with a 6.15 ERA -- but he will look to get back on track against the Tigers' AL Central rival.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez said the monkey on his back hadn't been getting any bigger in recent starts, but it was certainly big enough. He hadn't won a game since June 17, before he won on Friday against the Royals. Vazquez went six innings, giving up five hits and two runs. He had a shut out through the first five. It was the first time Vazquez gave up less than three runs since May 31.
away_pitcher_note: A reliever turned starter, Miner gave the Tigers a chance to win on Friday night, but he received little offensive support in a 5-2 loss to the Rays at Tropicana Field. Despite allowing Tampa Bay's leadoff man on in five of the game's first six innings, Miner scattered eight hits through 5 1/3 innings. He was charged with four runs (three earned) in his fourth loss this season. He will look to collect a "W" against Chicago at U.S. Cellular Field, a ballpark in which he has traditionally struggled. In appearances in six games -- including one start -- Miner is 0-3 with a 7.94 ERA at the White Sox home field.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers had a bizarre outing on Saturday night, in which the southpaw tied a season-low 3 1/3 innings and garnered a season-high eight strikeouts. The veteran hurler threw 109 pitches in that short span, with only 63 of those for strikes. Afterward, Rogers said he had good stuff, and was disappointed that his pitch count went awry. He had 65 tosses in the first two innings alone. Still, the 19-year veteran should have no problem bouncing back from the loss for Friday's start. In 36 starts vs. Oakland he is 21-7, with a 4.28 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dallas Braden: While battling sickness in his previous start against the Red Sox, Braden lasted just 3 1/3 innings, surrendering four runs on six hits while striking out one. It marked his third starting assignment of the season, a time span in which he has allowed nine runs on 16 hits through 15 innings. Braden owns a 0-1 record vs. Detroit in three career starts. His 12.34 ERA against the Tigers represents his highest mark against any team.

home_pitcher_note: The questions of whether Galarraga's hot start was for real are gone now that he has carried his success into August. At this point, he's the best starter the Tigers have going, delivering consistently efficient, stingy innings and leaving with his team ahead in his past three outings. He gave up three runs in as many innings against the A's on June 3, the day of his long-lost piggyback start with Dontrelle Willis.
away_pitcher_note: With right-hander Sean Gallagher battling irritation in his throwing shoulder, the A's decided to push his start to sometime in their upcoming home series against the Rays. In place of Gallagher, Oakland will start Meyer, who was called up to the A's on Aug. 3. Facing the Blue Jays in his last appearance, Meyer provided four solid innings of relief, allowing no runs on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson ended up with no decision Tuesday at Chicago after giving up four runs on nine hits in five-plus innings, which started the White Sox on their way to overcoming a 6-1 deficit. Three of his past six starts have ended up becoming extra-inning marathons after he left, but his bigger concern lately has been lasting deeper into games. He has worked through six innings just once over his past four starts, and his ERA has risen nearly a full run over his past five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Smith pitched well against the Blue Jays in his last start. He allowed just two runs on four hits over his six innings. He walked two, struck out four and needed 87 pitches in the outing. Though he left the game in line for the win, Smith eventually received a no-decision, as A's closer Huston Street allowed the Jays to win the game in the ninth inning. Smith has not collected a victory since June 30.

home_pitcher_note: From a pure pitching standpoint, Verlander actually took a step forward in his third straight loss, sending down 12 straight White Sox at one point and 21 out of 24 from the first inning into the eighth. The problem was that he allowed a Jim Thome three-run home run -- Thome's sixth career homer off Verlander -- before that streak began, and ended up with two more tack-on runs in the eighth. His last three losses have left him a combined 6-16 against the White Sox and Indians, but he'll get his first-ever matchup with the Blue Jays in his next scheduled outing.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the A's in his last outing, Marcum had his best start since returning form the disabled list on July 22. The right-hander allowed just one run on three hits over seven innings. He walked two and struck out seven batters, needing 89 pitches in the outing to collect his first win since May 26 -- a stretch of seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miner began the season pitching the middle to late innings in the Tigers bullpen, but Thursday's win over the White Sox improved him to 3-1 with a 2.31 ERA in four starts since joining the rotation. His latest outing saw him hold down a power-happy Chicago offense with one earned run allowed over six innings. While other Tigers starters have been up and down, Miner and Armando Galarraga have been surprisingly consistent this summer to help provide some stability to the staff. Miner tossed two scoreless innings against the Blue Jays in April, but he hasn't started against them since 2006, when he held them to two runs in six innings at Rogers Centre.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett continued to improve his ranking among the American League's top pitchers with a solid outing in his last start against the Athletics. Burnett allowed four runs on seven hits while striking out six over six innings of work. The majority of Oakland's damage came via the home run with first baseman Daric Barton hitting a two-run shot and outfielder Ryan Sweeney following three innings later with a solo homer. It wasn't Burnett's sharpest outing of the season but it was still enough to earn his 14th victory of the season. That moved him past Toronto No. 1 starter Roy Halladay for the team lead in wins and at least for the time being put himself in a tie with Angels left-hander Joe Saunders for third most in the AL. Burnett's outing also moved him into second place in the AL in innings pitched (157.2) and first in strikeouts (159). He is 2-1 with an 8.68 ERA over 18 2/3 innings in his career against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers couldn't gather career win No. 219 against the A's in his last start, but much of that had to do with a lack of run support. He allowed three earned runs in seven innings and earned a loss. Rogers has endured a tough stretch. In his last three starts, he has allowed 15 earned runs, jumping his ERA almost half a run. Rogers owns a 15-9 career against the Blue Jays. He faced them once this season, allowing four runs in 6 2/3 innings to get the win.
away_pitcher_note: Although he absorbed the loss while facing the Indians in his last start, Purcey tossed what was arguably the best game of his brief career. In just his fifth Major League start, the left-hander allowed three runs on six hits over six innings. He walked two and struck out a career-high eight batters, needing 97 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga fired his fourth straight quality start last time out against the Athletics. He gave up a long home run in the first inning, but recovered to allow only one more run over the next 4 2/3 innings. He had his usual poise and control, pinpointing his slider away from right-handed hitters. That pitch has helped him hold righties to a .155 batting average this season, which ranks near the best in the Majors. Galarraga ranks second among rookies in wins, trailing only Atlanta's Jair Jurrjens. He faces the Blue Jays for the second time. The last time, he allowed no runs on three hits in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Blue Jays recalled the 23-year-old Litsch from Triple-A Syracuse after the right-hander was sent down to work on his sinker. In three starts in the Minors, Litsch went 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA, striking out 18 and walking four over 20 innings for the Chiefs. Litsch rejoins the rotation after going 1-6 with a 6.12 ERA in nine starts from June 4-July 21. Toronto is hoping he looks more like the starter that opened the season 7-1 with a 3.18 ERA. Litsch has never faced the Tigers in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson left to a standing ovation after allowing one run on five hits over 7 2/3 innings in his last start, against Oakland. He faced only one real threat, a bases-loaded jam in the fourth, but he escaped thanks to fine defense. After that, he retired 11 straight A's hitters until they scored a run off him on two hits in the eighth. He earned a win for the first time since June 21. Robertson has not faced the Orioles this season. He is 4-1 with a 4.24 ERA against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Orioles rookie dazzled in his debut in Anaheim, one-hitting the league's best team through eight innings, but his encore performance on Sunday at Camden Yards was less than stellar. Waters lasted just four innings, allowing six runs on eight hits and three walks, to the Rangers. The left-hander struggled in the first inning, allowing a the first two batters to reach, then he surrendered a three-run homer to Josh Hamilton. The key for Waters will be location -- which was obviously strong in Anaheim and lacking in Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander's struggles continued in his last start against the Blue Jays. He got tagged for six runs on seven hits in just 4 1/3 innings to earn his fourth straight loss, and the usually poised right-hander tossed his glove down the dugout tunnel in disgust as he walked off the field. Verlander was one of the best pitchers in the league during June and July, but August has not treated him well. He has surrendered six runs or more in three of his last four starts, and he gave up five in the other one. He looks to get back on track against the Orioles, whom he held to one run on three hits in 8 1/3 innings on July 20.
away_pitcher_note: This rotation slot is notionally reserved for Sarfate, but the Orioles are believed to be weighing their options for a suitable replacement. Sarfate, an erstwhile reliever, has been knocked out before the end of the fifth inning in all three of his starts. Baltimore would like to push him back to the bullpen, but first it has to find another starter.

home_pitcher_note: Miner had another strong outing in his last start, allowing one earned run on five hits in six innings against the Blue Jays. He earned a no-decision, though, as the bullpen couldn't hold a late lead. In his five starts, Miner has a 3-1 record and 2.15 ERA. He has not faced the Orioles at all this season but has two career relief appearances against them.
away_pitcher_note: Olson has hit the skids in a big way, allowing at least five runs in six of his last eight starts. The southpaw has a 6.95 ERA in his six starts after the All-Star break and has pitched to a 4-5 record and a 6.83 mark on the road. The Orioles are poised to stick with him, though, and Olson will get a chance to redeem himself against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman -- 0-2 in his last four starts -- didn't lose his last time out in Boston, but it was his roughest start of the season. He allowed 12 runs, six earned, on 10 hits and three walks in just 2 2/3 innings as his ERA spiked from 4.82. Feldman will be looking to start Texas' series with Detroit out on the right foot. He hasn't faced the Tigers this season and has a 7.71 ERA against them in seven career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers surrendered at least four runs for the fourth straight start his last time out, which a rain delay ended with one out in the seventh inning. He looked sharp in every inning but the fourth. A bad hop gave the Blue Jays the bases loaded with nobody out, and Vernon Wells knocked a grand slam to left. Overall, Rogers allowed four runs on seven hits and three walks in 6 1/3 innings. He has allowed a total of 19 runs in his last four starts. Against Texas, he faces the team that drafted him in the 39th round of the 1982 Draft. He pitched for the Rangers from 1989-95, 2000-02 and 2004-05.

home_pitcher_note: Originally slated to pitch on Thursday, Padilla was been pushed back to Tuesday to start against the Tigers. In his last start, Padilla allowed six runs to the Orioles in four innings as his ERA rose from 4.59. After winning five of seven starts from June 11 to July 25, he's winless in his last three.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga had one of his best outings of the season last time out against the Blue Jays. He went eight innings, allowing one run on five hits, while striking out six and walking two. He threw a season-high 121 pitches. He said after the game he couldn't remember the last time he threw that many pitches, but he added that he won't need any extra rest. Next he faces Texas, the team that traded him to the Tigers last offseason.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood came off the disabled list and allowed five runs on 10 hits and one walk in 4 2/3 innings in a 7-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. He is 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA in his last four starts, and he is 4-2 with a 5.74 ERA in nine starts at home this season. The right-hander is 3-4 with a 4.23 ERA in nine career starts against the Tigers but will be facing them for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Only Carlos Silva has a higher ERA among American League starters without enough innings to qualify, and Silva and Livan Hernandez are the lone AL hurlers to give up more hits. Those two stats have meant a long season for Robertson, who owns one win in his past 10 starts. The latest was a loss to the Orioles last Friday, when he gave up four earned runs on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister's last outing was a disaster at Yankee Stadium. He lasted just one inning plus six batters, giving up 10 hits, three walks and 10 runs. There were three homers, including Jason Giambi's grand slam. All that came after a seven-inning stint, albeit a loss, in Chicago which left Bannister encouraged. Now he hasn't won in his last nine starts, since June 23 against Colorado. Maybe seeing the Tigers will revive him. Bannister beat them, 4-0, in the second game of the season on April 2.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to Thursday's off-day, Verlander will get a well-deserved extra day of rest between starts after outings of 130 and 110 pitches so far this month. He ended a personal four-game losing streak with his win over Baltimore last Saturday at Comerica Park, and he'll have a chance to build upon that by facing a Royals team he has generally met with success so far in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Davies was recalled from Triple-A Omaha on Friday to start on Saturday. He was optioned on Aug. 15, a day after lasting five innings in a start at Chicago. Davies gave up just three runs and struck out seven, but his command was off. In those five innings, he ran up 100 pitches (63 strikes) and gave up nine hits and two walks. With an open date looming, he wasn't needed for the next turn of the rotation and was sent to Omaha. Davies faced the Tigers on July 22 and lasted just four innings in a 7-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Miner had thrown four quality starts in five outings since joining the Tigers rotation, of all them with two runs or fewer allowed, so a setback was to be expected last time out. Still, Sunday's struggles against the Orioles were a shock. The first five O's batters to face him all reached safely, sending him on his way to five runs on six hits allowed over 1 1/3 innings. Whether it was an anomaly in an otherwise solid second half or a sign that hitters are adjusting to him isn't known, but a rematch with the Royals should be a strong sign. Miner tossed six scoreless innings on three hits in his first start July 21 at Kauffman Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Duckworth will make his first Major League start of the season against the Tigers on Sunday. The Royals called up the right-hander from Triple-A after Luke Hochevar went on the disabled list.  Duckworth had a record of 5-11 with a 4.75 ERA for Omaha. Duckworth spent a good portion of 2007 with the Royals. He went 3-5 with a 4.63 ERA as both a starter and reliever. He has a lifetime big league record of 20-31 with a career 5.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers ended a personal four-game losing streak with a win against his former club, holding the Texas Rangers to three runs on eight hits over six innings last time out. He'll try to build on that by taking on a Royals club that has had mixed success with him this year, plating 10 runs on 20 hits over 16 innings from Rogers in three meetings. He has won consecutive starts just once this season, but that included his last start against the Royals, whom he held to a run on four hits in six innings July 22 at Kauffman Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Now that Galarraga has dispensed his revenge on the Rangers for trading him last offseason by beating them last Tuesday, he'll try to get back to business as usual with a chance to beat Cleveland for the fourth time this season. The Indians have batted just .159 in three starts against him this year, during which he has lasted 17 2/3 innings. He's 4-0 in his last five starts, pushing him into a battle with former Tiger and current Atlanta Brave Jair Jurrjens for the Major League rookie wins lead this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson scuffled a bit in his second start since being called up from Triple-A Buffalo, but he gave the Tribe innings -- something he couldn't deliver in his first outing. Acquired in the trade that sent CC Sabathia to the Brewers, Jackson went seven innings and gave up five runs (four earned), which was more than enough to prevent him from picking up his first Major League win since July 17, 2006. Most of the damage came in a four-run fifth inning, where he surrendered a three-run double to Mike Aviles. Jackson has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers will purchase Lambert's contract from Triple-A Toledo to fill Nate Robertson's old spot in their rotation. It will mark the Major League debut of Lambert, a first-round pick of the Cardinals in the 2004 First-Year Player Draft who came to the Tigers system last summer in the Mike Maroth trade. He owns a 12-8 record and 3.50 ERA in 26 starts for the Mud Hens, including three complete games and a shutout. He ranks fifth in the International League in ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lee notched his American League-best 18th win of the season on Thursday with yet another quality start. The 29-year-old took a no-hitter into the fifth inning, ultimately saw it disappear and then proceeded to allow three runs, before settling down to escape after seven innings with just the three runs of damage. Lee skirted trouble throughout, inducing four double plays, but he was still able to strike out seven batters. Lee is just two wins shy of becoming the Indians' first 20-game winner since Gaylord Perry accomplished the feat in 1974. In two starts against the Tigers this season, Lee is 1-0 with a 7.20 ERA -- largely the result of a five-inning, six-run outing on July 31. Lifetime, Lee is 4-6 with a 5.46 ERA in 16 starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The young right-hander, who has struggled for much of this year, has gotten back on a little bit of  a roll lately with back-to-back wins. His victory against the Royals on Friday saw him display some of the better mix of pitch selections that he's had this summer, including a good dose of curveballs. If he can take that into his latest meeting with the Indians, he'll give himself a better chance than he has lately against a club that has hit him well. He's 4-8 with a 6.51 ERA lifetime against Cleveland, including 1-3 with a 5.84 ERA in four starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona was arguably as sharp as he's been all season his last time out against a potent Rangers lineup. In six innings, he allowed an unearned run on six hits and three walks and struck out five. It was just his fourth start of the season where his struck out more batters than he walked -- and his first since July 31. It was also his first victorious outing since that July 31 start against the Tigers, who Carmona will be facing his next time out. Wednesday will be his third start of the season against Detroit and he'll be going for his third victory against the Tigers this season. In 13 innings against Detroit in 2008, Carmona has a 2.08 ERA and five strikeouts to two walks.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough outing against the Orioles saw Miner charged with more runs (five) than batters retired (four), he rebounded with seven scoreless innings at Kansas City last Sunday, scattering three hits and a walk while striking out three. He has five quality starts in seven outings since joining the Tigers rotation just over a month ago, including 13 scoreless innings against the Royals, and he's making a strong case to put himself into the starting picture for next season amid the uncertain situations of Dontrelle Willis, Nate Robertson and Jeremy Bonderman.
away_pitcher_note: Davies made his first start since being called up from Omaha and saw his record drop to 5-5 in the process.  Detroit touched him for single runs in the second, third and fifth innings before Miguel Cabrera topped things off with a booming solo homer in the sixth.  Davies gave up only four hits. He struck out four, walked four, hit a batter and threw a wild pitch in his six innings and 89 pitches of work. Davies has a tendency toward high pitch counts.  He has only made it through the seventh inning in two of his 15 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Trade rumors could be circulating around Rogers with the deadline for postseason eligibility on Sunday and contract bonuses for innings coming up, but the 43-year-old's focus remains on the mound. He had a frustrating outing last Sunday at Kansas City, where the Royals hit him around for six earned runs in as many innings with help from some defensive miscues. It was his fifth loss in his last six outings, and it raised his second-half ERA to 6.41. He's 1-3 with a 6.55 ERA in four meetings with the Royals this season.
away_pitcher_note: Duckworth was brought up to start against the Tigers last Sunday because an injury put Luke Hochevar on the disabled list. Duckworth was a little shaky for two innings, giving up three runs, but settled down and lasted five innings. He earned credit for the 7-3 victory which snapped the team's seven-game skid. Duckworth had a 5-11 record and a 4.75 ERA for Triple-A Omaha, where he'd spent all season. But he has plenty of Major League experience with a 21-31 record in 128 games including 78 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga left some pitches up and paid for them Monday against Cleveland, including a pair of Grady Sizemore home runs early. However, the Venezuelan rookie recovered to salvage a quality start and a no-decision in the seven-inning performance, leaving him unbeaten in his last seven starts since July 18. His only meeting with the Royals this season saw him take a perfect game into the seventh before Kansas City put together three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Meche gave up a career-high 14 hits in losing to the Rangers on Monday night. He did manage to hold them to five runs, three on Nelson Cruz's homer. Meche has not won in his last four starts, although the previous three were no-decisions, and he was leading in two of them when he left the game. This was his first loss since the All-Star break. He was 4-0 with a 2.17 ERA in his previous seven starts. This season, Meche has started twice against the Tigers, and the Royals won both times.

home_pitcher_note: A couple of broken-bat line drives and an ill-placed fastball that resulted in a Kelly Shoppach two-run homer sent Verlander to defeat in his last start Wednesday against Cleveland. The loss prompted manager Jim Leyland to talk about the need for Verlander to shore up his fastball command, which has been inconsistent all season. Whether Verlander takes that to heart in his remaining starts this season remains to be seen. He beat the Yankees in both of his meetings with them last year, scattering three runs over 12 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson couldn't bounce back from a rough first inning on Wednesday night against the Red Sox. He gave up two early runs and four runs total to lose his third straight decision. He exited after 4 2/3 innings, and he allowed seven runs with four walks. It marked the second game in a row that Ponson did not complete five innings. He racked up 28 pitches in the first inning alone and threw 89 in his short night. Ponson has not faced Detroit this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers optioned Lambert to Triple-A Toledo after his Major League debut Tuesday night to add positional help, but they'll recall him once rosters expand from 25 to 40 players on Monday. Thus, he'll essentially spend his time preparing for a meeting with the Angels and shoring up his game after a six-run third inning derailed his start against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders had a rough outing in his last start as he allowed six runs on eight hits over 1 1/3 innings to take the loss against the A's. The left-hander has not won a decision since July 30 and has allowed 12 runs over his last 6 2/3 innings. Saunders allowed five runs in five innings to take a loss against the Tigers earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: It was deja vu for Miner on Friday when the right-hander impressed yet again against the Royals. He picked up his second straight win against Kansas City with six strong innings in which he allowed just one run on six hits. He'd shut out the Royals over seven innings in his previous start and allowed just three hits. Miner has pitched 3 1/3 innings of relief against the Angels this season and allowed just one hit. He's 5-1 with a 2.68 ERA in games he's started this season.
away_pitcher_note:
Garland battled back after allowing four runs in the first inning against the Rangers on Thursday, as he threw eight innings in the Angels' come-from-behind win. Garland allowed just three hits and one run after his rocky first inning to keep the Angels in the game. In all, he tossed eight innings, allowing five runs on eight hits while striking out three and walking one. Garland is 13-6 with a 3.90 ERA in
25 career starts against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers hasn't fared well against the Royals this season, having allowed 17 runs in the 22 innings prior to Saturday's start. It was much the same the latest time around, giving up six runs in six innings and picking up his 12th loss. He even commented afterward that he is disappointed with his ability level right now. Rogers has faced the Angels once this year and threw one of his better outings. Despite not factoring in the decision, the left-hander threw seven shutout innings and gave up just five hits.
away_pitcher_note:
Santana pitched brilliantly against the Rangers on Friday as the right-hander allowed just one run on five hits over eight innings. He complimented his fastball, which reached as high as 97 mph on the radar gun, with an assortment of devastating sliders along with an occasional changeup. He struck out seven batters and walked just one.
Santana is 4-2 with a 4.62 ERA in six career starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: In what appeared to be his best outing of the season for the Twins, Liriano gave up just one run on five hits over seven innings on Saturday against the A's. It was the longest start of the season for the left-hander, and he seemed to cruise though this one with relative ease. Liriano credited throwing first-pitch strikes and pitching to contact early in the game with allowing him to last deeper into his outing. Liriano's next start will come at home against the Tigers, a team he has yet to face this season. In four starts at the Metrodome, Liriano is 3-1 with a 1.17 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga tossed seven quality innings Sunday, and Detroit needed every one of them. The hard-throwing right-hander allowed two runs on eight hits and struck out seven batters. He didn't get credit for the win because the Tigers were slow in getting on the board, but they did end up beating the Royals. Galarraga has allowed three runs or fewer in his past eight starts and is 5-0 in that span. He'll be put to the test against the Twins, against whom he is 0-3 in four starts despite a solid 3.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the A's on Sunday, Baker delivered yet another quality start for the Twins, making it his 14th in 22 starts this season. Baker allowed just one run over six innings, scattered six hits while walking one and striking out four. It earned Baker his first victory since July 26, ending a string of six starts without a victory. Next up for the Twins right-hander will be a start against the Tigers. Baker is 2-0 with a 3.91 ERA in four starts vs. Detroit in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is 2-6 with a 7.29 ERA over his past eight starts since coming within a win of .500 for the season. Instead, he's among the American League leaders in losses, including the quickest exit of his Major League career in his last start Monday against the Yankees. New York chased him out after just 1 2/3 innings with eight runs -- five earned -- on seven hits. He's 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA in three starts against the Twins this year, with the loss coming at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays in his last start, Perkins was clearly not at his best. Although he received a no-decision in the Twins' loss, the left-hander allowed four runs on 10 hits over just five innings. He walked one, struck out one and surrendered two home runs during the affair. In three starts against the Tigers this year, Perkins is 2-0 with a 2.18 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lambert will get at least one more turn through the Tigers rotation after he was recalled from Triple-A Toledo for his second Major League start Tuesday against the Angels. He left with three runs allowed on six hits over four innings in a no-decision, but didn't get much help from his defense with a fly ball that fell in between three fielders as part of a two-run opening inning. Sunday will be the former first-round draft pick's first outing on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Miner ended up with a no-decision in previous outing -- on Wednesday against the Angels -- giving up five runs on eight hits over six innings. It was just his third non-quality outing out of nine starts since joining the Tigers rotation a month and a half ago. Miner is trying to make his case for a full-time starting spot. Whether he does depends a lot on what happens with other Tigers starters in the offseason, but his performance down the stretch is the part of that equation he can control. Miner's only outing against the A's this season was a June relief appearance at Oakland, where he suffered a blown save while allowing a hit and two walks over 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, a rookie with a live fastball and good breaking stuff, has struggled with him command since being called up from Triple-A in August and hasn't won since Aug. 12. In his past two outings, including a loss to the Royals on Tuesday, Sept. 2, Gonzalez has walked eight and allowed seven earned runs over seven innings of work. He only gave up two hits over four innings in Kansas City, but both of the hits were long home runs on balls that missed their intended spots by at least two feet. Gonzalez, 22, has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson will make a spot start on Tuesday for Kenny Rogers, who has been bothered by a sore hip, according to manager Jim Leyland. Robertson is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in two starts against the A's this year. The left-hander last started on Aug. 20, giving up six earned runs in 3 2/3 innings against Texas. He made three relief appearances after being moved to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland felt his stuff in his last start against Kansas City was as good as he's had all year. But a few bleeders and bloopers in the third inning resulted in four runs for the Royals. That was all Eveland surrendered in his six innings and he reached that juncture on 83 pitches. Eveland was able to locate all four of his pitches and pounded the strike zone. It was his third encouraging start since returning from Triple-A Sacramento on Aug. 21.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga's season-long struggles against the Twins continued on Friday, as he surrendered a Justin Morneau grand slam in a 10-2 Tigers loss. Galarraga went six innings and allowed six earned runs, walking six, his career high. He is now 0-4 against Minnesota and 12-1 against the rest of the league this season. Galarraga will next face the A's, to whom he gave up three earned runs in three innings on June 3 in a relief appearance during a 5-4 Tigers loss.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher, who was acquired in the July trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs, has been on the disabled list since getting shelled by the Twins on Aug. 19, and complaining of a dead arm. His arm looked awfully lively on Sept. 4, however, as he threw five shutout innings for Oakland's Triple-A affiliate in a playoff game, allowing three hits while striking out four and walking two. Gallagher, who throws a mid-90s fastball when he's 100 percent, won his Oakland debut on July 11 but went winless in six starts before going to the DL. He's never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Although he pitched well enough to win in Tuesday's first game of a doubleheader against Toronto, Vazquez came up on the short end of the Blue Jays' ninth straight win. The right-hander allowed two runs, both scoring after two were out in the sixth, on five hits, while striking out five and walking three. He dropped to 4-4 with a 3.l9 ERA in his last eight starts, after posting a 6.55 ERA in his previous nine starts. Vazquez will return on short rest Saturday afternoon after throwing 98 pitches Tuesday. Vazquez has a 1-3 record with a 5.33 ERA this season against Detroit. He holds a 5-7 career mark when facing the Tigers, with a 4.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander was originally scheduled to face the White Sox on Friday night and went through his full pregame routine before the game was finally called. Instead, he'll pitch the day game on Sunday as he tries to break the grip that the White Sox seem to have on him. He's 1-4 with a 6.09 ERA in five starts against Chicago this year.

home_pitcher_note: Ozzie Guillen made this starting assignment official on Wednesday, stating that he wants to go with a right-handed hurler against Detroit, as opposed to rookie southpaw Clayton Richard. Broadway has made one previous start this season, getting the win over Kansas City by allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings on Aug. 14, but he has not been nearly as effective pitching out of the bullpen, as his 8.49 ERA indicates.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers' start was pushed back four days because of hip soreness, and Saturday's rainout cost him another day, making it essentially a skipped turn in the rotation. The Tigers are hoping the rest does Rogers some good and eases some of the aches and pains in his 43-year-old body. He's 3-7 with a 7.45 ERA in 10 starts since the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy makes his fifth start for the Rangers after missing 4 1/2 months because of severe forearm/elbow inflammation. After two quality starts, he lost in his last outing against the Red Sox, allowing six runs in 5 1/3 innings in a 7-2 defeat. Opponents are hitting .250 off him, .300 by left-handed hitters and .200 by right-handed hitters. They are 3-for-17 (.176) off him with runners in scoring position. McCarthy is 1-2 with a 5.25 ERA in 10 games, including three starts, against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers will give Willis his shot at a start down the stretch after he spent most of the summer working on his command and delivery in a Minor League stint. He went from Class A Lakeland up through Triple-A Toledo and back to the big leagues, where a pair of simulated games earned him this test. How he fares could determine his course this offseason towards next year, the second season in the three-year contract he signed in December.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is trying to break a two-game losing streak and is 3-3 with a 4.46 ERA in his last six starts since coming off the disabled list (strained left groin) on Aug. 15. He beat the Tigers, 9-1, on Aug. 20 with a six-hitter for the first of two straight complete games. He is now 4-4 with a 3.78 ERA in 10 starts against the Tigers in his career. He is 5-3 with a 4.37 ERA in 11 starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: After Miner's outings in July and August became a godsend to the Tigers rotation, Miner is struggling down the stretch. The latest example came Monday against the A's, who roughed him up for eight runs on 11 hits and forced him to use 110 pitches over 4 1/3 innings. That outing alone bumped up his ERA by more than half a run. He'll have a couple extra days of rest thanks to weekend postponements in Chicago before facing the Rangers, whom he beat in April with 3 1/3 hitless innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Nippert has taken 163 points off his ERA as he's made his case to continue as a big league starter. His last time out in Oakland, he held the A's to one run on four hits and four walks in five-plus innings and he struck out seven. He shut the A's out over the first five innings, they finally scratched a run off him in the sixth when he couldn't record an out. Nippert will aim to extend his winning streak to three against the Tigers on Wednesday. It will be his first outing against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia hasn't pitched in the Majors on June 8, 2007, when he was a Phillies starter trying to pitch through discomfort in his right shoulder. An unsuccessful summer of rest and rehab stints led to surgery to repair his labrum and rotator cuff just over a year, and he has spent most of this year working his way back into pitching shape. The Tigers signed him last month in what has essentially been a two-way tryout: Detroit gets to see where he's at in his rehab and gauge whether to try to re-sign him this winter, while Garcia has had the chance to work with the Tigers coaching staff on the finishing touches to his comeback and get an idea about the organization before free agency.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona continued to prompt head scratches as he once again ran into trouble in the sixth inning on Saturday against the Royals. Staked to a 2-2 tie, the young right-hander gave up two quick runs, which stood to be enough for him to pick up his seventh loss of the season. In his last three outings, Carmona has given up 10 runs in the sixth inning. All told, he went 6 1/3 innings, allowing seven runs on 11 hits and three walks. Carmona has been dominant against the Tigers this season, picking up three wins in three appearances while allowing just seven runs over 19 innings pitched. Lifetime, Carmona has had similar success, going 6-2 with a 3.34 ERA in 11 appearances (eight starts).
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers wanted to give Galarraga some extra rest after he looked like he was tiring down the stretch over his last couple outings, but they weren't planning to sit him for this long. Thanks to rainouts at Chicago last Friday and Saturday, Galarraga hasn't pitched since giving up five runs over four innings against Oakland on Sept. 10. He hasn't won in his last four starts, but he'll get a chance to rebound against a Cleveland club he has beaten three times in four meetings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers continues to be a mystery this season, as he put up one of his shortest outings on Sunday against the Royals. Coming off his best start of the season, in which he held the Orioles to a run over eight innings, Sowers resumed his knack of nibbling to no avail and giving up big hits in tight situations. Over three innings and an obtuse 75 pitches, the 25-year-old left-hander gave up three runs on five hits to pick up a no-decision. In his two starts against Detroit this season, Sowers has labored, going 0-2 with a 10.24 ERA. Sowers is 1-3 with an 8.24 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander gets the start after going 7 2/3 innings allowing four runs, all earned, on nine hits against the White Sox on Sunday, which he took the loss in. In 14 career starts against the Indians, Verlander is 4-9 with a 6.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anthony Reyes, who was scheduled to make this start, was shut down for the rest of the season on Tuesday because of lingering inflammation in his right elbow. But the Indians certainly have a viable backup candidate in Lewis, who has made two starts in Reyes' place and has not allowed a single run. After tossing eight scoreless innings in his big-league debut against the Orioles on Sept. 10, Lewis worked six scoreless against the Twins on Monday, allowing just three hits with two walks and five strikeouts to get his second win. He gets by with less-than-electric stuff because of his precise command. Lewis will face the Tigers for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: In his first big league start since June 11, Willis had a solid game on Monday night against the Rangers. He went five innings, allowing three runs on two hits with four strikeouts and five walks. Both manager Jim Leyland and pitching coach Chuck Hernandez said they were pleased that Willis made progress. Although Willis was disappointed, the Tigers eventually lost the game, he said he felt good on the mound and left the clubhouse on a positive note. Willis will try and improve on that outing against the Tribe, a team he's 0-2 with a 7.42 ERA against in three lifetime starts.

home_pitcher_note: In 7 1/3 innings his last time out, Miner allowed only two runs on five hits and a walk. All five hits were mere singles and he left his bullpen a two-run cushion to give him his ninth victory of the season. It didn't work out. He's now gone three starts since earning his last victory, but his two runs allowed his last time out were a fast improvement to the 13 runs he'd allowed his previous 10 1/3 innings. He'll look to continue on the right track against the Royals on Monday. His last two victories came against Kansas City and he's 3-0 against the Royals in four appearances with a 1.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Meche's command was off, but this time he survived nicely. He went seven innings to gain a 5-2 win over the Mariners. He gave up six hits and three walks. Meche also notched seven strikeouts and, in his last 10 starts, he has 74 whiffs. His 172 strikeouts is a career high. Meche has faced the Tigers three times this season with a win and two no-decisions. Comerica Park is one of his favorite stops -- he's 4-1 with a 3.38 ERA in 11 starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia's 2008 debut was short and sweet. More importantly, it was efficient. In five innings, he held a potent Rangers lineup to a single unearned run in a hitter-friendly ballpark. The Rangers got only two hits off him and he struck out three to his one walk. In his next start, Garcia will face the Royals, whom he made his last start against in 2007 on June 8. He's 8-10 in his career against the Royals with a 6.01 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke worked seven innings of a 12-0 blowout in his last start and gave up just two hits and one walk with seven strikeouts. There haven't been many bad spots in his season. Only once did he fail to go five innings and only six times in 31 starts did he surrender more than four earned runs. This is his fourth go at the Tigers this year; he beat them, 4-1, on April 3, had a no-decision on May 13 and lost, 7-1, on July 23.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson returns from the Tigers bullpen for one final start this season after his previous start showed progress in his effort to hone his command. He pitched seven innings of one-run ball Sept. 9 against the A's, leaving with a lead before Oakland came back to win. His only outing since then consisted of 2 2/3 innings of relief with three runs and four walks last Wednesday at Texas. He has one start and two relief appearances against the Royals this year, none of them resulting in a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister struggled to put away White Sox hitters in his last start. He threw 93 pitches over five innings and surrendered a grand slam to Alexei Ramirez and a solo homer to Jim Thome. Bannister had snapped a 13-game winless streak in his previous start and will be looking to get back on track with a positive performance that he can take with him into the offseason.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga's incredible rookie season, which began as a Spring Training long shot and a season-opening stint at Triple-A Toledo, will close out with his final start against the Rays. He tossed seven innings of four-hit, one-run ball at Tampa Bay on Aug. 3 but left with a no-decision.
