He won three straight starts after that, but has gone winless in five outings since, including a no-decision for his 7 2/3 quality innings last Friday at Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: The Rays ace made history on Saturday night, as Kazmir's six-inning performance helped Tampa Bay clinch its first playoff spot. The lefty scattered five hits over six scoreless frames with five strikeouts. Kazmir stumped a potent Twins offense and exited after throwing 93 pitches. He will be facing Detroit for the second time this season, exiting with a no-decision after 4 2/3 innings on Aug. 1. He is a career 2-3 in seven starts against the Tigers, with a 4.33 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander said after his last start that he had some of the best stuff he has had at this late stage of a season. The results haven't caught up. Saturday's loss at Cleveland, where he gave up four runs on five hits and four walks in four innings, was his fourth straight defeat since his last victory Aug. 22 at Kansas City. He moved into the Major League lead in losses by himself with the highest single-season total by a Tigers pitcher since the infamous 43-119 season of 2003. Much of those struggles, however, have been against AL Central teams, and he has a chance to close out on a high note in his first start against the Rays since Aug. 6, 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine is coming off Sunday afternoon's loss in which the right-hander allowed four runs (two earned) in 6 2/3 innings. The 4-1 loss to Minnesota came just a night removed from the Rays' playoff-clinching win and Sonnanstine was the hard-luck pitcher in the flat game. The right-hander fanned four and walked two in the performance, but remains winless since Aug. 18. He will be facing Detroit for the second time this season, winning Aug. 2, when he tossed six innings of two-run baseball.

home_pitcher_note: After all the hope and setbacks of this trying season, Willis has one more start left to try to provide a glimpse of what he can provide the Tigers for next year before heading into the offseason. It was not a promising sight last Sunday at Cleveland, where he gave up six runs on five hits and six walks over 2 1/3 innings. It was a throwback to the control issues he had earlier in the season before heading to the Minors for three months to work on his mechanics. He had much better success in his return a week and a half ago, when he allowed three runs on two hits and five walks over five innings at Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Garza served up a gritty performance in his last outing, against the Red Sox on Sept. 17, when he pitched on three days' rest. During that start, Garza threw 75 pitches in 4 2/3 innings and was touched for five hits and three runs en route to a no-decision. Rays manager Joe Maddon wanted to allow Garza a chance to recover from that start, so he let him miss his next turn. Garza is 0-3 with a 4.84 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers. The 24-year-old Fresno State product has arguably the best stuff on the Rays staff, and he has allowed one run or fewer in 11 of his past 25 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miner will close out his two-month stint in the rotation by pitching the season finale, a fitting end to a year in which he ended up being one of Detroit's most effective starting pitchers. He's one of just two Tigers starters with a winning record, but he's winless in his past four starts. The latest occurred on Monday against the Royals, who plated four runs off of him over six innings with six hits and four walks. He has a 7.23 ERA over his past four outings, having allowed 30 hits over 23 2/3 innings. However, he has allowed just one home run in that span, sticking to his strength of keeping the ball on the ground.
away_pitcher_note: Shields earned his 14th win of the season Tuesday at Camden Yards, holding the Orioles to two runs on eight hits in seven innings. He walked one and struck out eight. Shields is 2-0 with a 2.42 ERA in three career starts against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd almost stopped the bleeding for the White Sox again on Thursday night at the Metrodome, going in search of his 10th victory this season after a White Sox loss. Floyd allowed four runs on 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings, walking one and striking out four, but he managed to strand seven Minnesota runners. Floyd finished with a no-decision, when the bullpen couldn't hold a two-run lead. Floyd has a 2-0 record with a 4.24 ERA against Detroit this season and is 3-0 lifetime against the Tigers. Floyd will be pitching on three days' rest, having lost his last time in Kansas City following the short break.
away_pitcher_note: The rotation order just worked out for Garcia to be on turn for a possible Monday outing if the game was necessary. If it is, he'll be in the curious position of having a chance to either knock his former team out of the division title or force them into a one-game playoff. All in all, it's not a bad way to end a late-season comeback from shoulder surgery that cost him more than a year off the mound. Since he was planning on starting his winter ball campaign in his native Venezuela in a few weeks, the extra work won't be a big deal.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay returns as the ace of a relatively young and inexperienced starting staff, taking the ball on Opening Day for the seventh year in a row. That streak is the longest such run for any pitcher in Toronto franchise history. Halladay finished last season as the runner-up to Cleveland's Cliff Lee in the balloting for the American League Cy Young Award in 2008, ending the campaign with a career-high 206 strikeouts and a league-leading nine complete games. Halladay compiled 246 innings -- the third season in a row Doc logged at least 220 innings -- and he led the AL with a 2.08 ground ball-to-fly ball ratio and a strikeout-to-walk rate of 5.28. During that impressive showing, Halladay did not encounter the Tigers, but he has handled Detroit well over his career. In 15 outings against his Opening Day opponent, Halladay has gone 11-2 with a crisp 1.93 ERA. Pitching at Rogers Centre has also been something that Halladay has enjoyed over his career. Using his dancing and darting arsenal of sinkers and cutters, Halladay has fashioned a 73-28 mark at the Dome with a 3.28 ERA over 135 games. Last year, all Halladay did in Toronto was go 10-4 with a 2.78 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The former All-Star's effort to bounce back from last year's shocking struggles begins here, with his second straight Opening Day assignment. His 1-7 record over the first month and a half last season sent him reeling toward an American League high in losses and a spiral he couldn't seem to escape no matter what adjustments he tried to make. He believes he has made the changes he needed, and he has the Spring Training performances to back it up -- one run allowed over a 19-inning stretch, including a 13-inning scoreless streak over his final three Spring Training starts before the Braves roughed him up in his finale for seven runs on nine hits over five innings. A return to a lower arm angle seems to have helped bring back much of his old velocity, bumping the fastball to 97 mph, while a change of stance with his landing leg is expected to help give him better command on all of his pitches. Part of last year's struggles included an Aug. 11 loss to the Blue Jays at Comerica Park in his first career outing against Toronto, which hit him for six runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings, the fourth straight loss in a season that included three different four-game losing streaks, two of them in the season's second half.

home_pitcher_note: Purcey is third on Toronto's depth chart, but has been moved up into the second slot in the rotation to break up the right-handed and left-handed starters. Purcey had an inconsistent stint as a rookie starter for the Jays last season, finishing with 58 strikeouts and 29 walks over 65 innings in 12 starts. Purcey -- a first-round pick by Toronto in the 2004 First-Year Player Draft -- pitches best when he has his curveball working well and he's consistently finding the strike zone. The left-hander can be exposed when his breaking ball isn't working properly.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's Tigers debut will come against one of his familiar division foes from his days in Tampa Bay, not to mention an opponent he faced little more than a week ago. There are likely no secrets between Jackson and the Jays, but both he and the Tigers believe that if he executes his stuff, it likely won't matter. He went 2-1 over his four starts against Toronto last year, allowing nine earned runs over 24 1/3 innings. At Rogers Centre, however, he has never lost in five career starts, striking out 28 batters over 33 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: At 24 years old, and with just two big league seasons under his belt, Litsch is the most experienced starter on the staff behind ace Roy Halladay. The right-hander has gone 20-18 with a 3.67 ERA over the past two years. Litsch works fast, fields his position well and pounds the strike zone. Last season, he added a four-seam fastball to his repertoire, helping to offset his cutter and sinker. After finishing with 196 innings between Toronto and Triple-A a year ago, Litsch is hoping to top 200 innings for the Blue Jays this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jeremy Bonderman's season-opening DL stint with shoulder tightness means that Miner, who has had two successful summer stints as a starter over the past three years, gets to open the season in a rotation for the first time in his brief Major League career. And he'll do it after manager Jim Leyland had just about ruled him out of contention for a starting job. He struggled with hanging sinkers and big hits while he was actually a starting candidate, then turned in 10 straight scoreless innings once he was ruled out. He has been incredibly effective against the Jays in his career, tossing 16 2/3 innings with three earned runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Romero, who was the first pitcher selected (sixth overall) in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft, beat out fellow left-handed prospects Brett Cecil and Brad Mills for a spot in the rotation this spring. Romero, 24, was considered out of the race after a handful of spring outings, but pitching coach Brad Arnsberg went to work on retooling the lefty's delivery and results came fast. Romero impressed the Jays in his last two Spring Training starts and convinced the club to take him north. Last season, Romero was 8-8 with a 4.55 ERA in 28 Minor League starts between Double-A and Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Less than two years after Porcello graduated from high school, he formally graduates to the big leagues. The Tigers' first-round Draft pick from 2007 accelerated his timetable dramatically and earned a rotation job with a consistent, solid spring and a bunch of nasty sinkers for quick ground ball outs, not to mention a maturity well beyond his tender age of 20. He was on a 75-pitch limit last year at Class A ball, but the Tigers appear inclined to let him go longer as the season goes along.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga was awarded the home-opener assignment partly as a reward for his breakout 2008 season, having led the Tigers in victories for the year. Just as important, though, is the fact that Galarraga never seems to get hyped up, a key advantage for a game that's an unofficial holiday in Detroit with an intense atmosphere. If his makeup gets him ready for it, his challenge before then is to make sure he's physically ready after having to catch up on innings after the World Baseball Classic. The fact that he'll face his old squad with a former Rangers catcher, Gerald Laird, possibly working with him is a nice bonus. He beat the Rangers last August with a quality start at Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Benson will be making his first start in a Major League game since Sept. 27, 2006, when he was with the Orioles. The right-hander was signed by the Rangers at the beginning of Spring Training and ended up winning a spot in the starting rotation. He missed much of the past two seasons with a torn rotator cuff and is 2-1 with a 2.38 ERA in three career starts against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: All the adjustments Verlander made in Spring Training didn't help him once a two-out walk to Alex Rios set up a four-run first inning on Opening Day in Toronto before four more runs chased him in the fourth. The eight earned runs tied Verlander's career high from his rookie season of 2006, but he feels comfortable that the changes he made are sticking. He made a point to throw breaking balls early and often the first time through the Jays order, and he caught himself losing command of his fastball before settling down in the second and third innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison was a nine-game winner for the Rangers in 2008, the most number of wins by a rookie left-hander in club history. His .750 winning percentage was the third highest in club history for a pitcher with at least 10 decisions. He did not pitch against the Tigers last year. He was 5-2 with a 5.94 ERA in 10 starts at home. He was 6-3 with a 3.43 ERA in 15 Minor League starts, giving him 15 wins on the season.

home_pitcher_note: If the Tigers can get anything close to the efficient success of Jackson's Tigers debut going forward, they might have the innings-eating workhorse for their rotation. Jackson threw just 89 pitches Tuesday in sending down the Blue Jays through seven innings of one-hit scoreless ball before Scott Rolen's leadoff homer and a subsequent error by Brandon Inge knocked him out in the eighth. Brandon Lyon's blown save left Jackson without a win to show for his work, but his ability to give the Tigers a chance in what had been a low-scoring duel could be huge for Detroit if he can keep it up.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood won for the first time in four Opening Day starts with a 9-1 victory over the Indians on Monday. He allowed one run on five hits, walked one and struck out five. He threw 113 pitches and said he still felt strong going into the seventh. Millwood is 4-4 with a 3.91 ERA in 11 career starts against the Tigers and 2-1 with a 3.15 ERA in three starts in Detroit. He was 4-7 with a 5.05 ERA on the road last year. That was the sixth highest road ERA among AL ERA qualifiers last year.

home_pitcher_note: Opening the season in a Major League rotation for the first time in his career, Miner recovered from four straight baserunners to open his season debut Wednesday at Toronto and tossed 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball, collecting Detroit's first win of the year in the process. Now he returns home to Comerica Park, where his career 5.28 ERA is more than two full runs higher than his 3.14 mark on the road. Opponents have batted .301 against him at home compared with .234 everywhere else.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander looked every bit as dominant during his first start of 2009 as his stellar Spring Training projected him to be. Floyd worked seven innings, fanning nine and walking two, while giving up two runs on six hits. Those two runs were two too many against the Royals, as Zack Greinke was just a little bit better. Floyd has made a living out of manhandling the Tigers, posting a 3-0 record with a 3.68 ERA against the Tigers in a 2008 to boost his career mark to 4-0. He holds a 2-0 record with a 2.63 ERA at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello's Major League debut Thursday at Toronto turned on a pair of home runs that sent him to defeat. However, he still gave a good look at the poise and pitching acumen that convinced the Tigers he could handle the jump from Class A ball to the Majors at the age of 20. Now he'll try to build off that outing with the extra challenge of facing a powerful White Sox known for chewing up young Tigers pitchers over the last few years, such as Justin Verlander.
away_pitcher_note: Although Danks felt as if he wasn't efficient enough with his 95 pitches, the southpaw still threw six scoreless innings during Thursday's loss to the Royals. Danks gave up just three singles, while walking three and striking out five. He also had to pitch out of a bases-loaded, one-out jam in the third, courtesy of Mark Teahen's line-drive double play. The southpaw posted a 2-0 record with a 2.41 ERA against the Tigers in 2008 and has a 2-1 career mark against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Any questions on whether last year's Tigers surprise story has the capability to repeat or better his breakout 2008 season seemingly were answered Friday, when Galarraga dominated the previously scorching Rangers offense for seven innings of one-run ball. His eight strikeouts marked a career high, and the Rangers that did hit the ball never made good contact, limited to five singles and a slew of groundouts. He ended up being the perfect starter for the always-intense home opener in Detroit, and he'll close out the opening homestand against the only division opponent he didn't start against last year. His lone meeting with the White Sox was his ill-fated relief appearance in the season's final game.
away_pitcher_note: It certainly wasn't a dominant effort for Contreras in his first start since rupturing his left Achilles tendon back on Aug. 9, 2008. But the Twins didn't exactly crush the right-hander, a performance somewhere in between that was somewhat expected from the veteran. Contreras gave up four earned runs on seven hits, including Joe Crede's home run, over five innings. He walked three, struck out three and threw 86 pitches. But most importantly, Contreras felt healthy after his first regular-season test. Contreras has an 8-8 lifetime record against Detroit and a 4-4 mark at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander struck out a season-best eight batters in his last start, but didn't have the same command he had against the Twins in his Opening Day win against the Twins. Three of the seven hits Hernandez surrendered to the Athletics went for extra-bases and drove in four of the five runs, including a decisive two-run home run to Oakland slugger Jack Cust, the second of his career off Hernandez.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's second start of the season didn't last much longer than his first, with the Rangers chasing him after five innings and 97 pitches last Saturday. However, both Verlander and manager Jim Leyland pointed to a vast improvement in his pitches, both with good velocity and easier effort while regaining some movement, evidenced by his eight strikeouts against four walks. Leyland wants to see Verlander lasting around seven innings consistently within the next three to five starts, which makes Verlander's matchup with the Mariners a big stepping stone. The more outs he can get early in counts, the deeper he'll last into the game.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched the best game of his tenure with the Mariners in his previous outing, holding the Athletics to two hits over the first eight innings and three hits in 8 1/3 innings. He retired 11 of 12 batters during one stretch and 13 straight in another. His left shoulder obviously is healthy again, and he threw 102 pitches overall, 67 of them for strikes. He has 14 strikeouts in his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson couldn't repeat the dominance from his first Tigers start when he took the mound last Sunday against the Rangers, but he kept the Tigers close enough for a late-inning comeback. The Rangers roughed up Jackson for two-run homers in the first and third innings, but he not only held Texas scoreless from there, he lasted six innings in the process. His 13 innings through two starts has reinforced team hopes that he'll emerge as an innings-eater on the staff, not to mention a maturing young starter set to follow up on last year's success with Tampa Bay. Jackson won both of his previous career starts against the Mariners, allowing a lone run on nine hits over 15 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Silva had his best outing in several months, holding the Angels to two runs over seven innings in the Mariners' home opener. Unfortunately for him, the Mariners also scored two runs while he was on the mound, so he had to settle for a no-decision. The good news is he had command of the strike zone and kept the ball down most of the time, resulting in just six outfield putouts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello's Major League debut Thursday at Toronto turned on a pair of home runs that sent him to defeat. However, he still gave a good look at the poise and pitching acumen that convinced the Tigers he could handle the jump from Class A ball to the Majors at the age of 20. He was originally slated to make his follow-up start at home Tuesday against the White Sox, but the rainout prompted the Tigers to push him back to the weekend series and back on the road. It not only keeps Detroit's top three starts in line, it gives the Tigers a chance to conserve innings on their young starter, who pitched just 125 innings last year as a teenager at Class A Lakeland.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver began the season with 9 2/3 scoreless innings before the Mariners broke through with four runs to hang a loss on the slender right-hander on Wednesday night in Seattle. Weaver has been in top form, despite the loss, serving notice that he could be returning to his rookie form of 2006, when he looked like a dominant starter of the future. He is putting his fastball in good locations and keeping hitters off-balance with quality breaking stuff. He has 10 strikeouts against four walks in 11 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga continued to dominate hitters in his second straight start to begin the 2009 season, firing 6 1/3 shutout innings against the Chicago White Sox on Wednesday at Comerica Park. Galarraga gave up four hits and struck out five batters while walking two. He threw 110 pitches, which wasn't quite as efficient as his first start on April 10 against Texas, when he threw 97 pitches in seven innings, struck out eight, walked one and gave up one run on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders demonstrated why he was an American League All-Star in 2008 with a superlative effort against the hot-hitting Mariners on Thursday night, snapping their winning streak at six games. The smooth lefty limited the Mariners to one run across seven innings on three hits, his only walk intentional. He struck out three, including a full-count whiff of Wladimir Balentien to leave the bases loaded. Saunders is emerging as one of the game's best and most dependable southpaws at 27, working several off-speed deliveries in with his bread-and-butter sinker. He's deceptively fast, consistently reaching the low 90s. He's 0-1 in two career starts against the Tigers with a 6.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander admitted to feeling as confounded as he's ever been in his last start, when he pitched four perfect, overpowering innings against the Mariners with, striking out seven before watching his night unravel in a five-run fifth inning. By his own account, Verlander was working with the best stuff he's had since his no-hitter in June 2007, but a leadoff double in the fifth by Adrian Beltre snowballed into a big inning when the Mariners bunted successfully, third baseman Brandon Inge committed a throwing error and Verlander uncorked a wild pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer will be recalled Thursday from Triple-A to face the Tigers in his fourth career Major League start. Palmer went 0-2 with an 8.33 ERA for the Giants last season and was 1-1 with a 11.74 ERA in two Minor League starts this season. Even though he's struggled at the Major League level, Angels manager Mike Scioscia liked what he saw from Palmer in Spring Training and called him the club's "best short-term option," with Darren Oliver moving back to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off an outstanding outing on Saturday against the Mariners in Seattle in which he went 7 2/3 innings, allowing no runs and five hits. Jackson kept the Mariners off-balance with offspeed pitches behind his mid-90s fastball and stuck out six. He is becoming the pitcher the Tigers hoped he would be when they traded for him during the offseason. Jackson allowed four runs over seven innings and took the win in his only start against the Angels last season.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is on a big-time roll to start the season. He has gone 20 innings without allowing a run and has his franchise-record scoreless-innings streak up to 34. He pitched the best game of his career on Saturday against the Rangers, notching his first career shutout with a seven-hitter, striking out 10. Greinke is working beautifully with catcher Miguel Olivo, who is forcing him to pitch inside more with his fastball. That is opening up the outer part of the plate and making his silder, curveball and changeup even more effective.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello won his first big league game -- in his second career start -- Sunday in dazzling fashion. He worked seven innings, allowing just five hits and one run in an 8-2 victory. He struck out three and didn't walk a batter in his 86-pitch outing. He yielded a third-inning home run then retired the final 14 batters in a row. His first victory comes at age 20 years, three months and 22 days.

home_pitcher_note: Davies walked four batters in the first inning of his last outing vs. the Rangers, and still left with a quality start. He gave up only three hits and had the lead when he left after six innings. He retired 10 of the last 11 batters he faced. Davies relies on throwing his fastball for strikes early, setting up his changeup and curveball. He said after Sunday's start against the Rangers that he needs to adjust quicker if he's pounding the strike zone with fastballs early in the game and not locating the pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Last Tuesday's rainout against the White Sox prompted the four-man rotation that put Miner back in the bullpen for a while. Now that the off-days have passed and the Tigers need a fifth starter again, Miner will make his first start since April 13, and presumably keep on turn from there for the foreseeable future. The sinkerballer struggled with the cold, dry conditions at Comerica Park last Monday to yield eight runs on nine hits over 3 1/3 innings. Though he didn't use it as an excuse, the conditions clearly hampered his ability to grip the ball. That shouldn't be a problem at Kansas City, where the forecast calls for high temperatures in the low 70s this weekend.

home_pitcher_note: After making it through his first two starts with creditable six-inning outings, Ponson bogged down last Tuesday night at Cleveland. He lasted just 3 1/3 innings and gave up six runs on eight hits and four walks. He also gave up his first homer of the year, Grady Sizemore's three-run shot. Ponson's command was off; he made 80 pitches and only 43 were strikes. So he'll have to upgrade his performance against the Tigers, against whom he's 4-4 with a 6.62 ERA in nine career games.
away_pitcher_note: After dominant outings in his first two starts, Galarraga finally had a struggle on his hands Tuesday, thanks to the Angels. A combination of well placed singles and early walks pushed Galarraga's pitch total past 80 before he could get the second out of the third inning. He made it through five innings, but needed 110 pitches to do it, including a Torii Hunter home run to tie the game and leave him with a no-decision. Fortunately for Galarraga, he has an excellent chance for a rebound at Kansas City, where his last outing, on July 23, saw him take a perfect game into the seventh inning before finally giving up a run on three hits.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander's stuff continues to impress, but his results remain disappointing. The right-hander's struggles rolled on in his last start Wednesday, when the Angels scored seven runs on nine hits over five innings. While Verlander's command was strong, the Angels fouled off numerous pitches to extend their at-bats and wait for pitches they could line into the gaps or ground through the infield. The Yankees pose another challenge for Verlander, who gave up five earned runs on seven hits over 1 2/3 innings in his only meeting with the Bronx Bombers last year, in September.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia gets the ball for his fourth start as a Yankee on Monday, looking for better results than in his last outing vs. the A's. On Wednesday in New York, Sabathia failed to hold leads twice and allowed seven runs -- six earned -- in a laborious 6 2/3 innings. Sabathia has never been a strong April performer but said that his struggles of late have been attributable to trying to be too fine and hit the corners instead of working the plate in thirds. Sabathia lasted only four innings and allowed a career-high nine runs in an April 16 start vs. the Tigers last year, his only start against them. He is 13-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 26 career starts vs. Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: After two dominant starts and another solid one, Jackson finally battled his command in his fourth outing as a Tiger. After two bases-loaded walks erased an early lead and a Torii Hunter homer put him behind against the Angels, Jackson has seemingly recovered until two infield singles and two errors sank him in the sixth. It was still a decent demonstration in damage control, but it wasn't enough for the Tigers to overcome. Jackson will face a familiar challenge with the Yankees, who have given him a 5.72 ERA in 13 career outings but who have homered just five times in 50 1/3 innings against him.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes will be recalled from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre for Tuesday's start, remaining in the rotation for the foreseeable future as Chien-Ming Wang straightens out strength and mechanical issues. Hughes last pitched on Wednesday at Triple-A, improving to 3-0 with 7 2/3 innings of one-run, six-hit ball in a 6-1 victory over Buffalo, walking one and striking out seven in a 105-pitch start. In three International League starts, Hughes had a 1.86 ERA, allowing four runs on 17 hits in 19 1/3 innings, walking three and striking out 19. Hughes had a 2.19 ERA in four Grapefruit League games (three starts) with New York this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello took the loss in his last outing at Kansas City, but showed signs of progress with his offspeed pitches. After surrendering two early homers to Kansas City, Porcello settled down and used all his pitches effectively to keep Royals' hitters off-balance. He wound up allowing four earned runs in six innings with a performance that manager Jim Leyland applauded. Leyland went so far as to say he liked what Porcello did in the loss at Kansas City better than what Porcello did in his win at Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Chamberlain allowed two runs -- one earned -- over 5 1/3 innings in his last start for New York, allowing a career-high nine hits to the Red Sox at Fenway Park, but dodged bullets all game by inducing three inning-ending double plays. Chamberlain struck out only two, matching a career-low, but has held opponents to three earned runs or less in 13 of his 15 career starts. Chamberlain pitched one scoreless inning against the Tigers last year in relief and has logged four career innings in four appearances against Detroit, though this will mark his first start and third appearance at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga allowed just three hits over six innings in his last start at Kansas City but wasn't happy about issuing five walks. He said he will be working on his mechanics so that walks won't be a problem as he goes forward. Galarraga made the big pitch when he needed it in Kansas City, and perhaps it's a good sign for the Tigers that he could hold the Royals to just one run despite those mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano has the ball for the first of a seven-game road trip, beginning in Detroit. The Twins hit Pavano hard in his last start, scoring five runs on 11 hits and a walk in five-plus innings. Pavano, who has spent a good deal of his career in the National League, has never faced the Tigers. He will go against a former teammate in Detroit slugger Miguel Cabrera, who was a part of the Florida Marlins' 2003 World Series Championship team, along with Pavano.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers used an off-day to shuffle their rotation so that Miner and similar sinkerballer Rick Porcello wouldn't be pitching on consecutive days, leaving Miner with six days of rest before he faces the Indians. It also allows manager Jim Leyland a little more flexbility to go to his bullpen early if he sees signs of trouble in Miner. Miner threw five innings of one-run ball at Kansas City last Saturday, but also walked three Royals and threw just 42 of his 83 pitches for strikes. He has never started against Cleveland, but owns a 1-1 record and 5.02 ERA in nine relief meetings with the Indians, walking eight batters over 14 1/3 innings. With Dontrelle Willis progressing quickly through the Tigers farm system in his rehab assignment, this outing could be a big test for Miner.
away_pitcher_note: Called up because of an injury to Scott Lewis, Laffey has been a major sparkplug for the Tribe's rotation. The Indians are 3-0 in games he starts. His ERA would rank among the league's leaders if not for him falling one-third of an inning shy of qualification. Pitching with a chip on his shoulder after losing out in the bid for the last spot in the Tribe's rotation out of spring camp, Laffey has had strong command of his sinker, and he's also using his breaking ball with more effectiveness. He limited the Twins to a pair of runs on five hits over 6 1/3 innings in a victory on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander has pitched well off and on this season, but his last start marked the first time good results and good performance matched up. His seven-plus scoreless innings against the Yankees saw him strike out nine while not walking a batter and scattering seven singles. Considering his struggles against New York over the last couple of years, it was an impressive performance, but his next start against Cleveland at Comerica Park will pit him against a division rival who has roughed him up over the years.
away_pitcher_note: Facing a potent Red Sox lineup on Monday, Lee was brilliant for eight innings in which he allowed just five hits and nothing more. He struck out five batters and induced two double plays, but all he had to show for his efforts was a no-decision. This was Lee truly in the form that made him a Cy Young winner last season, and his improvement is best demonstrated by the fact that his ERA, which was at 12.60 after his Opening Day debacle in Texas, is now under four. He says the key is mixing up his pitches earlier in the game and in the count, getting results out of his breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: Usually, the new guy gets a little better welcome than this. Jackson has taken a scoreless performance into the seventh inning in three of his first five starts as a Tiger, but has only one win to show for it. He threw 117 pitches over six innings in his last start to keep the Tigers in a scoreless game against the Yankees before New York erupted for 10 runs in the seventh. He's 1-2 with a 9.42 ERA in six career appearances, including three starts, against the Twins, but his lone meeting with Minnesota last year featured 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball for a much-needed victory at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty looked to be in his line for his first win of the season, after allowing just two runs over 6 2/3 innings to the Rays in his last start. But the Twins were unable to hold on to the lead, winning on a walkoff fielder’s choice in the ninth inning. For Liriano, it was a positive outing in that he started to show better command of his fastball while also mixing in his breaking. He’ll try to avoid becoming the second Twins Opening Day starter to begin a season at 0-5, the only other being Frank Viola back in 1989. Liriano is 2-1 with a 4.93 ERA in seven career appearances (five starts) against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers put Porcello in their season-opening rotation fully expecting he would struggle at times, and his last start hit the mark. He struggled to get his sinker down and his curveball on the corners, and the Yankees pounced, roughing him up for six runs on six hits over 3 2/3 innings. He isn't going anywhere, but look for the Tigers to work with the youngster on adjustments as he prepares for a Twins lineup that could pick him apart if he can't locate.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander delivered his second straight seven-inning outing in his last time out on the mound against the Rays. He held Tampa Bay to just two runs on eight hits while walking one and striking out three. The sinkerball pitcher was able to get plenty of groundouts despite the fact that he feeling light-headed and a little wobbly for most of his outing. After a little bit of a shaky start to the season, Blackburn is now 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in his last two starts. His next start will come against the Tigers at Comerica Park, where he is 0-2 with a 6.14 ERA in three appearances (two starts).

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle has now won four straight to start a season for the second time in his career and for the first time since 2002, after emerging victorious from Friday;s 4-3 win over Texas. Buehrle needed just 81 pitches to cover six innings, during which the southpaw allowed three runs on seven hits, while striking out two and not issuing a walk. He also was tagged for a home run by leadoff hitter Ian Kinsler. Buehrle has not faced the Tigers this season but has a 13-8 lifetime record against Detroit. Buehrle also holds a 70-40 career record with a 3.65 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: It's still too early to determine anything about Galarraga's followup to his breakout 2008 season, but his last three outings have shown hints of pitching away from contact instead of towards it, as he did as a rookie. He has 11 walks over 16 innings in that stretch, including three over five innings in his most recent outing. The Indians, who had never hit him well, roughed him up for five runs on eight hits, but it was a walk to ninth man Kelly Shoppach in a four-run second inning that seemingly allowed his outing to unravel. Wednesday won't give him any break. He's 0-4 with a 5.23 ERA against the Twins, walking 20 batters over 32 2/3 innings.

Buehrle needed just 81 pitches to cover six innings, during which the southpaw allowed three runs on seven hits, while striking out two and not issuing a walk. home_pitcher_note: Lee gave the Indians another strong effort Sunday in Detroit, but he was once again hurt by a lack of support from his teammates. Lee went seven innings, allowing three runs on 12 hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He pitched himself out of some jams early, but gave up the go-ahead runs in the seventh. Lee, who is now the Indians' all-time leader in winning percentage among those with 1,000 innings pitched, has allowed just six runs over his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander shook off his traditional struggles against the Indians with seven innings of one-run ball to outduel reigning Cy Young Award winner Cliff Lee on Sunday at Comerica Park. His next challenge will be to follow it up at Progressive Field, where he's 1-7 with a 9.00 ERA in eight career starts. That won't be easy, but it's been a while since he entered Cleveland with as much momentum as now, coming off back-to-back dominant seven-inning performances to beat the Indians and Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona received a no-decision against the Blue Jays Monday in his last start. He allowed four runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings. The right-hander walked one, struck out three and tossed 96 pitches in the outing. Carmona has logged at least six innings in each of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has allowed one run or none through six innings in four of his six starts as a Tiger, but has a lone win to show it thanks to one of the lowest run support totals in the American League. His latest defeat came Monday, when he took a 1-1 game against the Twins into the seventh inning before Minnesota plated five runs to take charge. Jackson has a start and a relief appearance for his career at Progressive Field, holding the Indians to a run on eight hits over 8 2/3 innings with nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Though he pitched well against Toronto in his last start, Reyes earned a no-decision after the Tribe's bullpen blew the lead. Reyes yielded three runs on six hits across six innings. He struck out six and did not walk a batter. Reyes has now earned no-decisions in each of his last four outings.
away_pitcher_note: The key to Porcello in good outings and bad over his first five Major League starts has been his ability to throw his sinker for strikes. When he does, he can get quick groundouts and avoid the kind of big hits that inflate his run total in a hurry. When he doesn't, he falls behind in the count and leaves himself to challenge hitters with his secondary pitches. His last start was very much a case of the former, as he held the Twins to four singles over seven innings with three walks and three strikeouts. He'll try for more of the same in his first meeting with the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey received his first loss of the season on Wednesday against the Orioles. It came under unfortunate circumstances: The game had four rain delays that totaled nearly four hours. Slowey was pulled after a long delay, giving up three earned runs in three innings. Slowey has had an interesting season. He's 4-1 but has a disappointing 5.50 ERA. He's given up eight or more hits in four of six starts, but has a superb 25-2 K/BB ratio. Next up is Detroit, a team that Slowey is 2-0 with a 5.74 ERA against in three career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Five of the six innings Galarraga threw Thursday against the White Sox were solid, but it only took one to cause problems. The right-hander gave up five runs on three hits and two walks in the first inning. He scattered only three more hits over his next five innings. It was the second start in a row that Galarraga surrendered five runs or more, and he's watched his ERA balloon from 1.85 to 4.08 in that span. Hell have his work cut out for him in Minnesota. In six career games against the Twins, Galarraga is 0-4 with a 5.23 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins went six innings in his last start against the Orioles. The left-hander allowed four earned runs on five hits while striking out two. Perkins went 2-1 with a 2.73 ERA in four starts against the Tigers last season. The Twins are 2-4 in his starts in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Willis will be activated to make his first start of the season after spending the past month and a half on the 15-day disabled list with an anxiety disorder. Tigers manager Jim Leyland said Willis will not be on any sort of pitch count -- he threw 118 pitches in his final rehab start for Triple-A Toledo. In that start, Willis gave up two runs in 7 2/3 innings, fanning four and walking four. The left-hander has only made one appearance against the Twins, giving up one run in an inning of relief.

home_pitcher_note: Scott Baker pitched precisely the sort of game that he needed to get back on track Friday against Seattle. Baker dealt seven shutout innings, striking out five and walking none in Minnesota's 11-0 victory. The previously struggling Twins ace was 0-4 with a 9.15 ERA in four starts coming into the game. This start came after Baker carried a no-hitter through six innings against the Royals but surrendered five earned runs in the seventh inning. Baker gets Detroit next. He is 4-3 in 12 career starts against the Tigers with a 3.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After going winless in his first four starts, Justin Verlander is back to dominating opposing hitters. His fastballs are hitting the upper 90s with ease, his curveballs are dropping for strikes and he's learning to use his abundance of adrenaline in his favor. The result is a string of three stingy starts, covering 23 innings of one-run ball with five walks, 31 strikeouts and only two extra-base hits allowed. He'll get a test of that new form at the Metrodome, where good pitches can turn into bad habits on a fast artificial surface.

home_pitcher_note: While Justin Verlander is the headline performer in the Tigers rotation, Jackson is quietly blossoming into a front-line starter by keeping his team in low-scoring duels. He has entered the seventh inning with fewer than two runs allowed in four of his last five outings, though Detroit's offense has helped him to wins in just two of them. That includes last Saturday's win at Cleveland, in which he tossed seven scoreless innings. His ability to pound the strike zone is a big step forward from his days with the Rays, and it's allowing him to eat innings in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Braden turned in another solid outing -- this time against the hot-hitting Blue Jays -- but he suffered another loss and was hit in his pitching hand by a first-inning line drive off the bat of Vernon Wells. Braden stayed in the game, allowing three runs and nine hits over six innings. X-rays of Braden's left hand were negative. He has a deep bone bruise but vowed to make his next start, when the A's open a road trip on Friday in Detroit, but manager Bob Geren left open the possibility of pushing Braden back. The A's have been shut out in three of Braden's seven starts. He has received run support of one run or fewer in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: What looked like the struggles you'd expect from a 20-year-old rookie has turned into two pretty effective starts. After Porcello turned a solid sinker into seven scoreless innings against the Twins on May 5, he overcame control woes with the same pitch to get hitters out with his secondary stuff over five innings of one-run ball last Sunday against Cleveland. He didn't give up a home run in either of those outings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Braden turned in another solid outing -- this time against the hot-hitting Blue Jays -- but he suffered another loss and was hit in his pitching hand by a first-inning line drive off the bat of Vernon Wells. Braden stayed in the game, allowing three runs and nine hits over six innings. X-rays of Braden's left hand were negative. He has a deep bone bruise but vowed to make his next start before manager Bob Geren pushed him back. The A's have been shut out in three of Braden's seven starts. He has received run support of one run or fewer in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: After leading Detroit in wins last season and earning Tigers Pitcher of the Month honors in April, Galarraga is encountering the first struggles of his Detroit tenure. He has lost his past three starts with an 8.64 ERA, allowing 16 runs on 20 hits with nine walks over 16 2/3 innings. From a pitch standpoint, his last outing Tuesday at Minnesota was an improvement, with a sharper slider. Two pitches, however, cost him the game, as they were both hit for two-run homers. While he's held right-handed hitters to a .218 average, left-handed batters have hit .286 off him. He'll have a chance to break his struggles against an Oakland lineup that has yet to find its stride.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, a 21-year-old rookie, went 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in four April starts, getting through the sixth inning once. In May he's gotten through the sixth in all three starts. In his most recent outing, Tuesday against the visiting Royals, he scattered seven hits and two walks while striking out two and allowing two runs over six innings to improve to 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA for the month. Armed with a heavy sinker with late movement, Cahill left the bases loaded in the first inning and stranded three more runners in the next two innings before working a perfect fourth. Coco Crisp broke up the shutout with a homer to open the fifth, and Mike Jacobs homered for Kansas City in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: The statistics from Willis' return to the big leagues weren't encouraging, with four runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings against the Twins last Wednesday at the Metrodome. The actual pitching was better than that, and it gave the Tigers a chance to win. He threw 53 of his 87 pitches for strikes, and both of his walks came on 3-2 counts with close calls. He not only changed speeds, but showed an ability to bust pitches inside on right-handed hitters with a fastball that consistently hit the low 90s. He picked up a no-decision last September at Texas, where he gave up three runs on two hits over five innings with five walks.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three starts in May. He went seven innings in his last start, his longest of the season, and the Rangers won, 6-5, in extra innings. He is 1-1 with an 8.40 ERA on the road with opponents hitting .355 off him. Overall, for the season, left-handed hitters are batting .315 off him while right-handed hitters are batting .219. He is 1-2 with a 5.11 ERA in 11 games, including four starts, in his career against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Not since Mickey Lolich in 1971 had a Tiger racked up double-digit strikeouts in three straight starts until Verlander followed up back-to-back 11-strikeout games with a career-high 13 strikeouts Thursday at Minnesota, most by a Tiger in one game since 2004. But that's just the surface of Verlander's success this stretch. He has given up three runs on 16 hits over 29 1/3 innings in his last four starts while racking up 44 strikeouts, and he's poised to do more of the same against a free-swinging Rangers squad. He's 4-1 with a 2.23 ERA in six career outings against Texas, striking out 33 batters in 36 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison has pitched two straight complete games and has won four straight starts with a 1.80 ERA. In those four games, he has pitched 30 innings while striking out 18 and walking two. He has allowed two earned runs in his last 28 innings, He made his first start of the season against the Tigers at Comerica Park and allowed four runs on nine hits and five walks over 52/3 innings in a 4-3 loss.

home_pitcher_note: In the wake of Justin Verlander's four-start tear, Edwin Jackson has been turning in some quality performances of his own. Jackson has now worked seven innings in consecutive starts, giving up only one run during the stretch. In his last start Friday, he stayed loose through a one hour, 13 minute rain delay after the fourth inning to complete a seven inning, one run performance. The start before that, at Cleveland on May 4, Jackson pitched seven innings of shutout ball, striking out seven. He's now made it through the seventh inning in half of his eight starts, and his 2.42 ERA is the lowest of all Tigers starters.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 3-1 with a 3.81 ERA in his last four starts. He is 1-2 with a 3.81 ERA in four starts on the road. That includes a start in Detroit in the first weekend of the season when he threw seven scoreless innings against the Tigers before they rallied for six runs in the eighth inning against the bullpen. He is 4-4 with a 3.56 ERA in 12 career starts against the Tigers, including 2-1 with a 2.33 ERA in four starts at Comerican Park.

home_pitcher_note: The learning curve that Tigers manager Jim Leyland has talked about all season is starting to take shape for Porcello. The right-hander has won his last three starts after a six-inning, one-run performance Saturday, which Leyland called the rookie's best outing of the year. During that time, Porcello has given up only two runs in 18 innings, while striking out 13 and walking seven batters. Seven starts into his career, the 20-year-old Porcello said he's learning how to utilize his breaking ball and not always try to blow his fastball past batters.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's last start, Sunday against the Pirates, was less efficient than his recent work, but it's hard to argue with one run and seven strikeouts in six innings of work. It all was washed away when his bullpen and defense managed to give up 10 runs in the seventh inning. Nonetheless, the start was significant. Being tested because he didn't have his best fastball, Jimenez pitched off his secondary pitches and threw enough good fastballs in strikeout situations. He is 2-1 with a 2.00 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: While the three starters ahead of him surge, Galarraga continues to struggle in the No. 4 spot in the Tigers' rotation. In his last start, on Sunday, he didn't make it through the first inning, giving up five runs and recording only two outs. He has now given up at least five runs in four straight starts. With Jeremy Bonderman scheduled to make his second rehab start for Triple-A Toledo on Thursday, a rotation shakeup could be down the road. But manager Jim Leyland hasn't set any timetable for Bonderman's return nor given any indication of when a change might happen.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis is coming off his best outing of the season, an eight-inning effort in which he allowed just one run on five hits against the Braves on Monday. In that outing, Marquis threw 71 pitches through the first four innings, and then settled in to throw just 32 through the last five. That lower pitch count was due in part to the four double plays he induced from Braves hitters using an effective sinker. Marquis hasn't faced Detroit since 2002, when he was pitching for Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard for the Tigers to know how Willis will perform in the start after a win, because he's never done so in a Tigers uniform. It took 17 months and nine starts, but Willis finally recorded his first win as a Tiger on Tuesday, when he one-hit the Rangers through 6 1/3 innings, striking out five and retiring 17 straight batters at one point. Teammates saw a newfound serenity to Willis, who spent the first month of the season on the DL with an anxiety disorder. Now the challenge will be finding some form of consistency.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has pitched better on the road than at home this season, and it's quite possible his last start, a loss to the Braves, could have gone differently. Hammel went six innings and gave up six runs, but three were earned. No runs were in when second baseman Clint Barmes committed his second-inning error. Two of the subsequent hits that inning were of the infield variety. Hammel has no record but a 7.88 ERA, in four career games, one start, against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: There was some good news for Meche last Wednesday night. He went six innings against the Indians, left with a 4-2 lead, experienced no backache and finished with ample energy. His season had been dogged by intermittent back pain and then, on May 14 against the Orioles, by early-game fatigue. Meche changed his workout routine, did more running and had more stamina against the Indians. Still, the Royals opted to lift him after 87 pitches to avoid risking a relapse. However, the bullpen couldn't maintain the lead and the Royals lost, 6-5. This will be Meche's first turn against the Tigers this year; he's 8-4 against them in his career and went 2-0 last season in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: His double-digit strikeout streak came to an end at three starts, but Verlander didn't have a bad game by any means in his last outing against Texas. His six-inning, one-run performance dropped his ERA below 4.00 for the first time since July 2008. In his last five outings, he's 4-1 with a 1.02 ERA. Verlander credits his turnaround to better control over his breaking ball and a more focused approach toward opposing hitters: "They're the enemy, and I'm focused in on that. I'm going to do everything within my power to get these guys out and not let them beat us," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke's usually sharp command was off last Thursday against the Indians. He built up a pitch count of 103 through six innings and was lifted with a 3-2 lead, which the bullpen gave up. After a brilliant start to his season in which he was 6-0, Greinke feels he's not been at his best in his last three outings, which have resulted in one loss, one win and one no-decision. In the only inning in which the Indians scored, he lapsed into two-seam fastballs, hoping to get ground balls, instead of his usual four-seamers and ran into problems with movement. Count on him to correct that against the Tigers, a team he dominated, 6-1, in a complete-game three-hitter on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's last two starts have been anything but ordinary: he weathered a 1 hour, 20 minute rain delay in the first, and went for a career-high 132 pitches in the second. Over the stretch, he totaled 15 innings and earned the win both times. Manager Jim Leyland admitted after Jackson's last start Thursday that he would have to keep a close watch on the right-hander in his next start. If Jackson's outing here is limited against the Royals, that could put a strong onus on the Detroit bullpen, because Jackson is slated to face Zack Greinke, the Major League leader in ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Davies is coming off a good six-inning effort against the Cardinals. He held St. Louis to just three hits and two runs but lost because the Royals were shut out. Davies' command wobbled a bit in the first inning, when he gave up both of his runs, but he then retired 15 straight batters. Davies has had problems in the first inning that he needs to resolve his next time out. For the most part, he kept his pitches down in St. Louis on his way to picking up seven strikeouts. In his other start against the Tigers this year, Davies was hammered for seven runs in 5 1/3 innings, giving up two homers.
away_pitcher_note: Another win in this start would make Porcello the first Major League pitcher 20 years old or younger to win five straight starts since Dwight Gooden did so in 1985. As it is, Porcello is already just the sixth pitcher since 1900 to pitch four straight starts and allow one or no runs before his 21st birthday, joining the illustrious group of Kerry Wood, Fernando Valenzuela, Walter Johnson, Christy Mathewson and Chief Bender. None of those outings for Porcello came against the Royals, who beat him in Kansas City last month when the right-hander allowed four earned runs over six innings, including two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez will be the second Oriole in less than a week to make his big-league debut when he replaces the injured Koji Uehara. Hernandez struck out 13 batters in his last outing at Triple-A Norfolk and has posted a 3-1 record and a 2.91 ERA through eight starts. Hernandez led the Eastern League in strikeouts last year and currently ranks second in the International League in that category.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers and Galarraga continue to work on the issues that turned the team's Pitcher of the Month for April into a pitching mess for May. After going 3-0 in the opening month, he's 0-4 with a 9.92 ERA in his past five starts, having allowed 25 runs on 30 hits over 22 2/3 innings. He was somewhat better in his last outing on Saturday, allowing four Rockies runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings, but his crushing blow was a Todd Helton solo homer he allowed immediately after the Tigers tied the game.

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen had another erratic start in his last outing, holding the Nationals scoreless through four innings and allowing two runs in both the fifth and sixth innings. And that trend holds true for the rookie: In his last five starts, Bergesen has allowed 11 total runs in the first five innings and seven in the sixth or later. Bergesen has allowed at least three earned runs in all but one of his outings.
away_pitcher_note: After many wondered -- with good reason -- whether Willis would ever pitch for the Tigers again going into the season, Willis has laid the foundation to become a potential go-to starter heading into the summer. While his last outing couldn't match his 6 1/3 scoreless innings from his season debut, his quality start -- three runs allowed over 6 2/3 innings -- gave the Tigers at least a chance at a victory, even though Detroit's struggling offense couldn't convert. Willis has allowed 16 hits over his 17 2/3 innings, including only one home run, and he's been hitting the corners of the strike zone with relative consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie managed a return to form in his last start, when he braved a steady downpour and allowed just one earned run over seven innings. That was just the second time in 10 starts he had managed to hold a team to less than three runs, and the other time happened all the way back in his second start. Last season, Guthrie managed to allow two earned runs or less in 17 of his 30 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Though Verlander doesn't boast the season numbers of Zack Greinke, his performance over the past five weeks have given a similar boost to a Tigers team that has been carried by solid starting pitching so far this season. Verlander is 5-0 with a 0.85 ERA over his last six starts, the latest an easy win over the Royals on Memorial Day in which he struck out eight and walked none over seven scoreless innings. He's getting swings and misses from all of his pitches at this point, including a fastball that remains steady in the upper 90s when he needs it late in games. He'll take that dominant stuff and put it up against the Orioles, whom he has beaten three times without a loss in four career meetings to go with a 1.29 ERA and just 17 hits allowed over 28 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Berken won his first start thanks to some timely home runs by the Baltimore hitters. The right-hander allowed runs in each of the first two innings but settled down as the game wore on and escaped a bases-loaded jam in the fifth. Berken, who had been 2-0 with a 1.05 ERA at Triple-A Norfolk, will likely keep getting opportunities as long as he keeps his team in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson remains among the American League's top pitchers in terms of ERA, but a pair of wayward throws on his part set up two unearned runs that helped break up his duel with Zack Greinke on Tuesday at Kansas City. The three-run sixth inning overshadowed what was his fourth straight quality start, including 13 ground balls over 6 1/3 innings. He generally did not fare well against the Orioles during his tenure with Tampa Bay, going 2-4 with a 5.44 ERA in eight starts and three relief appearances, including 17 hits over 8 2/3 career innings at Camden Yards.

home_pitcher_note: How does Porcello follow up a 5-0 May? Continuing the unbeaten streak into June would be an impressive step. In addition to being the first Tigers pitcher since John Doherty in 1984 to win five or more games in a month, the impressive rookie has posted a 1.50 ERA during his current five-game winning streak. According to Elias Sports Bureau, that makes Porcello -- at 20 years, 151 days old -- the second-youngest pitcher in Major League history to go 5-0 with an ERA of 1.50 or better in any five-start span (the Mets' Dwight Gooden went 5-0 with a 1.43 ERA in five starts at age 19 in 1984). While the Tigers are thrilled with the production, they will remain cautious with the future rotation cornerstone. He's worked seven innings only once in his nine starts, a clear sign that the Tigers will take a conservative approach and not overwork him.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka tied a team record with four wild pitches in Wednesday's loss to the Twins at the Metrodome. Matsuzaka's control was obviously as issue, as he needed 102 pitches to get through five innings. He allowed three earned runs on nine hits and three walks while striking out six. He is still winless in four starts this season. Matsuzaka is 3-1 with a 2.81 ERA in four career starts against Detroit, including his only career complete game. Matsuzaka allowed one run in nine innings against the Tigers on May 14, 2007 in his eighth career start.

home_pitcher_note: Has Galarraga turned a corner? The Tigers certainly hope so, and though the right-hander has dropped five straight decisions, he finally put together a better effort in a 5-1 loss at Baltimore on Thursday. Galarraga surrendered 10 hits, but kept the Tigers in the game. Where he was battered in previous outings this season, Galarraga surrendered only two runs, on solo homers to Luke Scott and Nolan Reimold. The homers, however, continue to be a problem for Galarraga, who has allowed 11 this season after serving up 28 long balls last year.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett had another strong outing, this time against the Twins at the Metrodome on Thursday afternoon. The ace righty received the win by allowing only one earned run on three hits and four walks in seven innings while whiffing eight. The only run came on a Joe Crede solo homer. Beckett has only allowed three earned runs over his last three starts, covering 22 innings. Beckett is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers are wondering which version of Willis will show up -- the somewhat effective lefty who compiled a 3.57 through three starts after he was activated from the 15-day disabled list after being treated for an anxiety disorder, or the guy who threw batting practice to the Orioles on Friday. In a disastrous outing at Camden Yards, Willis surrendered seven runs on 10 hits over five innings and his ERA jumped almost two runs a game. Willis is at his best when his herky-jerky delivery makes it difficult for hitters to pick up pitches. But that only works when he has command of his pitches, something that deserted him against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: He was Boston's best starting pitcher for the first six weeks of the season. However, Wakefield has taken a downturn of late. The veteran knuckleballer has surrendered five runs or more in three of his last four starts. Most recently, Wakefield gave up nine hits and six runs over 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Blue Jays. Wakefield has struggled on the road this season, going 2-3 with a 5.70 ERA. Lifetime at Comerica Park, Wakefield is 3-3 with a 10.21 ERA in 10 appearances. Against the Tigers in his career, Wakefield is 15-10 with a 4.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander got a little roughed up in his last start, giving up nine hits in six innings -- including his first home run in more than a month -- and allowed three runs in the outing, as many as in his previous four combined. Yet he still earned the win, giving him a team-high six on the year, all of which have been in his last seven starts, and he continues to anchor the front of the Tigers' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Santana did not fare well in his last start, surrendering eight runs on 10 hits over just 5 1/3 innings against Seattle. He walked three, struck out two and watched his ERA soar to 9.50 following the start. Santana earned a no-decision in the outing though, as the Angels defeated the Mariners, 9-8.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson's career season is continuing in Detroit, where his 2.30 ERA is second in the American League behind Zack Greinke. His last outing may have been his best of the season: eight innings, two hits against the Orioles. And Jackson continues to be an "innings eater," as manager Jim Leyland calls him, going seven or more innings in four of his last five starts -- including his 132-pitch performance May 21 -- keeping the bullpen fresh for rookie Rick Porcello behind him in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday has been a long time coming for Escobar, who underwent right shoulder surgery last year. It will mark the first time he has pitched in a Major League game since Sept. 29, 2007, when he defeated Oakland for his career-high-setting 18th win of the season. In three Minor League rehab starts this year, Escobar has posted a 2.30 ERA across 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello descended from the stratosphere he occupied throughout May when he threw 4 1/3 innings, giving up seven hits and three earned runs in his last outing Tuesday. Before that, Porcello had won five straight starts, earning a 1.50 ERA over 30 innings. It wasn't a bad outing Tuesday, but Porcello said he struggled keeping the ball down in the zone, and he will look for better command of his sinker as he hopes to return to his previous form when he next takes the mound against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays in his last outing, Saunders endured a rocky start. The left-hander yielded six runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings. He picked up the loss, which was his second straight and third in four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Richard encountered his first rough outing in four starts on Wednesday in a 5-3 loss to the A's. He lasted 5 1/3 innings and surrendered five runs on seven hits -- including three solo home runs -- while striking out four and walking four. His ERA rose from 3.38 to 3.97. Richard had posted a 2.70 ERA in four starts since becoming the White Sox fifth starter on May 12. He appeared in relief on April 15 against the Tigers, allowing two hits and no runs in one-third of an inning.
away_pitcher_note: It's still unseen whether Galarraga has officially turned the corner on the 2009 season, but his last two starts have been encouraging. He went seven innings and gave up three earned runs in his start Wednesday, coming off a similar performance in his previous outing in Baltimore. He hasn't returned to the form of his rookie season, when he went 13-7 with a 3.73 ERA, but it's an improvement from the month of May, when Galarraga compiled five losses in six starts. For now, manager Jim Leyland will take that as improvement.

home_pitcher_note: White Sox manager Ozzie Guillen announced that Contreras would make his return to the team's starting rotation in the second game of a split doubleheader on Monday against the Tigers. Contreras struggled early in the season and opted to be sent down to Triple-A Charlotte last month rather than head to the White Sox bullpen so he could hone his pitches and return to the starting rotation at a later date. Contreras last pitched for the White Sox on May 8 in a 6-0 loss to the Rangers. In that game, he threw 3 2/3 innings, allowing six hits and five runs (three earned). On the season, Contreras is 0-5 with an 8.19 ERA. Over the last month in Triple-A, however, Contreras went 3-1 with a 2.73 ERA in five starts. He struck out 27 batters while walking 16.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman is making his first start since June 1, 2008 after spending more than a year on the disabled list following surgery to correct a blood clot. After four rehab starts, his velocity hasn't returned to where it was before his injury -- his fastball is topping out at 90 when it used to hit 95, so Bonderman said he expects to throw more changeups than ever before. Before the injury, Bonderman had a career 59-66 record and a 4.22 ERA in five-plus seasons with the Tigers, mostly as a starter. Manager Jim Leyland has said his role past Monday is still up in the air.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle may have taken his second loss in his last start, on Thursday against the A's, but it was also the second time this season that he lasted eight innings and just the second time he allowed more than three runs in a start. Buehrle has not faced the Tigers this season, but he has a 13-8 lifetime record against Detroit. Buehrle also holds a 70-40 career record with a 3.65 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Willis is coming off his worst start of the season, when he walked four batters and hit another in the third inning of Thursday's game against the Red Sox. He finished with an unusual line: 2 1/3 IP, 0 hits, 5 ER, 5 BB. But he said that control wasn't so much the problem, but rather that he was rattled by some questionable calls. That's notable because Willis spent the first part of the season on the disabled list with an anxiety disorder, and said Thursday was the first time all year he lost his composure.

home_pitcher_note: Danks labored through 5 2/3 innings in his last start on Friday against the Indians, a 6-0 loss. He struck out four, walked two and allowed six hits, but three of those hits were home runs, including back-to-back dingers in the sixth inning, which knocked him from the game. Against the Tigers, Danks is 2-1 in six career starts with a 4.00 ERA. He has struck out 32 batters in those starts while walking seven.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Jim Leyland said after Verlander's Friday start that he is now at his best he's seen him during his three-year career with the Tigers, and it's hard to argue otherwise. The 26-year-old won AL pitcher of the month honors for May, and started off his June with eight innings of shutout ball against the Angels. That game marked the fourth time this year he has thrown seven or more innings of shutout ball. Verlander now has a 1.12 ERA in his last eight starts, and has officially turned the corner after a subpar 2008 and a slow start to 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd continued his pitching brilliance of late, producing his fourth consecutive quality start in a 4-2 victory against the Indians. Floyd retired 12 straight batters between the second and sixth innings. He lasted 6 2/3 innings, allowing five hits, two runs (one earned) while striking out seven and walking one. Over his last four games, Floyd owns a 1.82 ERA with 31 strikeouts. In the process he has lowered his ERA from 7.71 to 5.35. Floyd has experienced great success in his career against the Tigers. He is 5-0 with a 3.88 ERA and 43 strikeouts in 10 starts. The 10 starts mark the most against any single opponent for Floyd.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson pitched perhaps his best start of the year Saturday in Detroit, finishing the complete game while giving up only one run. Over his last two starts, he has thrown 17 innings and given up only one run as he continues to hold on to the second-best ERA in the American League, at 2.16. What's more, Jackson continues to eat up innings, throwing eight or more innings in three of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Snell pitched well in six innings against the Astros in his last start, scattering eight hits and giving up three runs but receiving a no-decision. Snell is now winless in his past nine outings. He has faced the Tigers once in his career, giving up four runs on seven hits in a loss during the 2006 season.
away_pitcher_note: Most expect a 20-year-old breaking into a Major League rotation to have his ups and downs, and after being up for all of May -- when he went 5-0 with a 1.50 ERA -- Porcello has slowed down a bit, although not much. In his last two starts, Porcello is 0-1, having allowed seven earned runs in 9 1/3 innings. Tigers manager Jim Leyland cited some control problems in his most recent outing, but the rookie has still been impressive 11 starts into his career.

home_pitcher_note: After finishing at least seven innings in five consecutive starts, Duke lasted only six in most recent. The six runs allowed matched a season high for the lefty and his 11 hits allowed was just one shy of the most he's allowed this year. Duke also served up three homers in his last start after only giving up four in his previous 11 outings this year. Until Monday's outing, Duke had not given up multiple home runs in any game this season. This will mark Duke's first career appearance against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga might be more frustrated with his game right now than at any other point in this sophomore slump of his. He's seemingly turning a corner, as his three straight quality starts suggest, but his early-inning struggles and hit totals are baffling him -- including a bases-loaded escape with a run allowed in a 33-pitch opening inning Monday afternoon against the White Sox. If he can get command back on his sinker and avoid the untimely sliders that spin a lot and stay flat, it should make a difference in his mix of pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf is looking to break a four-start winless streak, including back-to-back no-decisions. In his last start, Tuesday night in Atlanta, he pitched six strong innings -- he said it was as well as he threw all year -- and left with the lead, but got a no-decision when the bullpen could not hold the lead in a 4-3 loss. He credited improved balance after having worked with pitching coach Joe Kerrigan. Ohlendorf has no record against Detroit and has only faced them once, last April 29, as a member of the Yankees. He threw 3 1/3 shutout innings, allowing one hit, walking one and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Willis hasn't won in four starts since his 6 1/3-scoreless-inning victory against the Rangers on May 19, but his ability to compete even in the toughest of situations has earned him a spot in Detroit's rotation over a struggling Jeremy Bonderman. He overcame five walks and five hits over five innings -- and a sore knee he injured trying to make a sliding tag at the plate -- to keep the Tigers in their game against the White Sox in his last start on Tuesday. By starting Sunday's series finale at Pittsburgh, Willis gets the upshot of helping his own cause by batting for the first time in his Tigers tenure.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright got some nice run support and was victorious against the Marlins on Wednesday despite throwing 121 pitches (75 strikes) -- his highest mark since April 26, 2008. Wainwright gave up four runs on 11 hits while walking three and striking out four to help St. Louis snap its five-game losing streak. It was the 27-year-old's sixth straight decision -- a stretch that has him 3-3 with a 2.68 ERA. Wainwright gave up a run in two innings during his only career appearance against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Wednesday's complete-game victory over the White Sox continued the Detroit ace's roll through opposing hitters over the past month and a half. His 7-0 record and 1.10 ERA over his past nine starts is the best stretch by a Tigers starter since Doyle Alexander in 1987. His 81 strikeouts in that stretch gave him 106 over 13 starts this season, making him the quickest Tigers starter to fan 100 since Mickey Lolich in 1969. Now it's the National League's turn to face him, which has never been a fair challenge -- he's 8-0 with a 2.30 ERA over 10 career starts in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's fastball hovered in the 90-91 mph range in his last game, against the Marlins. That's about five mph slower than he was accustomed to averaging last season. Add the fact that Wellemeyer had significant trouble against the Marlins and you have a situation worth monitoring, in the least. Wellemeyer struck out just one Marlin in six innings and gave up five runs and 11 hits. The little-used Ross Gload got to him for two home runs, accounting for three runs. But Wellemeyer came away thinking he kept the damage to a minimum, especially considering his velocity woes. The Tigers, with a better-than-average offense, figure to be a significant test for him.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's no-decision Thursday against the White Sox ended his string of quality starts at six over the past month, but it also showed another sign of progress from previous inconsistencies in Tampa Bay. His struggles getting into sync and Chicago hitters' patience cost him 99 pitches over five innings, but with two runs allowed, he avoided the kind of big innings that plagued him in years past. He's 1-3 with a 6.80 ERA over 13 games in Interleague Play, nine of them starts.

home_pitcher_note: Quietly, Pineiro continues to turn in one solid start after another. His strikeout totals are coming up a bit, while his walk and home run numbers stay down.
