For Omaha, he was 10-5 with a 3.32 ERA in 29 games (23 starts) and was named to the Pacific Coast League's postseason all-star team. With the A's last year, he faced the Tigers once and gave up three runs on five hits in one inning.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn's left knee was too sore for him to make his previous scheduled start, against the Rays last Saturday, so he'll now go on nine days' rest against the Royals. Washburn, who said he's been told there's cartilage damage and received a pain-killing shot on the knee last Wednesday, was also skipped once with the Mariners earlier this year. Since coming over in the trade, the 35-year-old is 1-2 with a 6.81 ERA in six starts. In his last outing, against the Rays on Aug. 31, the lefty gave up eight runs in 5 2/3 innings. Washburn is 8-6 with a 2.94 ERA in 19 career games (18 starts) against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: It essentially came down to Robertson and Armando Galarraga to see who would get the Tigers' final rotation spot. After Galarraga gave up six runs in 2 1/3 innings against the Rays on Saturday, Robertson became the guy. The 32-year-old has only made two starts this season, but those two were good ones, as he combined to give up just one earned run in 10 innings (a 0.90 ERA). He will be facing the Blue Jays on seven days' rest. Robertson's pitched six shutout innings in his last start, against the Indians, giving up four hits and walking two while striking out four. Robertson is 3-3 with a 5.00 ERA in 10 career games (seven starts) against Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: It appears as though Tallet will be in the rotation for the rest of the season after serving as both a starter (21 games) and as a reliever (12) this season. He was pressed into a starter's role early in the season because of injuries in the rotation. Tallet beat the Yankees in his previous start to end a five-game losing string, four as a starter. It was his first win since June 23. Against New York on Sunday, he allowed five runs in five innings and fell behind, 5-4, but the Blue Jays picked him up with an eight-run bottom of the fifth in a 14-8 win. He probably pitched better than the five runs showed. He gave up three in the third with the hardest-hit ball by Mark Teixeira that hit Tallet's left leg. Tallet was able to retrieve the ball and get the out at first. He said it should not affect him in his next start. He has pitched twice this season against the Tigers, as a reliever, and had a clean inning each time, with two strikeouts in the second outing.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson's competitive nature was in full swing in a victory against the Rays on Sunday. Opposing Wade Davis, who was making his Major League debut and gave up just one run in seven innings, the ex-Ray kept his team in the game before Brandon Inge rewarded him with a go-ahead grand slam in the top of the ninth. Jackson finished with three runs on six hits in eight innings. Going into the eighth, the 25-year-old -- who turns 26 on Wednesday -- had logged 106 pitches, but he pitched through the frame in order to keep it a two-run game and eventually qualify for the win. Jackson is 3-1 with a 2.33 ERA against the American League East this year, but he has just two wins in his past 10 road starts.
away_pitcher_note: As Richmond tries to earn a spot in next year's rotation and searches for his first win since June 24, he continues to be plagued by one bad inning. Against the Minnesota Twins on Monday it was the first, when his pitches found too much of the plate and he gave up five runs. After allowing a second-inning double, he retired 13 in a row and lasted six innings, giving up one more run in a 6-3 loss. The six earned runs were a career high. He is 0-5, 7.15 ERA, in his past seven starts. He missed most of July with biceps tendinitis but says that has not been a factor, but patches of poor pitch location have been the problem. He has not pitched against Detroit in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Though many expected Porcello to be ahead of the curve when he made the Tigers rotation out of Spring Training, few could have imagined he'd end up so critical to the Tigers' success this season when he made his Major League debut against the Blue Jays back on April 9 at Rogers Centre. He lost that game in part on a couple of wayward offspeed pitches, but he has been much more of a power pitcher lately, using his fastball early and often to set up his sinker. Another win would give Porcello the highest win total in a season by a pitcher age 20 or younger since Dwight Gooden won 24 in 1985.
away_pitcher_note: After two losses in a row -- to the Red Sox and the Yankees, respectively -- Romero earned a victory over the Twins on Tuesday despite falling behind 3-0 after three innings. He lasted 6 2/3 innings, allowed seven hits, three walks ands struck out four and benefited from Toronto's six-run sixth. With 12 victories, Romero is tied for third on the franchise's list for wins by a rookie. Left-hander Jeff Musselman had 12 in 1987. Romero still needs to learn to finish off hitters when he is ahead 0-2 or 1-2. He made his Major League debut against the Tigers on April 9 and earned the victory in a 6-2 game with six innings, seven hits, two runs, one home run, two walks and five strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander still has a chance at his first 20-win season, but he's more concerned with helping the Tigers' sew up a playoff berth. The way he's pitching, he's giving the Tigers their best chance to sew up an AL Central title down the stretch. He has given up two runs in 14 innings over his last two starts, but split the decisions at Tampa Bay and Kansas City thanks mainly to run support. His Opening Day loss at Toronto dropped him to 0-2 in as many career meetings with the Blue Jays, who have hit him for 14 runs on 15 hits over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the season with Toronto, Purcey was soon in Triple-A Las Vegas, where he finished the season 9-6 with a 4.46 ERA in 24 starts with 139 1/3 innings pitched. He was recalled after the Triple-A regular season ended. He has made five starts with Toronto this year but was demoted after his April 27 loss to the Texas Rangers. His first start of the season was against Detroit, a no-decision after going seven innings, allowing three runs, two earned, five hits and three walks with five strikeouts. Last year he was  3-6 with a 5.54 ERA in 12 starts with Toronto. The first-round Draft pick (16th overall) from Oklahoma in 2004 made his Major League debut against Detroit on April 18, 2008, and held the Tigers to two hits, one earned run, and seven walks in 4 1/3 innings in a no-decision as the Blue Jays lost 8-4.

home_pitcher_note: The good news from Washburn in his last start was that he was able to pitch through the soreness in his left knee, lasting five innings over 105 pitches while giving up three runs on seven hits to Kansas City in a no-decision. It wasn't feeling significantly better, Washburn said afterwards, but he was able to deal with it. He'll get a rematch with the Royals, but at Comerica Park, where he hasn't won in five starts since joining the Tigers via trade from Seattle at the July 31 nonwaiver deadline. He's 1-2 with a 6.64 ERA in seven outings overall with Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Tejeda has made two masterful starts, filling in for Gil Meche who's been out with a tired shoulder. Tejeda shut out the Angels for 5 1/3 innings and followed that by blanking the Tigers for six innings last Wednesday night. He had no decision against the Angels but earned the victory against the Tigers -- his first win as a starter since late last year. Previously this year Tejeda had worked out of the bullpen but now he's thrust himself into the rotation picture for the rest of this season and 2010. In his last 19 innings, he hasn't allowed a run and has 25 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Not only will Bonine fill in for the injured Armando Galarraga, who was going to fill in for injured Nate Robertson, Bonine is going to replace them in the Tigers rotation. Manager Jim Leyland says it's Bonine's spot for the final three weeks of the regular season. He opened the season in the Tigers bullpen, but spent most of the year in the rotation at Triple-A Toledo except for a spot start in Detroit July 24, when he threw six innings and allowed three runs to help the Tigers sweep a day-night doubleheader from the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: DiNardo made his Royals debut last Thursday and did a creditable job against the Tigers, holding them to two runs on seven hits and three walks in five innings. Helped by three double plays, he left with a 3-2 lead but had no decision. Basically, he takes over the spot left open by Brian Bannister, who is out with shoulder fatigue. A left-hander, DiNardo was Triple-A Omaha's Pitcher of the Year with a 10-5 record and a 3.32 ERA. He's appeared in 90 Major League games and made 30 starts after spending five years with the Red Sox and A's.

home_pitcher_note: While Jackson continues to eat innings for the Tigers, his once-stingy outings have had a little more offense, raising questions whether he's tiring down the stretch as he approaches the 200-inning mark for the first time in his career. His no-decision Saturday against Toronto saw him tie a career high with three home runs allowed, including one in each of his last two innings. Without much command of his secondary pitches, Jackson attacked Blue Jays hitters and eventually paid for it.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke was done in by poor run support once again on Friday. He dominated the Indians, but the Royals left too many runners on base and Greinke left with a no-decision. It was his eighth no-decision of the season and the sixth time he's given up one run or none without getting a win. He pitched seven innings, giving up a run on four hits with six strikeouts and no walks in all. Greinke continues to pitch well in his attempt to win the Cy Young award, but his team will need to give him more wins to bolster his case. He is 10-5 with a 2.62 ERA career against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing continued to impress since joining the Twins rotation, holding the A's scoreless for seven innings in his last outing. The left-hander scattered eight hits while striking out six. It was the third time in his six starts for the Twins that he has lasted seven innings.  Since joining the rotation full-time on Aug. 22, Duensing is 3-0 with a 1.74 ERA in five starts. He has not allowed a home run in any of those starts. Duensing will next face the White Sox. He is 0-0 with a 2.08 ERA in four appearances (two starts) vs. Chicago this season.
away_pitcher_note: Not only did Porcello's six quality innings of two-run ball Sunday make him the first Major League pitcher with 13-win season before his 21st birthday since Dwight Gooden in 1985, it continued his late-season roll at a time when many expected the 20-year-old to be running out of energy. He's 4-1 with a 3.40 ERA in nine starts since the start of August, and he's becoming more of a power pitcher with a fastball that tops out at 96 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun. By using the heater to set up his sinker, Porcello is giving hitters a different look, and they're struggling to adjust.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a win against Toronto, Pavano allowed three runs on six hits through six innings of work against his former Monday in a no-decision versus the Indians. On the hook for the loss late in the game, Pavano was bailed out by a six-run inning from the Twins offense. He avoided falling to 0-2 against Cleveland on the season. Pavano has been a Tiger killer during his career, going 4-0 lifetime against Detroit and 1-0 as a Twin.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is winless in his past two starts after being among the AL wins leaders into September, but it was a five-run sixth inning that cost him a chance at a victory Monday against the Blue Jays. He had been dominant up to that point, and still racked up nine strikeouts with no walks over seven innings, but paid for some secondary pitches that Toronto hitters tagged. Now the Tigers turn to their staff ace for a critical start against the second-place Twins, the one division opponent Verlander hasn't beaten this year. He's 1-4 in four starts against Minnesota since 2007. He gave up five runs over six innings in a matchup last month at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Baker had his shortest start since Aug. 19 on Tuesday against Cleveland, lasting just 5 1/3 innings while giving up three runs on five Indians hits. He had to battle just to make it that deep into the game, throwing 101 pitches while striking out five and walking a pair. The fourth inning did him in as Cleveland put up three runs to take a 3-1 lead. Baker didn't factor into the decision, a Twins win. He would have improved to 4-0 against the Indians this season. Baker has posted a 9.58 ERA in two games against Detroit this year, but didn't factor into the decision in either start.
away_pitcher_note: Just days after being scratched out of the rotation with pelvic inflammation, Robertson is back in a starting role, likely for the home stretch after Jarrod Washburn's troublesome left knee swelled up on him. Robertson's combination of fastball, slider and changeup worked wonders, relatively speaking, before his injury worsened, so the Tigers are hoping he can get back that form. He's 5-5 with a 4.08 ERA in 11 career starts at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey is coming off a pair of rough outings. He's given up 12 earned runs over 9 1/3 innings over his last two starts against the Rangers and Twins. Both of those starts came on extended rest, so perhaps working on a more routine schedule will help him in this start against the Tigers. Before this run of rough outings, Laffey had been perhaps the most consistent member of the Tribe rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After stingy pitching with a power fastball and biting slider for the first half of the season, Jackson is struggling with the slider a bit, leaving opponents to jump on his fastball for damage. He has allowed 21 earned runs on 37 hits over 31 1/3 innings in his last five starts. His ERA has risen a half-run in that span, from 2.86 on August 21 to 3.37 now. He'll try not simply to throw the slider now, but throw it with confidence against a hyper-aggressive Indians lineup. He's 3-0 with a 2.74 ERA in four starts against Cleveland this year, including two earned runs allowed over 11 innings at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing just one earned run through six innings in his previous two starts, Masterson struggled in his most recent starting nod against the A's, surrendering five runs on six hits and four walks while striking out six through just four innings. Masterson attributed his less-than-stellar outing to his inability to locate his sinker, which proved especially costly when it resulted in a three-run homer off the bat of Kurt Suzuki. Still adjusting to his role as a starter after playing the reliever role in Boston until being traded July 31, Masterson will look to bounce back against the Tigers. In two games (3 1/3 combined innings) this season, he has allowed just two hits and one walk while striking out six against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: For a 20-year-old rookie in just his second full season of professional baseball, the numbers on Porcello since August have been like a second wind -- a 3.51 ERA, .232 batting average against, and a .626 OPS in his last 10 starts. That includes six innings and three runs allowed in a defeat in his last outing on Friday at Minnesota, where his offense was held scoreless. That stretch run began with eight innings of one-run ball August 1 at Cleveland, where he returns.

home_pitcher_note: Carrasco, three starts into his Major League career, continues to give up big hits at bad times. He allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits with a walk and three strikeouts over six innings in a loss to the Royals on Sept. 13. Carrasco, a key starting pitching prospect acquired in the Cliff Lee trade, has now given up 15 earned runs in 14 total innings over three starts. He's been tagged for six home runs, as he's had trouble getting movement on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Don't let the numbers from his last outing fool you. Verlander took a one-run game into the eighth inning before a fly ball lost against the roof of the Metrodome for a double helped spring open a five-run Twins rally. Verlander hit 101 mph on his 127th and final pitch of that outing, a Jason Kubel bloop single that brought in two runs and extended Verlander's winless streak to three consecutive starts. He won't get an extra day of rest after throwing 128 pitches Saturday, so his pitch count might have to be watched closely.

home_pitcher_note: The high-profile acquisition at the non-waiver Trade Deadline certainly wasn't perfect, location-wise, in his first start since June 8 when he was facing Arizona with San Diego. But Peavy had good life on his fastball, topping out at 94 mph, and his slider had good bite during his first American League victory in his first AL start. Peavy worked five innings, throwing 47 of his 73 pitches for strikes, while giving up three runs on three hits and striking out five. He would have gone out for the sixth, but the White Sox rallied for four in the fifth, and the length of the inning caused Ozzie Guillen to replace Peavy. The right-hander will have one more start after this one on Wednesday at Progressive Field in Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers used Monday's off-day to skip Bonine's spot in the rotation, but he has two critical starts left to try to help pitch the Tigers to a division title. The first outing comes against the White Sox, whom Bonine quieted with a six-inning quality start in a spot assignment in July. Bonine earned a September callup with the Tigers as an extra reliever, but became a starter when injuries to Nate Robertson and Armando Galarraga forced manager Jim Leyland to adjust.

home_pitcher_note: Make it six straight quality starts for the right-hander, who held the Royals to two runs on five hits over eight innings on Sunday. Garcia also struck out three and walked one, needing just 94 pitches to complete the eight. Unfortunately for Garcia, the offense could not support him during a 2-1 setback, his seventh straight loss to Kansas City. Garcia, who pitched for the Tigers last year, has a 15-5 career record against Detroit with a 3.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The odd man out of the Tigers rotation at the end of Spring Training is a starter again just in time to provide Detroit with a left-handed boost. While his five innings with two runs allowed Sunday at Minnesota don't sound like a major accomplishment, the outing met the challenge of holding down the Twins offense long enough for the Tigers to pull ahead and salvage a game in a key series. His slider is back to resembling its old bite, and his control has rounded back into shape.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson pitched admirably in his first Major League start, but he did not receive any run support in a 7-0 loss against the Twins on Monday at U.S. Cellular Field. He made it through five innings, allowing three runs (one earned) on four hits with four strikeouts and four walks. The loss marked Hudson's first at any level since June 15, when he pitched for Class A Winston Salem -- a span of 14 starts. Hudson, who has only made four big league appearances overall, has never faced the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: If Jackson was tipping his slider, as pitching coach Rick Knapp suggested, he doesn't seem to be doing it anymore. Combine his strikeout pitch with a fastball that hit 98 mph last time out, and he has his early-season power arsenal back to throw at hitters for the stretch run and into the postseason. It's bad news for the White Sox, who beat Jackson during the Tigers' last trip to Chicago in June before giving him a no-decision in an extra-inning game in July at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Armed with a four-run lead before taking the mound, Porcello overcame early command issues to cruise to victory with five innings of one-run ball in his last start Wednesday at Cleveland. He improved to 5-2 with a 3.23 ERA over 11 starts since the beginning of August, scattering 56 hits over 61 1/3 innings. Rather than running out of gas in his first Major League season, he almost had too much energy in his last start, working at too quick of a pace for manager Jim Leyland's liking. Now, he gets a rematch with the Twins, who beat him despite a quality start Sept. 18 at the Metrodome.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn looked much more like the first half version of himself in his last outing. While the second half of the season has been rough for Blackburn, he’s started to turn things around of late and his best outing came in his last start in Chicago. The right-hander pitched seven scoreless innings, scattering eight hits and striking out six in the victory. Blackburn mixed in all of his pitches and the Twins were pleased by the number of offspeed pitches he used in the outing. The club hopes to see more of the same from Blackburn when he faces the Tigers in the series opener. Blackburn is 1-1 with a 5.11 ERA in two starts vs. Detroit this season.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander gets a rematch against a Twins lineup he dominated for seven innings before a fly-ball double lost against the backdrop of the Metrodome roof and a broken-bat bloop single on a 101-mph fastball helped set off a five-run eighth inning in a difficult Tigers defeat. This time, he'll have the night sky of Detroit in his favor, and a chance at tying his career high in wins. His win Thursday at Cleveland, however, showed that he can't afford to get too fastball-happy.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing received his first real test in the rotation during his last turn in Chicago. The left-hander was knocked out of the contest after 5 2/3 innings, having allowed four runs (three earned) on nine hits. He was removed from the game after giving up a two-run homer to Jermaine Dye that cut the Twins lead to one in the sixth. Still, Duensing remained undefeated (5-0) since moving to the rotation full-time last month. The Twins hope that Duensing will be a little better at keeping his pitches down in the zone when he starts in Detroit during that critical series. Duensing is 1-0 with a 0.61 in three appearances (one start) vs. the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bonine's final scheduled start of 2009 will be the biggest of his career, giving him a chance to swing the Tigers' AL Central showdown with Minnesota in his club's favor. Bonine's simple goal -- give the Tigers a chance to win. His 6 2/3 innings against the White Sox certainly did that, as he took a no-hitter into the sixth inning of a scoreless game before Gordon Beckham homered for the game's only runs in a 2-0 loss. If he can mix his knuckleball and changeup again while commanding his 90-mph fastball, he could well put up another stingy performance.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano continues to show why the Twins were right to add a veteran starter to their staff. The right-hander picked up his second win in his past four starts, holding the Royals to four runs on eight hits over six innings. While it wasn't the prettiest of starts for Pavano, he only was hurt in two at-bats -- both resulting in home runs by Billy Butler. While the Twins needed Pavano against the Royals, they'll really need him to continue his season-long success against the Tigers. Pavano is 4-0 with a 1.69 ERA in five starts vs. Detroit this season, and he's 3-0 with a 1.61 ERA in the three starts that have come at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Which Robertson will show up in his final start of the regular season? Is it the veteran left-hander who used a biting slider and solid fastball to hold the Twins to two runs on five hits over five innings at the Metrodome two starts ago? Or is it the one with a flat slider and inconsistent command who struggled to five runs, four earned, on six hits in 3 1/3 innings last time out on Saturday at Chicago before the Tigers came back? How well Robertson commands his arsenal in the series finale could determine whether the AL Central remains a race into the season's final weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to quite a bit of offensive support, Baker was able to pick up win No. 14 of the season in his last start at Kansas City. Baker allowed four runs over 6 1/3 innings to the Royals as the Twins delivered a total of 11 runs in the blowout victory. The right-hander settled down for the middle of his outing at Kauffman Stadium, retiring a string of 13 straight batters after giving up back-to-back solo homers to start the second inning. The tests only get tougher for Baker, who will be the final pitcher in the Twins' critical four-game series with the Tigers. He's 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in three starts vs. Detroit this season.

home_pitcher_note: Just when Jackson seemed to be out of his September slump, on came the White Sox in the sixth inning Sunday for three straight extra base hits and three runs to take the lead. He ended up with five runs allowed over 6 1/3 innings to raise his September ERA to 5.08. His challenge to start October will be to make the adjustments to quiet the White Sox in the rematch at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night, Peavy outdueled Tigers pitcher Eddie Bonine, who took a no-hit bid into the sixth inning before surrendering a two-run home run to Gordon Beckham. On most nights, Bonine's effort would have been good enough, but Peavy completely shut down Detroit, allowing no runs on six hits in seven innings while striking out eight. It was Peavy's second successive victory since joining the White Sox rotation, and he owns a 2.25 ERA in those two outings. Peavy will be making his final 2009 start on six days rest.

home_pitcher_note: With Monday's rainout pushing back Rick Porcello to the point where he couldn't pitch Saturday on his regular rest, Figaro will make a one-time return to the rotation for what could be a critical next-to-last game of the regular season. He hasn't started at any level since he took the loss June 28 at Houston, a week after he won his Major League debut with five effective innings and seven strikeouts against the Brewers. Still, his 2 2/3 innings of relief last Saturday against the White Sox showed he has his stuff back after missing the better part of two months with a sprained right wrist. He's a high-strikeout hurler with a fastball in the mid-90s, but he has to mix in his breaking ball effectively to make things work.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia appeared on his way to producing his seventh consecutive quality start on Saturday night, until he hit a road block in the seventh inning against Detroit. He entered the frame holding a 5-3 lead but allowed singles to four of the five batters he faced in the inning. By the time the inning ended, Detroit had turned a two-run deficit into a two-run lead, and Garcia was saddled with the loss. He lasted 6 1/3 innings, allowing seven runs on 10 hits with three strikeouts. Garcia lost to Detroit for the first time since Sept. 2, 2005, a span of eight starts. Lifetime against the Tigers, he is 15-5 with a 3.63 ERA in 24 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander's 129 pitches likely ruled out any chance of starting on short rest for Saturday, but he should still be able to take the ball for the regular-season finale. He missed out on a quality start Tuesday night against the Twins, but his eight innings and four runs allowed held onto what was once a five-run lead and might have saved Detroit's division lead.
away_pitcher_note: During Monday's 6-1 victory over the Indians at Progressive Field, Danks accomplished two personal goals. The left-hander hurled his first complete game as a professional, and he set a single-season high in victories at 13 -- a total that figures to lead the White Sox in 2009. Danks will make one more start in search of another goal, which is reaching 200 innings pitched in 2009. Danks enters the game against the Tigers needing 4 2/3 innings to reach that target for the first time in his three-year career. Danks is one of just three pitchers in the history of the White Sox to make 25 starts in each of his first three seasons with the team. He has a 0-1 record against Detroit this season.

home_pitcher_note: Baker will go for the Twins in game No. 163 against the Tigers in a game that will decide the AL Central champion. It will be the right-hander's second crucial game against Detroit in as many starts, as Baker also faced the Tigers Thursday to help the Twins split the four-game series. In that start, Baker picked up the win by pitching five innings, allowing only one unearned run. He's been Minnesota's strongest pitcher during the second half of the season, going 12-4 since July 12. He is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in four starts against the Tigers this season.
away_pitcher_note: The AL Central tiebreaker between the Tigers and Twins will be unlike any of Porcello's previous 30 starts this season. He has pitched in high-pressure situations like Fenway Park in midsummer, Busch Stadium in a big Interleague Play matchup, and the Metrodome a few weeks ago to start Detroit's key three-game series there. Still, the last time Porcello pitched in a true win-or-go-home situation was likely high school. "I'm sure he's pitched in a tough environment," manager Jim Leyland said, "but I doubt that 50 scouts down the right-field line freezing their tails off in New Jersey somewhere is going to be like this." Porcello has two quality starts in as many tries against the Twins over the past 2 1/2 weeks, but he received two runs of offensive support in those two games combined. At the Metrodome this season, he is 0-2 and allowed seven earned runs in 10 innings.

summary: 2010-03-29 - Detroit Tigers @ Toronto Blue Jays (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Bush, the Brewers' No. 4 starter, will be making his final start of Spring Training. Bush has allowed 10 runs -- nine earned -- in 18 2/3 innings this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello, who won 19 games during his rookie season in 2009, has allowed six runs -- three earned -- over 18 innings this Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke makes his first Opening Day start and his first Kansas City appearance since winning the AL Cy Young Award in 2009. He spent Spring Training adding polish to the changeup that he added last year, which served him so well. Expect him to rely, too, on his formidable fastball and slider with an occasional curve. Excellent control is his forte -- last year he had 242 strikeouts against just 51 walks. Greinke has more victories over the Tigers than any other club, going 11-5 in 22 games with a 2.50 ERA. Last year he was 3-1 with a 1.00 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Six months after pitching the Tigers into a first-place tie with the Twins in Game 162, and two months after signing a five-year contract to stay in Detroit, Verlander has the tall task of pitching opposite Zack Greinke as he tries to get the Tigers off to a good start. Verlander, however, is treating it as another start, business as usual for the highly competitive right-hander, who will begin his fifth full Major League season with his third straight Opening Day start. His 9-2 career record and 2.32 ERA against the Royals includes two wins in three outings against them last season.

home_pitcher_note: This No. 2 spot in the rotation was supposed to belong to Gil Meche, but he's been delayed by a shoulder concern. Though Hochevar has been around for two years, this is the first time he's broken camp with the Major League club. This is a pivotal year for Hochevar, who has shown occasional brilliance but has developed no pattern of consistency. In his final 13 starts last year, he was 1-10 with an 8.21 ERA. When he keeps his sinking fastball low and throws strikes, he can be tough. Hochevar has faced Detroit four times and is 1-2 with a 6.87 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer's first start as a Tiger will come in his home state, not far from where he starred at the University of Missouri and became a highly-touted first-round pick of the Diamondbacks.  Detroit acquired him last December in the trade for Edwin Jackson, whom Scherzer essentially replaces in the Tigers rotation. Detroit needs not only quality starts from the 24-year-old, but also deeper outings than he had with the Diamondbacks last year. It's a big task for Scherzer as he begins his second full Major League season, but the Tigers believe the intensely competitive Scherzer is up to the challenge with his combination of power fastball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister missed the final month of last season because of shoulder fatigue, so he spent the winter working on exercises that would prevent that this year. He's also changing his approach, keeping the ball down in an effort to transform himself from a fly-ball pitcher who gives up a lot of home runs to a ground-ball pitcher. Bannister believes he made progress on that during last season and in Spring Training this year. This is an afternoon game, and Bannister's record in daytime games is 17-8, compared to 13-30 at night. Against the Tigers he's 4-2 with a 2.09 ERA in six career games.
away_pitcher_note: What seemed like a pie-in-the-sky scenario going into Spring Training became reality when Willis beat out Nate Robertson for a spot in the Tigers' season-opening rotation. Thus, after two seasons lost to injuries, pitch command and anxiety disorder, Willis gets a chance to prove he has made it back from the career-threatening control woes that plagued him. He put up a surprisingly solid Spring Training by corralling his once-wild delivery, pounding the strike zone and getting the movement on his pitches to force opponents mishit the ball. How much time has Willis missed? In two seasons as a Tiger, the D-Train has never faced the Royals, who play Detroit 18 times every season.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit's annual spring party, the home opener at Comerica Park, will feature the front-line starter who just recently turned 21. Porcello's Spring Training performance seemingly defied the idea of a sophomore slump looming. If anything, he looks physically bigger and stronger than he did as a rookie, and appears ready to use that to his advantage. He allowed just three runs on 11 hits over his 18 spring innings. More importantly, he showed an eagerness to find a middle ground between the sinkerball pitcher he was for the first half of last season, and the power pitcher who used a straight fastball to wear down hitters over the stretch run. Porcello went 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA in four starts against Cleveland last year.
away_pitcher_note: Huff was the Tribe's leader with 11 wins last season, but that didn't ensure him a rotation spot this year. He had to earn one in Spring Training. Huff had an inconsistent spring camp, at times struggling to find the strike zone, but he finished strong. The Indians see room for improvement from Huff, who, in his rookie year, had a 5.61 ERA, .301 average against and a 1.56 WHIP. But they also see big upside, as Huff went 4-1 with a 2.18 ERA over his last five starts of the 2009 season. Huff was in the Indians' rotation from mid-May through the end of last season, but he never came across the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: While Dontrelle Willis' comeback from two lost seasons attracted some well-deserved attention nationally, Bonderman's return from two injury-plagued campaigns means just as much to Detroit's fortunes. He seemed on his way to stardom in 2006 before an ERA jump in 2007 and then circulation problems in 2008 threw his career into question in just his mid-20s. Now 27, he still doesn't have the old strength in his arm or the same life in his fastball, but his workhorse slider is back and his willingness to throw an offspeed pitch is stronger than ever. Bonderman went 1-1 with a 6.92 ERA in five spring outings, but more than half of his damage came in two-thirds of an inning against Toronto in early March.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians acquired Talbot in the December trade that sent Kelly Shoppach to the Rays. His path to the big leagues with the Rays was blocked, and he's out of Minor League options. The Indians are giving him this shot in the rotation based on his 13-win seasons at Triple-A Durham in 2007 and '08 and his strong performance in spring camp. Talbot has four effective pitches, with his changeup getting the most rave reviews. He pitched briefly for Tampa in 2008, but this will be his first real exposure to life as a Major League starter. He gave up five runs in 2 1/3 innings in a relief appearance against the Tigers in '08.

home_pitcher_note: Though a pair of two-run innings denied Verlander a chance at an Opening Day victory and chased him out after five innings, he retired 10 straight Royals in between and felt like he finally found the rhythm he was struggling to locate during Spring Training. His fastball registered at 100 mph, surprising even for him in his first outing of the year, and he would be happy to take that stuff into his first home start of the season against the Indians, whom he beat four times in as many starts last year after going 1-5 against the Tribe in 2008. He went 10-2 with a 2.81 ERA at Comerica Park in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook made his first start in nearly two years when he got the Opening Day nod against the White Sox on Monday, and he showed every bit of the rust that no doubt accumulated in that time. Westbrook went just four-plus innings, allowing five runs on five hits with four walks, a strikeout, a home run, two hit batters and four wild pitches. The wild pitches tied a club record for a single game. But Westbrook said he enjoyed being back on the Major League mound nearly two years after Tommy John surgery, and he's eager to find his old form. He is 4-8 with a 6.05 ERA in his career against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Other than the fact that he didn't get a victory, Scherzer's first start as a Tiger couldn't have gone much better. He took a no-hit bid into the fifth inning and ended up with six innings of one-hit scoreless ball, stranding the bases loaded in the fifth with a called third strike on an inside fastball. He'll get a rematch against the Royals for his first Detroit start, this one a day game in what should be better conditions than the chilly downpour he countered in Kansas City that left him working to keep a solid grip on the ball.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar got off to a strong start in the season's second game, also against the Tigers. He pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings while giving up five hits and one walk. His sinker kept the Tigers whacking the ball into the dirt; he got 16 ground-ball outs and that included three double plays. Hochevar even managed to stop Miguel Cabrera, who came into the game with eight straight hits against the right-hander. Cabrera went 0-for-3 against him this time. Although the bullpen blew a 1-0 lead and Hochevar had no decision, the Royals did win in the 11th, 3-2. His career record against the Tigers remains 1-2 with his ERA lowered to 4.85 in five games.

home_pitcher_note: Though Willis didn't earn the win in his season debut last Thursday at Kansas City, his six innings of two-run ball earned him a measure of respect for the work he has put in to come back into the big league fold. He'll try to duplicate a lot of those same qualities in the rematch against the Royals at Comerica Park, where he earned his only Major League win last year with scoreless work against the Texas Rangers. Much like his Spring Training starts in Lakeland, Fla., a supportive crowd and a comfort level should help him on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: The schedule is playing right into Bannister's hands. This is his second start and both have been afternoon games. It's well known that he's a day tripper. His career record in 34 day games is 17-8 with a 4.08 ERA; in night games, it's 13-30 with a 5.13 ERA. Last Thursday afternoon, Bannister also went against the Tigers and held them to one run in six innings before the bullpen blew his 2-1 lead and lost the game, 7-3. As Bannister pointed out, the numbers were good, but he really wasn't satisfied because he didn't keep the ball on the ground enough. In fact, only two of his 18 outs were on the ground. Bannister is in the second year of a campaign to change his image from a fly-ball pitcher who gives up a lot of home runs to a ground-ball pitcher who doesn't. He hopes to do better this time.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello doesn't look rattled very often, so the fact that Cleveland hitters brought that out of him in the Tigers' home opener last Friday should say something about the emotions that built up inside of him. He has a much better chance of settling down for the end of the Tigers homestand, facing a Royals squad that actually roughed him up a little bit last year with 10 earned runs on 15 hits allowed over 18 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davies made his 2010 debut against the Red Sox last Friday night and did well enough -- one bad inning among his six. Three hits were turned into three runs, thanks mainly to a monster home run by J.D. Drew. Facing a club that likes to work the count, Davies did a good job of harnessing what for him has been on-and-off command, particularly of his fastball. He walked just one and 55 of his 89 pitches were strikes. There's no doubt that Davies has great stuff but he's a right-hander who has just never found consistent success. Davies considers his changeup his second-best pitch and he feels it gives him a lot of success against left-handed hitters. Last year, for example, he held lefties to a .239 average versus .284 by righties. The Tigers' big guns, though, are right-handed and Miguel Cabrera has hit .308 with three home runs and Magglio Ordonez .364 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Two starts into the season, the ace right-hander is still looking for his first win and he might have to pitch a shutout to get it. Though both of his outings so far, against the Athletics and Rangers on the road, have been quality starts, King Felix has yet to celebrate after a game the way he did at the end of last season, when he reeled off 15 wins in his final 17 decisions. The only glaring statistic on Hernandez's ledger so far is the walk-strikeout ratio. Through 13 2/3 innings, he has issued seven free passes and struck out nine.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman marked his return to the Tigers rotation last Saturday with five innings of one-hit, one-hit, one-run ball. He used his combination of his trademark slider and his newly-developed splitter to near-perfection, not to mention the kind of swings and misses he couldn't produce as often the past couple years while he tried to deal with decreased velocity. He'll try to repeat his success in his home state of Washington against a Mariners squad that has struggled offensively early on.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty from Australia is coming off a confidence-boosting outing against the Athletics. Though tagged with the loss in Seattle's home opener at Safeco Field, Rowland-Smith surrendered just three hits over seven innings. However, he also walked five batters, including the first three batters in the fourth inning, which led to a run. He's not a strikeout pitcher -- two in 12 innings this season -- so he must throw quality strikes consistently and put the ball in play. Rowland-Smith has started two games against the Tigers and received no-decisions in both. He has a 5.13 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: In many ways, Verlander's start to this season closely resembles his first month of last season -- potentially dominant stuff but inconsistent command of his secondary pitches, leaving him struggling to finish off hitters in tight spots. He had an encouraging sign against the Mariners in April of last season, despite a big inning, and he's hoping to find his first win of the year in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: A death in the family forced the right-hander to leave the team for a few days and return to his offseason home in Florida, but he's expected to make his third start on schedule. Snell is coming off a rocky outing, lasting just three innings against the Rangers, but manager Don Wakamatsu attributed some of that to the personal issues that were tugging at him. Snell is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: After the Royals put up better approaches at the plate against Scherzer in their second meeting, Scherzer gets an opponent he has never faced in Seattle. A foul ball dropped by Miguel Cabrera extended the fourth inning for the Royals on Monday, and they pounced on Scherzer with a two-run homer from Jose Guillen. Errors, combined with nine Royals hits, forced 101 pitches out of Scherzer over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro followed a so-so debut at home with a brilliant performance on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium, holding the Yanks to one run across seven innings on five hits and no walks while striking out seven, including Alex Rodriguez three times. Pineiro was in command from the outset, retiring 10 of the first 11 men he faced with his two-seam fastball getting exceptional bite, complemented by his changeup and slider. Pineiro has enjoyed success against the Tigers, going 6-2 with a 2.66 ERA in 11 career appearances, nine as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: While the erratically wild Willis form of the past couple years seems to be gone, his pitching remains a work in progress as he tries to build his confidence and, in turn, his velocity. He hit 95 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun in his last outing Tuesday against the Royals, but did it during an opening-inning escape in which he loaded the bases with two walks and a single before holding Kansas City scoreless. He ended up giving up two solo homers and a two-run ground-ball single in his five-inning defeat. His first-inning command will be worth watching as he tries to start in form rather than in search of it.

home_pitcher_note: Wanted: one missing slider. Kazmir couldn't find it Thursday night in New York, throwing only a handful of ineffective breaking balls in a season debut delayed by shoulder stiffness. The Yankees eventually teed off on his fastball and changeup, unloading seven extra-base hits while producing six earned runs in four innings. Kazmir's fastball was in the low 90s -- not as explosive as he'd like, but not bad - and his changeup was inconsistent. He needs all three of his deliveries to be effective.  Kazmir is 2-4 with a 4.69 ERA in eight career outings against the Tigers, and the former Rays ace is looking for his first career win at Angel Stadium. He's 0-2 in four starts with a 3.16 ERA in his new home park.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts into his second season, it's too early to tell whether Porcello is encountering a sophomore slump, but his struggles with hits and pitch counts suggest he's at least in a learning process in how to mesh his sinkerball that served him so well early last season with the power fastball that carried him through the stretch run. Now he'll go up against an opportunistic Angels lineup that can turn little innings into big ones. He had a no-decision in his only start against the Angels last year at Comerica Park, giving up two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver enhanced his credentials as the staff ace with another strong effort in Toronto on Friday night, moving to 24-14 in his career following an Angels loss by holding the Blue Jays to two solo homers across seven innings. Weaver was in command from the start, yielding five hits and walking none while striking out eight hitters. Fastball command is always the key for the cross-firing right-hander, who mixes in a quality slider and changeup. Weaver is 2-2 with a 7.36 in five career starts against the Tigers and is 28-12 with a 3.26 ERA in 55 outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman's last start read almost like two separate outings -- one batter reaching base safely the first time through the Mariners batting order, then only one out the next time through. He finished with 10 runs, eight earned, allowed on nine hits over four innings with four walks and four strikeouts, having used 93 pitches in the process as he tried to recapture the form that allowed him to work so easily through the lineup early. His splitter-slider combination has helped produce a strikeout per inning, but he'd trade some of those for quick outs and less damage. He's 3-3 with a 4.67 ERA in 10 career starts against the Angels, including 7 1/3 quality innings with seven strikeouts during a start in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: On the heels of two disheartening performances, Saunders put it all together in Toronto, throwing strike after strike across eight superb innings. He yielded two unearned runs on five hits and no walks, striking out two men. Pounding the strike zone, the lefty got six first-pitch outs and even threw a strike to second to pick off a baserunner. Saunders is 1-1 with a 5.18 ERA in seven career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is winless through his first three starts for the third consecutive season, and he went through four starts without a win the last couple years. He's hoping he can avoid that fate this time around, and he has the encouragement of his secondary pitches in his favor. He couldn't command his fastball last time out Saturday against the Mariners, but he mixed curveballs and changeups early and often in the counts to hold Seattle to three runs on seven hits over seven innings with six strikeouts and gave the Tigers their deepest outing by a starting pitcher this year. He's 1-2 with a 4.82 ERA for his career against the Angels, the lowest win total he owns against any American League opponent, but over just six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harden lasted just 3 2/3 innings in a 5-2 loss to the Yankees on Sunday. He faced 23 batters and 13 reached base on five hits, six walks and two hit batters. It was the first time in his career he hit two batters in a game. In three starts, he has struck out 15 and walked 14. Opponents are hitting .234 off him but with a .424 on-base percentage. Harden said he needs to do a better job of getting ahead of hitters right from the beginning. He is 3-2 with a 3.47 ERA in six career starts against the Tigers. In 23 career starts, Harden is 8-5 with a 3.35 ERA in 23 games in April.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer turned his fastball command into six quality innings against the Mariners on Sunday just when the Tigers needed it, helping them end a three-game losing streak and helping himself earn his first victory in a Detroit uniform. It was an encouraging sign for the Tigers, who are looking to Scherzer to fill a critical void in the rotation in his second full Major League season. He threw six innings of two-run ball with seven strikeouts against the Rangers in a start last year, numbers he would like to duplicate against an aggressive Texas offense.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman lasted just 2 1/3 innings in his last start, against the Yankees, allowing four runs on seven hits and two walks. It matched the shortest outing of his 59 Major League starts. In his first three starts, left-handed hitters are batting .414 off Feldman, while right-handers are hitting .189. He has given up eight of his nine runs in the first three innings. The last time Feldman went just 2 1/3 innings in a start was against the Tigers on July 29, 2009. He allowed six runs on 10 hits and two walks in a game the Rangers lost, 13-5, at the Ballpark in Arlington. Overall, he has an 8.82 career ERA against the Tigers, his highest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: Thomas gets the start in place of Dontrelle Willis, who was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness. In four appearances (no starts) this season entering Saturday, Thomas had a 7.04 ERA across 7 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis allowed three runs in five innings in his last start against the Red Sox on Tuesday. He left with a 6-2 lead, but the Red Sox rallied for a 7-6 victory. Lewis walked two, struck out five and threw 105 pitches. He has now walked 10 in 17 1/3 innings. He walked 19 in 176 1/3 innings in Japan last year. Opponents are hitting .206 off Lewis, including .222 by left-handed hitters and .185 by right-handed hitters. They are 1-for-15 against him with runners in scoring position. Lewis was with the Tigers organization in 2006, making 24 starts at Triple-A Toledo and two relief appearances for the Tigers at the Major League level. Lewis is 5-0 with a 3.75 ERA in his last seven starts and two relief appearances at the Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Three starts into Porcello's second Major League season, success has been anything but easy, reminding many that even with a big league campaign under his belt, he's still a 21-year-old right-hander learning the game at this level. His sinker, the pitch that earned him a plethora of groundouts and efficient innings last year, has been less consistent so far this year, and it has cost him in the hit column, including 18 hits and nine earned runs over 10 1/3 innings in his last two starts. However, it's easy to forget that he owned a 6.23 ERA in four April starts last year. Porcello has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison lasted just four-plus innings in his last start against the Red Sox on Wednesday, allowing six runs on five hits and three walks. He was given a 4-0 lead and couldn't hold it, allowing three home runs. One of them was a grand slam by J.D. Drew. The Rangers are 0-3 in his three starts. He has now made 29 starts for the Rangers over the past three years and is 13-9 with a 5.60 ERA. He is 7-4 with a 5.52 ERA in 16 starts at the Ballpark in Arlington. He is 0-2 with a 7.59 ERA in two starts against the Tigers in his career. Both starts came last year.
away_pitcher_note: After searching for his old form in his first two outings of the year, his last start looked more like the Bonderman fans remember. After giving up three runs within five batters of his outing, Bonderman allowed a lone infield hit among his next 19 batters. He commanded his fastball and slider down in the strike zone much better than he had in his previous start, and he worked with catcher Alex Avila to induce some key outs with his new-found splitter. If he can continue that kind of pitching, he has a chance to be a workhorse kind of pitcher at the back end of Detroit's rotation. Bonderman is 2-1 with a 4.71 ERA in six career starts against the Rangers, but hasn't pitched in Texas since 2004.

home_pitcher_note: If the parallels between this year and Verlander's outstanding 2009 season ring true, as they seemingly have so far, this should be the start where Verlander's season turns for the better. He struggled through his first four starts last year, including outings in Seattle and Anaheim, before finding the form that dominated hitters for the next five months. The hitch to that theory is that Verlander admits he has mechanical issues he needs to work out in order to find his command, and that could take longer than a few days. He earned his first win of the season on Thursday against the Angels, but he needed 125 pitches over five innings to do it, something no Major League pitcher had done in a victory since 1997.
away_pitcher_note: Early on this season, Liriano has given the Twins glimpses of the pitcher who dominated the American League during his 2006 rookie season and was once considered one of the up-and-coming starters in the game. A little over three years removed from Tommy John surgery, Liriano is starting to trust his stuff once again. He's beginning to locate his fastball and use it to then set up his nasty slider and strong changeup. It's allowed the left-hander to get off to a strong start and look on the verge of perhaps becoming the Twins' top starter again. He'll have to continue the trend and next up is a test against the Tigers. Liriano is 3-1 with a 4.76 ERA in 11 career appearances (seven starts) against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer gave the Tigers exactly what they needed in his last start Friday against Texas, even if Detroit lost, 5-4. He went seven innings, helping provide a break for a bullpen that is pitching more than three innings per game. Scherzer has 17 strikeouts and seven walks in 24 innings. He has given up three home runs. He has been the Tigers' most consistent starter so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker called his last start one of the "best-worst" outings of his career. In other words, the right-hander felt like he had really good stuff against the Indians but it didn't deliver the results he wanted. Baker allowed six runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings. Twins manager Ron Gardenhire felt that Baker left a few too many pitches up against an aggressive swinging Indians ballclub and that it was something he could improve upon his next time out. Baker will get that chance when he faces the Tigers in Detroit.  He is 3-1 with a 3.76 ERA in six career games at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Willis missed Saturday's start against Texas with flu-like symptons. He came back still under the weather to pitch an inning in relief on Sunday, walking three and giving up a two-run single in an inning. Manager Jim Leyland wasn't going to make Willis go much further than that, wanting to get him a tuneup for Thursday. Willis' biggest problem in his comeback season this year has been his command. He has 10 walks in 18 innings. He also has allowed 21 hits, a recipe for having the 5.00 ERA that he takes into his start against a Minnesota team he's faced once in the last three-plus seasons, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano got some redemption in his second straight start against the Royals. After giving up seven earned runs on 11 hits in just 3 1/3 innings against Kansas City at Target Field to pick up his first loss of the year, Pavano rebounded in the series opener at Kauffman Stadium. The right-hander allowed just two runs on four hits over seven innings, throwing first-pitch strikes to 21 of the 24 batters he faced. Still, Pavano was critical of himself after the contest, feeling he got into too many 2-1 and 3-2 counts. It's something he wants to work on his next time out. Pavano will next face the Tigers, a team he had a lot of success against in 2009. He was 4-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts vs. Detroit last season, three of those wins coming in four starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Sophomore slump or not, Porcello has some issues to work out with his mechanics, tweaks to try to put the sink back in his sinker and limit the kind of damage he has experienced in his past few starts. He allowed six runs on 10 hits over four innings last Sunday at Texas, and he has given up 12 runs on 18 hits over 8 1/3 innings in his past two starts. Though some of his pitch selections are up for debate, it's tough to question that his sinker hasn't been as effective this year. Porcello and coaches were looking over video after his last start to determine if he has dropped his arm angle and flattened out his pitches in turn.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers are hoping they have the same success the second time around against Pineiro that the Yankees enjoyed on Saturday. The sinker-ball artist coughed up as many runs (four) in Saturday's first four innings as he had in his first 20 1/3 innings in an Angels uniform, covering three starts. One of those was a blanking of the Tigers through 7 1/3 innings at Angel Stadium on April 19. Pineiro's success hinges on keeping his sinker down in the zone and complementing it with a quality slider and changeup. He's dominated the Tigers in Detroit, going 3-0 in three appearances with a 1.45 ERA. Overall, he's 7-2 in 12 games with a 2.40 ERA against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The main obstacle holding back Bonderman from an encouraging return this year has been the big inning, whether it's in his first inning or his second time through the order. He worked through three solid innings Monday at Texas, protecting a big early lead, but was chased after three hits, a walk and two runs in the sixth. His splitter has become a better pitch than many would have expected, especially potent when paired with a slider that has its old bite back, but it has so far proven difficult for him to find the combination to get through a lineup two or three times without some sort of struggle. He had a quality start against the Angels on April 21 with three runs allowed over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees managed to score four runs against Kazmir with only three hits in 5 1/3 innings on Sunday, aided by four walks and a hit batsman. Kazmir yielded a pair of homers and was down, 3-0, in the second, but he clamped down and left with a lead in the sixth. He appeared to find his absent slider mid-game, mixing it in with his fastball and changeup with his new delivery, in which his hands are held behind his head before uncoiling. Kazmir is 3-4 with a 4.50 ERA in nine career starts against the Tigers, having beaten them on April 20 at home while going 5 2/3 innings. In that start, he allowed six hits and two earned runs, recording seven strikeouts. He's 2-2 with a 3.25 ERA in five career starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: The immediate result from Verlander's last outing was a hard-luck loss Tuesday against the Twins, with two unearned runs allowed, but the long-term result could well be a return to the Verlander domination of last year. A tweak in his mechanics brought better command, plus the finishing pitches that allowed him to rack up seven strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings and hold Justin Morneau and Joe Mauer hitless. Though his pitch count still sits remarkably high -- his 19.4 pitches per innings ranked near the top of AL starters -- he was quietly encouraged. That said, he has topped 120 pitches in each of his past two outings, and he won't have an extra day in between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver turned in his fifth straight quality start when he allowed just one run on seven hits over six innings against the Indians on Monday at Angel Stadium. He didn't have his best command -- he needed 106 pitches to get through six innings --- but still struck out seven batters and walked just one. The right-hander last pitched against the Tigers on April 21, when he allowed just two runs over seven innings but was saddled with a no-decision. He is 2-2 with a 6.34 ERA in six career starts against Detroit and 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in one career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Baker is coming off back-to-back disappointing outings and he'll have to face the Tigers for a second straight time after they tagged him for five runs on nine hits over four-plus innings his last time out. The Twins had handed Baker a 6-1 lead heading into the fourth inning on Wednesday night, but Baker would give back nearly all of those runs in a tough inning. The right-hander got a lot of balls up in the zone during his start against Detroit, and he admitted that he didn't feel like he had good stuff at all against the Tigers.  He'll try to see if he can turn things around in his next start, this one coming at Target Field. Baker is 1-1 with a 5.68 ERA in two starts at the Twins' new home so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had his first quick hook as a Tiger in his last start, chased in the fourth inning Wednesday by a three-run Twins rally. He'll get his chance at a rematch, this time starting the Tigers' first game at Minnesota's new Target Field, but he'll have to do a better job of keeping the ball in the park. He has given up five home runs over his last four outings, including two to the Twins, while his ratio of groundouts to flyouts is almost even. The good news for him is that he has quality starts in each of his previous three outings on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn is set to come off the family medical emergency list for Tuesday's game. The Twins put Blackburn on the list Friday so he could tend to an undisclosed family situation, moving Kevin Slowey ahead in the rotation. Blackburn has not won since his first start this season, although his last two outings have been no-decisions. Blackburn will have his first shot this season against the Tigers, against whom he was 1-1 in three starts last season. In 19 1/3 innings last season against Detroit, Blackburn allowed eight earned runs against the Tigers, striking out 11 and walking five.
away_pitcher_note: Not since 2006, his younger years with the Florida Marlins, had Willis thrown six-plus scoreless innings with six or more strikeouts until Thursday, when he commanded the strike zone against a Twins lineup that initially waited for him to throw strikes before trying to attack him early. The Twins get another shot at him Tuesday at Target Field, and they'll likely have Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau back in their lineup after they were missing in the finale. If Willis can continue to get the late movement on his fastball to get opponents to mishit balls, he has a good chance at continued success.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey will be pitching on normal rest after pitching a day ahead last weekend against the Indians, when Nick Blackburn was placed on the family medical emergency list. Slowey mostly stayed out of trouble until the fifth inning, but pulled out the win after allowing just three runs on nine hits and no walks. Slowey fanned six in that outing. Slowey hasn't faced Detroit this season. Last year, the right-hander went 1-0 in two starts, the victory resulting from an eight-hit, two-walk effort in which he allowed a run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello returns to the site of his AL Central tiebreaker gem looking to regain his old form. Both Porcello and the Tigers believe the 21-year-old is close to getting back his old sinker that opponents would beat into the ground for outs last year. A mechanical tweak to raise his arm angle and change his release point in his delivery helped him work the Angels for nine ground-ball outs over 5 1/3 innings Friday night at Comerica Park. He gave up five runs on eight hits in the process, but much of that damage came around when Torii Hunter jumped on a first-pitch slider for a three-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Huff was victimized by the long ball in a loss to the Twins on Sunday. He allowed four runs on 10 hits with two walks and two strikeouts in five innings. All of the runs came in as a result of home runs. Since tossing a complete-game victory against the Rangers on April 15, Huff has lost three straight starts and given up 13 runs in 16 1/3 innings along the way. He faced the Tigers on April 9 and allowed four runs (one earned) on six hits over six innings in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman's first month back in the Tigers rotation was about slow, steady progress after shoulder surgery to correct a blood vessel restriction cost him the better part of two seasons. His last start was an encouraging one in that regard despite 10 hits allowed over six innings against the Angels. His fastball velocity averaged higher than at any point since surgery, and his top speed of 94 mph is believed to be his best since his younger days four years ago. He's throwing an increasing number of splitters and has been drawing more swings and misses as he sharpens it. Bonderman is 8-9 lifetime against the Indians, including a victory in the Tigers' home opener on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: One reason why Masterson has not been quite as effective as a starter as the Indians hope is his struggles early in the game. He has a 10.80 ERA and a .423 average against in his five first innings this season. The first time through the lineup, the opposition is batting .333 (14-for-42) off him. The second time through, they are batting .421 (16-for-38). Early, middle or late in games, left-handers continue to be Masterson's nemesis. They are batting .414 (24-for-58) with a 1.148 OPS against him.
away_pitcher_note: What used to be a house of horrors for Verlander in Cleveland became a springboard for him around this point last year, when some minor mechanical tweaks and an acrobatic catch by Curtis Granderson put him in line for a complete-game victory. Verlander beat the Indians four times last year and hasn't lost to the Tribe since 2008. He took a no-decision against Cleveland on the season's opening weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot was not nearly as dominant against the Blue Jays on Monday as he had been against his previous three opponents. He had allowed just two earned runs over his previous 21 1/3 innings, but the Jays changed his fortune by roughing him up for five runs on eight hits, including three homers, with four walks and five strikeouts over eight-plus innings. Talbot settled in after a rough early going, but the trouble he had keeping the ball in the park hurt him. He had allowed just two homers in his four previous starts this season. Talbot faced the Tigers on April 10 and gave up four runs on six hits over five innings in his Tribe debut.
away_pitcher_note: The good news for Scherzer is that he won't have to face the Twins again for a while after Minnesota's hitters roughed him up in back-to-back starts. But it won't mean much until he regains his command. Sliders that were meant for the corner ended up over the middle of the plate, and Twins hitters put them in the outfield gaps. He gave up 10 runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings Monday at Target Field, and has surrendered 16 runs on 18 hits in just eight innings over his past two outings. He has never faced the Indians, but his three quality starts this season were all on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Dontrelle Willis was originally scheduled to start, but he was a late scratch because he was feeling under the weather. In steps Thomas, who has started once in his seven appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mitre will slide into the Yankees rotation to make a spot start as the club pushes Andy Pettitte back to protect his left elbow inflammation. Mitre has appeared in five games this season for New York, all in relief, and is expected to be stretched out enough to throw 65 to 75 pitches against the Tigers. Mitre will be making his first career appearance against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has lost three of his last four starts, giving up fewer than five earned runs just once in those outings. Most recently, he allowed five runs, three earned, in a loss to the Twins, giving up five hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings, striking out three. The right-hander is at his best at Comerica Park this season. Both of his wins have come on the Tigers' home field, against the Angels and Indians. Porcello has faced the Yankees just once, giving up six runs on six hits and three walks. Porcello lasted just 3 2/3 that day, striking out one.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez will get another chance to figure out his issues as the Yankees continue their four-game series at Comerica Park. The Yankees pushed Vazquez back so he'd miss a start against the Red Sox in Boston, giving him time to throw two vigorous bullpen sessions and work on his mechanics. Something has to change -- he was raked by the White Sox for five runs in three-plus innings on May 1 and the innings-eater hasn't completed the sixth in any of his starts. Vazquez is 6-7 with a 4.50 ERA in 13 career starts vs. Detroit, but has not faced them since 2008.

The right-hander is at his best at Comerica Park this season. Both of his wins have come on the Tigers' home field, against the Angels and Indians. home_pitcher_note: Bonderman lucked out his last outing, when a rainstorm that blew in off Lake Erie canceled out a miserable night. Pitching with a 7-1 lead, Bonderman gave up six straight runs in the third inning of a game against the Indians at Progressive Field, ultimately being tagged for six runs on seven hits in 2 2/3 innings. Luck factored in because, when the rain came, the teams hadn't played five innings. When the game was later postponed, that meant that Bonderman's stats -- like those of everyone who played that night -- vanished. The rough outing would have raised Bonderman's ERA above 7. Bonderman last faced the Yankees in 2008, going 1-1 against the Bronx Bombers before ending the season on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes will try for his third consecutive winning effort on Wednesday as the Yankees play the third game of their four-game series against the Tigers. Hughes was money once more on Friday at Fenway Park, hurling seven innings of two-run, seven-hit ball against the Red Sox, walking one and striking out seven. He is 2-2 with a 5.30 ERA in five career appearances vs. Detroit (three starts), including his first start of 2009 at Comerica Park last April 28, when he hurled six innings of scoreless, two-hit ball in an 11-0 rout.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander came out on fire in his last start, striking out five Indians hitters in the first two innings, and held on to pull above .500 for the season. Verlander gave up three runs on four hits and four walks over six innings, punching out nine Tribe hitters in the victory. With the win, he improved to 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA over his last three starts (four earned runs in 20 innings). Verlander hasn't faced the Yankees since July 18, 2009, when he allowed two runs on seven hits and a walk over seven innings, still taking the loss despite fanning six hitters. Verlander went 1-1 in two starts against the Yankees last season.
away_pitcher_note: After finishing his last start one strike shy of qualifying for a win thanks to a rain delay, Sabathia will get the ball against the Tigers in Detroit on Thursday. He had a 2-2 count on Victor Martinez in the fifth inning on Saturday at Fenway Park when the tarp came out, ending his day in an eventual 14-3 Yankees rout. Sabathia has had plenty of experience in his career against the Tigers, owning a 14-10 record and 4.50 ERA in 28 starts. As a Yankee, he was 1-1 with a 2.40 ERA in two starts last season.

home_pitcher_note: After four pretty strong starts to begin his Tigers career, Scherzer has been rocked in his last three, giving up 21 runs on 27 hits over just 13 innings in two games against the Twins and one vs. the Indians. His strike percentage has been lower in those starts, but his walks haven't reflected it, meaning he's more often trying to attack hitters from behind in the count. His velocity, meanwhile, has been down on all of his pitches. The key for him, in manager Jim Leyland's view, is to command his fastball better, improve his slider and throw his changeup more often. He has made just two starts at Comerica Park this season, but a night game in Detroit can't be a bad thing against a Red Sox team that could make him pay for ill-placed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off his shakiest start of the year, as he gave up nine hits and six runs (five earned) over five innings against the Yankees. Buchholz has gone six innings or more in just two of his first six starts. Opponents are hitting .288 against him. Buchholz has pitched well on the road thus far, going 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts. He has pitched just twice against the Tigers in his career, going 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA. He was hit hard in his lone start at Comerica Park, giving up 10 hits and five runs over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: The expectation for now is that Willis will be able to make his next scheduled start after missing his turn in the rotation Monday with the flu. That said, manager Jim Leyland would like to get him a relief outing before then so that he isn't facing live hitters for the first time in 11 days when he takes the mound against the Red Sox. After proving that his command issues are largely behind him, he has shown the ability to get called strikes against hitters, 18 of them in each of his last two outings. He's spotting the corners these days while putting a little late movement on his fastball, and if he continues to pitch effectively, he's going to get his fair share of calls.
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty is on a roll, giving up a total of just three earned runs over his last four starts. In his last outing, Lester earned a victory over the Yankees, giving up four hits and two runs over seven innings, walking two and striking out seven. Interestingly, five of Lester's first seven starts have been at Fenway. On the road, he is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA. Lester has held opponents to a .222 average. This is his first career start at Comerica Park. In fact, he has only faced the Tigers once in his career, going 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be called up from Triple-A Toledo for the first time this season to get what is expected to be a spot start. Galarraga has boasted impressive numbers in Toledo, owning a 4-2 record with a 3.92 ERA. His command seems to have improved since last season with the Tigers, where he posted a 6-10 record in 25 starts before being relegated to bullpen duties. Galarraga owns a strike-to-ball ratio of better than 2-to-1, 427 strikes against 209 balls. The always dangerous Red Sox lineup will certainly test Galarraga's command, but Tigers manager Jim Leyland said he's been impressed with Galarraga's ability to pound the strike zone so far with the Mud Hens.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey's last outing was far from his best, but he still managed to get the win. The big righty gave up eight hits and six runs over six innings, walking three and striking out six. Lackey has given up three earned runs or fewer in five of his first seven starts in a Boston uniform. Opponents are hitting .278 against him. Lackey is 1-0 with a 2.63 ERA in his two starts on the road. He has enjoyed pitching at Comerica Park in his career, going 4-0 with a 3.46 ERA in four starts. Lackey has made nine career starts against the Tigers, going 6-1 with a 3.73 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling for the better part of a month to find the sinker that induced so many ground-ball outs last year, Porcello put it to work in his last start and got a gem of an outing from it. His seven scoreless innings against the Yankees last Wednesday included 13 groundouts, plus three big swings and misses from his four-seam power fastball. Now he'll try to carry that over against a White Sox team he faced only once last year, giving up five runs over 5 1/3 innings with two homers.
away_pitcher_note: As the fifth starter within the White Sox rotation, Garcia has pitched more like a No. 2 or 3 hurler for most of the 2010 season. The right-hander's latest strong showing came Tuesday night, during the South Siders' debut at Target Field, resulting in a 5-2 victory. Garcia gave up two runs on nine hits over seven innings, striking out three and walking two. Garcia showed his pitching guile by striking out Joe Mauer, the best hitter in Baseball, on three straight split-fingers in the fifth inning to escape a two-on, two-out jam. Garcia has a 16-6 career record against Detroit with a 3.76 ERA and has a 7-3 lifetime mark at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since tossing a perfect game, Braden took the loss in a 4-0 defeat against the Angels on Friday. Braden threw five scoreless innings before giving up four runs in the sixth, three of which came via a Hideki Matsui home run. Braden has struggled against the Tigers in his career, as his career ERA against Detroit is 7.34 -- his second-highest figure against any team.
