In six career starts (30 2/3 innings pitched) against the Tigers, Braden has gone 2-2, giving up 39 hits and nine walks while striking out 17.
away_pitcher_note: Two rainouts in the past week will provide Verlander an extra two days of rest before he faces the A's. Verlander has won each of his past three starts, holding the Angels, Indians and Yankees to four runs on 11 hits in 21 innings. He shut out New York for 6 2/3 innings in his most recent start. He is 3-3 with a 3.07 ERA in seven career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Ross will make his second big league start on Thursday in place of injured right-hander Justin Duchscherer. Ross made an emergency start for Duchscherer on Saturday in Anaheim, but was tagged for the loss. Ross retired the initial 11 batters he faced before giving up three straight hits, including a three-run homer to Kendry Morales. Ross said he feels most comfortable as a starter because that's what he's been his whole life. The 6-foot-6 rookie right-hander is yet to face the Tigers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman was expected to start on Tuesday, but his start was pushed back a day to allow Tigers ace Justin Verlander to stay on turn. In his last start, Bonderman looked strong but was unable to garner any run support, as the Tigers lost to the Yankees in the second game of a day-night doubleheader last Wednesday. He allowed only two runs in seven innings before the Yankees went off in the ninth and posted six runs. The right-hander still hasn't won a game since the Tigers' home opener, which was five starts ago. Nothing would make Bonderman happier than shutting down the Oakland A's, the team that drafted him in the first round in 2001 and traded him away the following season. He will be pitching on six days' rest for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has gotten away from trying to sink the ball, relying more on his four-seamer and curveball, and the result his last two starts has been an ERA drop of more than a full run. Billingsley went 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Padres on Sunday, and in his previous start he went 5 1/3 innings and allowed two runs in a win over the D-backs. He had a 5.06 ERA entering that start in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers' comeback against the Red Sox last Saturday night allowed Willis to stretch his unbeaten streak to three starts, but it didn't let him escape the frustration of a wild outing. With seven walks over 3 1/3 innings and just 40 of his 86 pitches for strikes, it marked the first time this season that Willis showed signs of his past control woes for more than an inning. He was pitching for the first time in 11 days, and he still seemed lethargic after missing his last start with the flu, but he didn't want to use that as an excuse. If pitching in his hometown doesn't give him a little energy boost, it would be a surprise.

home_pitcher_note: Ely is a strike-throwing machine, not having issued a walk to any of the last 84 batters he's faced. He's one of the rare players who actually has pitched better in the Major Leagues than he did in the Minor Leagues prior to his promotion. His manager likes the way Ely competes, and he surely is not intimidated by the opposition at the Major League level. He doesn't throw hard, but never has and has refined the more subtle skills of pitching, like command and composure to win a spot in the Dodgers' starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: What was initially thought to be a spot start for Galarraga last Sunday against the Red Sox became a two-start audition once the Tigers sent down the struggling Max Scherzer. The Tigers' series opener at Dodger Stadium is the latter half of that stint, but another solid outing would make it all but impossible to pull Galarraga from the rotation. He held Boston to a run on three hits over 5 2/3 innings, retiring 10 Red Sox in a row at one point, striking out five for the day and showing the aggressiveness that he seemed to lack for much of last year, partly due to a forearm injury. He's 4-2 with a 4.61 ERA in Interleague Play over the past two seasons, including seven scoreless innings against the Dodgers two years ago at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Kuroda uncharacteristically blew a three-run lead. But he stopped the damage there and went the final 3 1/3 innings without allowing a run while giving his offense a chance to come from behind and beat the Astros. This time, Kuroda said his slider wasn't working. Although he throws four pitches, it's rare when they all are effective together. Nonetheless, he's adept enough at pitching to win without his best stuff, which is what he did against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello has used his sinker for 24 groundouts over his last two starts, but unlike his seven scoreless innings against the Yankees, the White Sox managed to turn one extra-base hit and seven singles into four runs and another loss for Porcello in what has been a rough couple months to his sophomore season. Though he has alternated wins and losses in his last four starts, he has only one quality start in his last six outings and just two all season. Perhaps Interleague Play will be a remedy; he went 3-0 with a 1.90 ERA in four starts against the National League last season.

home_pitcher_note: Fister bounced back from a five-inning outing in Tampa Bay by throwing eight gutsy frames in a 3-2 loss to Toronto. The Jays got him on the ropes with three runs in the third and fourth, but he fought back and retired the final 14 batters he faced in order to notch his sixth quality start in eight tries. He also rung up a season-high five strikeouts in that contest and leads the Mariners talented pitching staff in ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners saddled Verlander with one of his two losses on the season during the Tigers' last trip to Seattle, where Verlander dropped a pitchers' duel despite seven innings of three-run ball. The Tigers are heading back to the Great Northwest, but it's a nastier Verlander coming with them, having allowed a lone run on eight hits in 15 2/3 innings over his past two outings. He's pitching to more contact these days and getting quicker, deeper outings from it. Verander has lost his past three starts against the Mariners and hasn't beaten them since 2008.

home_pitcher_note: His five-run season-debut aside, Vargas has been excellent, posting six-straight quality starts. He pitched well enough to win in his last outing but took a no-decision after the Mariners made a ninth-inning comeback to top Toronto, 4-3, and he's just 1-1 in May despite giving up nine runs in 27 2/3 innings across four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman comes back to his home state for the second time in just over a month with a chance for revenge after the Mariners roughed him up for 10 runs, eight earned, over four innings in April. What he's really seeking, though, is a continuing of a very solid May in which he has three quality starts in as many starting assignments and has honed the bite on his slider. He struck out eight Athletics while holding Oakland to a run on three hits over six innings on Thursday for his first victory since April 10. Opponents are batting just .219 with a .561 OPS against him in day games this year, compared with .253 and .684 at night.

home_pitcher_note: Willis' last start seemed like two different outings in one, which is a big reason why it's so difficult to judge where the D-Train stands with his pitching at this point in the season. He not only allowed one hit among the first 12 batters he faced, but that hit was the only ball the Dodgers put in play past the infield in that span against him. Once Matt Kemp singled, however, Willis allowed five hits and three walks among the final 13 hitters he faced, along with two wild pitches and a hit batter. One suspicion was that Willis ran into serious mechanical issues pitching out of the stretch, something they might work on between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Monday's off-day allows Sheets to pitch on normal rest while the A's decide if the injured Brett Anderson can go Saturday. The ERA may look unsightly, but Sheets has sliced more than two runs off his ERA since nine runs in 3 1/3 innings against Toronto in his first May start raised him to a season-high mark of 7.12. In four starts since then, he's failed to go fewer than six innings. His most recent outing, Sunday against San Francisco, was his best of the season -- six innings of two-hit shutout ball and eight strikeouts to match a season high. If Sheets has turned a corner, it couldn't come at a better time for the A's, who could use his veteran presence in their rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello took some damage from three hard-hit comebackers in his last start, including a bruise on his right leg, but he's expected to be fine for his next start on an extra day of rest. The 21-year-old has alternated losses and wins over his last six starts, the last being six innings of two-run ball to beat the Dodgers last Sunday. He has allowed just two extra-base hits over his last three starts, and he hasn't given up a home run in his last four starts. However, Porcello has lost both of his previous meetings with the A's in his brief career, allowing 10 runs on 17 hits over 9 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Assuming he gets through a Thursday bullpen session in  Baltimore without any soreness, Anderson will be activated off the 15-day disabled list to make Saturday's start against the Tigers at Comerica Park. Anderson has been out since April 25 with a left forearm strain and left elbow inflammation, but a three-inning rehabilitation start at Triple-A Sacramento on Monday was enough to prove to the southpaw -- and, presumably, manager Bob Geren, who watched the game on his laptop -- that he was ready to return. Anderson threw sliders without any pain in his rehab outing, a good sign, but he'll be on a short leash -- Geren said he would be limited to about 75 pitches. In the unlikely event that Anderson can't make the start, right-hander Tyson Ross would probably get the call.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers will recall Scherzer from Triple-A Toledo to return to the Tigers' rotation after a pair of dominant starts for the Mud Hens suggested he has made the adjustments in arm angle and delivery he was trying to find for the better part of a month in Detroit. He allowed a run on four hits over 15 combined innings, racking up 17 strikeouts in the process against just two walks. He was last seen on a Major League mound at Comerica Park on May 14, when he gave up three Red Sox home runs, two to David Ortiz, over five innings of six-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, who pitched a perfect game on Mother's Day, left his last start in Baltimore on Tuesday with a left ankle sprain. Four innings into the 1-1 game, pitching coach Curt Young and manager Bob Geren had seen enough of Braden favoring the injury, which resulted in uncharacteristic back-to-back walks and more pitches up in the strike zone than Braden usually throws. Since then, Braden has been receiving treatment and spent a couple of days off his feet and away from baseball activities. Assuming Braden is good to go in Motown, he will pitch. But any sign that the ankle is still tender and Braden might be in line for another early exit.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will get an extra day of rest before his Memorial Day assignment, thanks to the Tigers' off-day Thursday. But judging from his frustration level after his most recent outing last Tuesday at Seattle, he might not have minded pitching again a couple days later. He took a lead into the seventh inning and a pitching duel into the eighth, but ended up with the loss thanks to two home runs earlier and a Milton Bradley RBI single in the eighth. He did not feel comfortable with his pitches, but he also had some complaints over a wet mound at Safeco Field thanks to a rain shower that hit with the roof open.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill looked rather sharp in a win over the Orioles in his last start, permitting just two hits and one earned run while walking three and fanning three over six innings. Baltimore's lone run came on a third-inning homer to Garrett Atkins, but Cahill settled in after that, relying on his sinker to give up fewer than three earned runs for the fourth time in six outings this season. The young righty has made significant strides from his rookie campaign, in which he offered up an Oakland rookie record 27 homers while compiling a 4.63 ERA. This year, he's held the opposition to a .221 average that has helped him put together a formidable 1.10 WHIP. Cahill will have to get his sinker working early and often against a power-heavy Tigers lineup, one against which he's 0-1 with a 8.68 ERA in two career starts. In a combined 9 1/3 innings vs. Detroit last year, Cahill gave up nine runs, 12 hits and five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Yes, Bonderman owns only one win out of his last eight starts, but with the way he pitched in May, it's hard to blame him for it. He owns quality starts in each of his last four official starts, not counting the rough night he had in a rained-out performance in Cleveland. He allowed just four earned runs on 23 hits over 27 innings in May, walking seven and striking out 26. That includes seven innings without an earned run last Wednesday in Seattle. Now, he'll begin June with a rematch against the Tribe, whose damage against him at Progressive Field consisted almost entirely of one inning.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was not at his sharpest in a loss to the White Sox on May 26, as he allowed five runs on six hits over seven innings. But Westbrook did keep his team in the ballgame, and the endurance and pain-free outings he's turned in this season are signs that he's made it all the way back from Tommy John surgery in 2008. Now, he just needs to find the consistent command that made him a consistent winner before injuries derailed his career. This will be Westbrook's first start against the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers chose Galarraga to stick in the rotation over Dontrelle Willis, who was designated for assignment over the weekend. Now, Galarraga will try to back up the vote of confidence on the mound when he starts for the first time in a week and a half. His future was in serious question after the Dodgers roughed him up over four-plus innings May 22 in Los Angeles. He had an extended side session last Wednesday in which he tried to work on his slider, his workhorse pitch that needs more consistency, then took it into a relief outing Friday against Oakland with some effectiveness. Galarraga earned three of his 13 wins in 2008 at Cleveland's expense, but lost all three of his meetings with the Indians last year.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona hung in there against the Yankees in a loss Friday night, but he had some issues with control that hurt him and ran up his pitch count. He needed 34 pitches to get through the sixth inning, and with his count over 100 after that point, he wasn't able to take it any further. He gave up four runs on seven hits with three walks and three strikeouts in six innings. The good news is that Carmona has gone at least six innings in all but one of his 10 starts this season. He's generally been able to keep the Indians in games. This is his first start against the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has alternated wins and losses in his past seven outings, though he owns quality starts in three of his past four assignments. He gave up two runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings last Saturday against Oakland, taking the loss. Porcello beat the Indians in the Tigers' home opener back in April, adding to his success against the Indians. He's 4-0 with a 2.10 ERA in five career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Huff is making his next turn in the rotation, and that seems like a miracle to those who saw him whacked in the head by an Alex Rodriguez line drive in the third inning of his start against the Yankees on Saturday. Huff was taken off the field on a motorized cart and taken to a nearby hospital, where a CT scan showed no brain damage and doctors determined he had no signs of a concussion. Huff threw a bullpen session two days later and was confirmed to be making this start. The only question is whether he'll have any lingering fear of another lined shot.

home_pitcher_note: Chen, a veteran left-hander, stepped into the rotation last Sunday to fill in for disabled Gil Meche (shoulder) and pitched well enough to earn an encore start. Facing the Red Sox at Fenway Park, Chen worked four innings and gave up one run on two hits and two walks. In fact, a leadoff walk in the third resulted in the lone run. He threw 75 pitches in the outing, about 35 more than in any of his previous relief performances but he'd started earlier in the season for Triple-A Omaha. Chen has faced the Tigers seven times in his career, going 0-2 with a 6.97 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer showed the impact of what a couple weeks at Triple-A Toledo to work on his delivery could do. With his old arm angle rediscovered and the life on his fastball renewed, Scherzer struck out 14 A's over 5 2/3 innings last Sunday at Comerica Park, becoming the first Major Leaguer since at least 1933 to fan that many batters without getting through the sixth inning. He faced the Royals in back-to-back starts to begin his season back in April, tossing six scoreless innings in his Tigers debut April 7 at Kauffman Stadium before the Royals beat him in the rematch five days later.

home_pitcher_note: Coming into his last start, against the Los Angeles Angels, Hochevar had given up only two home runs in his last 60 innings of work. That streak went by the wayside when Hochevar gave up two home runs in seven innings as he picked up his third loss of the season. The Angels tagged Hochevar for five runs. Hochevar will look to get back on track against the Tigers at Kauffman Stadium. In five career starts against the Tigers, he is 2-2 with a 5.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander has lost his past two starts, but as much for lack of run support as for giving up the big hit in close games. He trailed the A's after a pair of first-inning runs Monday and never recovered despite seven strong innings, and he left the field arguing with home-plate umpire Laz Diaz over two curveballs that didn't get the call for third strikes. Verlander took a no-decision against the Royals on Opening Day, giving up four runs on six hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister equaled his career high with a fourth consecutive victory on Tuesday against the Angels. Nevertheless, Bannister felt his performance was spotty and credited a strong bullpen effort with helping him earn that win. Over 5 1/3 innings, Bannister gave up seven hits and three earned runs. Bannister has allowed a homer in nine straight starts and will be looking to end that streak, which is the longest of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman has quietly become the Tigers' most consistently effective pitcher over the past month or so, tossing quality starts in each of his last five starting assignments since May 1. That includes eight innings of three-run ball against the Indians that gave Detroit a shot in a pitchers' duel before dropping a 3-2 decision Tuesday night at Comerica Park. He's showing the impact of a stronger, healthier arm, but more importantly, the wisdom of a veteran hurler who has learned how to mix his pitches, get quick outs and work deeper into games. He faced the Royals in three mop-up relief assignments last year, but this will be his first start against Kansas City since he opened the 2008 season.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd had pitched well going into his last start, against the Texas Rangers, but 2 2/3 innings later, he had been chased after allowing eight hits and six runs after just 19 batters. Of the eight hits he surrendered, five were extra-base hits, including four doubles. After the game, White Sox skipper Ozzie Guillen said, "Maybe the first year in his career here, but I don't think I've ever seen him this bad. Bouncing balls, getting hit hard. That's the first time I've seen him pitching this way. This kid, every time he is in there, we believe we have a chance. Nothing was working with him. I tried to stay with him as long as I can, because our bullpen is very thin, and I couldn't." Floyd is undefeated against the Tigers, with five wins over no losses, and a 3.34 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hard to believe now, but there had been speculation that Galarraga would be skipped in the Tigers' rotation here with the team off on Monday. Of course, that speculation was before Galarraga's would-be perfect game last Wednesday, when only an errant call from first-base umpire Jim Joyce kept Galarraga from becoming the first Tiger ever to achieve perfection. Tuesday will mark Galarraga's first start since that amazing outing and the incredible sympathy he showed afterwards towards Joyce. He might never pitch anywhere near that well again, but if he can find that same nasty sinker and slider, he'll have a chance to pitch effectively and give the Tigers a chance at a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Even though Garcia entered the season as the nominal fifth starter for the White Sox, he's pitched like their ace so far. Not only do his five wins pace the team, but his 4.94 ERA is the second-lowest of the five starters. In his last start, Garcia went seven innings, giving up three runs. The White Sox offense bailed him out, however, by scoring four runs in those seven innings, earning Garcia the win. Lifetime against the Tigers, Garcia is 17-6 with a 3.73 ERA in 185 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello will look to even his record as he faces the White Sox in game two of a three-game series Wednesday. In his last start, Porcello was shaky in a no-decision against the Indians last Thursday, allowing six runs -- three earned -- on seven hits, while striking out two in 5 1/3 innings. Before his mishap against the Indians, Porcello had made four-straight solid starts and he will look to get back on track in Chicago. Porcello has never pitched at U.S. Cellular field, but is 0-2 with a 6.57 ERA against the White Sox in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Danks struggled in his last start en route to earning a loss against the undermanned Cleveland Indians. Danks cruised through his first five innings, but he could not keep it going, eventually letting five of six Indians batters reach base in the sixth. Danks earned the loss on four earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. Jhonny Peralta's double provided the biggest blow to Danks' sixth. Lifetime against the Tigers, Danks is 2-3 with a 4.10 ERA in eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his fifth loss of the season, Scherzer is looking to rebound from a shaky performance in Kansas City. Scherzer lasted just five-plus innings, allowing five earned runs on nine hits. Detroit manager Jim Leyland said that Scherzer would never become a complete pitcher until he perfects his slider -- something Scherzer is hoping to work on against Chicago. This is Scherzer's first career start against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will welcome the Pirates for Game 1 of a three-game series that kicks off a nine-game homestand of Interleague Play for the Tigers. Verlander is fresh off his sixth victory of the season, in which he pitched seven-plus innings and allowed only five hits and two earned runs as the Tigers beat the Royals, 4-2. Interleague Play has been kind to Verlander. In 13 career starts, he is 9-1 with a 2.90 ERA to go along with 89 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Another stellar outing once again did not result in a win for Ohlendorf, who was aided by tremendous fielding in his last outing, a 6-5, 10-inning home loss to the Giants on Sunday. Ohlendorf went six innings, giving up three runs on eight hits while striking out two and walking three. He added a single off Tim Lincecum in the fifth. In two career appearances (one start) against the Tigers, Ohlendorf is 1-0 with a 0.96 ERA, having surrendered just one run on three hits in 9 1/3 innings. The right-hander has stuck out seven and walked just three.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman is coming off a rough outing against the Royals in which he picked up his fourth loss of the season. Coming into his last start, Bonderman had only given up four runs in his last 21 innings, but that all changed against the Royals. Bonderman was hit hard for five runs in the first two innings and ended up giving up seven on the day. He lasted 5 2/3 innings, while giving up 11 hits with a walk and two strikeouts. Bonderman will look to rebound against the Pirates in game two of a three-game series. Bonderman is 7-7 in 21 starts in Interleague Play with a 5.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Make it three quality starts in a row for Maholm, who continues to be the Pirates' steadiest rotation presence. The left-hander picked up his team-leading fourth win on Saturday with a strong 6 1/3-inning performance in which he kept the Giants to six hits and two runs. Maholm seems to have found better efficiency as of late, too, evidenced by the mere 86 pitches he needed in his last start. Maholm has pitched at least six innings in 10 of his 12 starts this year as well.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be making his first start at Comerica Park since his bid for a perfect game a week and a half earlier set up a surge of national publicity and made him a name in Detroit. He got back to some sense of normalcy in his last start Tuesday at Chicago, where he gave up two runs over five innings against the White Sox. The Tigers aren't expecting complete games from him, let alone perfect games, but the more innings they can get out of him, the better. He owns a 4-3 record and 5.12 ERA in nine career Interleague starts but was roughed up was four runs on eight hits in two innings against the Pirates last June in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens put up a good effort on Tuesday, especially considering it came in one of the most hyped games (Stephen Strasburg's debut) in recent memory. Karstens actually took a lead into the sixth inning, before two Washington home runs sunk him. Still, the outing earned Karstens a stay in the Pirates' rotation for the time being. The right-hander has been a fairly stable presence in the Pirates' rotation when called upon to start this season. As a starter, Karstens is 1-2 with a 4.40 ERA in five games. He has, however, allowed six home runs in 28 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Max Scherzer continued to show that his short stint in Triple-A Toledo was extremely beneficial. Unfortunately, in his three starts since being recalled, his win-loss record hasn't indicated how much improvement he's made. Scherzer has posted a 1-2 record, but has only given up a combined eight earned runs in three starts. In his last start, Scherzer allowed three runs on five hits in 7 1/3 innings, while fanning seven batters. But the Tigers' offense was unable to provide any run support to back a solid outing -- a problem many of the Tigers' starters have dealt with of late.
away_pitcher_note: A day after Stephen Strasburg's dominating performance, Lannan went to the mound and had one of his worst outings on Wednesday night. However, the bullpen and the position players helped the Nationals defeat the Pirates, 7-5, in front of 18,876 fans at Nationals Park. Lannan lasted 4 2/3 innings and allowed five runs -- four earned -- on 10 hits. He said he didn't feel any pressure following up Strasburg's huge performance.

home_pitcher_note: Considering at least half of Verlander's four losses have come in part from low run support, he was due for a game in which offense and defense helped him out. Verlander called his fastball "horrible" in his previous outing. And while he ended up with more walks (four) than strikeouts (three), he still managed seven-plus innings of two-run ball against the Pirates for another Interleague victory. He's 10-1 with a 2.88 ERA lifetime against the National League, and he'll have at least three more meetings with the Senior Circuit before the Tigers close out Interleague Play.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez was solid on the mound as the Nationals defeated the Pirates, 4-2, and swept the three-game series. Hernandez pitched six innings and allowed two runs on five hits. It was his first win since May 4 against the Braves. He also picked up his 10th quality start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman owns four quality starts in his last five outings, the latest being seven innings of two-run ball last Saturday against the Pirates in just 91 pitches. His fastball has been gaining velocity and, especially lately, he has been able to keep up the fastball later in games. At times, manager Jim Leyland says, he looks as good as at any point Leyland has been here, which dates back to 2006. All in all, the ingredients are there for a big summer if he can get just a little more run support, which he hopes he can find against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano started for Washington and lasted five-plus innings, allowing six runs -- three earned -- on seven hits against the Indians. The first three runs were scored in the first inning. With one out and Carlos Santana on first, Russell Branyan hit a perfect double-play ball to second baseman Adam Kennedy, who booted the ball for an error. Austin Kearns was the next hitter and hit a three-run homer to give Cleveland a 3-1 lead.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga has recorded two straight no-decisions since his near-perfect game on June 2 against the Indians. But he's been good enough to earn wins in both starts. He allowed only two earned runs in each game and walked a combined three batters. However, he only recorded two strikeouts, total. This is credit to his ability to find the bottom of the strike zone and induce opposing hitters to uncomfortable flyball and groundball swings.
away_pitcher_note: Willis is making his third start for the D-backs after being acquired June 1 in exchange for Minor League right-hander Billy Buckner. Willis had been designated for assignment by the Tigers after going 1-2 with a 4.98 ERA in eight starts and one relief appearance. Control continues to be an issue for the left-hander. In 10 innings with Arizona, he has allowed just two runs on eight hits, but he has walked 10 and fanned five. The high pitch counts have forced his exit early in games. Willis' last outing was June 10 against the Braves, when he allowed a pair of runs on three hits and six walks over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello is best known for his sinker. But of late, he hasn't had good command of the pitch and it has been running up in the strike zone, instead of staying down. In Porcello's last start against the White Sox on June 9, he surrendered eight runs in 3 1/3 innings. Because the Tigers had an off day on Monday, manager Jim Leyland opted to skip Porcello to give him extra time to try to regain command of his go-to pitch. "If he gets the sinker back the way we want it to be on a consistent basis, then we think everything else will fall into place as well," Leyland said.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson will face off against his former team after being dealt to the D-backs during the Winter Meetings in a three-team trade that also included the Yankees. The right-hander got a no-decision in his last start against the Cardinals at Chase Field, but certainly deserved a better fate. He scattered eight hits and allowed just a pair of runs over 6 2/3 innings. He also got a no-decision in his start prior to that against the Braves at Chase Field when he allowed four runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: To say Scherzer's last start was a battle would be an understatement. Scherzer struggled from the get-go on Tuesday against the Nationals. He found himself falling behind in counts and threw 81 pitches through four innings. Scherzer admitted he didn't have good command early in the game, but after allowing three earned runs through the first four innings, he settled in as it progressed and made it through the sixth inning to earn his first win since striking out 14 batters in 5 2/3 innings on May 30 against Oakland. He still showed his ability to fan batters on Tuesday, striking nine Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy will face off against Max Scherzer. The pair were part of the three-team trade that also sent Edwin Jackson to the D-backs. The right-hander has been the club's most consistent starter this season. Last time out against the Red Sox at Fenway Park, though, he did not have his best stuff and Boston wound up hitting him for six runs on nine hits over six innings. In his start prior to that, he allowed just three hits in seven shutout innings against the Braves, but came away with a no-decision in Arizona's 2-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching in front of scores of friends and family in his home state of Ohio, Niese was not nearly as sharp in Cleveland as he was during his one-hit shutout against the Padres one start earlier. But he was plenty sharp enough to win, holding the Indians to three runs on eight hits over seven innings. For his next outing, Niese will return to Citi Field, where he is 2-1 with a 2.65 ERA in six starts this season. He has never faced the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers ace had lights-out stuff in his last start and struck out a season-high 11, thanks in large to his breaking ball. He weaved his offspeed pitches in and out of the strike zone in his last outing, a feat he struggled to accomplish in his previous starts this season. Couple his high-velocity fastball with his revamped curveball and changeup, and Verlander may be en route to surpassing his previous season-high total in strikeouts when he faces the Mets to kick off the Interleague Series.

home_pitcher_note: It's difficult for a knuckleballer to be dominant, and Dickey certainly wasn't on Thursday against the Indians. But he was good enough, scattering seven hits and three runs throughout his six innings at Progressive Field. Dickey also struck out seven batters, the third time he has fanned seven or more in a game this season. Taking a tip from pitching coach Dan Warthen, Dickey began exclusively throwing his harder, low-80s knuckleball -- which he was better able to command -- in the middle innings, allowing him to retire the final six batters he faced. Dickey's next start will come against the Tigers, a team that touched him for four runs in three innings last season.
away_pitcher_note: Tigers manager Jim Leyland loves what Bonderman brings to the table. It's his no-fear attitude and ability to pound the bottom of the strike zone that has impressed the skipper so far this season. In his most recent start, Bonderman gave up four deep flyballs to the warning track in the first two innings that were sure home runs in most ballparks. But not in spacious Comerica Park. Bonderman recovered from his shaky start and went on to allow only two runs in seven innings of work, his fifth quality start in his past six outings.

home_pitcher_note: After two successive sub-par starts, Takahashi's spot in the starting rotation seemed less than concrete going forward. But in his past two outings, the left-hander has allowed just one run in 13 innings of work on the road against the Orioles and Yankees. He earned the win in both of those games and has now pitched 12 innings of shutout baseball against the Yanks this season. John Maine does not look ready to return to the rotation, as he has had mixed result in his two rehab assignments. As a result, Takahashi will take the mound against the Tigers, holding his spot in the rotation for at least one more orbit.
away_pitcher_note: In a battle against former teammate Dontrelle Willis -- the man who's spot in the Detroit rotation Galarraga filled -- the near-perfect righty lasted only 4 1/3 innings and allowed four earned runs. Maybe it was the hot and muggy temperatures, or the D-backs' lefty-heavy lineup, that gave Galarraga problems on the night. He didn't have command of his slider early and strayed away from the pitch much to the disliking of Tigers manger Jim Leyland, who said Galarraga was being "too tentative" on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander continues to impress and make the most of his time in the starting rotation with Jair Jurrjens out until late June with a hamstring injury. Medlen hasn't surrendered more than four earned runs -- which he did just once -- in eight of his starts this season. His past two outings were fairly respectable. In each the 24-year-old allowed three earned runs but pitched at least 6 1/3 innings, as well. Medlen is more of a contact pitcher, though during his last two starts, he did strike out five batters in each.
away_pitcher_note: A year after Detroit selected Oliver in the second round of the Draft, and mere months after Oliver began his pro career in the Arizona Fall League, the Tigers will call up the 22-year-old lefty to take over just-demoted Rick Porcello's rotation spot. With a consistent mid-90s fastball and an improving slider, Oliver steadily improved as his Double-A season continued at Erie, where he went 6-4 with a 3.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 77 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 2010 season has been a struggle for Kawakami, who has yet to win a game this season. He's come fairly close on numerous occasions, only to see a fluke hit or bullpen lapse derail his win attempt. But recently, the right-hander hasn't made things easy for himself. He left his past start against the Royals after just two innings, having surrendered four earned runs. In his outing before against the Rays, Kawakami allowed five runs. Before his shortened start against the Royals, the 35-year-old had thrown 100 or more pitches in each of his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: A temporary return to facing National League hitters has done a world of good for Scherzer, the former Diamondbacks rookie who has won back-to-back starts against NL foes in the past week and a half. He allowed one run on four hits over seven innings against his old squad last Sunday in Detroit. Combine that with his victory over Washington last week, and he has struck out 17 batters over his past 13 innings. Monday's off-day gives him an extra day of rest coming into this outing, which could be a blessing after he used up 118 pitches against the Diamondbacks and 112 in dealing with the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the month of June in dominating fashion during his first three outings, Hanson allowed the most runs of his career on Tuesday against the White Sox. The right-hander will look to rebound from that forgettable 3 2/3 innings in which he surrendered nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: While there wasn't much good news coming out of Verlander's drubbing by the Mets at Citi Field Tuesday, it's two-fold coming into Atlanta. First, he used up just 61 pitches before a 58-minute rain delay knocked him out with two runners on and nobody out in the third. Second, he'll be pitching on his standard four days of rest, which he says he actually prefers over an extra day because it fits his between-starts routine better. The stats support his point, especially this year: He's 5-1 with a 2.21 ERA on four days rest, 3-4 with a 5.20 ERA with any more rest than that. His 11-2 career record in Interleague Play includes seven innings of one-run ball against the Braves at Turner Field in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano didn't get a chance to deliver yet another quality start for the Twins, as National League play forced the pitcher out after just five innings in his start vs. the Brewers. Despite having allowed just three runs and throwing 77 pitches, Liriano was removed in the top of the sixth when his turn to bat came with the Twins trailing by one and runners on first and second. Still, Liriano managed to strike out seven in the contest and improve his K/BB ratio to 100/25 on the season. He'll next face the Tigers, who he held scoreless over eight innings in his only start against them so far this year.
away_pitcher_note: The basic numbers from Bonderman's last outing Wednesday against the Mets -- four runs over six-plus innings -- probably don't reflect how he pitched. He needed just 66 pitches through six innings and had 70 when he was lifted following back-to-back singles leading off the seventh. With one early-count ground ball after another, it continued his maturation from the young power pitcher of 2005-06 to a more efficient, pragmatic hurler looking for quick outs and deeper outings. He'll face the Twins for the first time since his plunking of Delmon Young last October drew a three-game suspension.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn's rotation spot has become tenuous, as he's gone 0-4 with a 12.05 ERA in his last five starts. Blackburn has been unable get through four innings in four of his past five starts, and an inability to command his sinker could be to blame.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga owns just eight strikeouts over 32 innings in June, but his work to pitch to contact is working. His six innings last Thursday against the Mets earned him his first win since his would-be perfect game June 2, but the Tigers have won all five of his starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: Like teammate Nick Blackburn, Slowey has been going through a rough stretch of late, going 0-2 with a 12.41 ERA over his past three starts. The right-hander said after his outing against the Mets that he needs to make better two-strike pitches and minimize the big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oliver made a solid first impression with his poise Friday against the Braves but lost a pitchers' duel in his big league debut despite two runs on five hits over six innings. His 95-97 mph fastball gives the Tigers their first power lefty since former first-round pick Andrew Miller.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will try to continue the high-powered, high-strikeout pitching that brought him back from the doghouse in June. He came an out shy of his fourth straight quality start Saturday, but still finished with 5 2/3 scoreless innings and eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start following a monthlong disabled-list stint with shoulder fatigue, Fister exceeded his prescribed pitch count of 75-80 pitches by throwing 92 in four frames. An off-day earlier in the week gives Fister an extra day's rest for this outing.

home_pitcher_note: An extra day of rest has usually meant extra trouble for Verlander this year, and he'll face that again this time around. He talked last week about changing up his routine and learning to keep his arm fresh, but this will be his first time trying to put that into practice.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas allowed a series of baserunners in the fifth inning of his last start, in Milwaukee, leading to a pair of runs and ending his day earlier than any other June start. Still, his streak of three earned runs or fewer extended to 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman was brutally honest about his last outing, saying he escaped Minnesota with a win by luck. He owns quality starts in his last five home outings despite inducing more flyouts than groundouts each time, but he has won only one of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: With the clock ticking toward the non-waiver Trade Deadline, Lee, a potential free agent, begins a new month in pursuit of his fourth consecutive complete game and sixth of the season in 13 starts. His control has been practically perfect -- five walks in 96 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Oliver will make his home debut for the Tigers in his third Major League start with a chance to pick up his first win. His combination of mid-90s fastball and hard slider gave Detroit a chance to win twice on the road trip, but the run support didn't return the favor.
away_pitcher_note: All six runs charged to Millwood on Wednesday against Oakland came in a poorly defended fourth inning. That was all the damage he allowed in five innings. He is 4-5 with a 3.65 ERA in 13 career starts against the Tigers and 2-2 with a 2.83 ERA in five starts at Comerica.

home_pitcher_note: A month after falling a bad call short of a perfect game, Galarraga would settle for consistency these days. After picking up his first win since the memorable night, he struggled mightily in Minnesota, lasting just four-plus innings with six runs allowed on seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: He was better on Thursday against Oakland than in his two previous starts, but still hasn't reached the level that got him started 2-0 after his first two starts. Against the A's, he allowed three earned runs on seven hits, two walks and two errors in six innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has gone unbeaten in his past four starts and has pitched some solid baseball doing it. He fell an out shy in one outing of having five straight quality starts, allowing eight earned runs on 22 hits in 34 innings while striking out 39 in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen had one of his best outings Friday at Fenway Park, limiting the Red Sox to three earned runs -- two of which were solo shots by J.D. Drew -- over 7 2/3 innings. He fanned a season-high seven and didn't issue a walk.

home_pitcher_note: A win Friday would give Verlander 11 before the All-Star break for the first time in his career. Considering his first victory this year didn't come until April 22, it's quite a feat. He has rolled off five wins in his last six starts and nine in his last 12.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano put up good numbers in his last start against the Rays on Saturday. The lefty fanned 10 batters and walked only one. That is the most strikeouts he has had this season since retiring 11 on June 11. He pitched seven innings and gave up only one run on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman's pattern of quality outings gone unrewarded in low-scoring games has been replaced by struggles in his last three starts, allowing 15 runs on 25 hits in 16 1/3 innings. His normally nasty slider has been inconsistent and hit hard when it doesn't snap.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn's rotation spot had become tenuous after he went 0-4 with a 12.05 ERA in his first five June starts. The majority of those struggles came on the road, and his next start will be in Detroit for an important series against the Tigers to finish off the first half.

home_pitcher_note: Oliver fell victim to inconsistent command and bad defense behind him in a loss at Minnesota last week, but Jim Leyland likes the idea of pitting his lone lefty starter against Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau. Oliver was knocked out in the second inning of his last start.
away_pitcher_note: The Twins flip-flopped Pavano and fellow starter Kevin Slowey in the last turn of the rotation. It allowed the club to get an extra start before the All-Star break from its most consistent starter.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander will look to pick up his sixth win of the year as the Tribe's No. 1 starter after the All-Star break. He gave up five runs on eight hits in six innings while taking his fifth loss of the year despite striking out seven batters against Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has the tough task of throwing the first game back after the All-Star break. He threw a bullpen on Sunday and said he will play catch on Tuesday and Wednesday to help keep his arm fresh. But even he doesn't know what will happen coming off such a lengthy break.

home_pitcher_note: The Tribe's lone All-Star will start the second half having won his last start, when he went 6 2/3 and allowed just two runs against Tampa Bay. Carmona walked four, but he only gave up five hits and struck out four en route to his team-high-tying eighth win of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander said his curveball was the best it has been all season after his last start. In fact, he said it was actually too good. In his last outing, the Twins hitters were sitting on the breaking pitch and waiting to get in fastball counts.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot, who has been a welcome surprise for the Indians so far this season, will look to get back on track after losing his last two starts and four of his last five. The righty is tied for the team lead with eight wins in his first full season as a Major League starter.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello hasn't been posting great numbers in Triple-A Toledo, but manager Jim Leyland decided to recall the right-hander for the nightcap of the doubleheader. Porcello was sent down to the Minors to work on his sinker, which was hanging up in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez will be promoted to make this spot start against the Tigers, then he'll head back to Triple-A Columbus. It's been a disappointing season for Gomez, who was Eastern League pitcher of the year at Double-A Akron in '09. He is 6-8 with a 5.70 ERA in 18 starts for Columbus.
away_pitcher_note: Oliver was roughed up in his last two starts for the Tigers and hasn't shown good command of his pitches since his June 30 start in Minnesota. He has combined to throw only 6 1/3 innings over his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman worked six innings of three-run ball in the Tigers' 7-4 victory against the Twins on July 10, his first quality start since June 17. The 27-year-old right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.63 ERA in nine appearances at Comerica Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Orioles, Feldman earned the no-decision after a late O's rally. He pitched seven innings while giving up two runs on eight hits with two strikeouts. It was just the third time in his last 11 starts that he pitched into the sixth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit plans to recall Galarraga after a one-start stint with Triple-A Toledo. The 28-year-old righty worked 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball against the O's on July 6, his first quality start since June 13. He's 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in six appearances at Comerica in '10.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter is the first Rangers pitcher since Esteban Loaiza to win his first six decisions in a season. This is only his third start on the road this season and he is 4-4 with a 5.90 ERA in 12 road starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer yielded five runs on five hits and five walks over five laborious innings in the Tigers 8-2 loss to the Indians on Friday. The setback snapped a four-game winning streak for the 25-year-old right-hander, who is 4-1 with a 2.32 ERA in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 5-1 with a 3.13 ERA in his last seven starts after beating the Red Sox on Friday at Fenway Park. He is 4-4 with a 3.44 ERA in 10 starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .209 off him, including .175 with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander did not receive a decision for the first time since April 11 on Saturday, when he scattered six hits and five walks over six innings of three-run ball against the Indians. The 27-year-old right-hander is 2-0 with a 2.95 ERA in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Romero ended a three-start losing streak and picked up his first victory since June 16 with a strong seven-inning showing against the Orioles on Friday. The lefty allowed two runs (none earned) on five hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello had a stellar return to the big leagues last weekend, tossing eight innings of one-run ball against the Indians, inducing 11 ground-ball outs. Now he'll face a Jays lineup boasting a little more home-run power, with Jose Bautista and Vernon Wells.
away_pitcher_note: Over his past five starts, Marcum is 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA for the Blue Jays. On Sunday, making his first start after a stint on the 15-day disabled list, the righty held the Orioles to one run on nine hits over five innings en route to a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello had a stellar return to the big leagues last weekend, tossing eight innings of one-run ball against the Indians, inducing 11 ground-ball outs. Now he'll face a Jays lineup boasting a little more home-run power, with Jose Bautista and Vernon Wells.
away_pitcher_note: Over his past five starts, Marcum is 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA for the Blue Jays. On Sunday, making his first start after a stint on the 15-day disabled list, the righty held the Orioles to one run on nine hits over five innings en route to a victory.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Galarraga was that he pitched deep into his last start against Texas, with 7 1/3 innings. The bad news was that the Rangers got the ball into the air for 19 fly balls and line drives, many of them deep. He'll need more grounders from the Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil walked away with a no-decision in his last outing, against the Royals on Monday, when he gave up three runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings. The left-hander is 1-0 with a 2.33 ERA in three July starts for the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: The comeback kid in the Tigers rotation has hit a rough patch of late, with 19 runs on 31 hits over 21 2/3 innings in his past four starts. However, he says his arm, which was the team's big concern after he lasted just 5 1/3 innings against Texas Monday, is feeling great.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Litsch earned his first win since Sept. 28, 2008. The righty held the Royals to one run on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings. Litsch has made seven starts since returning after a year-long recovery from Tommy John surgery on his right elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Garza got a no-decision in his last outing Tuesday at Baltimore after allowing seven runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings. Garza is 0-4 with a 5.85 ERA in six career starts against the Tigers; he is 17-10 with a 3.31 ERA in 42 career appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has won all six of his home starts since being recalled from Triple-A Toledo in May, but he's 0-3 in four road starts in that same span. In fact, he hasn't won away from Comerica Park since beating the Mariners on April 18 at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Shields picked up his eighth win of the season Wednesday against the Orioles when he allowed four earned runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He is 3-0 with a 3.93 ERA in six career starts against the Tigers; he is 26-19 with a 3.66 ERA in 69 career starts at Tropicana.
away_pitcher_note: While Verlander's fastball is as tough as ever, he's winning games lately on his secondary stuff, an adjustment when hitters start sitting on his heat. He tossed eight innings of two-run ball against Toronto in his last start July 22.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann allowed two runs on five hits against the Indians on Friday to take his third loss of the season. The 6-foot-9 right-hander is 0-1 with a 2.04 ERA in three career appearances against Detroit; he is 10-5 with a 2.94 ERA in 25 career appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Bonine has spent the entire season in the bullpen, but with Sunday's day-night doubleheader forcing the Tigers to use a spot starter, manager Jim Leyland turns to Bonine and his knuckle-curveball combination for his first start since September.

home_pitcher_note: Price allowed three earned runs on three hits and four walks against the Indians on Saturday to earn his 13th win of the season. He is 1-0 with a 0.90 ERA in three career appearances against the Tigers; he is 14-4 with a 2.52 ERA in 21 career appearances at Tropicana.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello still isn't getting the consistent results he enjoyed last year, but he's a work in progress. He tossed a quality start against Toronto on Saturday, but with four walks and five hits over six innings, he was in and out of trouble every other inning.

home_pitcher_note: Lester was perfect through 5 1/3 innings in his last start, but wound up with a loss to the Mariners, giving up four hits and four earned runs over 7 2/3 innings while striking out a career-high 13. He is 6-2 with a 2.84 ERA at Fenway this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers' decision to push back Jeremy Bonderman to make two starts next week left Friday's series opener at Fenway all to Galarraga, who beat the Red Sox in his return to the Majors in May. He's winless in two starts since the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka labored at times in his last start but got the job done, giving up a run on four hits and five walks in six innings while fanning four. He took a no-decision. Matsuzaka has started five times at Fenway in '10, going 3-2 with a 4.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer will stay on his regular four days' rest for a rematch with the Red Sox, who tagged him for three home runs in five innings May 14 in his final start before being sent to Triple-A Toledo. He's winless on the road since April 18.

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz thrived in his second start back from the disabled list, giving up five hits and a run over seven innings while walking one and striking out seven. Opponents are hitting .233 against Buchholz. He is 5-3 with a 3.08 ERA at Fenway.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander pitched a gem at Fenway last summer with eight scoreless innings and eight strikeouts. The Tigers could use a repeat. He's 7-2 with a 2.69 ERA this year when pitching on four days' rest, which the Tigers set up by moving him up to Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello is winless in his three starts since coming back to the big leagues, but he's back to being a reliable member of the Tigers rotation. A pair of infield singles that caromed off Miguel Cabrera cost him three runs to the Rays last Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle struggled early in his start against the Mariners, but he was able to right the ship: after giving up five runs in the first two innings, Seattle did not score again. That allowed the White Sox to come back for the win.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman will make his first start since July 25, hoping to pick up his first win since the All-Star break and find some of the life he had in his pitches a month ago. He has a 7.29 ERA and a .928 OPS allowed in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Carlos Torres was recalled from Triple-A Charlotte to start Game 2 of the doubleheader. He was 7-7 with a 3.41 ERA for Charlotte. He pitched in eight games, five of them starts, last season for the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga says he's fine after a Kevin Youkilis line drive off his right ankle knocked him out of his last start Friday at Boston. He hasn't won at Comerica Park since his almost-perfect game June 2, but he tossed a quality start there July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson will make his White Sox debut after being acquired from the D-backs prior to non-waiver Trade Deadline. He'll be debuting with Chicago against the Tigers, the team for which he pitched in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer lost his chance at his fourth July win when the Tigers bullpen couldn't hold a ninth-inning lead, but his 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball continued his trend of solid pitching since mid-June. He's 4-2 with a 1.92 ERA in his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has posted a dominant 18-6 career record and 3.74 ERA against the Tigers. Garcia has an 8-3 record at Comerica Park and a lifetime mark of 49-22 in starts made for day games.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit's ace has quality starts in his last four outings, but only one win to show for it. He has lasted at least seven innings in three consecutive starts, including seven innings of three-run ball in a no-decision Sunday at Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is has four consecutive quality starts heading into this outing. During that span, the 27-year-old sports a 2.33 ERA. Weaver gave up one run (none earned) in seven innings against the Rangers his last time on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit will start Bonderman on three days' rest rather than use a spot starter. If he can keep up his slider and change of speeds, he could have a chance at another solid start. He held the White Sox to a run on five hits over 6 2/3 innings Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir returns from the disabled list for his first start since July 11 in Oakland, when he yielded 13 earned runs, before going to the disabled list with shoulder fatigue. He feels he is ready to return, refreshed, to make up for lost time.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has had what manager Jim Leyland called his best stuff and his worst stuff since returning to the big leagues in his last two outings. His secondary pitches, including the slider, will likely be the key to his fortunes against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: This is Bell's second straight start after a strong 5 1/3-inning effort last Tuesday against the Orioles. He found success with his fastball and pitched in the aggressive manner he needs to remain tough to hit.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga needs to trust his stuff more, according to manager Jim Leyland, and pitch on the defensive less. He spent too much time on the outside corner against the White Sox, who homered three times in his 7 2/3 innings Wednesday at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Price pitched well enough to win Wednesday but came away with a no-decision against Minnesota despite allowing just one run in seven innings. Price is 2-0 with a 1.65 ERA in his career against Detroit; he is 1-0 with a 0.90 ERA at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will be looking for a better result against the Rays at Comerica Park after Matt Joyce spoiled his no-hit bid in the sixth inning July 26 at Tropicana Field. He has allowed three runs over 13 1/3 innings in two no-decisions since.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson, who won his Major League debut on Aug. 2 against the Twins, will get the start on Tuesday in place of Wade Davis, who has been battling right shoulder pain and may be on his way to the disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander is winless in his last three outings despite lasting at least seven innings each time. Early damage was the problem. Nine of the 10 runs off him in those games came in the first three innings, including all four Saturday against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Garza was handed his sixth loss of the season in his last start, vs. the Jays on Friday. He went eight frames -- good for a CG -- yielding just two unearned runs. Two errors, including one his own, spoiled an otherwise strong outing.

home_pitcher_note: Mark Buehrle brings a 15-8 lifetime mark against the Tigers into this series opener. He also has a stellar 81-48 record during his 184 career appearances at U.S. Cellular Field. Buehrle lost his last start in Baltimore, working seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman will get an extra day's rest between starts after his start last Saturday on three days' rest went badly with four runs and four walks over 4 1/3 innings. He beat the White Sox with 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball on Aug. 3.

home_pitcher_note: After a victorious White Sox debut in Detroit, Jackson allowed just two runs in six innings during a no-decision when facing the Orioles. He fanned seven and showed great command.
away_pitcher_note: The good news for Porcello is he's coming off a quality start in beating the Angels. The bad news is that the White Sox have beaten him twice in as many tries this year, including June 9, when they scored eight runs in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in his past four starts, the usually-steady Garcia was unable to last three frames. Garcia gave up six runs and three homers over 2 1/3 innings in a loss to the Twins, after allowing just four long balls in his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers believe their perfect-game pitcher is trying too hard to make the perfect pitch. He's 1-4 with a 5.10 ERA in 11 starts since his memorable performance June 2, and he has walked 11 in his last 17 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez hopes to rebound from a rough outing against the Rangers, when he allowed six runs on eight hits during 4 1/3 innings. He is trying to reverse a trend of not going seven innings; he hasn't reached the plateau in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has three straight starts of at least 6 1/3 innings with two earned runs or fewer, but Detroit's offensive woes have left him winless in four starts since July 21. He hasn't won away from Comerica Park since mid-April in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia nearly went the distance in his last start, allowing three runs and finishing one out shy of a complete game in a win over the Royals. He's gone at least eight innings in back-to-back outings, and he's won seven of his past 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander stopped a Tigers skid in its tracks with a solid outing vs. the Rays last Wednesday in Detroit, but more important for his outing was his ability to find a middle ground between commanding his fastball and controlling his offspeed stuff.

home_pitcher_note: Moseley ran into trouble in the fifth inning of his last start, finishing with eight hits and four runs in 4 1/3 innings vs. the Royals. He's 2-2 since replacing the injured Andy Pettitte in the rotation, with three starts of at least six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman has fallen into a pattern in which one or two really bad pitches ruin an otherwise solid start. In his last outing Friday against the White Sox in Chicago, two poorly placed fastballs led to a three-run home run and a two-run shot.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes earned won No. 14 in his last outing, throwing six innings and allowing three runs, though he proved hittable, ceding nine. He forced the Royals' hitters to put the ball in play, finishing with one walk and no strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello returns to Yankee Stadium, where his dad used to take him to games as a kid, with hopes of building on his seven solid innings of two-run ball last Saturday against the White Sox. He didn't get a decision, but the Tigers got a comeback win.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will make his first start since he got into a dugout argument with catchers Alex Avila and Gerald Laird over their game plan for pitching to the White Sox. The dispute isn't expected to have any impact on Galarraga or the catchers.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson was effectively wild Sunday against the Mariners. In six scoreless innings, he allowed just one hit. But he walked six guys. Of his 100 pitches, only 49 went for strikes. Masterson has been wildly unpredictable all year.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer earned his first win in five starts with six scoreless innings Monday at Yankee Stadium, but he has quietly been one of baseball's best pitchers for nearly a month. He owns a 1.37 ERA and a .610 OPS over his past last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start on Aug. 11, Tomlin was tagged for three runs (two earned) on 10 hits over five innings in a loss to the Orioles. The rookie righty has yielded two or fewer earned runs in three of his first four Major League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander called his game vs. the Yankees "the worst I've ever felt on the mound as a professional baseball player." He needed 114 pitches to last five innings with three runs allowed on five hits, walking five and striking out five in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Gomez might have suffered his first Major League loss Tuesday in Kansas City, but he still looked impressive in doing so. He allowed just two solo home runs over six innings but didn't get run support. He commanded his changeup well.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman has lost his last three starts, giving up 16 earned runs on 17 hits over 15 1/3 innings combined, including a three-homer barrage from the Yankees last Wednesday. He gave up seven runs on 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings to the Royals June 6.
away_pitcher_note: Although Chen doled out 11 hits in 5 2/3 IP, he made enough good pitches when he needed them to hold the Indians to four runs and earn the win. In 15 starts since taking over for Gil Meche, he's 7-6 and has won three of his last four outings.

home_pitcher_note: If Porcello continues to alternate good losses with bad, he should be due for a quality outing here. But the Tigers need to support their struggling sophomore, who has won once in his last 11 starts. He took a no-decision against the Royals in April.
away_pitcher_note: Davies had one of his finest efforts last Thursday night at the Indians, holding them scoreless on three hits through the seventh. He ran into trouble in the eighth, charged with three runs and had no decision.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga has never lost to the Royals, but he hasn't faced them this season. He's coming off seven scoreless innings against the Indians last Friday, which improved his home record to 3-3 with a 3.26 ERA at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching one inning of a rainout on Friday night, O'Sullivan wasn't brought back for doubleheader duty and was kept in his regular rotation spot. He's still looking for his first victory after going 0-4 in five official starts for the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: According to manager Cito Gaston, Romero was dealing with an acute case of strep throat in his last outing vs. Boston. Fully healthy, the left-hander should bounce back from a mediocre performance that saw him surrender four runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: No Tigers starter has been as stingy over the past month as Scherzer, who has a 1.35 ERA and 27 hits over 35 innings in his last five starts. He gave up an earned run over seven innings with eight strikeouts last Saturday against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: After a shaky outing against Boston August 11, Marcum appears to have righted the ship. Over his last two outings Marcum has allowed just five hits, one walk, and four runs over 16 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander seems to be rounding into form where he can mix his pitches early, still overpower hitters and last into the late innings. He tossed eight innings of one-run ball with eight strikeouts against the Indians last Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: After topping out around 90 mph in Oakland on Aug. 17, Morrow had plenty of life on his fastball against the Yankees Monday, hitting upwards of 95 mph regularly. The return in velocity and control lead to a solid two-run, 12 strikeout performance.
away_pitcher_note: Figaro will make his fourth Major League start in place of the injured Jeremy Bonderman. Over two stints and 4 2/3 innings with the Tigers this season, the righty has allowed three earned runs. In 23 starts at Triple-A, Figaro went 10-6.

home_pitcher_note: Rzepcznyski labored in his last start, lasting just three innings in a loss at home against the Yankees. The left-hander yielded six runs on eight hits, including three home runs, and ended with two walks and one strikeout in the 68-pitch effort.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello returns to the place where he made his first Major League start in April 2009, now looking continue the adjustments he's been making to go from a pure sinkerballer to someone who can attack hitters with four or five different pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing suffered his first loss as a starter this year, giving up four runs on six hits in six innings to the Rangers. He's 4-1 since joining the rotation on July 23 and has won nine of his 11 decisions as a starter dating back to last season.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be looking for better results than his last start at Target Field, on June 29, when he allowed six runs in four-plus innings en route to a loss. The right-hander has a 3.48 ERA in August.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano tied his career high in wins in his last start against the Rangers, pitching seven innings while allowing two runs. Liriano has been one of the Twins' best starters since the All-Star break, going 6-0 with a 2.47 ERA in eight outings.
away_pitcher_note: In winning his last three starts, Scherzer has allowed a total of two earned runs, putting his early-season struggles further in the past. The righty has exceeded 100 pitches in 15 consecutive starts.

home_pitcher_note: Baker won his fifth straight decision in his last start against the Mariners, which is the longest such streak of his career. He has not lost since July 19 against Cleveland. Baker has a 3.02 ERA with 33 strikeouts during the streak.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander hasn't strung together back-to-back wins in more than a month, but he'll have a chance to do so in his next start, against the Twins, whom he held to two runs over 5 1/3 innings in a victory on July 9.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke logged his ninth eight-inning start of the season Saturday, but the Indians tagged him for three runs on eight hits and four walks in a no-decision. The 26-year-old righty is 7-3 with a 3.61 ERA across his past 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman missed his scheduled start last Saturday at Toronto with tightness around his right rib cage, but he felt well enough throwing Tuesday that he expects to make his next assignment. If not, Alfredo Figaro would fill in for a spot start again.

home_pitcher_note: Chen worked six-plus innings of two-run ball against the Indians on Sunday for his team-leading ninth win of the season. The 33-year-old lefty is 8-7 in 17 starts since joining the Royals' rotation May 30.
away_pitcher_note: After all the ups and downs of his sinker, Porcello might be rounding into a nasty late-season form. He has allowed a run on five hits over 14 innings in his last two starts, including seven scoreless innings against the Royals at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Davies went 8 1/3 innings, longest outing in his Royals career, but lost, 3-0, to the Rangers. It was a good bounce-back start from a drubbing at Detroit and his control, often a problem, was on target -- 72 strikes and just one walk in 112 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Don't let the win total this late in the season fool you. Galarraga has left with the lead after solid starts in his last two outings, only to watch Detroit's bullpen lose it. He has allowed three runs over 19 1/3 innings in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Teammates believe Scherzer might be the best starter in the AL at the moment, and he's making a strong case. He's 3-1 with a 1.25 ERA over his last seven starts, including nine innings with one run Wednesday at Minnesota in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Over his five starts in August, the right-hander posted a 3-0 record with a 1.47 ERA, racking up 45 strikeouts in just 35 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander didn't allow an extra-base hit at Minnesota on Thursday, but 10 Twins singles and some defensive miscues set up six runs, three earned, over six innings in a no-decision. Incredibly, Verlander has yet to face the White Sox this season.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia left early from his last start in Cleveland with a stiff back but said over the weekend in Boston that he'll be ready to go against the Tigers. Garcia, tentatively listed as the starter, is trying to improve on an 18-6 career mark vs. Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman struggled early in his last start at Kansas City, allowing four runs on five hits in the second inning. But he recovered nicely and didn't allow a run over the next 5 1/3 innings as the Tigers rallied to win.
away_pitcher_note: With the team needing every win possible to keep pace with Minnesota, the White Sox will go with Danks on three days rest as opposed to Carlos Torres or Lucas Harrell. Making his 28th start of the year, Danks is 6-2 in his last 11 trips to the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has won his last three starts, all of them seven-inning performances, and has five quality starts in his past six outings. He's winless in three starts against the White Sox this year but scattered two runs over seven innings August 14.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd didn't have his best stuff against the Red Sox Saturday night but still pitched well enough to pick up his 10th victory. The White Sox rotation now features four starters with double-digit win totals. Floyd is 5-0 lifetime vs. Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga allowed just four hits and one run through five innings in his last start at Kansas City. However, Galarraga walked five, complained of elbow stiffness and said he didn't have good movement on his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: The American League leader in losses, Millwood has pitched better than his record indicates. The veteran lasted 5 2/3 innings in Friday's loss, giving up four runs on seven hits while walking five.

home_pitcher_note: The White Sox cooled off what had arguably been the AL's hottest starter Monday, but Scherzer's 7 1/3 innings with four runs allowed got no decision. He had allowed seven earned runs in 50 1/3 innings over his previous seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie has emerged as the unquestionable ace of the staff, and he had another strong outing on Saturday, tossing seven innings of two-run baseball. Guthrie settled down after a leadoff homer to pick up his second consecutive win.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander joined Tim Hudson as the only active pitchers to win at least 15 games in four of their first five seasons. Sunday could make Verlander the only one to do it with 16 wins. Consider his 4-0 career record against the O's; he has a good shot.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start back in the rotation, Tillman fared well. The 22-year-old right-hander held the Rays to three runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings, giving Baltimore a chance to secure the win.

home_pitcher_note: Holland went six innings in an 8-1 victory over the Blue Jays in his last start and is 1-1 with a 2.81 ERA in three games since being called up from Triple-A on Aug. 28. He is 9-15 with a 5.84 ERA in 28 starts over the past two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Just when Bonderman's future seemed in serious question, he had three consecutive solid starts, allowing seven runs on 18 hits over 21 1/3 innings. That included eight innings of three-hit ball with eight strikeouts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 4-2 victory over the Blue Jays on Thursday, allowing one run in 6 1/3 innings. He is 2-7 with a 4.75 ERA in 11 starts since the All-Star break. He is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts vs. the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Armando Galarraga had his start moved up a day so the Tigers can start him Wednesday in place of the injured Rick Porcello. Galarraga allowed three runs in seven innings in a start Friday vs. the O's. He has struggled on the road with a 1-2 record.

home_pitcher_note: The worst performance of Jackson's seven starts with the White Sox came on Saturday against the Royals, when he allowed six runs on 13 hits over five-plus innings. Jackson gets to face one of his former teams, the Tigers, for the fifth time in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer's run of five straight solid starts ended with a relative crash last Saturday against the Orioles, who roughed him up for 12 hits and four runs over six innings. He's 0-1 with a 3.74 ERA in three starts against the White Sox this year.

home_pitcher_note: With Freddy Garcia ruled out for his scheduled Saturday start, look for Harrell to get his second straight call in place of the veteran right-hander. Harrell gave up six runs on nine hits over 3 1/3 innings in his last start against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: One more win will give Verlander 17 for the fourth time in his first five big league seasons, something no Major League pitcher has done since Dwight Gooden. Verlander's next inning will give him 200 for the fourth straight season.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw allowed four runs over seven innings during a 9-3 loss to the Twins, dropping him to 1-3 with a 5.55 ERA over his last four starts. Danks has allowed seven homers in his last six starts, after allowing one in his previous eight.
