away_pitcher_note: The 2007 NL Cy Young Award winner is coming off back-to-back complete games for the first time in his career. Peavy boasts a 1.93 ERA in two career starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: After 119 pitches weren't enough to get Scherzer out of the fifth inning Sunday at Yankee Stadium, he went to video of last year's starts to find out what was different. He believes he has found the problem.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd came within eight outs of throwing the 19th no-hitter in White Sox history during Sunday's 4-1 victory over the Red Sox. In the process, he fanned nine and gave up just three hits in 6 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Detroit's rookie southpaw held the White Sox to two runs in six innings with strikeouts in his last start, which actually qualified as his worst outing so far. He has fanned 21 batters in 18 innings over his last three starts, mixing pitches well.

away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is showing signs of finally falling into midseason form, racking up nine strikeouts in back-to-back May starts following a rough April. He fanned 11 White Sox over six innings of three-run ball April 13 in a hard-luck defeat.

away_pitcher_note: Blackburn had trouble keeping the ball in the park vs. the Blue Jays on Friday, allowing three homers in five-plus innings, but still picked up his first win since July 8. The sinkerballer allowed five runs on six hits and three walks to get the win.

away_pitcher_note: Smyly earned his second career victory in a 10-6 decision over the Twins on Friday. He gave up six hits and three earned runs in five innings of work. He will concentrate on limiting his pitches, as he threw 93 pitches in the outing.

away_pitcher_note: Scherzer's outing against the Twins on Saturday was cut short by a rain delay in Detroit's 6-3 victory. Even so, Scherzer earned the victory, pitching 5 1/3 innings, yielding three runs and striking out nine.

away_pitcher_note: Sabathia was a winner in his last start, holding the A's to two runs in seven innings on May 26. The lefty was 3-2 with a 2.75 ERA in five May starts and beat the Tigers on April 29 with eight innings of two-run ball in New York.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello took a physical beating Sunday against the Twins, taking a comebacker off his left leg and catching a cleat in the mound on a delivery, but he endured for a quality start in a no-decision. He induced 13 ground-ball outs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda hurled a gem his last time out, holding the A's to four hits over eight scoreless innings on May 27 in one of his best starts of the year and his first road win. He was 2-3 with a 4.25 ERA in five May starts.

away_pitcher_note: Hughes was hit for seven runs and 11 hits, both season highs, on May 28 by the Angels in a no-decision. Hughes was 3-2 with a 4.66 ERA in six May starts and faced the Tigers once last year, allowing five runs in four innings.

away_pitcher_note: Jimenez continued his inconsistent season last Sunday against the White Sox as he allowed seven runs on seven hits in only four innings of work. He walked four and struck out three in the losing effort.

away_pitcher_note: Lowe put Saturday's bad outing against Chicago behind him when he allowed only one run in 6 2/3 innings Friday against the Twins. Lowe struck out two and walked only one in the game.

away_pitcher_note: A year and a half into his Major League career, the 22-year-old left-hander will start under the bright lights of Sunday Night Baseball, hoping for his first quality start since May 9. He has allowed four runs in each of his last five outings.

away_pitcher_note: If Scherzer can come anywhere close to his previous Interleague outing this season, last month's 15-strikeout gem against Pittsburgh, he'll be pleased. But he'll have to get back to that form to do it after a rough outing against Cleveland last week.

home_pitcher_note: Wood didn't have his good stuff in his last start, against the Twins, giving up three runs on six hits and three walks over five innings. This will be his first career start vs. the Tigers. Wood has faced only one AL East team, the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Considering how tough it is for division foes to hit Verlander when they've seen him so often, NL foes seeing him for the first time are usually in for a treat. The Reds got him for two runs in six innings, but the Cubs could be challenged.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers used Monday's off-day to push back Crosby's start a few days, slotting him back home, where his two previous starts have taken place. He beat Cleveland with 5 1/3 innings of three-run ball June 7, but has had off-and-on trouble with walks.
away_pitcher_note: Francis' return to the Rockies, after spending last year with the Royals and beginning this year in Triple-A with the Reds, saw him allow eight runs in 3 1/3 innings in a loss to the Angels. Last year, Francis was 0-2 against Detroit with a 2.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Fister will be activated from the disabled list to return once again from the left side strain that has bothered him for most of the season. He had four quality starts in May before the Red Sox hit him for six runs on 11 hits in five innings May 28.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich was hit hard in his second loss Sunday vs. the Angels, giving up nine runs (eight earned) on 10 hits and three walks with five strikeouts in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer allowed three earned runs Tuesday against the Cubs for the third time in his last four starts. Unlike those two previous times, he left with a no-decision rather than a win.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie, who has given up 19 runs in his past three starts, is running out of chances to prove he can be an effective member of the Rockies rotation. He is much better away from Coors Field, though, with a 4.23 road ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander's extra day of rest was once again erased, as the reigning AL MVP was moved up to start Tuesday in the series opener against the Cardinals. He threw eight innings of two-run ball in his last start to earn his first victory in five games.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn set a career high with 12 strikeouts in his last outing, giving up three hits in 7 1/3 shutout innings against the White Sox. Lynn is tied for the NL lead with 10 wins and has allowed two earned runs or fewer in four straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello's previous two outings have been almost identical -- four earned runs on nine hits through five innings in each. He'll look to fix that as he makes his second career start against St. Louis, against whom he is 1-0 with a 1.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook retired 12 straight last time out before bowing out after six quality innings vs. the White Sox. A three-run shot was the only damage of his first win since May 8. Prior, he'd lasted five innings or less in four of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Turner was tabbed as a favorite for the fifth spot in the rotation until shoulder tendinitis sidelined him for most of Spring Training and into April. Drew Smyly's DL stint earns Turner what is likely a spot start vs. the team he followed growing up.
away_pitcher_note: While Lohse allowed three runs through seven innings in his last start, the righty was touched up for 10 hits. The loss was his first since May 4. Lohse has been sharp in June, however, allowing four earned runs in 20 2/3 innings over three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will seek to win a seventh consecutive start for the first time since 2005. Beginning with a pair of no-decisions, he is 6-0 in his last eight starts with a 2.19 ERA and .218 OBA and 41 strikeouts in 53 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fister returned Saturday from a three-week stay on the disabled list with a left side strain and looked like he was in midseason form, tossing six scoreless innings with six strikeouts against the Rockies to earn his first win of the year.

home_pitcher_note: His recent starts nearly cost Lincoln his spot in the rotation, but the former No. 1 Draft choice's potential saved it. The Pirates still hope to have him get comfortable as a starter after being an early-season relief hit.
away_pitcher_note: Few, if any, pitchers in baseball have run as hot and cold this season as Scherzer, whose eight scoreless innings with no walks and 12 strikeouts Sunday marked his sixth outing with nine or more strikeouts in 14 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Correia ended a winless year in PNC Park by beating Minnesota on Tuesday, yet needing 97 pitches to get through 5 1/3 innings was short of convincing. The Pirates want to see more before considering his job safe.
away_pitcher_note: After losing three consecutive starts from mid-May into June, Verlander has gotten back rolling with back-to-back wins against the NL. He'll get one more Interleague outing against a Pirates team he nearly no-hit May 18 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his Major League debut, Grimm gave up six hits and three runs in six innings during an 8-3 win over the Astros. That was his fifth straight quality start, including his time with Double-A Frisco.
away_pitcher_note: Only one of the 10 hits off Porcello over seven innings went for extra bases last Wednesday against the Cardinals, but it was enough to cost him a pitching duel. Triple-digit temperatures in Texas make it imperative he keep the ball on the ground.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish improved to 9-4 in his last start, allowing five hits and two runs over eight innings in a 4-2 win over the Padres on Wednesday. In his last start against the Tigers, he gave up two hits and one run over 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A stint on the disabled list allowed Smyly to vanquish the troublesome blister on his left index finger. Still, he says heat and humidity have caused blisters in the past, so triple-digit temperatures in Texas could be a test.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt won his Rangers debut Friday, scattering nine hits in 6 2/3 innings, allowing one run while striking out six and walking one. He will make his first appearance against the Tigers and is 3-1 with a 2.24 ERA against the AL Central in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Fister looked unusually hittable last Friday at Pittsburgh, allowing eight knocks over six innings, but his own throwing error on a sacrifice bunt cost him two unearned runs. He has struck out 13 batters over 12 innings since coming back from the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Shields earned a no-decision on Saturday against the Phillies when a two-run homer and a three-run homer accounted for all of the Phillies' runs during Shields' five-inning stint. Shields is 2-2 at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Two days after his brother's death, Scherzer rejoined the team and pitched six quality innings last Saturday at Pittsburgh, his damage coming on Andrew McCutchen's three-run homer. He's winless in three starts against Tampa Bay despite a 3.06 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Price chalked up his 10th win of the season Sunday in Philadelphia, when he held the Phillies to one run on four hits and three walks while striking out eight. Price is 25-16 with a 2.79 ERA in 53 career appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Don't look now, but after a four-game winless streak, Verlander has regained form, winning his last three starts and allowing just 15 hits over 24 innings. He tossed a five-hitter in Pittsburgh last Sunday, striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson will return from the 15-day DL (right shoulder inflammation) for his first start since June 14, when he gave up eight runs in just 3 2/3 innings against the Mets. Hellickson owns a 2.94 ERA and a 1.20 WHIP in eight home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: What happens when one of baseball's young sinkerballers meets an offense that tends to do more with less? Surprisingly, they produce a lot of fly balls over three career meetings. Porcello won the last one with seven innings of two-run ball April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb pitched a complete game Monday, but not a particularly pretty one. He grinded out eight innings on 113 pitches, but allowed eight runs on 13 hits against the Royals. He has 26 K's in 25 2/3 innings at home, compared to seven in 20 road frames.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly returned from the disabled list showing no ill affects from his blister problems despite triple-digit heat in Texas on Tuesday, but bloop hits and smart baserunning helped sink him with a four-run fourth inning. He gave up six runs in defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Fister says he's healthy, but that his execution has been a problem. His pitches have become progressively more hittable with each outing since his return from the disabled list, failing to pound the lower end of the strike zone with consistency.
away_pitcher_note: Hendriks turned in his second quality start of the season on Tuesday against the White Sox, but he still didn't pick up the win. He's now 0-6 in 11 career starts and has allowed a homer in 10 of those 11 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Below will make his first start of the season in a spot assignment for Max Scherzer, who was scratched with a tight hamstring. He made two starts last July and was a rotation candidate in Spring Training before a rough finale landed him in relief.
away_pitcher_note: After four decent innings on Wednesday against Chicago, things took a turn for the worse. Blackburn allowed back-to-back home runs and exited after six runs on nine hits in five frames. The righty is seeking his second quality start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will get one more start before the break, the timing of which puts him in line for a potential start in the All-Star Game. However, the Rays got him for three homers in six innings Friday at Tropicana Field to end a three-game win streak.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing, making his second start of the season, lasted just four-plus innings against the Royals on Friday. The lefty allowed three runs on eight hits and threw 66 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has allowed three runs over 20 innings in his past three starts, including seven scoreless frames on four hits last Saturday against the Rays. The stretch has lowered his ERA by nearly a full run and might have solidified his rotation spot.
away_pitcher_note: Diamond has continued to be the club's most consistent starter and had another strong start against the Royals on Saturday. He went eight innings for a second straight start and gave up just two runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly held the Rays hitless for four innings before a two-run fifth escalated his pitch count and sent the Tigers to their bullpen for the sixth. The rookie southpaw tossed six innings with an unearned runs against the Royals April 17 at Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez struggled in his last outing where he gave up 10 hits, six walks and six runs in 4 1/3 innings. After missing more than a month with a biceps problem, he's 0-2 with a 6.86 ERA in four starts. He's also averaged 20 pitches per inning.

home_pitcher_note: Whether he's knocking the rust off his game after two DL stints or he's compensating for the rib muscle strain that landed him on the DL, Fister has been quite hittable his last three starts, allowing 25 hits and 16 earned runs over 14 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chen had a 5-1 lead after six innings on Sunday at Minnesota but was KO'd in a five-run blitz and took the loss. He gave up three home runs and a triple among six hits allowed. Chen has been steady since going 0-4 in his first six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has rounded into his 2010 form over his last three starts, allowing five runs on 14 hits over 20 innings with three walks and 26 strikeouts. He fanned nine Twins over 5 1/3 innings in a victory at Target Field on May 26.
away_pitcher_note: Teaford earned another start following his first win on Monday as he tries to secure a permanent spot in the rotation. This will be his fourth start. In two stays at Triple-A Omaha this year, he was 4-0 with a 1.09 ERA in seven games.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel fell short of his bid to go to the All-Star Game, but the 29-year-old has still been the Orioles' most consistent starter this season. The right-hander went 6 1/3 innings on Saturday, but was outdueled by Angels ace Jered Weaver.
away_pitcher_note: Fister wasn't great in his last outing vs. Kansas City, but he wasn't awful either. His six innings of eight-hit, four-run ball was just enough to earn his second win of the 2012 season. He is 2-1 in four career starts against Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old rookie lefty closed the season with a career-low four innings, allowing a career-high three homers on Sunday to the Angels. Still, Chen ended the first half 7-5 with a 3.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer capped off his first half with seven strikeouts in seven innings of five-hit, one-run ball vs. Kansas City. He's recorded quality starts in six of his past seven games and is 2-1 in three career starts vs. Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old Gonzalez won his first career start on Friday night, tossing seven dominant innings against the Angels to earn a spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Tigers manager Jim Leyland wanted his ace lined up against the White Sox and Indians after the break. Pitching him Sunday rather than Friday does just that. The reigning AL MVP And Cy Young winner is 6-0 vs. Baltimore in nine career starts.

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer posted a 5.18 ERA through his first 13 starts but has pitched to a 2.28 mark since. He allowed 12 hits and lasted just 3 2/3 innings in his last outing but managed to limit the damage to three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Santana will look to bounce back from an up-and-down first half that ended on a sour note -- eight runs on six hits and three walks in 1 1/3 innings vs. the Indians on July 4. His velocity and stuff is fine. His location and mechanics aren't.

home_pitcher_note: With Drew Smyly headed to the DL, Turner makes his second start of the year. The 21-year-old allowed one run on four hits and five walks in five innings in his previous start. He threw a shutout in his last game with Triple-A Toledo.
away_pitcher_note: Richards made a nice impression early in his stint with the Angels, but he has struggled of late. The 24-year-old right-hander gave up 12 runs over his last two outings in the Majors, then got shelled in his first start back with Triple-A Salt Lake.

home_pitcher_note: After suffering through two stints on the DL, Fister looked to be in prime shape in his last outing, shattering bats and notching eight strikeouts in seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson didn't get the win, but still pitched well against the Yankees on Friday, giving up only a two-run homer to Mark Teixeira and constantly getting out of trouble in seven innings. He's given up two runs or less in 11 of his 12 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer struggled to control his fastball in his last outing, allowing four runs on nine hits and two walks in only five innings on Saturday against the Orioles, snapping a streak of five consecutive quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Williams gave up a couple of two-run homers while surrendering five runs in seven innings and getting tagged with the loss vs. the Yankees. The 30-year-old, who's 0-4 with a 7.54 ERA over his last four starts, came out of it with no breathing issues.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe in the All-Star Game, fans don't want to see Verlander hit the corners at 90 mph, but it gets opponents out for him these days in the regular season. He has won five of his past six starts, the latest being eight shutout innings in Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Working on the two-year anniversary of his surgery to reattach a lat muscle, Peavy came up short against the Royals. He allowed five runs on 12 hits over seven-plus innings, while hitting 120 pitches for the third time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello not only has two wins in as many tries against the White Sox this season, they were two of his stronger outings this year -- 14 innings of two-run ball combined. He has won his past four starts against Chicago since September 2010.
away_pitcher_note: The bad news for the lanky left-hander was that he allowed 10 hits against the Royals on Sunday. The good news is that he limited the Royals to one run over eight innings in picking up his eighth straight win.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers' top prospect got shelled in his second start against the Angels, lasting two innings and giving up seven runs on six hits. He'll look for better results in a pivotal series finale vs. Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Humber returned from a right flexor strain, making his first start since June 16 and beating the Red Sox on Tuesday. Humber gave up two runs over six innings but allowed only three singles over his final five scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez gave up five runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings in his last outing against Tampa Bay. He's given up 13 earned runs in his last two starts after 13 in his previous five. Jimenez has lost four of his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing 23 runs in 20 1/3 innings before the All-Star break, Fister has allowed two runs in 15 innings since returning. He is 2-0 with a 1.20 ERA through two second-half starts and seems fully healthy for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe continued to struggle in his last outing against the Orioles, allowing nine runs in three-plus innings. Lowe walked five and didn't strike out a batter. He is 2-6 with an 8.31 ERA in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer hurled a gem in his last start vs. the Angels, tossing seven innings, allowing one run on three hits and fanning nine. He's notched quality starts in seven of his last nine games and is 4-4 with a 5.44 ERA in his career vs. Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: McAllister pitched well in his last start against the Orioles, but was a tough-luck loser. He allowed three runs on five hits over a career-high 7 2/3 innings. He has allowed three or fewer runs and struck out at least five in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander comes into Progressive Field on a roll, having allowed three runs on 11 hits over 25 innings while going 3-0 in July. He lost a tough decision in Cleveland in May despite eight innings of two-run ball as part of a three-game series sweep.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings during his last start against Boston. He now has three quality starts in four outings since joining the rotation on June 27. The success has secured his spot in the rotation for the foreseeable future.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Porcello fell three outs shy of his first career complete game; back-to-back singles to start the ninth ended his day. Regardless, it was a great start for Porcello, who went eight-plus vs. Chicago, allowing five hits and one run.

home_pitcher_note: Alvarez allowed seven runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Red Sox during his last outing. His biggest problems this season have come in the first inning, where has has posted a 7.58 ERA in 19 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will make his Tigers debut north of the border against a Jays team that roughed him up for six runs over 3 1/3 innings June 22 in Miami. Sanchez has four quality starts in his five outings since then, including back-to-back seven-inning gem.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil allowed just two runs during six innings of work in his last start against Oakland. The two runs came on a home run by Derek Norris, as homers continue to be Cecil's Achilles' heel this season. He has now surrendered eight in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: The numbers say Fister is as good or better with two strikes this year compared to last, but the Indians touched him up for a half-dozen two-strike hits Tuesday in Cleveland, yielding three runs over seven innings and ending a three-game win streak.

home_pitcher_note: The righty has been Boston's best pitcher since the break, going 0-1 with a 2.53 ERA in three starts. In nine home starts this year, he's 5-1 with a 4.83 ERA. He's 1-1 with a 3.83 ERA in seven career starts vs. the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is 4-0 with a 2.81 ERA in his last five starts, striking out 35 batters over 32 innings over that stretch -- with three seven-inning outings. He beat Boston with a quality start on May 31 at Fenway Park, fanning six Red Sox in six frames.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett's last start was decent; he allowed Texas four runs on nine hits in seven innings. The final run was scored on a wild pitch, which snapped a 3-3 tie. Beckett is 2-5 with a 4.55 ERA in nine Fenway Park starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander was seemingly on his way to a fourth straight win and a Tigers series victory in Cleveland last Thursday when back-to-back homers set up a four-run seventh inning to beat him. He had given up three runs in his previous three starts combined.
summary: 2012-07-31 - Detroit Tigers @ Boston Red Sox (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer will try to recover from a tough outing against the Yankees, who touched him up for seven hits and six runs over four innings. Cook is 1-2 with a 4.71 ERA in four Fenway Park starts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello lost for the first time since June 20 in his last outing against the Jays. The righty, who entered the tilt with a 2.89 ERA over his past six starts, was tagged for five runs -- four of which came in the fourth inning -- to drop to 7-6.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez lost his Tigers debut, which snapped a string of three consecutive quality starts. The righty surrendered three homers, which matched a career high, issued three walks and allowed five earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson continued to be inconsistent in his last start against Minnesota, allowing 10 runs (eight earned) on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. The sinkerballer struck out two, walked two, and allowed a home run in the outing.

home_pitcher_note: Fister recorded his fourth straight quality start in a dominant effort over Toronto his last outing. Over that stretch, the righty is 3-1 with a 1.80 ERA, registering 31 strikeouts to just five walks. He has lowered his ERA to 3.77 in the process.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez allowed four runs on six hits over 6 1/3 innings in his last start against Minnesota. He struck out six, but walked three and allowed a home run. Jimenez hasn't won since July 7, and he is 1-5 in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer's loss in Boston on Monday was his first since June 23 and his highest run total allowed in nearly two months. He'll try to recover against a Tribe lineup he held down for seven innings of two-run ball with eight strikeouts last Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians plan on promoting Seddon from Triple-A Columbus to start against the Tigers on Sunday. Seddon, who hasn't pitched in the Majors since 2010 with Seattle, has gone 6-2 with a 2.66 ERA in his last 10 Triple-A starts.

home_pitcher_note: It took a torrential downpour in Boston, but Verlander's streak of 63 straight games throwing at least six innings ended in his last outing. He'll try to start a new streak vs. a Yankees team he is 0-1 with a 5.11 ERA against this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nova had one of his worst starts of the season his last time out, spoiling a five-run Yankees first by allowing seven innings the next frame and nine over five innings. He started once against Detroit this year and allowed six runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer allowed four runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings vs. Boston in his last start and picked up his eighth victory. He'll now face the Yankees at Comerica Park, where he held them to one run in six innings on June 2.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes labored through six innings his last time out, claiming he had none of his pitches, yet limited the Orioles to one run over six innings of work. He threw the second complete game of his career earlier this season in Detroit, allowing one run.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing five runs to Toronto in his Tigers debut, Sanchez rebounded with six-plus innings, allowing two runs (one earned) vs. Cleveland at home. Next he'll duel CC Sabathia and a Yankees lineup he hasn't seen since his MLB debut in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia allowed one hit through the first eight innings his last time out until a homer in the ninth tarnished an impressive line. He still went the distance against Seattle and struck out 10, allowing three runs. He's 2-0 this year against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Fister threw his first complete game as a Tiger on Saturday vs. Cleveland. After going 8-1 with a 1.79 ERA down the stretch for Detroit in 2011, Fister is getting on a similar roll, as he's 4-1 with a 1.62 ERA since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda came out on the wrong end of a pitchers' duel his last time out, allowing one run in 6 1/3 innings against the Mariners. He took a no-decision earlier this season in Detroit, limiting the Tigers to two runs over seven innings in a Detroit win.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman has won six straight decisions over six starts and one relief appearance after holding the Royals to two runs in 7 2/3 innings on Saturday. During that winning streak he has a 2.81 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer missed out on the Tigers' four-game series in Texas back in June, so this will be his first outing in Arlington since Game 6 of the ALCS. He has back-to-back nine-strikeout outings, but has given up nine runs on 17 hits over 11 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Holland is 1-3 with a 7.00 ERA in his last four starts after allowing six runs in six innings against the Royals on Saturday. During those four games, he allowed nine home runs in 27 innings. Holland is 3-4 with a 6.19 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, Verlander fanned 14 Yankees batters in eight innings and broke a two-game losing skid. The 14 K's and 132 pitches both matched career highs. He's 7-2 with a 2.10 ERA vs. Texas in his career and has never lost in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish has beaten the Tigers twice this season. He allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings in a 10-3 victory April 19 and four runs in seven innings in a 7-5 win June 26. But since that game, Darvish is 1-4 with a 7.04 ERA in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello faces a Rangers team he's had little success against. He's 2-2 with a 8.47 ERA in four career starts vs; them and has faced Texas twice this year, enduring a tough start in April but holding Texas to one run over six innings in June.

home_pitcher_note: Deduno struggled against the Indians on Tuesday, allowing four runs on five hits and five walks over four innings. He also hit a batter and struck out three. He's now issued 25 walks in 34 innings this year.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has one quality start in three outings since his trade from Miami, but a first matchup with the Twins could be his chance to add one. He gave up seven runs on as many hits over three innings against the Yankees last Wednesday in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing wasn't at his best vs. Cleveland on Wednesday, allowing six runs (four earned) on 11 hits and a walk in seven innings. But he wasn't helped much by his defense either, as the Twins had several misplays behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Fister faltered briefly in the second inning of his last start, allowing the Yankees two run. But he regrouped to throw 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision. He is 1-6 with a 4.36 ERA in seven career starts vs. the Twins and 0-2 at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: De Vries turned in the worst outing of his career against the Rays on Friday, giving up eight runs (seven earned) on seven hits over just 1 1/3 innings. He had gone at least five innings in each of his previous 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough 2010 season against the Twins, Scherzer has won both of his starts at Target Field over the last two years, including 5 1/3 innings of three-run ball in May. A victory would earn him his third straight season with at least 12 wins.

home_pitcher_note: One reason Tigers manager Jim Leyland felt comfortable extending Verlander's pitch count his past couple starts was the extra days of rest coming up. He'll have five days' rest for the O's, whom he blanked for eight innings on July 15 at Oriole Park.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter allowed only three runs on eight hits, but he lasted just five innings against the Royals on Sunday. He has given up 2.17 home runs per nine innings this season, higher than any other pitcher with at least 100 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello has a 5.40 ERA and a .329 batting average allowed over his past seven starts, yet his strikeout-to-walk rate is up, including 10 strikeouts against just two walks in August. He hasn't beaten the O's since he was a 20-year-old rookie in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Britton starts for Baltimore as he tries to rebound from his previous outing, on Aug. 7 against Seattle, in which allowed seven runs (four earned) in five innings of work, walking four in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Fister didn't get much help from his defense in his last start, with Detroit's two errors in the third against Minnesota costing him four unearned runs. But he refocused to go eight innings, allowing just five hits to pick up his seventh win.
away_pitcher_note: Although he allowed a career-high nine hits on Tuesday, Chen scattered them over six innings to surrender only one run. He has posted 13 quality starts in 24 outings this season, but has allowed five or more runs five times.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer encountered trouble in the second inning against the Twins, walking the first two hitters. But he rebounded with three straight strikeouts and finished with 10 on the way to seven shutout innings. He has won 11 of his last 14 decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Romero alllowed six runs on eight hits during his last start against the White Sox. He is now 0-9 with a 7.45 ERA over his past 10 starts, which represents the worst losing streak in the American League. He hasn't won since June 22 in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez will be pitching on eight days' rest after his spot was pushed back in Detroit's rotation, but that might not compare to the pressure from Tigers fans who have been hoping for him to be their team's big boost since his July trade from Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey continues to be plagued by the long ball. The lefty gave up three hits over six innings in his last start, but all three were homers. He has allowed eight homers over his past five starts, winning just one, and has a 7.39 ERA in that span.

home_pitcher_note: In the words of Alex Avila, Verlander pulled of a "Houdini act" in his previous start, vs. Baltimore. He walked four but held the O's to three runs on six hits through six innings. He's 2-2 with a 5.18 ERA in six career starts vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Happ shut down the Rangers in his last outing, going six strong innings. He gave up just one run on two hits in the 3-2 win. The lefty struck out eight while walking one. He is holding opposing batters to a .268 average.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello had a gem of an outing for six innings Saturday, striking out six O's, before two singles and a Chris Davis home run on a down-and-away sinker ruined it. His use of his slider and curveball for outs was a bright spot for the sinkerballer.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has struggled since being traded to the Angels, going 1-2 with a 6.19 ERA in five starts. He allowed six runs in six innings in his last outing against the Rays, but struck out eight. The right-hander has not faced the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly returns to the Tigers' rotation, at least for one start, in place of injured Doug Fister. It'll mark the rookie's first Tigers start since July 6, after which he was sidelined by an intercostal injury until he was optioned to Toledo.
away_pitcher_note: Haren hasn't gotten past the fourth inning in each of his previous two starts. He's allowed 12 runs on 12 hits over his last seven innings. Haren is winless in his past three outings, and the Angels are 2-4 in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer tossed seven innings of five-hit, one-run ball while striking out eight on Tuesday in a win over the Jays. He is now 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA in four August starts, and took over the Major League lead in strikeouts, with 186.
away_pitcher_note: Santana has been the Angels' best starter in August, going 2-0 with a 3.16 ERA in four outings. He beat the Red Sox on Tuesday, giving up two runs in 6 1/3 innings. The right-hander hasn't walked more than two in any start since July 4.

home_pitcher_note: After being on a four-game roll in which he was 3-1 and made it into the seventh inning in each start, Mendoza hit a snag last Wednesday vs. Tampa Bay. He gave up just two runs, but had command issues (four walks and a hit batter).
