home_pitcher_note: Price becomes the first pitcher other than Justin Verlander to start Opening Day for the Tigers since Kenny Rogers in 2007. In the process, he'll open arguably the biggest season of his career, a contract year as the Tigers ace.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes is coming off a career year and gets his first Opening Day start. He set an MLB strikeout-to-walk ratio record last year, striking out 186 and walking just 16 in 209 2/3 innings for an 11.63 ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez was slated to start the third game of the season before Justin Verlander's triceps strain delayed his start. Sanchez had his own health issues last year, limiting him to 21 starts, but looked strong this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco's struggles last year are well-documented, as he posted a career worst 5.38 ERA in 27 starts in his first year with the Twins. But he came into Spring Training in better shape and the Twins are counting on a bounce-back year from him.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers saw some of the best of Shane Greene during his summer stint in the Yankees' rotation, leading Detroit to give up starting prospect Robbie Ray to get him. He's a sinkerballer in an early Rick Porcello style.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson's first full year in the rotation was full of ups and downs, so he's looking to build consistency. He finished with a 4.47 ERA, but had a 1.42 ERA in his 13 wins and an 11.04 ERA in his 12 losses.

home_pitcher_note: McAllister showed impressive command and velocity throughout Spring Training, convincing Cleveland to give him another shot as a starting pitcher. The big righty has gone 19-25 with a 4.38 ERA in 72 games in parts of four seasons with the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Simon had an up-and-down spring in Tigers camp, failing to get through the fifth inning until he pitched six-plus in his next-to-last tuneup. He'll try to recapture the first-half form that made him an All-Star last year.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Opening Day start, Kluber showed why he won a Cy Young Award last year. Over 7 1/3 innings, the righty struck out seven and held Houston to two runs on three hits in 7 1/3 innings in a hard-luck loss.
away_pitcher_note: Price fell an out shy of an Opening Day shutout on Monday, settling for 8 2/3 innings against the Twins. His matchup opposite Corey Kluber is a rematch of their matchup last September in Cleveland, a Price gem and Tigers win.

home_pitcher_note: The lone lefty in Cleveland's rotation, House won one of the two available starting jobs during the spring. He made 19 appearances for the Indians last year with a 3.35 ERA in 102 innings. House posted a 2.53 ERA in his 10 second-half starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lobstein steps in for Justin Verlander and finds a favorable matchup against a lefty-heavy Indians lineup. He struck out 10 over 5 1/3 innings of two-run ball his last visit to Cleveland last Sept. 2, taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Cole draws home opener honors and takes a good personal history into the assignment against the Tigers. He has a 4-1 Interleague record in six starts, with 39 strikeouts in 38 1/3 innings, and an 11-6 career mark in PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez looked a lot like the 2013 AL ERA champ in 6 2/3 shutout innings against the Twins Wednesday in Detroit. He allowed just three hits, walked two and struck out six. He has allowed a .204 career average to the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty was drawn back to Pittsburgh, and to PNC Park: He went 13-10 with a sub-3.00 ERA there as a Pirate from 2012-13, and even last season, with the Phillies, he had one of his finer efforts vs. the Bucs (five hits in seven innings).
away_pitcher_note: Not even a 3 1/2-hour rain delay could throw off Greene against the Twins, tossing eight innings with an unearned run on four hits. He faced the Pirates in Spring Training and gave up three runs, two earned, over 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Making a second start delayed by the birth of his fourth child, Liriano faces a familiar AL Central foe. The former Twin is 5-9 lifetime versus the Tigers with an ERA (5.82) that is his highest against any opponent he has faced 10-plus times.
away_pitcher_note: Simon had a gem going in Cleveland last Friday before five straight hits and three sixth-inning runs knocked him out. He's 3-4 with a 3.50 ERA in 18 meetings with the Pirates, more games than he has against any other opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Price was chased in the sixth inning Saturday in Cleveland, having tossed 100-plus pitches without getting through six for just the second time as a Tiger. He tossed 8 2/3 innings against the White Sox in September.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija built upon a rocky season debut, striking out six and walking none in seven innings of work vs. the Twins. He did still allow four runs, though, and his ERA sits at 6.23 after two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez gave up three home runs in a game for the first time since the 2013 AL Division Series against Oakland, courtesy of the Pirates on Monday in Pittsburgh. Trend or anomaly, he won't have it easier against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Sale is making his second start after fracturing his foot at home in late February. He showed no rust in his season debut, throwing 72 of 98 pitches for strikes and allowing one run on five hits in six innings of work, striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: No Tiger has ever gone three starts into a season without giving up an earned run. Greene, who has allowed one unearned run over 16 innings, has a shot. He shut out the Pirates with eight innings of three-hit ball on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana continues to keep the opposition in the ballpark, having allowed just one homer this season over 11 innings after giving up 10 in 200 1/3 innings in 2014. Quintana will work on regular rest with two off-days this week.

home_pitcher_note: Simon has been everything the Tigers hoped for through his first two starts. He allowed just two hits in eight scoreless innings at Pittsburgh in his last time out, and he has a 2-0 record with a 2.03 ERA this year.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia has shown encouraging signs early despite a pair of losses, recording 15 K's against 1 walk in 2 starts while permitting just 1 homer. He has not faced the Tigers since April 7, 2013, in Detroit, when he hurled 7 scoreless innings for a win.

home_pitcher_note: Lobstein will make his second start this year in place of the injured Justin Verlander. In his first start, Lobstein gave up three earned runs on eight hits over five innings, picking up the win at Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi held the Orioles to two runs and eight hits in his last start, striking out nine, but burned through 101 pitches in five innings. He will try to be more economical in this outing. Eovaldi has faced the Tigers once and got a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Price shut down the White Sox his last time out, giving up four hits and one earned run over eight innings with nine strikeouts. A solo home run was the first earned run Price has allowed in three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Warren was disappointed with his most recent outing, lasting just four innings against the Rays in St. Petersburg. He served up two homers in the brief effort and said that he must be more consistent with his breaking balls against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up nine runs over 3 1/3 innings against the White Sox, Sanchez has already allowed more home runs this year (five) than he did all of last season (four). Sanchez is 1-2 with a 7.71 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Tanaka turned in his most dominant performance of the season Saturday, handcuffing the Rays on two hits over seven scoreless innings with eight strikeouts and no walks. He retired 15 straight at one point and is facing the Tigers for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Not since Frank Tanana in 1988 has a Tiger won his first four starts to open a season. Greene can do that, but he'll have to quiet an Indians lineup that offers up plenty of left-handed hitters, who challenged Greene last year.
away_pitcher_note: Salazar was dominant in his season debut, throwing six innings with 10 K's in a 4-2 victory over the Twins. Salazar gave up two runs, but the second scored on a solo homer by Kurt Suzuki in the seventh inning. Salazar left with a two-run lead.

home_pitcher_note: Simon had a gem going against the Indians on April 10 in Cleveland before five consecutive sixth-inning hits led to three runs and an early exit. He has tossed 15 1/3 innings of one-run ball over two starts since then.

Lobstein has survived early game struggles to settle in and limit damage in both of his starts, including April 12 at Cleveland. The Tigers are hoping for more of that in the rematch against a lefty-heavy Indians lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Carrasco allowed just one run in five innings Tuesday vs. the White Sox in his first outing since being hit in the face with a line drive on Apr. 14. He left that outing after just 60 pitches because he was getting tight in the cold weather.

home_pitcher_note: Milone was saddled with a no-decision against the Royals on Tuesday, giving up four runs on five hits and four walks over 5 2/3 innings. He left with a two-run lead, but the bullpen couldn't hold it.
away_pitcher_note: Price gave up more runs to the Yankees (eight) than he did in his previous three starts this season combined, in addition to 10 hits over just 2 1/3 innings. However, he fell an out shy of a shutout of the Twins on Opening Day.

home_pitcher_note: The righty turned in his strongest outing since joining the Twins in 2013, tossing seven scoreless innings against the Royals last Wednesday. He scattered four hits and two walks to earn his first win since Aug. 20, 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez took a no-decision out of 6 1/3 innings of one-hit ball against the Yankees thanks to a run-scoring balk. He has a stingy track record against the Twins, including 6 2/3 scoreless innings on April 8 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes took a tough loss in Seattle despite going the distance with eight innings of two-run ball. He struck out nine and did not walk a batter. The righty is 7-7 with a 4.07 ERA in 15 appearances (13 starts) against Detroit in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Greene paid in sinkerballer fashion for pitches up against the Indians, allowing eight runs on nine hits over four-plus innings. He gave up an unearned run on four hits over eight innings against the Twins on April 9 in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Duffy has a curious history against the Tigers -- he's had five quality starts in nine tries against them but is just 1-6. He has a 3.42 career ERA against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Simon could become the ninth Tiger in the last 100 years to win each of his first five starts to begin a season. His latest victory came with 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball Saturday against the Indians at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Young could make his first start as a Royal against the Tigers. Young has been used in long relief so far, but the Royals need a spot starter for Edinson Volquez, who is serving a five-game suspension. Young is 1-0 with a 1.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: With Justin Verlander on the shelf, Lobstein has settled into the Tigers' rotation. Last time out, he overcame his first-inning woes by simulating an inning in bullpen warmups, helping him toss seven strong innings against Cleveland Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is coming off his five-game suspension for trying to throw a punch vs. the White Sox on April 23. Volquez was good for five innings last Sunday against Chicago, allowing no runs. Then he gave up five runs (one earned) in the sixth, in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Price took a step forward in a sturdy outing against the Twins on Monday, but he still wasn't thrilled with the results. "I pitched good enough to get by, but I've got to get better," he said after pitching 6 1/3 innings in a 5-4 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie takes the mound in the finale of the series with Detroit. Manager Ned Yost opted to flip Guthrie and Jason Vargas in the rotation so Guthrie would get the Tigers. Guthrie beat the Tigers last Sept. 21 in a must-win game for the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Sanchez limited the Twins to one run over the first six innings, but tired a bit in the seventh and gave up two runs to take his third loss of the season. Still, he has posted back-to-back quality starts after two rough outings.

home_pitcher_note: Baltimore scored six runs in the first inning off Samardzija and then cruised to victory in the Wednesday afternoon contest played in a fan-less ballpark. Samardzija held Detroit to one run in eight innings on April 17.
away_pitcher_note: Brad Ausmus took enough interest after back-to-back rough outings that he caught Greene's bullpen session Friday to get a better idea how Greene's pitching. He has given up 15 runs over 8 1/3 innings in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: As pitching coach Don Cooper said, the story with Sale is when he has a bad start, as he did against the Twins on Thursday when he allowed a career-high nine runs over three innings, including seven in one inning, is that it's a rare occurance.
away_pitcher_note: Simon's perfect start came crashing down last Thursday with six runs on nine hits over 4 1/3 innings to the Royals for his first loss as a Tiger after four straight wins. He did not face the White Sox in Detroit two weeks ago.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana has allowed three earned runs over his last 14 innings and two starts combined, but he has a no-decision and a loss to show for his work. He is 12-13 lifetime at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Lobstein recovered from a three-run first inning to allow a run on six hits over his final 6 1/3 innings last Friday at Kansas City. By staying on turn, Lobstein faces the White Sox rather than a Royals rematch in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Price threw a five-hitter against the Royals last Saturday night at Kauffman Stadium, falling a Lorenzo Cain ninth-inning home run shy of his first shutout with the Tigers. The lefty doesn't have to wait long for the rematch.
away_pitcher_note: Ventura makes his first start since serving a seven-game suspension for an in-game altercation on April 23. The righty is 2-0 against the Tigers with a 3.12 ERA. He has pitched once at Comerica Park -- allowing three runs in seven innings in a win.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez retired his first 15 batters in order in 7 1/3 quality innings last Sunday at Kansas City, improving his record to 6-2 with a 1.40 ERA in eight meetings with the Royals. His mid-April struggles with home runs appear over.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie faced the Tigers last Sunday in Kansas City and got roughed up for six runs and 11 hits in six innings. The right-hander is 2-5 with a 4.53 ERA in his career at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Greene has allowed 20 runs on 23 hits over 11 innings in his past three starts, walking nine and striking out 10. His ERA, in turn, has jumped from 0.39 to 5.56. He missed the Royals in last week's series.
away_pitcher_note: Young is 3-0 in his career with a 1.41 ERA against the Tigers. He's had two career starts at Comerica Park with a 2.08 ERA. Young threw five no-hit innings against Detroit in his previous start on May 1.

home_pitcher_note: Simon won his first four starts as a Tiger, but he has struggled in two outings since, allowing nine runs on 14 hits over 9 1/3 innings against the Royals and White Sox. He didn't face the Twins in either of their series in April.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson was solid again, tossing six scoreless innings against the A's on Wednesday to get his second straight win. He's now thrown 17 straight scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Only one member of the Tigers' rotation has lasted at least seven innings in each of his last three starts. That would be Lobstein, who tossed 7 2/3 innings with an unearned run last Thursday against the White Sox in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco took the victory Thursday, despite giving up four runs over five innings pitched. He has yet to pitch past the fifth inning in any of his three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez gave up six runs in his first four innings Saturday against the Royals, yet lasted six innings in just 99 pitches. He got a win and a loss in two quality starts against the Twins in April, albeit in colder weather.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched well again on Friday, giving up just two runs over seven innings in a win over the Indians. He's gone at least seven frames in three of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez has allowed seven runs in each of his last two starts. He has drawn some criticism from his manager for not controlling his emotions well enough and trying to overthrow when he gets into tight spots.
away_pitcher_note: After three miserable starts, Greene got back to his groundout ways Sunday and quieted the Royals, who hit 10 consecutive groundouts in a stretch of 15 outs. Greene got a no-decision for eight innings of one-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Lyons was much-improved in his second start for the Cards, and that had much to do with his fastball command. Lyons won his first two starts for the club in 2013, but has been winless in 12 starts since.
away_pitcher_note: Price will get a couple extra days to treat his right hamstring after suffering a mild strain in his last start against the Royals last Friday, when he slipped on a bat behind home plate. He has never faced the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has fanned 25 batters over 19 innings in his last three starts while posting a 1-1 record. He struggled against the Cubs on May 6 but rebounded by earning a win at Cleveland on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: After beating the Cardinals twice in three starts during the NL Central race for the Reds last year, Simon returns to St. Louis in a Tigers uniform, hoping to build on 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball Tuesday against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Lobstein's stretch of starts with seven-plus innings ended Wednesday with six runs on seven hits over 2 1/3 innings against the Twins. He'll face a Brewers lineup struggling mightily this season against left-handed pitching.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers retired the first 11 batters in his most recent outing before an error and an infield hit allowed the next two men to reach base. He's produced 49 strikeouts in 35 1/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers have 51 hits over 37 1/3 innings against Sanchez, but he hasn't faced them since 2012, before his trade to Detroit. He tossed eight innings of one-run ball with nine strikeouts against the Twins in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson had never surrendered multiple home runs in any of his first 18 Major League starts, but he's allowed a combined five over his last two outings. He's 0-2 with a 7.07 ERA in three starts on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Greene pitched five scoreless innings against the Cardinals on Friday before having to leave early with mild ulnar tendinitis. Greene underwent an MRI on Saturday that came back clean. He has given up one run on his past 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse carried a 7.03 ERA into the Brewers' road trip and lowered it to 5.85 with eight outstanding innings against the Mets. By Bill James' "game score," it was one of the eight best outings of Lohse's career.

home_pitcher_note: Price survived three solo homers in St. Louis to get a no-decision over 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball last Saturday. He'll face an Astros lineup among the MLB leaders in home runs, though he gets them at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is coming off a season-high 10-strikeout performance Saturday against Toronto to snap a two-game losing streak. A key will be the first inning. He has a 12.38 ERA in the first inning of his starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Simon remains winless since April 25, taking a 2-1 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday night despite six innings of two-run ball. He has nine walks over 18 2/3 innings in May after walking just six batters over five starts in April.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros are 7-1 in games started by McHugh this year. He's 5-1 with a 4.09 ERA that's skewed by his May 12 start vs. the Giants, in which he gave up a season-high seven earned runs. Five of eight starts have been quality.

home_pitcher_note: Lobstein recovered from a rough start to pitch 6 2/3 quality innings, recording 13 ground-ball outs in defeat. He'll face an Astros lineup that has generally struggled against lefties though is hitting for power along the way.
away_pitcher_note: This will be McCullers' second Major League start after coming up from Double-A. The 21-year-old made his debut on Monday against the A's and allowed one run and three walks, while striking out five batters in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up three consecutive home runs Tuesday to the Brewers, raising his total to nine on the season, Sanchez meets up with an Astros lineup that is among the MLB leaders in home runs. He has paid for leaving pitches up.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander has worked at least six innings in seven consecutive games, allowing two runs and seven hits Tuesday for his fifth quality start of the season. His 3.99 ERA is his lowest through eight starts since 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Hahn will look to snap a career-high three-game losing streak, which includes his last start in which he surrendered three runs on five hits and two walks in six innings. In four home starts this season, he is 0-1 with a 3.52 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Athletics have had a rough time offensively in May, but they have enough of an arsenal from the left side to make things miserable for Greene, who's giving up a .314 average and .842 OPS to left-handed batters this season.

home_pitcher_note: Chavez will try to secure his first career win against the Tigers. In nine appearances (two starts) against Detroit, he is 0-3 with a 9.90 ERA. Chavez owns a 0-1 record in Oakland this year, posting a 4.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Price has just four decisions in his first nine starts, an oddity for a pitcher who usually works deep into games. A combination of seventh-inning exits, big innings and pitching duels have left him with more no-decisions.

home_pitcher_note: After Kazmir won each of his first two starts, the A's have won just one of his past seven starts. He has posted a quality start in all but one of his home starts this season, and in 15 career starts against the Tigers, he is 5-5 with a 3.51 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: With the Tigers placing Alfredo Simon on the bereavement list late Tuesday night, Ryan was recalled from Triple-A Toledo. Ryan has never faced the A's, and he last pitched on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson will open a four-game series against the Tigers looking to rebound from two straight four-run outings. He hopes to return to the form that saw him post three straight starts of at least seven innings and two earned runs or fewer to open May.
away_pitcher_note: Farmer, who made two fill-in starts with the Tigers last August, will get his first Major League callup this season to fill injured Kyle Lobstein's rotation spot. He's 5-1 with a 2.98 ERA in nine starts for Triple-A Toledo.

home_pitcher_note: Santiago has notched four consecutive quality starts but took a loss against the Red Sox in his latest outing after allowing three runs in 6 2/3 innings. The left-hander is 3-3 with a 2.47 ERA on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez produced an odd line in his last outing, allowing seven runs in 5 2/3 innings while striking out 11. He retired 12 of 13 at one point, but two big innings was his undoing.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough start to the season, the veteran Weaver has turned things around recently with four strong starts in a row -- the latest a 6 2/3-inning, one-run, seven-strikeout performance against the Padres on May 25 in a 4-3 Angels walk-off win.
away_pitcher_note: Greene took a shutout into the sixth inning and ended up allowing four runs on eight hits in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Shoemaker will wrap up the month of May for the Angels in the series finale against the Tigers. In his last start, the right-hander threw seven scoreless innings against the Padres to rebound from an eight-run outing against the Blue Jays on May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Price threw seven stellar innings in a 1-0 victory over the Athletics on Tuesday night. He's been stellar all year, with the exception of one bad game against the New York Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Simon is expected to return from the bereavement list following the passing of his father. He was scheduled to face the A's last Wednesday before his dad fell gravely ill, prompting him to return home Tuesday night.
away_pitcher_note: Graveman left the A's on Sunday because of a family issue, but manager Bob Melvin said the right-hander should be ready for his start Tuesday. Graveman was recalled from Triple-A Nashville on May 23, and is 1-0 with a 2.31 ERA since returning.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez said confidence and conviction were his biggest adjustments after a barrage of home runs two starts ago. He'll try to keep that up against the A's, but he's just 2-3 with a 6.81 ERA in seven home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Gray has been one of baseball's most dominant pitchers, posting a 6-2 record and 1.82 ERA. He most recently tossed eight innings and gave up two runs in a 6-2 win over the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: No pitcher in modern Major League history had given up five homers in an outing of just five outs or fewer before Greene on Saturday night against the Angels. He lost to the A's with a four-run sixth inning last week in Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Hahn most recently gave up three earned runs in the A's 5-3 loss to the Yankees on Saturday. He has thrown more than 100 pitches in six straight starts and has gone at least five innings every start this season.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana has made five quality starts over his past seven trips to the mound but has a 1-5 record during that stretch. He has an 11.00 ERA in two starts against the Tigers this season and a 4.32 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Ryan didn't arrive in Oakland with enough time to make a spot start last Wednesday, though he pitched three-plus innings in relief. He has ample time to prepare for the White Sox in Justin Verlander's rotation slot.

home_pitcher_note: The first White Sox complete game of the 2015 season went to the veteran left-hander, who shut out the Astros on 10 hits, including four doubles and one triple. Danks topped 1,000 career strikeouts in his fifth quality start of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Price gets an extra day's rest coming off a 121-pitch outing last Sunday at Anaheim, his highest pitch count as a Tiger. He tossed eight innings of one-run ball with nine strikeouts against the White Sox on April 17 in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The defense didn't help Samardzija in his last start against the Rangers, but his location also was slightly off by his own admission. Samardzija has been hit hard in the first inning this season, allowing 16 runs on 23 hits in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Simon had a one-hit shutout through six innings Tuesday despite five walks before an A's seventh-inning comeback knocked him out. He gave up three runs on five hits in five innings against the White Sox on May 6 in Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez still is seeking some consistency. Two of his last three starts have been shaky, including his Wednesday outing against the A's (seven innings, four runs). Before that, he had a solid outing at the Angels (seven innings, two runs).
away_pitcher_note: Lester lost his first game in June, getting roughed up for six runs in five innings. He is 2-4 in his career against Detroit with a 4.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Greene, who has been in danger of losing his rotation spot, faces the Cubs -- a right-handed-heavy lineup. He has not gotten out of the fifth inning in his past two starts, lasting 4 1/3 against the A's on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta was brilliant last time out, tossing six innings of one-run ball in a win against the Nationals. He has 27 strikeouts compared to four walks over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Price hasn't won a start after a complete game since July 2013. He'll get his chance to change that against a Cleveland squad that knocked him out in the sixth inning for a no-decision back on April 11 at Progressive Field.
away_pitcher_note: After a pair of shaky outings, in which Salazar (6-1, 3.50 ERA) walked seven batters, he rebounded with a dominant 10-strikeout, one-run performance vs. Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander makes his season debut after missing 2 1/2 months with a right triceps strain. He had nine strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings against the Indians' Triple-A affiliate, the Columbus Clippers, in a rehab start last Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Carrasco (7-5, 4.35 ERA) is coming off a start that snapped a six-game streak of throwing at least six innings with six or more strikeouts and two or fewer walks. He ranks 10th in baseball in strikeout percentage.

home_pitcher_note: The Indians tend to be a bad matchup for Simon, but he used his splitter to beat them twice in April on his way to a 4-0 start. He's had a rougher go since then but presents a tougher matchup than in previous seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Kluber (3-7, 3.53 ERA) is coming off another tough-luck loss after allowing just two earned runs against Seattle his last time out. Kluber's average run support of 2.46 runs per game is the fourth-lowest in the MLB.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez has some momentum going after 7 2/3 shutout innings against the Cubs, but his recent ability to keep the ball in the park will be tested by a Cincinnati lineup that ranks second in the National League in home runs.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander earned his first career win last time out against the Phillies, allowing two runs over six innings at Great American Ball Park on Wednesday. He's walked five and struck out five in 11 innings over his two big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ryan, who made a spot start for Justin Verlander earlier this month, steps in again for the recently demoted Shane Greene. He gives the Tigers another lefty starter against Joey Votto, not that it makes much difference with the slugger.
away_pitcher_note: Lorenzen struggled in his last outing, surrendering a season-high five earned runs, but he also posted a season-high six strikeouts. Since being called up, Lorenzen has served as one of the Reds' more consistent pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto gave up more than three runs for the first time since May 9 in his last outing, but he still continued to keep batters off base. His 0.95 WHIP ranks among the best in the game as he continues to shoulder the load on a depleted staff.
away_pitcher_note: Not since Jack Morris 25 years ago has a Tigers starter tossed a complete game in three consecutive starts. Price has a chance. He also could join Rick Porcello as the only Tigers since Morris in 1986 to toss back-to-back shutouts.

Verlander hopes to stretch out his arm a little longer into the game after lasting five innings over 87 pitches last Saturday against Cleveland. He'll also hope to keep the ball down at hitter-friendly Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Warren makes his 13th start of the season, looking for his third career win over the Tigers. In his last outing, in Baltimore, Warren gave up three runs on six hits in 4 2/3 innings for the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander hopes to stretch out his arm a little longer into the game after lasting five innings over 87 pitches last Saturday against Cleveland. He'll also hope to keep the ball down at hitter-friendly Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi struggled mightily in his last outing against his former Miami club, unable to get out of the first inning and surrendering eight earned runs on nine hits. Eovaldi is 1-0 in his career in two starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Simon has done an exemplary job of avoiding home runs lately, but he'll have a challenge doing so at Yankee Stadium. His combination of changeup and splitter has kept hitters off-balance over the last few starts.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka will look for his first career win against the Tigers after having just one appearance against them. In his last outing at Miami, Tanaka took the loss after throwing seven innings of nine-hit, two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez hasn't given up a run in 20 2/3 innings, including a two-hit shutout in his last start on Monday against the Reds. But the combination of Yankees hitters and a cozy ballpark will test Sanchez's ability to avoid home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer picked up a win in Wrigley Field on Tuesday by blanking the Cubs over seven innings, finishing with seven strikeouts and three walks. He has a 2.51 ERA in his past seven starts for the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Ryan paid for three solo homers to the Reds on Tuesday, but he'll get a chance at redemption against an Indians lineup with several left-handed hitters. He tossed six innings with an unearned run against Triple-A Columbus April 16.

home_pitcher_note: Salazar (6-2, 3.56 ERA) had his last start shortened to 4 2/3 innings (three runs, two earned) due to a lengthy rain delay on Thursday against the Cubs. The right-hander has gone 2-1 with a 3.03 ERA in his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Price was on a roll covering innings with back-to-back complete games before a rain delay knocked him out after five innings on Wednesday at Cincinnati. He shut out Cleveland on seven hits with eight strikeouts June 12 in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Over his past six turns, Carrasco (8-6, 4.35 ERA) has gone 4-2 with a 3.62 ERA for Cleveland. He took a loss Friday after yielding three runs on 10 hits with five strikeouts and no walks in 6 2/3 innings against Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Justin Verlander was scratched from this start with mid-back stiffness, and Farmer was called up from Triple-A Toledo to make the start.

home_pitcher_note: Statistically, Simon's start last Saturday at Yankee Stadium was his worst of the season, with seven runs on eight hits over just 2 2/3 innings. Yet the control battles behind it date to a few outings before that.
away_pitcher_note: Rodon picked up his fifth quality start in six outings his last time out, allowing two runs on four hits in six innings of work. He struck out five in his last start, marking the sixth game in eight starts that he has thrown five or fewer strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Though Sanchez saw his scoreless streak end at 21 2/3 innings with two home runs, he still has given up just three runs over 23 2/3 innings in his last three outings, all of them victories. He has been tougher at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana posted his 10th quality start last time out, allowing two runs and five hits across seven innings, but picked up another no-decision. The White Sox average 2.21 runs of support per his start -- the lowest among all qualified MLB starters.

home_pitcher_note: Ryan pitched in relief Wednesday on his day to throw a side session, but manager Brad Ausmus said it wouldn't affect his status. He threw his best outing against the White Sox on June 5 with seven innings of two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks took full credit for a shellacking on Monday against the Twins. He gave up nine runs -- five earned -- and was unable to pitch over a costly Alexei Ramirez error.

home_pitcher_note: Price is 3-0 with a 1.21 ERA in four starts this month, including a complete-game five-hitter with 11 strikeouts against the White Sox on June 6. He has allowed two runs in 17 innings with 20 strikeouts against Chicago this year.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija has given up 19 of his 52 runs in the first inning. He gave up a solo home run in the first in his last start, against Minnesota, but settled down for his third consecutive quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander, who missed his last scheduled start with a stiff back, threw a bullpen session on Saturday without any issues, paving the way for his return.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will look to rebound from allowing five runs in 4 2/3 innings to the Reds on June 24. He needs to correct mechanical issues that had him throwing across his body, flattening his pitches. He has a career 6-1 record in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: According to manager Brad Ausmus, Simon has been the most consistent pitcher for the Tigers this year, but the righty has struggled lately, allowing 12 runs over his last two outings -- including three homers.
away_pitcher_note: Bouncing back from his first sour start of the season, Burnett turned in his 12th quality start on June 25 and continues his All-Star campaign in a park that has been tough on him (6.26 ERA in five starts, despite 3-2 record).

home_pitcher_note: Ryan was supposed to pitch Saturday until a rainout and Justin Verlander's return forced the Tigers to push back his start. The lefty has started three games this year, but his last outing was 12 pitches in relief on June 24.
away_pitcher_note: Dealing with a losing record despite his 1.01 WHIP and .189 opponents' average, Liriano could find some reward under ideal conditions: ERAs of 2.30 ERA on the road and 2.25 in daylight, balanced by the 5-10 record vs. Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Homers continue to plague Sanchez, who's allowed 18 this year, including five in his last two starts. Manager Brad Ausmus believes opponents have generally been lucky to capitalize on a handful of poorly-located pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Hutchison not been pitched well on the road; in eight starts, he has an 8.92 ERA with opponents hitting a stunning .356. In eight home starts, Hutchison has a 2.12 ERA with a .218 opponents' average.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty veteran had an uncharacteristically poor outing last Sunday, allowing four earned runs for the first time since May 8. Price has allowed three runs or fewer in all but four starts and hasn't taken a loss since May.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer has just one win since May 22, despite owning a respectable 3.98 ERA over those seven starts. He allowed three runs over six innings in his last start, against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: The 2011 AL Cy Young Award winner will be making his fourth start this year after missing time with a triceps strain and then back stiffness. Verlander lasted six-plus innings on Tuesday night, walking five batters for the first time since '13.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada is coming off the shortest start of his career after allowing four runs over 2 1/3 innings to Boston. He also snapped a 16 2/3 innings streak without having surrendered a home run as both Jackie Bradley Jr. and David Ortiz took him deep.

home_pitcher_note: The 34-year-old returns from a 10-week stint on the DL after starting the year 0-1 with a 6.61 ERA in 3 starts. He was 37-19 with a 2.97 ERA in 77 starts the previous three seasons, including 1-1, 2.35 in four games vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has allowed 18 runs on 29 hits over his last three games, the latest a 15-hit barrage against the Pirates on Wednesday. He's also struggled away from Comerica Park, posting a 5.03 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing 22-year-old has been on point his past seven starts (6-1, 1.68 ERA with three walks and 51 strikeouts). He's gone 27 1/3 innings without a walk after opening the season 1-5 with a 7.33 ERA with 23 walks in nine games.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has made four starts for the Tigers this year, the latest Thursday's four-plus-inning outing, in which he allowed two runs. Ryan struggled with command that afternoon, throwing just 47 strikes on 94 pitches and walking five.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty ended a streak of nine straight starts without a win with a 9-5 victory over the A's on Friday, when he gave up three runs over six innings. That run support was welcome for Happ, who is 4-5 with a 3.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander flirted with a no-hitter on Friday, tossing 7 1/3 innings before allowing his first hit. Sanchez has endured an up-and-down season, mixing outstanding starts with six outings in which he has allowed multiple home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey has struggled to an 8.50 ERA over his past five starts. He's also been unable to get past four innings in three of those outings, including his last two.
away_pitcher_note: Detroit's ace hasn't taken a loss over his last six starts. Price has surrendered more than three earned runs in a contest just three times this year, and the Tigers are 14-3 overall when he starts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana was sharp in his Twins debut, giving up two runs on three hits over eight innings in a no-decision against the Royals. He showed no signs of rust after his 80-game suspension for the use of a performance-enhancing drug.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's mechanics suffered when he pitched from the stretch Sunday, and he surrendered seven runs in the loss. Verlander hopes to regain his consistency during his fifth start this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes has been solid over his last six starts with a 2.95 ERA. He gave up just two runs over 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Orioles last Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Simon picked up his first win in three weeks on Monday at Seattle, but he gave up five runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings along the way. He topped the Twins with 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball on May 12 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson has been on a roll recently, as he's 3-0 with a 1.74 ERA over his last three starts. He's coming off a strong start against the Orioles on Tuesday, giving up two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greene will be called up to make his first start in the Majors since June 10. He has a 3.42 ERA in five starts at Triple-A Toledo, and manager Brad Ausmus said Greene has been using his changeup more.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez gets the first start of the second half for the Tigers in part because manager Brad Ausmus didn't want the right-hander to have too much time off. Sanchez, who last pitched July 8, has won five of his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez took a no-decision in his last start, in which he tossed five scoreless innings, allowing seven hits and three walks while striking out five in Minnesota. He has allowed just one run over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Price, who earned the win for the AL in the All-Star Game, finished the first half 9-2 with a 2.38 ERA. He won his last start before of the break, giving up two runs -- none earned -- in eight innings against the Twins on July 9.
away_pitcher_note: Tillman posted his fifth consecutive quality start in Interleague Play in his last outing, going six innings while giving up two runs and striking out six in a no-decision vs. the Nats. The Orioles have won six of Tillman's last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander was sharp July 10 against Minnesota, mixing speeds and using his curveball and slider effectively in a 7 2/3-inning no-decision. After coming back from a triceps injury in June, he's still looking for his first win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez went five-plus innings, allowing six runs, including two homers, in his last start against the Nationals. It was the second time in his last three starts the right-hander gave up six runs.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is the only starter in baseball this year to allow five or more earned runs in five consecutive appearances. Simon has surrendered 33 hits over his last three starts, spanning just 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Happ allowed four runs while lasting just four innings in his last start vs. the Tigers on July 8, then went to the Minors to open up a roster spot prior to the All-Star break. He’s 1-0 with a 3.66 ERA in four games against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Greene has made one appearance since spending a month at Triple-A Toledo. He yielded seven runs over 4 2/3 frames against the Twins on July 12 and has allowed four earned runs or more in each of his past five Major League starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old is 6-2 with a 3.03 ERA and 51 strikeouts with four walks over his last nine starts, including a no-decision against the Tigers on July 7 (6 hits, 5 runs in 5 innings). This will be his first time pitching in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing 18 home runs through 16 starts this season, Sanchez has surrendered only one over his three outings in July. The righty scattered eight hits over six innings against the Orioles on Friday for his sixth consecutive winning decision.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old rookie has pitched well since his June callup, with the fourth-lowest ERA (2.51) of any Mariners pitcher in his first nine career starts. He’s 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA in four road outings and struck out nine last time out vs. the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit's ace allowed only one run over seven innings and matched a season high with 12 strikeouts Saturday against Baltimore, but he took his first loss since May 31. He has lasted at least six innings in all but one start since April.
away_pitcher_note: After missing 10 weeks with a strained lat muscle, Iwakuma gave up four homers in five innings in a no-decision vs. the Tigers in Seattle on July 6. But in two starts since, he’s 2-0 with a 1.32 ERA with wins over the Angels and Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello's first start after the All-Star break mirrored his first-half struggles. He had shaky command, but limited the damage, allowing three runs on four hits in five innings. He’s allowed 18 home runs on the season, fourth-most in the AL.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander, who missed the first two months of the season with a triceps strain, says he's been experiencing mechanical issues when pitching from the stretch. He allowed seven runs over 3 2/3 innings Sunday against Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer will be recalled from Triple-A Pawtucket to start for the second time in less than a week. Last time out in Anaheim, Wright gave up six hits and six runs over five innings in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Simon has gone seven outings without a quality start, and four outings in July without making it through the sixth inning. He has allowed 34 runs, 32 of them earned, on 53 hits over 28 1/3 innings in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty will try to recover from a tough first start after the break, when he was shelled for six hits and seven runs over 1 2/3 innings. This is Rodriguez’s first career start against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: A stretch of eight consecutive Mariners retired was something to build on for Greene in his last start Tuesday, but even many of his outs were hit hard on a night when he gave up five runs on six hits over 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Karns pitched well Tuesday night when he held the Phillies scoreless on three hits and two walks while striking out four in five innings to pick up his fifth win. He is 2-4 with a 3.71 ERA in 11 starts at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez is 7-0 over his last eight starts. He has pitched into the seventh inning in nine of his last 10 starts, reinforcing his front-line role in Detroit’s rotation.

home_pitcher_note: In his fourth start back from an oblique injury, Odorizzi will look to get back to pitching deep into games. In 11 starts before getting injured he pitched six innings or more in all 11 outings, but has been unable to reach the sixth since returning.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty ace has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 11 of his last 12 starts, including Thursday's extra-inning loss to Seattle. Though the rest of the rotation has been inconsistent, Price has tossed eight innings seven times.

home_pitcher_note: Archer is 0-2 with a 4.29 ERA in four July starts after receiving a no-decision in his last start vs. Baltimore despite allowing one run. In three career starts vs. Detroit, he is 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's winless stretch extended to seven games after Saturday's no-decision, but the right-hander still impressed by spinning eight frames of one-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is 2-0 following the All-Star break, going 7 2/3 innings in his last start against the Rays while giving up just one run on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Simon left his last start Saturday at Boston with a groin strain, but is expected to be able to make his scheduled start. He has never faced the Orioles, the team that called him up for his Major League debut back in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Chen saw his streak of six consecutive quality starts snapped in his last start against the Rays, when he gave up two runs on six hits in a 5 1/3-inning performance.
away_pitcher_note: Farmer takes over the rotation spot of Shane Greene, who was shifted to the bullpen earlier in the week. Farmer made spot starts for Detroit on May 28 and June 24, taking losses in both without getting through the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman posted a career-high 7 2/3 innings in his last start against the Braves, which was his second scoreless start of the season and fourth of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed three runs on eight hits and two walks with six strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings on Monday against the Rays. It marked his first loss since June 3; he had been 7-0 over the eight previous starts.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up two runs on four hits in a 25-pitch first inning, Jimenez responded by throwing six scoreless innings while walking three batters for his ninth quality start of the season vs. Atlanta on July 28.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will make his Tigers debut three days after joining the team as the centerpiece of the David Price trade with Toronto. It will be his first big league outing since April 30, part of an up-and-down month in the Blue Jays' rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The case can be made that Verlander became the Tigers' ace again with David Price dealt to Toronto. He pitched like one his last start with eight innings of one-run ball and 10 strikeouts Wednesday to beat the Rays and Chris Archer.
away_pitcher_note: Duffy (4-5, 4.28 ERA) takes the hill to open a three-game set at Detroit to finish off a 10-game road trip. Duffy struggled in his last start, a 5-2 loss to the Blue Jays on Thursday. He gave up all five runs over six innings, allowing three homers.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd, recently acquired in the David Price deal, will make his Tigers debut Wednesday in place of Buck Farmer, who took a comebacker off his left knee in his last start, Saturday at Baltimore, but stayed in the game and said he’d be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto will make his second start in a Royals uniform after a solid debut in Toronto last Friday night. He left with a 6-3 lead after six innings, but in a rarity, the bullpen couldn’t hold the lead and the righty took a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: The home run bug bit Sanchez again Saturday in Baltimore, this time for a pair of home runs in a six-run, 6 2/3-inning performance. He has lost back-to-back starts since winning seven decisions over an eight-start span.
away_pitcher_note: Ventura is coming off a rough outing at Toronto last Saturday -- seven innings, six hits and five runs. But the right-hander held on long enough to witness the Royals rally for a thrilling 7-6 win.

home_pitcher_note: Norris dazzled in his Tigers debut with 7 1/3 innings of one-run ball last Sunday at Baltimore. He’ll make his Comerica Park debut against a Red Sox lineup that he faced in his Major League debut last September at Fenway Park.
away_pitcher_note: With a dearth of options for their hobbled starting rotation, the Sox will stick with Kelly for now. The righty has gone five starts without pitching six complete innings.

home_pitcher_note: Simon is tentatively scheduled to start, but a groin injury that hampered his last start at Baltimore could push him back further. It left Simon struggling to get velocity on fastballs, relying on splitters and eephus pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Excluding a subpar start against the White Sox, Miley has turned in another strong stretch of late, spinning three quality starts in his last four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander’s path back to dominance took a wrong turn last Tuesday against the Royals, who put up five runs on 10 hits in seven innings. But Verlander’s roll started with eight stellar innings against the Red Sox two weeks ago.
away_pitcher_note: Owens gave Boston fans hope for the future in his Major League debut Tuesday. He took the loss, but tossed five-plus innings of three-run ball in the Bronx.

home_pitcher_note: The righty has put together two quality starts since being acquired from the Reds, but he's still searching for his first win as a Royal. Cueto took a loss last Wednesday despite allowing just two runs over seven innings to the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd induced a dozen outs in the air compared with three groundouts over seven innings of one-run ball against the Royals last Wednesday. Like Comerica Park, Kauffman Stadium is pitcher-friendly with extra space.

home_pitcher_note: Ventura is coming off a rough outing against Detroit in his last start -- five innings, eight hits, six runs in an 8-6 loss last Thursday. "He just had a bad game," manager Ned Yost said of Ventura.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez can’t shake the home-run bug, but he can pitch around it if he limits his baserunners. He didn’t do that against the Royals last Thursday, and he paid for four walks, one with the bases loaded, in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is coming off a terrific outing against the White Sox. He went seven innings and gave up just four hits and one run as the Royals held on for a 3-2 win. He is 1-3 over his career against the Tigers with a 4.98 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty struggled to locate his slider and didn't make it out of the fourth inning last Friday against Boston in his home debut. Norris has started twice since joining the Tigers, and he carries a 4.43 ERA over 12 career Major League appearances.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty is 10-0 with a 1.26 ERA and 90 strikeouts in 85 2/3 innings at Minute Maid Park this year. He’s the first pitcher in franchise history to win his first 10 home decisions and first in the Majors since Zack Greinke (2011).
away_pitcher_note: Simon has been dealing with a groin strain his past couple starts, and his numbers have shown it, with 10 runs over 12 1/3 innings against Baltimore and Boston. His fly-ball tendencies further his risk for trouble in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh is making his 24th start of the season, which is one shy of his career high of last year. Despite throwing 9 2/3 fewer innings than he finished with last year, McHugh has allowed more hits, runs and homers than in 2014.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander has posted stingy numbers in three of his past four starts, though he has only one win to show for it. He’ll get a test in Houston from cozy Minute Maid Park and an aggressive group of Astros hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers will be making his second start since coming to the Astros in a July 30 trade with the Brewers and his first at Minute Maid Park with the Astros. He’s faced the Tigers once in his career, throwing 5 2/3 innings in May with Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Though Boyd took the loss Monday night in Kansas City, he showed the ability to adjust on the fly against a Royals lineup that walloped him early. He’ll need to adjust more to get some ground outs and survive in Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel hasn't been too pleased with early exits in his past two outings. Both times, manager Joe Maddon said the decision was made strictly on a strategic basis. Hammel has not gone beyond 5 2/3 innings in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will start on six days’ rest thanks to a pair of Tigers off-days. Considering his recent frustrations over yielding home runs -- six of them over his past three starts, 28 on the season -- he can use the extra time to regroup.

home_pitcher_note: Lester is 4-0 with a 2.04 ERA in his past five starts, giving up two runs or fewer in each of those games. He's 2-5 with a 5.25 ERA in 10 career starts against the Tigers, including a loss June 9 in Detroit when he gave up five runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris makes his first Interleague start on a week’s rest after tossing 6 1/3 innings with four runs, three earned, last Wednesday in a no-decision at Kansas City. He’ll face an aggressive-hitting Cubs lineup in a cozy park.

home_pitcher_note: Simon has struggled his last three starts, allowing 14 runs on 17 hits over 17 1/3 innings with twice as many walks (eight) as strikeouts (four). He owns a 4-2 record and a 3.92 ERA this season at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Perez is 1-0 with a 2.21 ERA in his last three starts. He beat the Mariners in Seattle on Aug. 8 when he allowed three runs (two earned) in six innings. He has a 12.79 ERA in one career start and one relief appearance against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Don’t call him vintage Verlander, because the way he’s been pitching lately is the form he’s been working to find. He owns a 1.75 ERA in 36 innings over his last five starts, including seven scoreless innings Saturday at Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 5-1 with a 3.73 ERA in six starts since the All-Star break and he is 7-4 with a 4.04 ERA in 12 starts on the road this season. He has made eight starts against the Tigers since 2010 and is 3-3 with a 6.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf’s first Major League appearance since June 2014 will be just his third AL start in a career that began in 1999. The Tigers acquired him from the Blue Jays Thursday after losing Anibal Sanchez and Daniel Norris to the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo beat the Rays on Sunday and is now 2-0 with a 5.54 in his last five starts. He is 3-5 with a 3.53 ERA in 13 starts on the road. He has made one start against the Tigers and that was back in 2009 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd gave up two Colby Rasmus homers as part of five runs over five innings Sunday at Houston. He pitched 6 2/3 innings of four-run ball with seven strikeouts against Texas in his big league debut for Toronto on June 27.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed three runs in seven innings in his last start vs. the M's. It was his third start for Texas and first after being skipped in a start because of a strained left groin muscle. His only start against the Tigers was in 2013, a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: After two strong starts, Sampson has not been sharp in his last two. While lasting only 8 1/3 innings combined, he’s allowed six earned runs and 14 hits. In a 4-3 loss to the Royals on Wednesday, he threw 95 pitches over 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Farmer returns to the Tigers' rotation for his fourth start this season and first since July 31. He has two losses and a no-decision, allowing 15 earned runs on 23 hits over 14 2/3 innings with four walks and nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Simon halted his summer swoon with a one-hit shutout of the Rangers last Thursday, flashing a fastball that hit 94 mph while throwing his splitter with a more deceptive motion and in better locations down in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver has made three starts since coming off the disabled list, and he has a 2.08 ERA in his 17 1/3 innings. The veteran's latest outing was his best -- 6 1/3 shutout innings with no walks and five strikeouts to beat the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander has a 1.67 ERA and .514 OPS allowed over his past six starts, averaging just over seven innings per outing. He has only one win to show for that stretch, and the Tigers are 2-4 in those starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Angels' off-day Monday lets Santiago start on normal rest on Wednesday in Detroit. The left-hander only lasted 3 2/3 innings in a loss against the Blue Jays on Friday after throwing 48 pitches in a four-walk, three-run first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf took the loss in his return to the big leagues thanks to five straight singles in a four-run third inning, but his seven innings suggest he can still provide a quality start and a chance for a team to win, even at age 39.
away_pitcher_note: Shoemaker will be called up from Triple-A Salt Lake to start Thursday’s series finale. The 28-year-old was optioned after giving up 13 runs over a two-start stretch, then gave up three unearned runs in six innings in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey surrendered five runs in the first inning of his last start against the Angels, but he didn't allow another one over six innings. That was enough to pick up the victory.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd starts against a Blue Jays offense that his hitting .284 with a league-high .829 OPS against left-handed pitching. He gave up three runs on five hits over six innings against Texas last Sunday at home.

home_pitcher_note: Hutchison will make his return to the rotation following a brief one-stint start in the Minors. Toronto temporarily went with a four-man rotation because of three off-days in the span of eight days, but the plan all along was for Hutchison to return.
away_pitcher_note: Farmer took a no-hit bid into the fifth inning and a shutout bid into the sixth inning Monday at Cincinnati but ran out of gas in a hurry with two home runs in three batters. Still, it was the best outing in his brief career.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle has been reliable, but he has hit a bump lately. Over his last two starts, he has surrendered nine runs over 10 innings. In his last start, vs. the Rangers, his velocity was down, but more important, his pinpoint command wasn't there.
away_pitcher_note: Five days after throwing a one-hit shutout of the Rangers, Simon gave up three runs on wild pitches, walked four batters and hit another in 4 1/3 innings against the Angels. The Tigers would gladly take something in between.

home_pitcher_note: After delivering a quality start in each of his first four outings as a Royal, Cueto has struggled in his last two trips to the hill, allowing 12 earned runs and 21 hits in a combined 11 innings. He is 1-1 with a 1.13 ERA vs. the Tigers this year.
away_pitcher_note: Vintage Verlander or not, the former AL MVP has dominated again, allowing eight runs on 33 hits over 52 innings in his last seven starts for a 1.38 ERA. He took a no-hit bid into the ninth inning last week against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Ventura has tossed four straight quality starts, including a scoreless six-inning effort Thursday in which he K'd a career-high 11 in a 5-3 victory over the Orioles. Ventura is 1-0 with a 5.29 ERA in three starts vs. the Tigers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf has lost both of his Tigers starts, but he’s beating Father Time. The 39-year-old has allowed four runs on 14 hits over 14 innings with 10 strikeouts, including seven innings of one-run ball in a 2-0 loss to the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is 0-2 with a 4.85 ERA vs. the Tigers this year, with both starts coming at Kauffman Stadium. He posted a quality start on May 2, but was less effective in his most recent outing, allowing five earned runs on eight hits over seven on Aug. 12.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers moved Boyd up two days for his season debut and saw him struggle in the cold, giving up five runs in 2 1/3 innings against the White Sox while battling command of his breaking ball. He'll get better weather Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago was on a limited pitch count against the Royals but made the most of it, allowing one run over five-plus innings to get the win. He'll be pitching without any restrictions against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer showed no hints of any sophomore slump over six scoreless innings in the Tigers' home opener against the Red Sox, striking out four against two walks with help from a fastball that topped out at 98 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson was saddled with a no-decision in his first start, allowing three runs in five-plus innings against the Royals. He was mostly solid, but hurt by a pair of solo homers.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann didn't have his dominant stuff from last April, but he was healthy in six innings of one-run ball to beat the Red Sox on Saturday, mixing pitches and eventually finding command for his first win since last June 14.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes, making his first start since June after undergoing surgery to alleviate thoracic outlet sydrome, looked like his old self against the White Sox. He gave up one run over six innings in a win.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer allowed four runs and struck out seven in 5 2/3 innings in his season debut against Arizona. In 49 2/3 career innings against the Tigers, the right-hander has a 6.89 ERA with 43 strikeouts and 23 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Few Tigers pitchers beat the Indians last year in Cleveland, but Norris was one of them, tossing five innings with one earned run and six strikeouts last September. He returns to Cleveland to start the series opener.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start of the season, Kluber went six innings and allowed three runs (two earned) against Arizona. In 2016, Kluber posted a record of 3-0 with a 2.25 ERA and 27 strikeouts in four starts against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander dueled to a no-decision opposite former division nemesis Chris Sale on Monday with an unearned run over seven innings. Now he'll face the Tigers' nemesis last year in the Indians, a team they have to beat.

home_pitcher_note: After earning the win on Opening Day against the Rangers, Carrasco started the Tribe's home opener and allowed one run in seven innings of work en route to a no-decision. Carrasco is 6-6 with a 4.95 ERA in his career against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd tossed six innings of one-hit ball against the Twins Tuesday with essentially fastballs and changeups. He'll try to put his arsenal together against Cleveland, a team he blanked for 4 2/3 innings in relief last April.

home_pitcher_note: Andriese pitched out of trouble throughout his last start Thursday night when he held the Yankees to one run in six innings, but he came away with a no-decision. He is 1-1 with a 5.73 ERA in five career appearances against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer enjoyed two of his best outings last season against the Rays, combining for 14 innings of one-run ball with two walks and 21 strikeouts. He tossed six quality innings against the Twins to win his last start Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Archer will look to continue his strong start. He improved to 2-0 on the year after winning his last start, against Boston. Archer has fanned 18 batters over 20 1/3 innings thus far and has eclipsed the 100-pitch mark in all three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann battled command in his last start with little feel for the ball, setting a career high with five walks in 4 2/3 innings, allowing five runs and walking consecutive batters for the first time since 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Ramirez will be making his first start of the season in place of the injured Jake Odorizzi. He pitched a strong four innings after Odorizzi suffered left hamstring tightness Saturday in Boston, allowing one run in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris faces the Rays for the first time since April 25, 2015, when he was in the Jays rotation. He tossed seven innings of one-run ball with seven strikeouts that evening for his first Major League quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Santiago is off to a hot start, and is coming off throwing seven scoreless innings against the White Sox. He's walked only three batters in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander owns a 17-8 record and 3.06 ERA in 33 career starts against the Twins, including two wins in three starts last season with 30 strikeouts over 21 1/3 innings. He last lost to Minnesota in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Mejia was slated to start on Wednesday, but it was rained out, and he'll get extra rest. Mejia was better in his second career start, limiting the White Sox to one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd gets a rematch with the Twins after tossing six scoreless innings of one-hit ball against them April 11 at Comerica Park. Despite a slider that wasn't working, he mixed fastballs and changeups for six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson has struggled this year, giving up four homers through his first three starts. He's yet to go deeper than 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer was a hard-luck loser in his last start against the Rays. Aside from a couple of sliders that he left out over the plate that resulted in three earned runs, Fulmer was solid over six innings, scattering six hits and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmerman didn't get the results he expected in a no-decision against the Rays in his last start. Zimmerman allowed five earned runs on 10 hits in six innings but said his fastball command and his slider was stronger than it has been.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez has been throwing strikes in his first four outings (20 strikeouts with just one walk), though he gave up 12 hits and 4 runs in 6 1/3 innings in a win over Miami in his last outing. He’s 9-3 with a 2.48 ERA in 15 starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Norris’ streak of 22 consecutive starts with three or fewer earned runs ended Wednesday at Tampa Bay, when a three-run second inning and defensive miscues doomed him en route to a fifth-inning exit with five runs allowed (four earned).
away_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old’s scoreless streak ended at 23 innings when he gave up five runs and nine hits in 4 1/3 innings in a no-decision at Oakland on Thursday, but he still has a 1.78 ERA and impressive 30-5 strikeout-to-walk ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Not since his rookie season had Verlander walked as many batters as the six he walked in his last start, Friday in Minnesota. He walked the bases loaded to set up a six-run sixth inning and a hasty exit, erasing an early lead.
away_pitcher_note: The 36-year-old has been hurt by the homer as he’s allowed six in 20 1/3 innings in his first four starts, including two solo shots in a 3-1 loss at Oakland on Friday. He’s 2-2 with a 3.47 ERA in eight games (seven starts) vs. Detroit.
