away_pitcher_note: The right-hander gets to face his former team in this series opener. Pelfrey spot-started for the injured James Shields in his White Sox debut, allowing two earned runs over 4 1/3 innings. Pelfrey is 4-8 with a 6.22 ERA lifetime at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer recovered from a rocky opening inning to deliver seven innings and seven strikeouts Sunday at Minnesota. He faced the Indians four times last year, going 1-2 with a 6.98 ERA and nearly two baserunners per inning.
away_pitcher_note: Holland gets to stay within the AL Central after dominating Cleveland yet again in his last start. The southpaw is 1-0 against the Tigers over four career starts and won his only start at Comerica Park by fanning seven over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: After one home run in his first three starts, Zimmermann allowed three in his last outing, but survived six innings with five runs against Seattle. He has allowed five runs in each of his past two outings, giving up 21 total hits.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has emerged as the ace of the staff with his early-season dominance. The righty has lasted at least eight innings in back-to-back starts for the second time in his career, allowing one earned on five hits (four infield) over 16 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Norris overcame command woes to toss six scoreless innings against the Indians on April 14 despite four walks. He’s 2-0 with a 1.69 ERA in four career starts against Cleveland, with 15 strikeouts and no home runs allowed.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has posted just one quality start and averaged 18.7 pitches per inning in April. It continued a troubling trend for Bauer, who wrapped up last season with a 6.39 ERA in September and enters May at 6.26.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander allowed an unearned run on five hits over seven innings with eight strikeouts against the Mariners in his last start. More interesting was the mix, with a heavy dose of mid and upper-90s fastballs and few changeups.
away_pitcher_note: The 2014 AL Cy Young Award winner was the first Cleveland pitcher to reach three wins, striking out 10 over seven innings in a 4-3 victory over Houston on Thursday. On the flip side, Kluber is allowing a career-high 1.57 homers per nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd was dealt a second-straight no decision in his most recent start against the White Sox. Against Cleveland on April 16, the second-year lefty allowed just one run on seven hits and two walks in six innings to earn the win.
away_pitcher_note: Carrasco has thrown eight innings in back-to-back starts, but he has been plagued by poor offensive support. The Indians have only scored 12 runs in his five outings this season, leaving him with a 2-2 record despite a sparkling 2.04 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Triggs picked up his fourth win in his last start, twirling seven scoreless innings with a career-high nine strikeouts in Houston. He’s held opponents to a .194 batting average and .256 on-base percentage.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer walked three batters for the first time this season, a reflection of command woes that frustrated him in a six-inning no-decision against the White Sox on Saturday. He has five quality starts in as many outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hahn has completed at least six innings in each of his four starts this season, most recently allowing four runs (three earned) on eight hits with no walks and six strikeouts in Houston on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: A tweak in Zimmermann’s delivery to go back to his Nationals days regained some old deceptiveness in his pitches, helping him put up five strikeouts over five quality innings in a win against the White Sox on Sunday in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Gray returned from the DL on Tuesday to make his season debut. The right-hander was bit by the long ball, allowing three homers in six innings against the Twins. He allowed four runs over that span, walking two and striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had command issues but a nasty slider in six innings of one-run ball against the Indians on Monday in Detroit, walking four but striking out eight. He has never faced Oakland, a team hitting lefties for a higher average.

home_pitcher_note: Ray was dominant in his last outing against the Nationals. In six innings, he allowed four hits and a walk, with 10 strikeouts, and both runs came as the result of questionable defensive plays behind him.
away_pitcher_note: After battling pitch-tipping, then fastball command in April, Verlander is showing signs of rounding into form around his usual time. He has tossed seven quality innings his past two starts, beating Cleveland last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Godley will be called up from Triple-A Reno to start. This is his second audition in the battle to replace the injured Shelby Miller in the rotation. On April 26 against the Padres, Godley allowed two runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has pitched deep into each of his past two games but been stung by low run support. He's gone 14 2/3 innings combined over those two outings, allowing six earned runs on 12 hits and five walks while striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old has fared well since being thrust into the starting rotation due to injuries. In five starts, Ramirez is 1-2 with a 3.45 ERA, 1.15 WHIP, 30 strikeouts and nine walks in 28 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In Fulmer's last start, against the A’s in Oakland, he worked eight innings, allowing two runs (one earned) on eight hits with two walks and a season-high nine strikeouts to earn his third win.

home_pitcher_note: Shoemaker was knocked around for five earned runs over six innings in his last start against the Astros. He's 2-1 with a 1.01 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers, the lowest mark for any team he's faced more than once.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has won three of his first four decisions. Last time out, at Oakland on Saturday, he worked 5 2/3 innings, allowing four runs on five hits, including three homers, in a Tigers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco, 34, struck out 10 batters for the first time since 2013 in his last start against the A's, as he went seven innings and didn't walk a batter. But he has given up a pair of homers in each of his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The second-year left-hander has split his first four decisions. Last time out, Sunday in Oakland, he didn’t make it out of the fifth inning, allowing five runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Filling in for the injured Tyler Skaggs, Meyer went a career-high 5 1/3 innings in his last outing vs. Oakland. Meyer is looking to find his control as he has 11 strikeouts and eight walks over 9 1/3 innings in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander beat the D-backs for his second win last time out on Tuesday night at Chase Field, pitching into the seventh and notching a quality start -- three runs on seven hits with three walks and seven strikeouts in six-plus innings.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd will be looking for his first win in a month when he takes the mound on five days' rest. Despite that, Boyd has recorded three consecutive quality starts and has a 3.96 ERA in four games since his last victory on April 16.
away_pitcher_note: Miley will be making his eighth start. He has limited opponents to a .214 average through 36 2/3 innings. But walks have been an issue -- he has allowed a team-high 23 to go with 28 hits.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer faced the Orioles twice during his Rookie of the Year campaign last season, giving up six earned runs in 11 1/3 innings (4.76 ERA). His first two starts in May have been excellent, however (15 IP, 2 ER, 16 K).
away_pitcher_note: The righty went 7 2/3 innings and gave up four runs, though three came on Adam Lind's homer. Jimenez was solid for most of Tuesday night against Washington, taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has yet to make it into the seventh inning in any of his seven starts this year. He owns a 5.82 ERA in seven career starts against Baltimore, his worst mark against any AL club he’s faced at least three times.
away_pitcher_note: Bundy has recorded eight consecutive quality starts to begin the season. He needed 112 pitches to get through six innings last Friday in Kansas City, but he allowed just four hits and two runs while taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Norris has walked multiple batters in all seven of his starts this year after doing so in seven of his 13 starts in 2016. His only other career start against Texas in September 2015 was the shortest of his career (1 1/3 IP, 6 R, 2 ER).
away_pitcher_note: Martinez is 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his last three starts and he is winless in his last 11 starts, going back to 2015. He is 1-1 with a 4.82 ERA in two career starts and one relief appearance against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander walked five in his most recent start, but none came in to score. He’s stuck to his usual workhorse ways, throwing 100-plus pitches in seven of eight starts. In 17 career starts versus Texas, he is 9-5 with a 2.71 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Griffin allowed four runs in five innings in a no-decision against the Athletics his last outing and is 4-0 with a 2.32 ERA in his last five starts. He is 1-2 with an 8.53 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd got rocked in his latest start, allowing seven earned runs in the third inning. He’d allowed three or fewer earned runs in each of his previous six starts. Boyd is 1-3 with a 5.24 ERA in four career starts against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish is 3-0 with a 2.38 ERA in his last five starts, including a seven-inning win Tuesday against the Phillies, in which he allowed just one run. In his career against Detroit, he's 6-0 with a 3.46 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock, normally a reliever, will make a spot start in place of Dallas Keuchel (placed on DL with pinched nerve in neck). Peacock is 2-0 this season with a 1.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has tossed seven or more innings with three earned runs or fewer in four of his past five starts, including his 5-4 win over Baltimore in his outing Wednesday at Comerica Park. He has never faced the Astros.

away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann used a strong curveball to get a season-high six strikeouts and a win in his last start. He also threw six innings for the first time in four starts. He’s 2-0 with a 0.47 ERA in his past three starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Morton surrendered three home runs and eight hits in the Astros' 5-3 loss against the Indians on Friday. He also had two walks and five strikeouts in 26 batters faced.
away_pitcher_note: Norris gave up a pair of homers on 2-0 pitches in his last start Friday against the Rangers, but it was a bases-loaded walk that frustrated him on the way to five runs allowed over 5 2/3 innings. He has never faced the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers is coming off one of his best outings of the season when he held the Indians to two runs (one earned) on two hits in six innings on Saturday. He gave up just one home run, snapping his streak of consecutive multi-homer-allowed games at six.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander has won three of his last four starts, most recently seven quality innings against the Rangers on Saturday. He has won his last three starts against Houston, including a complete game with 11 strikeouts last July.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey lasted 4 2/3 innings on April 28 against Detroit, allowing three runs on six hits in a no-decision. Pelfrey picked up his first White Sox victory by allowing one run in six innings and not issuing a walk vs. Seattle on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd, winless since April 16, has given up 11 runs on 20 hits over 7 2/3 innings in his last two starts to the O’s and Rangers. He surrendered five runs in 2 1/3 innings against the White Sox April 6 on a frigid day in Chicago.

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer, the reigning AL Rookie of the Year, has continued to impress this season, going 5-2 with a 2.55 ERA in nine starts. He’s been able to go deep into games as well, lasting at least six innings in each of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Holland went eight innings for the first time in his White Sox tenure when Chicago cruised to victory over Seattle on Sunday. The southpaw yielded one run, struck out six and walked two. Holland is 3-0 with a 1.67 ERA over four day starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Farmer makes his season debut in the second game of Saturday’s doubleheader. It’s his ninth career big league start. Farmer went 1-3 with a 4.12 ERA in nine starts at Triple-A this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez looked as strong as any AL starter in his first four trips to the mound of '17, going 3-0 with a 2.00 ERA in 27 innings. But in his last five starts, which all finished as losses, Gonzalez yielded 22 runs in 28 1/3 innings for a 6.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann tossed his best outing in eight starts last time out, holding the Astros to five hits over six innings but paying for two solo homers and two unearned runs. He beat the White Sox with five solid innings April 30.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel starts the opener of a three-game set with the Tigers. Hammel made an adjustment with his setup, squaring his shoulders more, and the results were solid in his last start against the Yankees -- six innings, three runs allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Norris took the no-decision but was strong his last time out against Houston, giving up two runs (one earned) and going at least six innings for the fourth time this season. He's 0-1 with a 3.47 ERA in four career starts against Kansas City.

home_pitcher_note: Skoglund is slated to make his first career start on Tuesday. In eight starts with Triple-A Omaha this season, Skoglund is 2-3 with a 4.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander got hit hard his last time out, giving up three Astros homers and didn't go at least six innings for the first time in five starts. He's 22-9 with a 3.23 lifetime ERA against the Royals, his most wins against any opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy gets the start in the final game of the series against the Tigers on Wednesday. Kennedy went five innings against the Indians on Friday in a 6-4 win. He gave up three hits and four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd worked through mechanical issues that impact his command to give up three runs in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the White Sox on Friday. He's 0-4 with a 6.92 in May and hasn't gone at least six innings since May 10.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer delivered seven or more quality innings in all five of his starts in May, but the Tigers haven’t scored a run of support for him in his last two outings, saddling him with 1-0 and 3-0 losses to the Astros and White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Holland has put up back-to-back excellent starts in his most recent times out, allowing just two earned runs in a combined 14 innings while striking out 14. Control has been a problem though, as he's averaged 3 walks in his last 4 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann gave up three home runs to the White Sox on Sunday, his third three-homer outing in 10 starts this year. He has yielded 16 homers in 55 2/3 innings, two more than he allowed over 105 1/3 innings last season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez took a perfect game into the seventh inning in his last time out, but lost it after 18 outs. He ended up allowing three earned runs in 7 2/3 innings, continuing an eight-game streak of going at least five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander moves up a spot to start on regular rest, earning a meeting with a White Sox club he beat with 10 strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings on Opening Day. He tossed seven innings of one-run ball in defeat Tuesday at Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Holmberg has been excellent out of the bullpen so far this year for the White Sox, putting up a 2.51 ERA in 14 1/3 innings. He was rewarded with a chance at starting, despite a 6.98 ERA in 13 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Norris has lasted six innings only once in his last five starts, but the Tigers are 3-2 in those outings. He gave up three runs over five innings at Kansas City on Monday in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Chavez will make his 12th start of the season against Detroit on Tuesday. Chavez enters on an active streak of 11 2/3 innings without allowing an earned run against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Farmer returns from Triple-A Toledo trying to build on the 6 1/3 scoreless innings and 11 strikeouts he posted against the White Sox in a May 27 spot start. If he does, he could end up filling Matthew Boyd’s rotation spot.
away_pitcher_note: Meyer is making his seventh start of the year. He earned a win in his start against Detroit on May 14, pitching 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball while matching a career-high seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer gets an extra day’s rest after giving up five runs on seven hits in seven innings against the White Sox last Friday. He tossed seven innings of one-run ball with seven strikeouts against the Angels on May 11 in Anaheim.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez gave up a season-high seven runs in a season-low 4 1/3 innings in his latest start against Minnesota. The right-hander allowed five runs over seven innings in his lone career start against Detroit on May 11.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson returns for his third callup of the season and will try to build off the shutout he fired against the Mariners on May 27. The lefty is filling in for Eduardo Rodriguez, who is out indefinitely with a right knee subluxation.
away_pitcher_note: A likely tough matchup in a homer-friendly park for Zimmermann, who has allowed 16 homers in 61 2/3 innings, hinges on his slider. He found it in his last start and delivered six innings of one-run ball to beat the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The ace labored through a 39-pitch first inning thanks to some misplays behind him in his last start at Baltimore, and was dominant for the rest of the game, striking out nine. In 30 career outings against the Tigers, Sale is 8-8 with a 3.01 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander will start on turn but with an extra day's rest after groin tightness forced an early exit from his last start Sunday against the White Sox. He struggled through a 39-pitch opening inning with several foul balls.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty threw 123 pitches over just five innings in his last start, but he allowed just one earned run and got the win at Yankee Stadium. At Fenway this season, Pomeranz is 4-1 with a 4.11 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Norris tossed six quality innings Tuesday against the Angels at Comerica Park, but needed 110 pitches to do it. As with many of his starts over the past month, a big inning ballooned his count early with 30 pitches in the third.

home_pitcher_note: Farmer will make his third start of the season with a 13-inning scoreless streak, tied for the longest in the American League and the longest by a Tiger at any point this season. He also has 16 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off a win against the Padres in which he gave up three earned run in five innings, tied for his shortest outing of the season. In 28 career games against the Tigers, Greinke is 13-7 with a solid 2.79 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is coming off his best back-to-back starts of 2017 -- allowing three runs over 12 innings. Current D-backs batters haven’t seen much of him, going 11-for-51 (.216) combined.
away_pitcher_note: Walker will make his first start in nearly a month after developing a blister in a start at San Diego on May 19. Walker has cleared all of the hurdles the club asked him to, but he is expected to be on a pitch count watch for this outing.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander threw his standard 100-plus pitches last time out in his first start since leaving a game on June 4 with groin tightness. He hasn’t faced the Rays this year, but he’s 2-0 with a 1.57 ERA against them in three previous starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cobb is feeling stronger about his changeup, his go-to pitch before losing feel for it early this year. His results were similarly positive: six innings of one-run ball, five strikeouts and only four hits allowed in a win vs. the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Norris hasn't completed the fifth inning in three of his 12 starts, including on April 20 in a road loss vs. Tampa Bay. He has as many hits allowed as strikeouts in his previous four starts, with a 3.63 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez flirted with danger Saturday against the A's, allowing 10 hits and a walk in 5 1/3 innings but holding Oakland to three runs. He beat the Tigers in the finale of a Rays three-game sweep in April, allowing just two hits and one run.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer hasn’t pitched since June 8, missing his most recent turn in the rotation after an MRI revealed inflammation in the bursa of his right shoulder. He’s allowed five runs in back-to-back starts for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Archer took a no-decision in his last outing against Oakland, giving up four earned runs while striking out eight over six innings. His start against Detroit in April was similar: Five innings, four runs, nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Farmer had his 13-inning scoreless streak snapped abruptly in his last start, allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings against the D-backs. Farmer faced the Rays once in relief in 2015, allowing a home run in one-third of an inning.
away_pitcher_note: Faria's Major League career has gotten off to a fast start with a pair of quality starts, both resulting in wins. Faria allowed one run across 6 1/3 innings in each of his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old rookie has pitched well as a fill-in starter for Seattle’s injury-plagued rotation, going 3-1 with a 3.34 ERA in six starts. He’s yet to go beyond six innings, but he’s kept games close and the Mariners are 5-1 when he’s started.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez returns from Triple-A Toledo for at least a spot start, his first for the Tigers this season. He went 0-2 with a 5.17 ERA in four starts for the Mud Hens, striking out 20 batters over 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miranda has been Seattle’s most consistent starter but gave up 10 hits and six runs -- five in the first inning-- in a 6-2 loss at Minnesota in his last outing. He picked up his first career win in relief last August vs. the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann pitched a season-high eight innings in a win on Wednesday, and is riding a string of three straight quality starts. On April 25, the Mariners recorded 11 hits off Zimmermann, which is the most he’s allowed this season.

home_pitcher_note: Paxton was 4-0 with a 1.26 ERA through seven starts, including a strong outing after returning from the DL with a strained elbow. But he’s 1-2 with a 9.95 ERA in his last three outings and gave up 7 runs in 3 2/3 innings vs. Texas on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander threw seven solid innings on Thursday, yielding just two runs. He also walked five, however, and now has the most walks in the Majors, with 42. He gave up one unearned run in seven innings versus Seattle in April.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old right-hander will make his MLB debut after being called up to replace veteran Yovani Gallardo in the rotation. Seattle’s No. 4 prospect, per MLBPipeline.com, was 4-3, 2.72 ERA in 14 games between Triple-A Tacoma and Double-A Arkansas.

away_pitcher_note: Boyd gets a rematch of his duel with Marco Gonzales and the M’s from last Saturday in Detroit, a game he won with six-plus quality innings and six K's. The Seattle native will be making his first start at Safeco. He pitched in relief there in '16.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano has given up eight runs on 11 hits over 8 1/3 innings in his past two outings, walking seven batters and striking out six. He was 3-1 with a 2.97 ERA in his first six starts this season prior to that, thanks in part to better command.

away_pitcher_note: Boyd struck out a career-high nine in his previous start in his hometown of Seattle, mostly using a slider at 79-84 mph after losing fastball command early on Thursday. He has quality starts in six of his eight games this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson was roughed up by the Brewers last time out on May 18. The right-hander surrendered five runs on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings and took the loss to fall to 1-2, while his ERA stands at 3.96.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up nine earned runs in 10 2/3 innings of his last two starts, both vs. the Mariners, Fulmer faces a team he hasn't lost to in 3 career starts. He last started at Minnesota on April 23, 2017, allowing two runs in 7 innings with 7 K's.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers tossed six shutout frames against the White Sox on April 8 without breaking 90 mph on the radar gun. He has two quality starts in five outings since then, while allowing 10 home runs and a .553 slugging percentage in his last 37 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez pitched the best game of his career last time out, twirling eight scoreless and giving up just two hits against the Rangers. He’ll make his second start of 2018 vs. the Tigers, looking to build on a seven-inning, one-run outing on April 8.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano rebounded from his May struggles to take a no-hitter into the seventh last Sunday at Seattle. He didn’t get a win after eight scoreless innings thanks to the Mariners' comeback off Detroit’s bullpen, but he showed he can shorten slumps.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago is settling into the White Sox rotation following the demotion of Carson Fulmer. Over his last two starts, Santiago has given up five runs in 11 innings. He pitched well last time out but allowed three solo home runs to the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: The versatile reliever will make his third start in place of injured Jordan Zimmermann, having tossed a pair of serviceable outings already. He threw five innings of two-run ball in a no-decision Monday at Minnesota, walking none and fanning four.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran of the White Sox staff, Shields has dominated his last two starts. In a combined 14 1/3 innings, Shields has given up three runs while striking out 13 and walking five. He owns a 3.27 ERA in five May starts.

away_pitcher_note: Skaggs allowed three earned runs over five innings in his last start Wednesday against the Blue Jays. He has recorded six or more strikeouts in each of his past five starts. In two career starts against the Tigers, Skaggs is 1-0 with a 0.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer tossed 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball in his last outing against the Twins on Wednesday, earning his first win since April 7. His ERA in May has spiked from 2.76 to 5.46, but he has a 3.38 ERA in four games vs. the Angels, earning a 2-2 record.
away_pitcher_note: Tropeano picked up his second win of the season on Thursday after holding the Blue Jays to one run over a career-high 7 1/3 innings. He is slated to face the Tigers for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers got a no-decision in his May 25 start vs. the White Sox while surrendering four runs on nine hits in 5 2/3 innings. He struggled with command and equaled his second-highest WHIP of the season at 1.33. Fiers was 2-1 vs. the Angels last year.
away_pitcher_note: After getting an extended break between starts, the two-way phenom will take the mound for the first time since May 20. Ohtani wasn’t inactive during the break, hitting in six straight games. He boasts a 4-1 record and 3.35 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter gets the call from Triple-A Toledo to make his third Tigers start, this time in place of injured Francisco Liriano. He yielded six runs, five earned, on seven hits in five innings against the Indians on May 16 at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Heaney limited the Yankees to one run over 6 1/3 innings in his last start on Friday. He is pitching to a 1.45 ERA over his last six outings. Heaney is set to make his first career appearance against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his best outing of the season, the lefty reliever will make his fourth start for the injured Jordan Zimmermann. Hardy tossed seven innings of one-run ball on Saturday vs. the White Sox. He has a career 3.60 ERA in 10 innings vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia returned from the disabled list in his last start and enjoyed his best outing as a Blue Jay. The veteran lefty needed just 73 pitches to get through seven innings of one-run ball against the Phillies. It was his longest start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd will put his breakout season to the test against his old squad in their first meeting since July 2016. He tossed five scoreless innings on two hits against the Angels on Monday despite three walks, keeping their right-handed hitters off-balance.
away_pitcher_note: Happ has struck out at least eight in seven starts this season, which after his last outing was tied for the fourth most in the Majors. He leads the Blue Jays with six quality starts and he allowed two earned runs over 6 2/3 innings last time out.

away_pitcher_note: Sanchez surrendered a career-high seven earned runs in his last start against the Red Sox. He has not pitched more than five innings since April 30 and he's coming off a month in which he posted a 5.96 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Severino's unbeaten streak is now at nine starts, coming off a victory against the Astros in which he tied a season high with 11 strikeouts. Severino is 6-0 with a 1.95 ERA since taking his only loss of the season on April 10.

away_pitcher_note: German showed some encouraging signs in his last outing, though it resulted in a 5-1 loss to the Astros. Since firing six hitless innings in his first start on May 6, German is 0-2 with a 9.42 ERA in 14 1/3 innings over three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer is making a spot start because the Red Sox had 26 games in 27 days. Wright has been strong out of the bullpen since coming back from the disabled list. The expectation is that he can pitch five to six innings in his first start.
away_pitcher_note: Lewicki will make his second career big league start as the Tigers fill spots for the injured Jordan Zimmermann and Francisco Liriano. The UVA product has been effective in long relief and escaped a bases-loaded jam he inherited Friday vs. Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has quietly settled into a better rhythm, allowing three earned runs or less in his last five starts. In three career starts against the Tigers, Rodriguez is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Boyd overcame spotty breaking balls and a couple home runs to deliver seven innings against the Blue Jays, keeping the Tigers in position for a late-inning win. The Red Sox will test his .221 average and .646 OPS to right-handed hitters.

away_pitcher_note: Clevinger gave up four earned runs and a pair of homers over six innings in his start vs. the Twins last Sunday and was not afforded a decision. He is 4-1 with a 2.28 ERA in six career games (five starts) vs. the Tigers.

away_pitcher_note: Kluber was dominant once again in his last start against the Brewers on Tuesday, giving up just one run and striking out seven over seven innings. He pitched eight scoreless innings and struck out a season-high 13 Tigers in April.

away_pitcher_note: Lynn has thrown at least six innings and allowed two runs or fewer in each of his last four outings dating back to May 22. In his most recent start on June 8, he struck out seven against the Angels and lowered his ERA to 5.08 on the season.

away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is expected to return from the 10-day DL for this start after a six-week absence with a right shoulder impingement. He compiled 12 scoreless innings over his last two starts before the injury, followed by two Minor League rehab starts.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time since Opening Day, Shields emerged victorious in a start. He was brilliant vs. the first-place Tribe on Tuesday, allowing one run on four hits over seven innings. The veteran has gone 10 straight starts working at least six frames.
away_pitcher_note: Hardy could be headed back to the bullpen after this start, depending on how Francisco Liriano fares in his rehab outing for Triple-A Toledo. But Hardy has held his own in the rotation, going 2-1 with a 3.63 ERA over the past month.

home_pitcher_note: Romano is coming off the best start of his season: eight innings of one-run ball for a no-decision on Tuesday at KC. He had his sinker working well and induced a lot of contact and grounders. It was exactly the confidence boost he needed.
away_pitcher_note: Keeping the ball in the park has been a contributing factor behind Boyd’s breakout season, but he’ll get a test in the hitter-friendly confines of Great American Ball Park with summer weather settling in. He’s 1-3 with a 3.97 ERA on the road.

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has posted seven innings of one-run ball in each of his last two outings, getting back to his old form by pounding hitters with 97-98-mph sinkers down in the strike zone. Expect more of that in Cincinnati, even on a hot summer afternoon.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber picked up his first career MLB win on Sunday, when he held the Twins to one run over 5 2/3 innings. The righty struck out seven and walked one, showing flashes of the command he displayed in the Minor Leagues (6 walks in 76 2/3 IP).
away_pitcher_note: Fiers has held the Tribe to two runs over 13 innings in two meetings this year.

home_pitcher_note: A rain delay ended Bauer's Monday start against the White Sox at seven shutout innings, in which he struck out eight and walked two. Over his past seven turns, the right-hander has a 1.99 ERA with 12 walks and 72 strikeouts in 49 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano is set to come off the DL for Saturday’s start after missing the last three-plus weeks with a right hamstring strain. He has a loss and a no-decision with a 6.10 ERA against Cleveland this year.

home_pitcher_note: Plutko's last start was on June 12, when he allowed five runs in 4 2/3 innings with five strikeouts and three walks against the White Sox. He returns to the rotation after a temporary stint in the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd will be looking for a return to form after a short-porch grand slam doomed him to defeat in Cincinnati on Tuesday. He tossed seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball in his only meeting with the Indians this year on April 10 in Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann returned from the DL with five innings against the White Sox on June 16, allowing three earned runs on four hits with four strikeouts. He pounded the strike zone, but survived with flyouts, which he should get at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: The well-traveled veteran will make his A's debut after joining the team Sunday in Chicago. The A's will be his 13th Major-league team. Jackson made three starts with Triple-A Nashville after signing a Minor League deal, going 0-1 with a 4.02 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Montas has pitched well since being recalled from Triple-A Nashville in late May. He has allowed two runs or less in four of his five starts. He allowed just one run on five hits in 6 2/3 innings in his last outing against San Diego last Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers is winless in three starts since June 4, but has given up two runs or less in each of his last three outings at less homer-prone Comerica Park, including seven innings of one-run ball June 9 against the Indians, recording 12 flyouts.
away_pitcher_note: Bassitt allowed a combined 11 runs (six earned) across 9 1/3 innings in his last two starts, after yielding just one run over seven innings in his first outing. On Friday, he was struck for five runs and six hits in 5 1/3 innings vs. the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer gets seven days of rest between starts after back-to-back home runs doomed him in Cincinnati and spoiled five shutout innings with nine strikeouts. He tossed seven innings of one-run ball in each of his past two starts at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Manaea has been up and down this season and is currently on an upswing. He is 2-0 with a 2.81 ERA in four June starts. He's coming off a dominant performance against the White Sox when he allowed just one run on five hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Stroman will make his second start since returning from the DL when he takes the mound in the opener with the Tigers. The right-hander had a terrific outing on June 23 at Anaheim, throwing six scoreless innings with one walk and five strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The former Blue Jays pitcher, traded last summer for Teoscar Hernandez, returns to Rogers Centre with trade rumors beginning to pick up around him once more. He returned from the DL with four innings in defeat at Cleveland last Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Gaviglio will look to do something he didn't in his previous three starts -- pitch past the fifth inning. He hasn't reached the sixth since June 6, when he threw seven shutout frames vs. the Yankees. Gaviglio is 0-1 with a 4.74 ERA in June.
away_pitcher_note: Three years after Boyd made his big-league debut with the Blue Jays, the lefty returns to Rogers Centre for the first time since 2016, hoping to reverse his recent struggles in back-to-back rough outings in Cincinnati and Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Happ will start vs. the Tigers, seeking his 11th win of the season after a solid June. He was 3-0 with a 3.16 ERA in that span. The lefty last faced Detroit on June 2, allowing four earned runs over five frames.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has gone five innings in two outings since his return from the DL, including five scoreless in 79 pitches Monday against Oakland. He could get a longer leash to go deeper into games under new pitching coach Rick Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Borucki will make his second start of the year with Aaron Sanchez on the DL. The 24-year-old lefty went six innings, allowing two earned runs in his MLB debut against Houston last week. He had a 3.27 ERA over 13 starts in Triple-A Buffalo.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers took a hard-luck defeat against the A’s on Wednesday, but his seven innings of one-run ball marked his second such outing in his last four starts as his potential trade value picks up. He’s 0-2 with a 5.91 ERA in two starts at Rogers Centre.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off an abbreviated start against the Dodgers in which he lasted 2 2/3 innings. He gave up six runs in that short span on eight hits. The right-hander has a 2.96 ERA in eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has settled into form just in time for trade speculation. He took the loss last Thursday against Oakland, but tied a season high with eight innings, the last four scoreless with one hit allowed. He has three walks over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana did not get a decision in his last outing against the Dodgers, giving up three runs over 5 1/3 innings. He has not won a game since May 31, going 0-2 with a 4.33 ERA in five June starts. He's 2-2 with a 6.00 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano remains winless since his strong April, including losses in each of his last three outings, but tossed a quality start Friday at Toronto with no hard-hit contact aside from Justin Smoak’s two-run homer. Expect trade interest to build.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd is winless in his last four starts, but he tempered his struggles with a quality start Saturday in Toronto, settling for a no-decision. He’s 3-1 with a 2.61 ERA at Comerica Park this year.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo will be making his fourth start of the season for the Rangers. His best start came in his last outing against the White Sox on Friday, when he allowed three runs on four hits and struck out seven in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann was superb on Sunday vs. the Blue Jays, allowing one run through seven innings to help the Tigers snap an 11-game losing streak. He hasn't given up a home run since April 25, though he was on the disabled list for six weeks in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Colon earned the 245th win of his career in his last start against the White Sox on Saturday, allowing three runs on seven hits in five innings. Colon is tied with Dennis Martinez for the most wins by a Latin American pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has pitched a combined 15 innings and allowed just two runs over his last two starts. Against the Blue Jays on Monday, Fiers completed eight innings of three-hit ball and gave up one run.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off a loss to the White Sox on Sunday in which he allowed a season-high seven earned runs on nine hits. Hamels is 3-1 with a 2.05 ERA in eight road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer was sharp on Tuesday against the Cubs, when he allowed three runs over six innings. Fulmer is expected to be a desirable trade target for teams as July progresses, but his value could change with each start.
away_pitcher_note: Bibens-Dirkx, who allowed five runs on nine hits in a loss to the Astros on Tuesday, will be making his sixth start of the year. He is 1-0 with a 3.97 ERA in two road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Archer will come off the disabled list (left abdominal strain) to make his first Major League start since June 2. He pitched four hitless innings July 3 for Class A Advanced Charlotte. Archer is expected to be limited to about 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has a rough history at Tropicana Field, where he’s 1-2 with a 9.43 ERA in five starts and two relief appearances. Much of that damage came last season, with 10 runs on 11 hits over five innings in three games with the Jays and Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Stanek made his 10th start of the season Friday against the Mets and tied a season high with four strikeouts. Nine of his 10 starts have been scoreless, including his last eight starts. His average fastball velocity this season is 98.1 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has yielded 20 earned runs on 25 hits over 17 innings in his last four starts, all Detroit losses, tempering what were two very good months for him before June. He tossed six innings of one-run ball against the Rays on May 1 in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has been impressive since being recalled on June 30, particularly on Monday, when he inherited a two-on, one-out situation and stranded both runners on his way to 2 2/3 innings of scoreless relief.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is pitching like the frontline starter the Tigers signed a few years ago. He has allowed two runs over 20 innings in his last three starts with no walks and 20 strikeouts, including eight innings and 11 strikeouts to beat Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel will begin the Astros' final series before the All-Star break. He is 2-0 in his past two starts, stretching out seven innings in each and lowering his ERA from 4.22 to 3.95.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers returns to Houston to face his former squad for the first time since the Astros non-tendered him last fall following the World Series. He returns to town throwing stingy ball, with three runs allowed over 21 innings in his past three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has one more chance to extend his club record of 169 strikeouts prior to the All-Star break. He threw six scoreless innings and struck out 11 on Monday against the A’s but didn’t get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: As trade speculation builds around Fulmer, the Tigers' ace hopes to build his game a little further, mix his pitches and keep the ball in the cozy confines of Minute Maid Park. He threw seven innings of one-run ball in Houston in May 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will be facing his former team for the first time since the Tigers traded him to Houston last Aug. 31. Verlander won 183 games for the Tigers in 480 starts between 2005-17, winning the '11 Most Valuable Player and Cy Young.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano returns to Houston for the first time since the World Series, when he was a lefty in the Astros' 'pen. He has been an effective Tigers starter but bumped his ERA up nearly three-quarters of a run in just 2 1/3 innings vs. Tampa Bay on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd will open the Tigers' second half with his 19th start of the season. He struggled to end the first half with a 9.78 ERA in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Price allowed three runs (two on homers) while striking out eight in his last outing against the Blue Jays, leaving him with a 9.20 ERA and 1.5 WHIP in his last three starts. That outing was his longest during that span, though, at 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers allowed three runs in six innings Friday against the Astros. His 3.70 ERA is the lowest among all Tigers starters, and this will be his fourth career start against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson makes his fourth start on Saturday, coming off strong showing against the Blue Jays during which he held Toronto to two runs over 4 1/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Hardy (4-3, 3.61 ERA) will make his third consecutive start for the Tigers. Hardy has a 4.01 ERA in 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer is in search of his first win since June 14 and has struggled to remain healthy, dealing most recently with a left oblique strain. Fulmer is coming off a outing against the White Sox in which he allowed an earned run over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gant has been garnering attention for his bat recently -- he has two home runs this season, and no other hits -- but he has been solid on the mound as well, going 3-1 with a 3.06 ERA in August.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano gets another rematch with his old club after ending a four-month winless drought Monday with five innings and five strikeouts against the White Sox last Tuesday. He tossed three innings of one-run ball against the Astros in Houston in July.
away_pitcher_note: A little over a year since he made his last start for the Tigers, Verlander returns to Comerica Park as a visitor. Since joining the Astros in a waiver-wire deal last August, the seven time All-Star is is 19-9 with a 2.47 ERA and 291 K's.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has built some late-season momentum with one earned run over 11 innings in his past two starts. He’s 2-3 with a 3.09 ERA in seven career starts against the Astros, striking out 37 batters against six walks over 43 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Cole and teammate Justin Verlander are neck and neck for the AL strikeout lead. Cole is also one of only three AL pitchers with an opponent batting average under .200 (.197).

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer was tagged with five runs (three earned) over 6 1/3 innings in his last start against St. Louis, but his first five innings were perfect. Fulmer has a 4.87 ERA since coming off the DL on Aug. 24 and hasn't won since June 14.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber piled up a career-high 11 strikeouts, including two in each of his first five innings, in 6 2/3 innings against the Rays on Tuesday. The rookie is 4-3 with a 4.93 ERA in seven starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano gave up three runs over six innings in his last start against the Astros, but none of them were earned. Liriano has lost nine of his last 10 decisions, dating back to May 26.

away_pitcher_note: Moya will work the "opener" role for the third time this month. He opened against the Royals last Thursday and was excellent, allowing only one baserunner in two innings.

away_pitcher_note: Lopez left his last start against the Twins in the fifth inning because of a left rib contusion after allowing three earned runs on nine hits. He's started six games for the Royals since being acquired from the Brewers, going 2-3 with a 4.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano has tempered his second-half struggles with back-to-back quality starts, including three runs over seven innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Indians last Sunday. He’s 1-0 with a 2.28 ERA in four starts against the Royals this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy earned his second win of the season last time out, allowing two runs (one earned) on six hits over six innings against the Twins. He struck out seven over six scoreless innings against the Tigers on May 4.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in two starts against the Royals this year. He’s coming off back-to-back losses at home, haunted by the long ball, but could benefit from cooler weather heading through Michigan this weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Junis is coming off the shortest start of his career on Sunday, when he allowed 4 earned over 3 innings and was saddled with a no-decision vs. the Twins. He's 4-0 in 4 starts vs. the Tigers this season, including a complete game on Aug. 28.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is still searching for his first win, but his work the last few weeks might have won him an inside track on a starting job heading into next year. He tossed five scoreless innings against the Twins on Tuesday before a two-run sixth doomed him.
away_pitcher_note: Keller struck out seven while allowing four earned runs over six-plus innings in a no-decision against the Pirates on Monday. He's completed six or more innings in each of his last four starts, going 2-1 with 2.57 ERA over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Moya will serve as the opener for the fifth time this season and has a 3.60 ERA in that role. He started twice in Detroit last week and didn’t allow a run in two innings. Kohl Stewart will follow him.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull gets another chance in the Tigers' rotation after his first Major League start went awry Wednesday against the Twins. The Tigers are hoping to see more of the power fastball and slider that flummoxed Triple-A hitters last month in Toledo.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi has been pitching well since early August, posting a 3.83 ERA over his last nine starts. He gave up two runs over 6 1/3 innings in Detroit on Sept. 18.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd suffered his shortest outing in two years when the Royals roughed him up for six hits, two of them homers, in 1 1/3 innings Thursday. He’s 3-9 with a 5.52 ERA on the road this year, including two losses in as many visits to Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Moya will serve as an opener for the sixth time this season and the fourth time against the Tigers. He's yet to allow a run against Detroit in his role as opener. Lefty Stephen Gonsalves will serve as the primary pitcher.

away_pitcher_note: Zimmerman will look for a strong outing in his final start of the season. He tossed seven innings and held the Royals to three hits last time out on Saturday.

away_pitcher_note: From a results standpoint, Norris delivered his best start of September in his previous outing against the Royals. The 25-year-old held Kansas City to one run on six hits and walked just two over five innings.
