home_pitcher_note: Stroman is set to make the second Opening Day start of his career. He will be trying to make amends for a disappointing 2018 that was marred by injuries and an ERA above 5. Prior to 2018, Stroman tossed at least 200 innings in back-to-back seasons.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran will make his second consecutive Opening Day start looking to get back to the stingy variety of pitches that helped him build a quietly impressive first half last year, including seven innings of one-run ball at Rogers Centre last July.

home_pitcher_note: Shoemaker was one of the Blue Jays' buy-low targets this offseason, and the move has looked pretty good so far. The 32-year-old hasn't tossed a full season since he went 9-13 with a 3.88 ERA for the Angels in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Four years after he came up to the Majors with the Blue Jays, Boyd returns to Toronto having established himself in the Tigers rotation. He was better last year than his 9-13 record would suggest, from a 1.16 WHIP to 8.4 strikeouts per nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off a pair of disappointing seasons, but he was borderline dominant this spring. The 26-year-old allowed just three earned runs over 17 2/3 innings and could be in line for a big year now that he's finally healthy.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull steps in for injured Michael Fulmer following a strong Spring Training and encouraging September stint. Lost amid the bevy of highly-rated pitching prospects in the Tigers system, Turnbull has nasty stuff, including a power fastball.

home_pitcher_note: A spot became available in Toronto's rotation late in camp when Ryan Borucki went down with an elbow injury. Thornton had been under consideration for the 'pen, but instead he gets to continue as a starter, where he posted a 4.02 ERA in Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Moore begins his Tigers tenure against an old AL East rival from his Rays days. The lefty owns a 5-3 record and 3.81 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Blue Jays, striking out 53 batters over 56 2/3 innings. His last win over them came in 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong spring, German will start the series opener against the Tigers. As a starter, German went 2-5 with a 6.19 ERA in 14 outings last year.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers signed Ross last fall for veteran stability, and they’ll turn to him in a place where they’ll need that experience, pitching in Yankee Stadium against a formidable lineup. It’ll be a huge test of Ross’ low home-run rate for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka provided a strong effort on Opening Day, limiting the Orioles to two runs (one earned) and six hits over 5 2/3 innings. He was the first Yankees starter to record at least five strikeouts without a walk on Opening Day since Catfish Hunter.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann had a 12-inning scoreless streak over the last two years at Yankee Stadium before three sixth-inning home runs denied him a chance at a win last August. He was perfect through 6 2/3 innings on Opening Day in Toronto before giving up a hit.

home_pitcher_note: Loaisiga was recalled from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Wednesday. The righty had a rough spring, posting a 6.75 ERA in 16 innings, but was 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA in four big league starts after being promoted from Double-A last June.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd’s fly-ball tendencies will be tested by the comfy confines of Yankee Stadium. He allowed three runs on five hits over six innings in a win there last September despite two solo homers. A four-run inning doomed him in his season debut at Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Normally the home opener goes to a Tigers veteran, but manager Ron Gardenhire was so impressed with Turnbull this spring that he lined him up for this outing in his fifth big league start. A three-run fourth sunk him to defeat Saturday in Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Junis makes his second start of the season. He pitched five scoreless innings on Saturday against the White Sox before getting nicked for three runs in the sixth in an 8-6 win.

home_pitcher_note: Moore dusted off his cutter after leaving it alone for most of Spring Training, and it helped him flummox Blue Jays hitters for seven scoreless innings on two hits with six K's, his longest outing since 2016. His fastball topped out at 95 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez started strong Sunday against the White Sox, striking out five of the first 10 batters he faced. He has faced Detroit once in his career, giving up seven runs in one inning last September.

home_pitcher_note: Ross made his Tigers debut on Monday night, and two homers ended up costing him against the Yankees in a 3-1 loss at Yankee Stadium. Ross pitched five innings and allowed three runs (two earned) on four hits, striking out four batters.
away_pitcher_note: Keller (1-0, 2.08 ERA) will get the start in the series finale vs. the Tigers. He battled through traffic in his six innings on Tuesday vs. the Twins, but managed a quality start by limiting the damage to three runs off five hits and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will put his stingy start to the test against an Indians lineup that has flummoxed him since joining Detroit. He’s 0-5 with an 11.08 ERA in seven career starts against Cleveland, allowing 48 hits over 26 innings despite 20 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Kluber labored through 3 1/3 innings, allowing six runs (four earned) on eight hits, and walked three batters. It was the third time since the start of the 2018 season that the right-hander failed to complete four frames.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd has been one of the American League’s more impressive starters early, racking up 23 strikeouts in 11 1/3 innings over his first two starts with help from a devastating slider. The Indians handed him a loss and two no-decisions last season.
away_pitcher_note: Despite walking six batters on Thursday, Bauer was able to keep a no-hitter intact through seven innings. The right-hander’s 117 pitches forced him from the game. He's allowed just one hit through his first 14 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: A week after racking up 10 strikeouts over six quality innings against the Royals in the Tigers’ home opener, Turnbull will close out the homestand in search of his first Major league win. He made his MLB debut against Cleveland last September.
away_pitcher_note: Bieber made his first start of the year on Friday, making just one mistake that resulted in a two-run homer. The 23-year-old allowed just one other hit through six innings, recording nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Pineda makes his third start of the season. In his last start against the Phillies, Pineda earned his first victory as a member of the Twins. It was his first victory since 2017 when he was with the Yankees. Pineda will face the Tigers for the fifth time in his career. He is 1-2 with a 3.91 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Ross’ exposure to the early spring chill of the Upper Midwest continues with his first outing at Target Field since 2012. He tossed seven innings of one-run ball with eight strikeouts in his last start against the Royals on Sunday at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Berrios was as dominating like he was during his Opening Day start against the Indians. He pitched six innings, allowed two runs and struck out seven during a 2-1 loss to the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann’s hot start to the season cooled from three Indians home runs Monday at Comerica Park. It was his first defeat since a loss to the Twins last September. An effective slider is the key to his new repertoire, which is less reliant on the fastball.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have roughed up Boyd in each of the last two seasons, but the lefty’s improved slider could be a problem for a less experienced Pittsburgh lineup. A three-run homer from Jose Osuna sunk Boyd in a loss last April in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Musgrove held the Cubs to two unearned runs on four hits while striking out six over 6 1/3 innings Thursday at Wrigley Field. The righty has yet to allow an earned run this season, and he has 15 strikeouts with only three walks in 15 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull continues his search for his first Major League win against a team that hasn’t seen him. His struggles with secondary pitches in cold weather led Cleveland hitters to sit on his fastball in a loss last Thursday at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Williams put together another quality start on Friday night at Nationals Park, holding the Nats to two runs on four hits and three walks over 6 1/3 innings. Williams has completed six innings in each of his first three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Ross is unbeaten in four starts and a relief appearance against the White Sox, but walked 11 batters in 9 1/3 innings over two starts against them in 2017. A bout of bad mechanics in a four-run third inning doomed him in his last start at Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Nova pitched well enough to win on Saturday at Yankee Stadium, giving up one run over six innings, while striking out five. But the White Sox managed just one hit behind him. Nova is 0-3 with a 7.33 ERA in his career at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has lost the slider that served him well through two stellar outings to begin his season. He spent his time between starts trying to find it again, a critical step towards containing a White Sox lineup that hit him aggressively last year.
away_pitcher_note: Rodon had a better balance among pitches in Sunday's victory over the Yankees, mixing in 16 changeups to go with his 38 sliders among his 112 pitches. Rodon is 1-1 with a 5.21 ERA over three starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: It’s time for the Tigers to figure out what they have in Norris, who rejoins the rotation with Matt Moore out for the season. While Norris’ fastball velocity has been up and down since Spring Training, secondary pitches will be key to his fortunes.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez won for the first time this season in his start against the Royals on Tuesday, when he allowed one run on five hits, struck out five and walked two, in what was clearly his best effort of 2019. Lopez has a 1-0 record and 4.38 ERA at Comerica.

home_pitcher_note: Sale struggled in his last start, allowing four earned runs over five innings against the Yankees. After calling his 0-4 start to the season "flat-out embarrassing," Sale will look to turn the page against the Tigers at Fenway Park.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd heads into his fifth start leading Major League starters in fWAR, FIP and tied in strikeouts. His slider has been one of the nastiest pitches in baseball this year.

home_pitcher_note: Sale struggled in his last start, allowing four earned runs over five innings against the Yankees. After calling his 0-4 start to the season "flat-out embarrassing," Sale will look to turn the page against the Tigers at Fenway Park.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd heads into his fifth start leading Major League starters in fWAR, FIP and tied in strikeouts. His slider has been one of the nastiest pitches in baseball this year.

home_pitcher_note: For the third time this season, the righty will swing from the bullpen to the rotation. This time, it is due to Nathan Eovaldi going to the injured list with a loose body in his elbow. Velazquez has pitched well at Fenway in his career, going 6-2 with a 2.09 ERA in 29 appearances (five starts).
away_pitcher_note: While Turnbull’s mid-90s fastball has snuck up on a lot of hitters with its spin rate, his slider/cutter has become a devastating pitch, generating seven swings and misses over six innings last Wednesday in a no-decision against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was touched for four runs (three earned) in 5 1/3 innings on Friday against the Rays, but still saw his ERA decline steadily through three April starts. He’s 2-1 with a 3.52 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: When Ross is rolling, he’s a quick-working innings-eater who avoids hard contact from hitters. When he gets out of sync, often with runners on base, he has had trouble getting back in line. His four home runs this season have been on hanging sliders.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello, a Tigers first-round Draft pick in 2007, will take the ball against the team that drafted him. The right-hander struck out five and limited the Rays to a pair of runs over 5 2/3 innings during his last start, but his ERA still sits at 8.47 on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will try to end a personal three-game losing streak, but he’ll need to hit the corners of the strike zone to do it. He didn’t get those calls on Friday against the White Sox and paid for it with four walks, one of them with the bases loaded.

home_pitcher_note: Rodon again sees the Tigers after allowing a run in six innings of a 7-3 victory exactly a week ago. It will be his 20th career start following six or more days' rest. He's 6-9 in his previous 19, and his 3.46 ERA in those starts is about a half-point lower than his overall career mark.
away_pitcher_note: Norris gets a rematch against the White Sox after tossing five scoreless innings against them on Sunday for his first win since Sept. 28, 2017. He struck out six, retired 11 of his final 12 batters and looked in control all day.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough start to the year, Lopez has responded by posting consecutive quality starts. He'll be working on five days' rest, on which he's posted a 4.18 ERA during his career.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has pitched 7 innings in his past two starts, the most recent a win against the Red Sox on April 23. He credits attacking and finding the strike zone early as keys to his success.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been a pleasant surprise early this season, keeping the Phillies in the game in each of his first four starts. He has not allowed more than two runs in any start, although he has pitched six innings only once.
away_pitcher_note: With Tyson Ross going on paternity leave, Turnbull takes the mound for the first time in a week after battling the Red Sox for five scoreless innings over 94 pitches for his first MLB win. He hasn’t given up an earned run since April 11, tossing 11 innings with more walks (6) than hits (5).

home_pitcher_note: Has Nola turned a corner after a slow start? The Phillies hope so. He has a 2.92 ERA in his last two starts after posting a 7.45 ERA in his first four. Better command is the key to Nola's success. He has walked just two in his last 12 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris' start was moved up to Wednesday after Tyson Ross was placed on the paternity list. That means Norris, who is 1-for-6 with a bat in his career, will get to start in a National League ballpark. The lone hit was a homer in his first career at-bat.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd has been the model of consistency, turning in five consecutive quality starts. He's also racked up 48 strikeouts in just 37 1/3 innings, which equates to 11.6 strikeouts per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez got a no-decision in the Royals' 9-4 win over the Angels on Saturday, lasting just 3 2/3 innings. He gave up six hits and four runs while walking three. He struck out two.

home_pitcher_note: Ross returns from the paternity list to face a Royals lineup he tamed for seven innings of one-run ball and eight strikeouts on April 7 at Comerica Park. An equal opponent could be rust, since he has not pitched since his April 24 loss at Boston.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Bailey wobbled in the first inning, giving up three runs to the Angels on Sunday. Unlike his previous start, this time Bailey grinded it out for six innings, giving up four runs. Most encouraging was he walked none.

home_pitcher_note: A month after striking out 10 Royals over six quality innings in a no-decision, Turnbull is rolling into a rematch, having allowed one earned run in 17 innings over his last three starts, notching his first two Major League victories.
away_pitcher_note: Keller came off his five-game suspension and was rusty on Monday against the Rays, giving up four runs through the first two innings. He lasted five innings, giving up six hits and five runs while walking three and hitting a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Norris had five innings of one-run ball last Wednesday at Philadelphia before getting a relatively early hook at 64 pitches. If he’s dealing, he should get a longer look against the Angels with the Tigers beginning a stretch of 14 games in 13 days.
away_pitcher_note: Canning showed flashes of dominance in his big league debut but was ultimately charged with three runs over 4 1/3 innings against the Blue Jays on Tuesday. However, he struck out six, only allowed one walk and registered 18 swings and misses.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd has tossed quality starts in his last six outings, including seven innings of two-run ball and nine strikeouts last Friday against the Royals. He leads MLB pitchers in Wins Above Replacement as well as Fielding Independent Pitching.
away_pitcher_note: Skaggs has been solid since missing two weeks with an ankle sprain, allowing two runs and striking out 10 over his last 11 innings. Both runs came in his six-inning outing against Toronto on Thursday, a win.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Toledo to fill the injured Jordan Zimmermann’s spot in the rotation. The big lefty went 1-2 with a 7.25 ERA in a handful of starts last year but tossed 11 scoreless innings in Spring Training.

Odorizzi's 2.78 ERA this season is impressive, but his last two starts have been doubly so, as he threw 13 shutout innings against the Astros and Yankees with 15 strikeouts en route to being named American League Player of the Week.
away_pitcher_note: Ross will try to rebound after the Royals roughed him up for five runs on seven hits in 1 1/3 innings on Saturday in his return from paternity leave. Detroit pushed this start back a day as Ross gets back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Pineda has been the only Twins starter who has struggled in this recent dominant stretch by the rotation, as he has allowed at least three runs in his past five starts. He had a season-high eight strikeouts against the Yankees in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull has yielded just two earned runs on 14 hits in 24 innings over his past four starts, including a career-high seven innings of one-run ball last Sunday against the Royals. His 2.31 earned run average leads American League rookie pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Stewart will be recalled from Triple-A Rochester for the second time this season after allowing five runs in six innings in a spot start against the Astros on April 24. He is 2-2 with 23 strikeouts and a 4.50 ERA in five Triple-A starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Soto got the call from Double-A Erie for the nightcap to make his MLB debut. The hard-throwing 24-year-old is Detroit’s 26th-ranked prospect by MLB Pipeline. He has just three outings above Class A ball but features a power arsenal.

home_pitcher_note: Perez has a 1.64 ERA with 27 strikeouts and seven walks since he joined the rotation on April 15, and has won five straight decisions for the second time in his career. He hasn't allowed a run in his last 15 innings, with 16 strikeouts over that span.
away_pitcher_note: Norris didn’t give up an extra-base hit in his five innings of work Tuesday vs. the Angels, but he paid for three consecutive singles with a three-run third inning that doomed him to defeat. He gave up a solo homer over three innings of relief against the Twins April 14.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd starts a three-game home set against Houston. The left-hander has won his last two starts and hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in any of his eight outings, becoming Detroit's most reliable starter in the process.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock is coming off the best start of his career, striking out 12 batters in seven scoreless innings Wednesday against Kansas City. He began working out of a full windup once again after throwing out of the stretch since 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter gets a second start after giving up six runs in five innings in his first Major League game of the year on Thursday against the Angels. Detroit needs a fifth starter to step forward with Jordan Zimmermann (right elbow UCL sprain) on the injured list.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 24 consecutive starts (since May 2, 2018), which is the longest streak in MLB by a traditional starter; he’s 18-6 with a 2.79 ERA in that span. Miley has a 6.63 ERA in his career against Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Soto, who made his Major League debut with a start in last Saturday’s doubleheader in Minnesota, returns to start on three days’ rest with a chance to stick around. He gave up seven runs in four-plus innings, but showed a lively power fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is 5-1 with a 1.79 ERA in his past six starts, striking out 49 batters and allowing only 17 hits in 40 1/3 innings. He had a 0.62 WHIP in that span and allowed one run or fewer in five of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull has given up only four earned runs on 18 hits in 29 2/3 innings over his last five starts, dropping his ERA to 2.42. His curveball has become an increasingly effective swing-and-miss pitch for him, with a 40-percent whiff rate this season.
away_pitcher_note: Bassitt has been incredibly consistent this season, pitching to a  2.55 ERA over four starts and going at least seven innings twice. But the A's haven't been able to capitalize, winning just one of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: The routine of a stable rotation spot is yielding results for Norris, who tossed 6 1/3 innings of two-run ball this past Sunday against a dangerous Twins lineup at Target Field. Opponents are hitting just .121 (4-for-33) off his slider this season.
away_pitcher_note: Montas has been the A’s most consistent starter all season, going six innings in five of his eight starts while holding opponents to a .701 OPS. He hasn’t given up a homer since April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd hasn’t faced the A’s since 2016, but their power lineup should pose a good test for the Tigers' ace. He’d given up three homers all season before the Astros hit two off him in one inning of a four-inning start Monday night at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Mengden gave up four runs in 5 1/3 innings in his '19 debut on Sunday vs. the Indians, though he seemed to find his footing after a shaky first two innings. Mengden pitched seven scoreless innings in his only career start against the Tigers, on Sept. 20, 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull paid for five unearned runs, including a Jurickson Profar grand slam, in a season-low-matching four innings of work in his last start, Thursday against Oakland. He had allowed just five runs (four earned) over his previous five starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: In six of Smith's eight starts, the left-hander has struck out at least eight, with a career-high 11 mixed in. His K/9 is 12. His groundball rate is up from last year and fly ball rate down -- 32.3% GB/42.4% FB. Last year he was 28.4%GB/50.8% FB.

home_pitcher_note: Norris continues to benefit from consistent turns in the Tigers rotation, showing a four-pitch mix with a sneaky fastball and improved changeup. But he paid for two home runs as part of six runs allowed over 5 1/3 innings last Friday vs. Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: The wins may not be there for Urena, but the performance has been, especially in his last six starts. Despite being 1-3, he has a 2.77 ERA over that span, working at least six innings in each of them. On the road overall, he is 0-2  with a 3.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd’s stellar opening month has given way to recent struggles, thanks in large part to the long ball. After holding opponents to two home runs in 44 1/3 innings over his first seven starts, he has allowed five homers in his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: It took nine starts for Richards to get his first win of the season, and he now seeks his first away win. He's 0-2 (5.40) in three road starts. Hitters are hitting .181 off Richards' changeup, a pitch on which he has a 34.6 swinging miss percentage.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets can only hope that Syndergaard, whose early-season struggles were somewhat of a mystery to them, is finding his groove. Syndergaard has delivered quality starts in three of his last four outings, with a 2.40 ERA over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Soto’s fourth Major League start will be his first one on regular rest, which should allow the 24-year-old some time to polish his secondary pitches to get hitters off his mid-90s fastball. Opponents are hitting .393 off his power sinker.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas will return from a three-week stay on the injured list rehabbing a strained left hamstring. He was in something of a groove prior to sustaining his injury, with a 3.00 ERA and nearly a strikeout per inning in his four most recent starts.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts for the team this year, Carpenter has allowed 13 earned runs over nine innings. Most of Carpenter’s season has been spent with Triple-A Toledo, where he was 1-4 with a 4.15 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Since delivering two clunkers to open the season, Wheeler is 3-2 with a 3.74 ERA, 61 strikeouts and 15 walks in 53 innings. He’ll be making his first career start against the Tigers, one of seven teams Wheeler has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull’s promising start to the season has turned south his last two outings as hitters lay off his secondary pitches off the plate and slug his fastball. All seven Marlins hits off him over five innings Tuesday had a high exit velocity.

home_pitcher_note: With Dan Straily sent to the bullpen, Ynoa will make his first start of the season Monday against the Tigers. It will be the right-hander's eighth career start and first since 2017. It will also be his first career outing vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Norris pitched six solid innings and allowed two runs on six hits against the Marlins. Norris, who is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA against the Orioles, will face them for the fifth time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bundy will try to continue a strong May as he takes the mound at Coors Field for the first time. So far this month, he’s posted a 2.28 ERA over four starts. He’ll have his work cut out for him in the Majors’ most hitter-friendly ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd is arguably the Tigers' best starter, with a 3.11 ERA and 80 strikeouts in 66 2/3 innings. In his last start, Boyd pitched six shutout innings against the Marlins, but he didn't figure in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Means has been a bright spot in an otherwise difficult season to this point for Orioles starters, and continued to show promise in his last start, holding the Rockies to three runs over five innings at Coors Field to take a 2.96 ERA into a home start against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter will start on short rest after his most encouraging outing of the season. He needed just 56 pitches to toss five strong innings against the Mets last Saturday at Citi Field, allowing two hits – both to Wilson Ramos – and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz's fastball velocity has increased, and his slider has been more effective during both of his past two starts. He'll be pitching with two extra days of rest Friday, following his strong six-inning effort against the Cardinals last week.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull will make his third start in a row against a National League opponent, and his fifth this season. He’s winless in five starts since beating the Phillies April 30. A four-run fourth inning doomed him in his last start, Sunday against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie hurler has built a strong All-Star resume, as he has allowed one earned run or less in each of his first eight starts. He posted a 0.79 ERA and limited opponents to a .145 batting average over five May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Norris continues to build trust as a reliable part of the rotation, displaying an effective four-pitch arsenal while keeping his team in games despite a three-game winless stretch. He’s seeking his first hit since homering against the Cubs in 2015.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 5.35 ERA through his first seven starts, Teheran produced a 0.98 ERA and limited opponents to a .128 batting average in five May starts. But he has issued four walks in two of his past three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd is winless in his last three Interleague starts despite just four runs allowed over 20 innings with 25 strikeouts, including six scoreless innings and seven strikeouts on May 23 against the Marlins at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter has improved from a non-competitive fill-in to a viable big league starter thanks to back-to-back solid outings, including five decent innings in a team win at Baltimore on Wednesday. Detroit would gladly take the same outing again.
away_pitcher_note: Since giving up a career-high seven earned runs against Kansas City on May 1, Snell has not allowed more than two in his past five starts. During that stretch, Snell has recorded 42 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Though Turnbull racked up just two strikeouts and seven swinging strikes on Friday in Atlanta, he earned his first win since April 30 by keeping hitters off-balance with a heavy dose of sliders that induced soft contact and ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has just two career starts against the Tigers, which is tied for his fewest against any team. In those starts, Morton is 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA over 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Norris has been throwing the kitchen sink lately and worrying less about fastball velocity, a big reason why he has become reliable. He’s also throwing those pitches for strikes, which will be key against a Rays lineup that ranks high in OBP.
away_pitcher_note: Stanek will be making his 17th start of the season and his 25th overall appeareance on Thursday. The right-hander has found more success opening games, posting a 1.73 ERA, as opposed to his relief appearances, where he has a 7.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Though Boyd has held the Twins to a .208 average for his career, they’ve had success against him thanks to 14 home runs in 15 starts the past three years, including five in as many meetings en route to three wins over him last season.
away_pitcher_note: Pineda, who missed the Twins' last eight games with right knee tendinitis, comes off the 10-day injured list to make his 12th start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Farmer will make his first start of the season after appearing in 29 games out of the bullpen. In four relief appearances against the Twins this year, the 28-year-old has fanned four over 2 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson dealt with traffic on the basepaths and an elevated pitch count against the Rays in his last start but allowed only one unearned run on six hits in five innings as he was effective for the second straight start and lowered his ERA to 3.75.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter has become a more effective pitcher his past three starts, holding opponents to a .206 average since his return from Triple-A Toledo. He tossed seven innings of two-run ball with three strikeouts against the Rays on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi continued his tear with six more scoreless innings against the Rays in his last start, lowering his ERA to an American League-best 1.96. He has held opponents scoreless in six of his last seven starts, dating back to April 29.

home_pitcher_note: Junis went 4 1/3 innings last Tuesday in a loss to the Red Sox. He gave up eight hits and six runs (five earned), while walking three and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull has been dominant against the Royals this year, striking out 17 batters over 13 innings of three-run ball in a win and a no-decision. But he battled command in his last start, walking three Rays and hitting another in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duffy had thrown two scoreless innings last Wednesday against the Red Sox when he was hit in the right knee with a line drive. He wasn't the same in the third inning as he hit a batter and gave up four hits and four runs while recording just one out.
away_pitcher_note: Norris survived with less than his best stuff last Thursday against the Rays, striking out six batters over 5 2/3 innings despite 11 hits allowed. He’s 1-2 with a 3.99 ERA in nine starts and a relief appearance against the Royals in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey had a strong outing Friday in a 6-4 Royals’ win over the White Sox. He went six-plus innings and gave up seven hits and three runs, walking one and striking out three. He left with a 2-run lead but got a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd returns to Omaha six years after he starred there for Oregon State in the College World Series, tossing a four-hit, 11-strikeout shutout of Indiana in a 1-0 win. He struck out nine Royals over seven innings of two-run ball in a May 3 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will try to bounce back from a rough outing against the Twins on Sunday. In 3 2/3 innings, he surrendered 10 hits and eight runs.
away_pitcher_note: Plutko will look to secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season after allowing two runs on three hits through six innings with four strikeouts in the Indians' 8-4 victory over the Yankees on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Soto returns from Triple-A Toledo for his first start since May 24. His work with Mud Hens pitching coach Juan Nieves yielded some much-needed progress in his last start, when he notched eight strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings of two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Bieber will look to bounce back from matching his shortest career start last time out, when he allowed five runs on five hits through 1 2/3 innings. In three career starts against the Tigers, he's pitched to a 2.25 ERA with 19 strikeouts in 20 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull threw six scoreless innings on Tuesday in Kansas City, but he left after 96 pitches and received a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer started to look like his early-season self last time out after posting a 5.50 ERA over six May starts. Against the Reds, he allowed one run through 7 2/3 innings with five walks and six strikeouts on 118 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Top prospect Keller gets his third big league start when the Pirates open a five-game homestand following a 10-game trip and an off-day. Keller has struggled in his first two outings -- both on the road. Opponents are hitting .472.
away_pitcher_note: Norris makes his fourth Interleague start this season, looking for his first win of the bunch after having taken a loss in Atlanta and hard-luck no-decisions against the Marlins and Phillies. He’s 1-for-4 at the plate in 2019 with a run scored.

home_pitcher_note: According to manager Clint Hurdle, the Bucs intend to have Williams (right side strain) return from the IL after one rehab start at Triple-A, where he got his pitch count up to 90. Williams faced Detroit in April, giving up two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has been on the injured list since April 26 with a right UCL sprain. He completed two rehab outings in June, allowing three homers and six runs over 7 1/3 innings and the right-hander yielded six home runs over 30 1/3 innings before going on the IL.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer is coming off a gem in Detroit last time out, when he tossed a four-hit shutout and struck out eight. Over his last two starts, Bauer has a 0.45 ERA (1 ER/16 2/3 IP), 14 strikeouts and a .175 opponents' batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has broken out this season, and the underlying metrics confirm it, as evidenced by his 3.00 FIP. But Boyd has struggled in June, posting a 5.63 ERA across three starts, due in part to allowing four homers in 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Civale will be the fifth Indians player to make his Major League debut this year. He'll make a spot start in place of an injured Mike Clevinger (left ankle sprain). Civale logged a 2.67 ERA in five Double-A starts and a 3.38 ERA in two starts in Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull gave up a season-high six earned runs on Sunday vs. the Indians, but he's been a solid piece in the Tigers' rotation. In eight of his 15 starts, he's pitched more than five innings, and he hasn't worked a start shorter than four.

home_pitcher_note: Plesac built on his early success with another seven-inning quality start -- his third in five outings this season -- as he earned the victory against the Rangers on Tuesday. He carried a no-hitter into the fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Norris gave the Tigers length in his six-inning start on Tuesday, helping Detroit snap a four-game skid. Four of those innings went 1-2-3 in order, and he allowed just two earned runs in the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann returned from the injured list on Wednesday and tossed four innings in Pittsburgh, allowing three runs on five hits with a walk and four strikeouts. His elbow, by all accounts, felt fine, which should allow him to stretch beyond 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Chavez has been used as an opener four times this year, but this is his first legitimate start since July 30, 2017. He is 2-1 with a 0.58 ERA and 0.94 WHIP in his last 21 outings. He went five innings and 59 pitches against the Indians on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: What looked like an All-Star season for Boyd has hit a rocky patch with consecutive rough starts, including three home runs over six innings on Friday in Cleveland. His strikeout rate remains high, but opponents are making more solid contact.
away_pitcher_note: Minor is 5-2 with a 2.19 ERA and a 1.23 WHIP in his past 11 starts. He is 3-2 with a 3.04 ERA in eight starts on the road. He is 0-2 with a 6.63 ERA in two career starts and six relief appearances against the Tigers. He hasn’t pitched in Detroit since 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull has struggled to coax hitters into chasing his slider lately, which has left the rookie right-hander to improvise to get through lineups. He used a fastball and curveball to survive five inefficient innings on Saturday in Cleveland with two runs allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Jurado's performance has declined slightly but steadily since he became a regular starter. He has a 5.67 ERA over 33.1 innings in his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Norris paid for defensive misplays behind him in a loss Sunday in Cleveland, but he delivered seven innings for the first time since Aug. 2, 2015. His changeup has become an increasingly effective pitch, helping him to eight strikeouts vs. the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will make his first career start against Detroit, where he went 46-49 with a 4.43 ERA in 151 games for the Tigers from 2012-17. He's coming off a four-run, six-strikeout outing on Saturday against the Braves. The Nats have won five of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Soto makes the short drive up Interstate 75 from Toledo for his sixth Tigers start this season and his first since June 15, when he tossed four scoreless innings against Cleveland despite four walks. He’ll be pitching on three days rest.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season on Sunday, Voth allowed two runs on four hits against the Braves. He set career highs in strikeouts (seven) and innings (six) in just his third MLB start. It earned him another start, according to manager Dave Martinez.

home_pitcher_note: The last time Zimmermann was matched up against his old team, on May 11, 2016, his seven quality innings were overshadowed by Max Scherzer’s 20 strikeouts against his former club. That was Zimmermann’s first season in Detroit after signing as a free agent.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer hasn't started at Comerica Park since joining the Nationals in 2015, and his 20-strikeout game in '16 was the last time he faced his former team. The ace right-hander is 5-0 with a 0.97 ERA and three straight double-digit strikeout starts in the month of June.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a disappointing first half for Lopez, who has the worst ERA among qualifying pitchers. Lopez has been slightly better over his past four starts, posting a 4.63 ERA over 23 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd is 0-5 with a 6.23 ERA in seven career starts at Guaranteed Rate Field. The way the ball travels there on hot summer nights, he’ll have a test keeping the ball in the park, having allowed three homers in both of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The long-awaited Major League debut of MLB Pipeline’s No. 18 overall prospect takes place Wednesday. Cease, 23, has a 4.48 ERA in 15 starts for Triple-A Charlotte and will have a regular rotation spot moving forward.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had the makings of a quality start last Friday before a left groin cramp prompted manager Ron Gardenhire to pull him after 77 pitches over five innings of two-run ball. He tossed five scoreless innings against the White Sox in an April 21 win.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander picked up his first victory since pitching for the A’s in 2016 during his White Sox debut Friday against the Twins. Detwiler threw 73 pitches over five innings, but he could go deeper in start 2.
away_pitcher_note: Tyler Alexander will make his Major League debut in Game 2 of the Tigers' doubleheader vs. the White Sox. Alexander has had an up-and-down season at Triple-A Toledo, going 2-9 with a 6.23 ERA in 14 starts this season, but he pitched better in June with a 3.81 ERA in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez was scheduled to start Tuesday’s series opener against the Tigers, but it was postponed. With Lopez having gone through his full warmup when the rain started, the White Sox held him back until the series finale.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd pitches in Thursday's series finale after getting washed out in Tuesday's planned opener. Boyd took the loss in his last start vs. Texas and was bit by the home run bug, giving up three homers to the Rangers during his seven-inning performance.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will return to the Tigers for his third stint in the Majors this season. The southpaw threw six scoreless innings in his last Triple-A start after allowing 11 runs in 3 2/3 innings in his previous outing.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off a June 30 outing against the Yankees in which he issued four walks, his highest total this season, but he has done well to work deep into games recently, which the Red Sox will need in their opener against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann looks for his first win of the season against the team that roughed him up in Boston on April 25 before he went on the injured list with right elbow inflammation. He tossed six innings of one-run ball on Sunday against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello is looking to drag his ERA back below 5.00 after one of the toughest outings of his career on June 29. He allowed six runs on five hits while recording just one out, but at least he'll be fresh after throwing just 33 pitches that day.

home_pitcher_note: After returning to the Tigers' rotation on three days’ rest last Saturday, Soto will serve as the Tigers’ opener on one day of rest, having pitched an inning in relief Friday. His fastball has reached 98 mph with sink in each of his last two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Price continues to be the steadying force in Boston's rotation, and the Sox will need that to continue down the stretch. The veteran lefty walked a season-high four batters in his most recent start, in Toronto, but still made the right pitches at the right times to earn his sixth win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Duffy provided a quality start on July 3 against Cleveland in a 4-0 loss. He went 6 2/3 innings and gave up five hits and two runs. He walked a season-high five batters.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull is expected to return from the 10-day injured list after battling shoulder fatigue. The rookie last started June 27 against Texas, leaving after two innings when his fastball velocity dropped. He tossed six scoreless innings in Kansas City on June 11.

home_pitcher_note: Keller grinded through 5 2/3 innings against the Nationals on Friday in a game the Royals won 7-4 in 11 innings. Keller gave up six hits and one run, but walked five batters while striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Scouts will be tracking Boyd closely out of the break as the Trade Deadline nears and contenders sort out their options. They’ll catch the left-hander coming off a no-walk, 13-strikeout performance against the White Sox last week in Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey went five innings on July 4 in an 8-4 loss to the Indians. He gave up six hits and two runs in a no-decision. He walked two and struck out two.
away_pitcher_note: With seven days’ rest, it’s anyone’s guess which Zimmermann will show up on the mound. Will the pitcher who dueled Max Scherzer for six innings return? Or will it be the one who gave up 13 hits over 3 1/3 innings against the Red Sox?

home_pitcher_note: After moving to the bullpen for the past few weeks, Adam Plutko will take the mound again on Monday. The right-hander has kept himself stretched out, pitching simulated innings after a 93-pitch relief outing in Baltimore on June 28.
away_pitcher_note: Norris struck out eight over seven innings in just 93 pitches against the Indians in his last visit to Progressive Field on June 23, but defensive lapses saddled him with six runs. He has fanned five batters over 10 innings in two starts since then.

away_pitcher_note: Carpenter, who was recalled from Triple-A late Monday, will be making his ninth start of the season. He surrendered six earned runs on eight hits with four walks over three-plus innings against Cleveland on June 14.

home_pitcher_note: After a slow start coming off the injured list, Clevinger said he has felt more like himself on the mound in his past two outings. In that span, he's pitched to a 0.82 ERA with 15 strikeouts in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull’s return from the injured list on Friday in Kansas City showed a rejuvenated arm but spotty command, especially with his fastball. He’s 0-3 with a 7.07 ERA in three starts against the Indians, accounting for nearly half of his losses this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer will look to have a more consistent outing than his last trip to the mound. Against the Twins on Saturday, he gave up three homers in two innings -- two to Max Kepler -- but he settled in to record 11 strikeouts in six frames.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd could become the first pitcher in Tigers history to post double-digit strikeouts in four consecutive starts, but he’ll have a challenge on his hands in Cleveland, where he gave up three home runs over six innings in a no-decision on June 21.

away_pitcher_note: Stroman has made four starts against the Tigers in his six-year career, but Friday will be his first start in Detroit. He held the Tigers scoreless over seven innings on Opening Day in Toronto.

away_pitcher_note: Thornton has faced Detroit once this season, throwing five scoreless innings with eight strikeouts. He pitched just 1 1/3 innings in his last outing on Monday against the Red Sox. Thornton gave up five runs without a strikeout, and will look to bounce back against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Alexander will make his second big league start as the revolving door continues to turn on the Tigers’ fifth starter spot. Alexander held the White Sox to a pair of solo homers over five innings in his MLB debut, striking out four in a no-decision on July 3.
away_pitcher_note: Waguespack’s challenge in his second career start will be to work through the middle innings. He held the Red Sox to one run through the first four innings his last time out, but he was unable to escape the fifth inning.

away_pitcher_note: Nola has been the surest Phillie arm the past two months, even with his four-run outing on Thursday. That start was just the second this season in which he allowed three home runs. Nola has been K-heavy recently, with 48 in his past 40 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann’s July numbers are ugly, with 20 runs on 28 hits over 11 innings in three starts. Within the damage, however, is a midseason transition in arsenal, including a sinker he has been developing. But Zimmermann needs to find his slider again.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez has allowed 16 runs (15 earned) in 21 1/3 innings since his return to a starting role on June 16. He allowed a career-high four home runs his last time out, against the Dodgers on July 16.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander gets his second start as an opener -- and seventh overall start -- and then will be followed by veteran lefty Wade LeBlanc. Swanson gave up 2 hits and 2 runs in 2 innings at Oakland on July 17 in his first shot as an opener.
away_pitcher_note: Nearly 12 weeks after his last work out of the Tigers bullpen, VerHagen returns from Triple-A Toledo for his first start since June 4, 2018. The 28-year-old went 4-2 with a 4.42 ERA in 11 starts for the Mud Hens, with 51 strikeouts over 53 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi was still searching for answers in what’s been a challenging rookie season following Sunday’s loss to the Angels, when he gave up a season-high seven earned runs. Location and deception remain an issue for the Japanese left-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Norris should have plenty of energy after a rain delay limited him to four innings and 58 pitches against the Blue Jays Saturday at Comerica Park. He induced seven ground-ball outs that night while leaning on a fastball-changeup combination.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales appears to be back on track following Monday’s win over the Rangers, when he threw seven innings of two-run ball, retiring 17 of his final 18. The lefty has won six of his past eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Alexander used 10 fly-ball outs, a handful of them testing the depths of Comerica Park, to deliver seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball against the Blue Jays Sunday in his second Major League start. Seattle could be similarly hospitable.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old right-hander gets his second shot as an opener, having pitched a scoreless inning against the Angels last Saturday, then will turn the ball over to lefty Tommy Milone. Wisler was acquired from the Padres on July 4.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd returns home to his Seattle-area roots for what could be his last start as a Tiger with next week’s Trade Deadline looming. He struck out eight Phillies over six innings Tuesday, with a home-run accounting for his only scoring damage.

home_pitcher_note: Barria bounced back after a rough outing against the Mariners, allowing one run over five innings against the Dodgers on Wednesday. Barria allowed just three hits and struck out three.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will look to replicate his success at Angel Stadium, but with a different outcome. In two career starts there, the veteran right-hander has a 2.70 ERA, but his record is 0-2. After a few solid starts in June, he’s posted a 14.09 ERA over four July starts.

home_pitcher_note: After being forced to pitch two innings in relief in extra innings against Baltimore on Thursday, Canning will be pushed back to get some rest. Pitching the night before his scheduled start, Canning gave up five runs.
away_pitcher_note: VerHagen will look to build on some of the positives he had in his start Thursday, which was his first outing since June 2018. After a Minor League demotion in May, VerHagen hopes to give the Tigers some rotational depth.

home_pitcher_note: Suarez was mostly solid against the Orioles, allowing two runs over 4 1/3 innings in a no-decision on Thursday. He struck out six, though he needs to be more efficient with his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Norris tossed six scoreless innings his last start before giving up a critical two-run homer in the seventh that led to a loss to the Mariners on Saturday. In three career starts vs. the Angels, he is 0-2 with a 4.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has pitched at least six innings in 17 straight starts, going 11-4 with a 3.18 ERA and a 1.14 WHIP. He has pitched 113 innings in that stretch, striking out 136 and walking just 25. He is 2-3 with a 4.60 ERA in five career starts vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: After a couple of solid outings to open his Major League career, the rookie left-hander was roughed up a bit in his third career start, getting tagged for four runs on eight hits and one walk in 4 1/3 innings against the Mariners on Saturday. More encouraging were Alexander's nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson is making his first career start against the Tigers and is looking for his first win since June 23. He is 0-4 with a 9.12 ERA in his past seven outings. He is 5-2 with a 3.36 ERA in seven starts and six relief appearances at home.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd is coming off a pair of quality starts, including a 10-K outing against the Mariners on Sunday. This will be Boyd's second time facing Texas this year, having allowed four runs in seven innings while striking out 11 in a June 26 start at home.

home_pitcher_note: Payano is making his second Major League start and fourth appearance. He allowed three runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start against Oakland. He pitched six innings over two relief outings, allowing just one run on three hits with seven strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: In his most recent start, Zimmermann picked up his first win of the season in 14 tries, holding the Angels to two runs in 5 1/3 innings while striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: Expect Turnbull to be limited to around 75 pitches in his return from the injured list, having been shelved since July 18 with an upper back strain. He tossed 3 2/3 scoreless innings, giving up just one hit in a rehab start for Triple-A Toledo last Tuesday, while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Giolito bounced back from his worst start of the season by allowing just one run over seven innings Wednesday vs. the Mets. That came on the heels of his July 25 outing in which he allowed seven runs on seven hits, including four homers, vs. the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Norris has allowed just three runs on 13 hits over his last three starts, striking out 16 batters over 15 1/3 innings. He tossed five scoreless innings with six strikeouts against the White Sox on April 21, during their last visit to Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Cease turned in the longest outing of his brief career Thursday, tossing seven innings against the Mets. Though he allowed four runs, he showcased his potential in a game in which he received zero run support.

home_pitcher_note: VerHagen gets a third turn in the Tigers rotation as Detroit tries to get innings out of its fifth-starter slot, but it hasn’t been easy. The converted reliever has allowed 11 runs (nine earned) on 16 hits over 8 2/3 innings in two starts since his return.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago will make his first start in his third stint with the White Sox. He signed with Chicago on June 20 after posting a 6.75 ERA in eight relief appearances with the Mets this season.

home_pitcher_note: In Alexander's last start at Comerica Park, on July 21, he used the ballpark's dimensions to his advantage on four warning-track fly balls and got a great catch from JaCoby Jones to toss seven innings of one-run ball vs. the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Nova allowed two runs (one earned) Friday vs. the Phillies but had his outing cut short after letting the first two runners reach base in the sixth. The right-hander threw only 78 pitches. He has a 0.90 ERA over 20 innings in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lost amidst the trade rumors and decision by the Tigers to keep Boyd, the left-hander is back to throwing stingy, having struck out 27 batters in 18 innings over his last three starts. Just as important, he has allowed just two homers in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez will make his first start since May 25 in place of the injured Danny Duffy. In two starts against the Tigers this season, Lopez is 0-1 with a 3.46 ERA. The right-hander has a 4.81 ERA on the road, compared with an 8.07 ERA at home.

home_pitcher_note: Ten years after Jackson’s lone season for the Tigers, the 35-year-old right-hander returns, having signed a Minor League deal a couple of weeks ago. He struggled with the Blue Jays this season, but he’s 11-4 with a 3.99 ERA for his career at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: After earning three straight wins, Keller has lost his last two starts. He will look to bounce back against the Tigers, against whom he is 1-1 with a 2.79 ERA in three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull returned from the injured list Monday with a 34-pitch first inning on his way to a three-inning, 76-pitch battle with the White Sox. While his back and arm were healthy, his pitches were moving too much for him to command the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery said he felt like a "normal starter" after being stretched out to 90 pitches in his last outing against the Red Sox on Monday. He struck out 7 and gave up 4 runs (2 homers) over 5 innings in a loss. Manager Ned Yost praised Montgomery, saying, "He gave us a chance to win the game."

home_pitcher_note: Norris is 1-5 with a 4.84 ERA in eight starts at Comerica Park this season, despite a lower WHIP and better strikeout-to-walk ratio compared to his road splits. A matchup with the Royals, a team he handled well in Kansas City in June, could help those splits.
away_pitcher_note: Junis has thrown at least six innings in six straight starts. In his last outing on Tuesday against the Red Sox, he pitched six innings with seven hits, one run, one walk and four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd gets a rematch against his hometown Mariners, whom he fanned 10 times over 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball July 28 in Seattle. He’ll try to rebound from a three-homer, five-run outing last Thursday against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi is 1-7 with a 7.18 ERA in his last 13 starts, but he allowed just one run on four hits in five innings his last start vs. the Padres. The 27-year-old rookie from Japan held Detroit to two runs in 6 2/3 innings on July 26 in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson gets another start in the Tigers' rotation after tossing 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball last Friday against the Royals, his first win in a Detroit uniform since 2009. His fastball showed surprising zip, topping out at 97 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzales' last win came against Detroit on July 27 when he allowed 6 hits and 1 run in 7 innings. He equaled a career-best nine strikeouts in his last start before getting hit in the left calf by a ground ball and removed in the seventh vs. the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull’s 3-10 record doesn’t reflect his strong pitching lately, including losses on quality starts in two of his last three outings. The Tigers haven’t won for him since May 31, having provided two or fewers runs of support in seven of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler has thrown six scoreless innings with just two hits, no walks and five strikeouts in four previous opportunities as an opener. He’ll be followed by veteran lefty Tommy Milone.

home_pitcher_note: Morton looks to continue his success this season at Tropicana Field, where he has posted a 2.75 ERA in 11 starts. The right-hander has recorded 95 strikeouts over 68 2/3 innings at home.
away_pitcher_note: Norris is the rare pitcher to yield a lower slugging percentage away from Comerica Park, a 55-point difference this season. He has given up five home runs over his past two outings, both at home. He hasn’t pitched at Tropicana Field since 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Yarbrough has excelled as a starter this season, going 3-2 with a 3.16 ERA in six starts. Since the All-Star break, the left-hander has a 1.78 ERA in six appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will be activated off the IL prior to Saturday's start after receiving a nerve block injection last week to alleviate his cervical spasm. The righty struck out a season-high seven during his last start, Aug. 4 against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Richards, acquired from Miami on July 31, will make his Rays debut after posting a 3-12 record with a 4.50 ERA in 23 outings with the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has allowed seven home runs over eight innings in his past two starts as hitters jump on his fastball. His 30 home runs allowed on the season, the second-highest mark in the AL. The Rays are in the middle of the pack in slugging percentage against lefties.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has allowed three or fewer earned runs in all but two of his 25 starts and four earned runs or fewer in each start. Miley is 5-0 with a 2.42 ERA in his last nine starts, allowing 41 hits in 52 innings. He's 5-1 with 2.02 ERA in 10 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is 2-0 since rejoining the Tigers on Aug. 9. Last time out, he went five innings against the Mariners and allowed a pair of solo home runs. He's 2-2 with a 4.09 ERA in 10 career games (nine starts) against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez, acquired from the Blue Jays on July 31, went 2-0 with one earned run and three hits allowed in 11 innings over his first two starts with the Astros before giving up six runs, including four home runs, on Thursday vs. the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull will be seeking his first win since May 31 when he faces the Angels. The righty struck out eight in five innings the last time out but continued to struggle out of the stretch during a three-run third inning against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will face his former team riding a franchise-record streak. The right-hander has struck out at least 10 batters in a career-best six consecutive starts, and he's 5-0 with a 2.30 ERA in his last seven starts, striking out 75 in 43 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris' innings are limited the rest of the season, but the lefty made the most of his three innings on Friday, holding the Rays scoreless and allowing just one hit. He's 2-4 in 15 games (13 starts) on tthe road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cole returns to the rotation after being scratched from his Aug. 13 start at Chicago with hamstring discomfort. He’s second in the Majors behind Justin Verlander with 226 strikeouts and was 10-0 with a 1.98 ERA and 126 strikeouts in his last 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann was solid in his return from the injured list, firing five one-hit innings at the Rays on Saturday. The righty, who missed one start after receiving a nerve block injection Aug. 4, has a 3.06 ERA over his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Berrios was hit hard for the second time this month when he gave up seven runs (three earned) to the Rangers on Saturday, just the second time this season in which he was unable to complete five innings. He has allowed 19 runs (15 earned) in his past three starts.

away_pitcher_note: Skubal earned his first Major League win Saturday with two runs on three hits over five innings. The highly regarded prospect will get a nice test with a rematch against a bolstered Twins lineup.

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has won all five career starts against the Twins, including a 3-0 record and 2.55 ERA in three outings at Target Field. He struck out six batters over three scoreless innings Tuesday in Milwaukee.

away_pitcher_note: Houser is 0-3 with a 6.92 ERA in his last five outings. He's making a second straight start against Detroit after allowing five runs on nine hits in five innings at Miller Park on Sept. 2.

away_pitcher_note: Burnes is on a nice roll since rejoining the rotation, including consecutive wins against the Pirates and Indians in which he allowed no earned runs and struck out 17 in 12 total innings.

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer continues to search for a consistent breaking pitch he can use with his fastball and changeup. His slider, a tremendous out pitch before his Tommy John surgery last year, has been inconsistent through seven starts and 19 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his second consecutive Opening Day start for the Tigers, Boyd is looking to rebound from an MLB-high 6.71 ERA and 15 home runs allowed in 2020. He tweaked his arsenal this spring with a renewed emphasis on his changeup to complement his sharp slider.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight year, Bieber will get the Opening Day start for the Indians. Last year, he set a franchise Opening Day record by striking out 14 batters in six innings against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran didn’t earn a seventh Opening Day start after making six with Atlanta, but he came close, dominating the Grapefruit League to not only earn a roster spot but also a front-line role in Detroit’s rotation. His velocity is back to 92 mph with a sharp slider.
away_pitcher_note: Plesac settled in during his sophomore campaign in 2020, owning a 2.28 ERA in eight starts. While his numbers weren't exceptional in camp, Plesac said that he felt much better than his stats indicated.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal, one of baseball’s top pitching prospects, won a rotation spot in Detroit based on his impressive Spring Training performance and a focus that impressed manager A.J. Hinch. He faced Cleveland once last year, striking out five over 2 1/3 innings of one-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Civale will quickly find out just how much his new delivery will help him in 2021. He spent the entire winter revamping his mechanics and entered camp with a completely new arm angle and windup.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers signed Ureña to provide veteran stability to the rotation, but also because they saw upside in his game. He had an up-and-down Spring Training, including more walks (nine) than hits (seven) over 14 innings, but he showed an electric arsenal.
away_pitcher_note: Shoemaker has only made 18 starts in the last three seasons due to a series of setbacks, but he’s hopeful that his “freak injuries” are behind him, as the 2014 AL Rookie of the Year Award runner-up aims to rebuild his stock with the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers’ top pitching prospect had to fight for a spot while battling command issues in Spring Training, but he still struck out 21 batters over 14 innings. Mize faced the Twins three times last year, posting an 8.49 ERA with 11 strikeouts in 11 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: There was some question as to whether Happ would be fully prepared for the start of the season, due to a positive COVID-19 test at the start of camp, but he appears to be stretched out and ready to pitch. Happ had a 3.47 ERA for the Yankees last year.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd actually pitched better against the Twins last year than any of his other opponents in an otherwise miserable season for him, holding the Bomba Squad to three earned runs -- all on home runs -- over 12 innings with no walks, 14 strikeouts and a 1-1 record.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda struggled with his mechanics and couldn't command his slider effectively for much of his Opening Day start against Milwaukee, but he still fanned five and held the Brewers to one earned run over 4 1/3 innings. He struck out 25 Tigers in 18 innings last season.

home_pitcher_note: Plesac said he was fighting some first-start butterflies when he took the mound against the Tigers last week. But after settling in, he permitted two runs in six frames. In four career starts against Detroit, he owns a 1.14 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran paired sinkers and sliders to hold Cleveland to one run over five innings in his Tigers debut Saturday at Comerica Park. He’ll have another go at the Indians at Progressive Field, a place he pitched only once in his career in 2019.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in a week, Civale will get the start against the Tigers. Last time out on Sunday, he permitted three runs on two hits -- two homers -- with six strikeouts and three walks in seven frames.
away_pitcher_note: Skubal gets a rematch against the Indians after he allowed two runs on four hits and two walks in 5 1/3 innings Sunday in Detroit. His fastball drew six swings and misses, but he induced only one from his slider, curve and splitter combined.

home_pitcher_note: Allen proved that he earned his spot in the rotation in his start against the Royals in the Tribe's home opener on Monday. Now, he'll look to build on that momentum. After battling his command early, Allen settled in, allowing two runs in five frames.
away_pitcher_note: Ureña’s Tigers debut did not go according to plan Monday, as he surrendered six runs (five earned) on four hits and four walks over three innings while throwing just 39 of 81 pitches for strikes. His command woes continue a trend from Spring Training as he has tried to corral an array of pitches that move.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has two of the longest outings by an Astros starting pitcher so far this season, throwing six innings April 1 and seven innings Tuesday. He's given up two earned runs, eight hits and one walk in 13 innings (0.69 WHIP).
away_pitcher_note: Mize looked solid in his season debut but still lasted just four innings with one run allowed, thanks in part to pitch count. His four-seam fastball and sinker were both well up in velocity from last season’s averages.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi, who signed with Astros on March 8, makes his debut with his new team. He's coming off a season in which he pitched only 13 2/3 innings with Twins due to three stints on the injured list but is completely healthy.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has given up seven home runs in four career starts against the Astros, accounting for most of his 5.91 ERA against them. He hasn’t pitched at Minute Maid Park since 2015, when he gave up five runs in as many innings to A.J. Hinch’s Astros.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers makes third start of 2021 but first against a team other than the A's. In each start vs. Oakland, he went five innings and allowed one run and two hits but had one inning in which he threw more than 30 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer steps into Detroit’s rotation to fill in for the injured Julio Teheran. The former All-Star will try to take his rejuvenated arsenal from his brief bullpen stint into a starting role. His four innings of one-run ball in Cleveland were encouraging.

home_pitcher_note: Through two starts, Manaea has had a taste of the good and the bad. Fortunately for him, his more recent outing was the better one, as he worked six innings of one-run ball in a no-decision against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Skubal allowed three home runs over four innings on Saturday in Cleveland and looked relatively flat with his pitches. Through two starts, his fastball velocity and spin rate are down a tick from last year, but his secondary pitches are better.

home_pitcher_note: Montas earned a win in Houston on Saturday, the first of the season for the A's rotation. He'll be eager to do more, though, given that he has posted an 8.31 ERA and 1.96 WHIP through two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Ureña has as many walks as strikeouts -- nine each -- over 7 2/3 innings through two starts to go with a career-high 47 percent hard-hit rate, putting his rotation spot in potential danger as Spencer Turnbull nears a return from the injured list.

home_pitcher_note: Irvin has yet to record a win in two 2021 starts, but he'll have a clean slate this time against a team he's never faced: the Tigers. A mere 55 innings into his career, Irvin is allowing an .860 OPS to opponents.
away_pitcher_note: Mize looked like the dominant starter from his Auburn days on Monday in Houston on his way to seven scoreless innings on four hits and his first Major League win. His splitter was an effective pitch as much for soft contact as for swings and misses.

home_pitcher_note: Bassitt hasn't had any blowups yet, but through three starts, he has lacked shutdown stuff. He has pitched at least five innings in each start and allowed no more than four runs, but he still maintains a 4.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd is winless in two career starts against Oakland despite walking none and striking out 15 across 11 1/3 innings. That includes a 2016 visit to the Coliseum when he allowed two homers and three runs over five innings while striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer earned his first win since 2018 by holding the Astros to two runs on three hits in five innings on April 14 in Houston. He hasn’t won back-to-back starts since July 2017. Fulmer has allowed one run in 14 career innings against the Pirates.

The Red Bull returns to the Tigers rotation after opening the season on the injured list due to health and safety protocols. He makes his season debut against a welcome opponent, having allowed one earned run in 13 career innings against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Yajure, who was acquired in the package for Jameson Taillon in January, will make his Pirates debut and his first MLB start. The club's No. 12 prospect allowed three runs in six innings with seven strikeouts in Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Ureña might have saved his rotation spot with last week’s seven strong innings and eight strikeouts in Oakland, where he attacked the strike zone and let his pitch movement do the work. He owns an 8.18 ERA in seven career outings (three of them starts) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Keller has struggled to start the 2021 season. Through three starts, he holds a 1-2 record and an 8.74 ERA, with 12 strikeouts and eight walks. He'll look to improve in those areas against the Tigers on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Mize faces his first meeting with the Royals coming off a three-homer loss Saturday in Oakland, when all three long balls came after he retired the first two batters in the inning. He continued to attack the strike zone, but left too many pitches in the middle.
away_pitcher_note: Minor allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings for his first loss of the season in Game 1 of the doubleheader against the Blue Jays on Saturday. He didn't allow any walks and struck out three, but he was tagged with two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd’s 6.05 ERA in 22 career starts against the Royals is his highest vs. any AL opponent, despite a decent home-run rate. He handled them better last season with a 3.78 ERA in three starts, accounting for two of his three wins overall for the year.
away_pitcher_note: Singer spun his best start of the season on Sunday against the Blue Jays, allowing just two hits in six innings, with three walks and six strikeouts. The Blue Jays only reached third base once against Singer, and he got out of the jam with a strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: Fulmer will start on three days' rest after a three-run fourth inning beat him in a 3-2 loss to the Pirates on Wednesday. He’s 2-5 with a 4.96 ERA in 11 career starts against the Royals, including eight runs over five innings in two meetings last year.
away_pitcher_note: Duffy turned in another gem Monday against the Rays despite being dealt the loss. Notching his 1,000th career strikeout in the fourth inning, Duffy allowed two unearned runs on four hits in six innings, striking out eight with two walks.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull made his season debut Wednesday by doing something he had never done in his Major League career: Completing five innings in just 62 pitches to beat the Pirates. He’s winless in six career starts against the Royals, despite a 3.27 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Keller will look to turn around his season after making it through 1 2/3 innings in Tuesday's loss to the Rays. Keller wasn't hit hard, but ran into unlucky plays and walked three. He was tagged for five runs on three hits and his second loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Giolito was originally scheduled to start Sunday but was moved back a few days after suffering a cut on the top of his middle finger when trying to open a glass water bottle on Monday in Cleveland. He has thrown a bullpen and will be ready to go vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Ureña has been a strike-throwing, grounder-inducing machine his last two starts after walking nine batters over 7 2/3 innings in the two starts prior. He has tossed seven innings of two-run ball in those last two outings against the A’s and Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Rodón will have eight days off in between starts before taking the mound on Thursday night against the Tigers. Rodón's last two starts have come against Cleveland, both victories, including the 20th no-hitter in franchise history.
away_pitcher_note: Mize gets a third career meeting with the White Sox, the team against which he made his MLB debut last year on Aug. 19. home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has made four starts this season and has not completed five innings in any of them, lasting 3 1/3 innings Friday against Texas. Cease has nine career wins, with a 5-0 record vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd’s stingy start to the season gets a test against a team that teed off on him last summer. The White Sox greeted him with back-to-back homers to begin his outing in back-to-back starts last August, with Tim Anderson leading off both times.

home_pitcher_note: Cole outdueled reigning AL Cy Young Award winner Shane Bieber on Saturday, striking out 11 Cleveland batters over seven strong innings. The Yankees’ ace will now take on the Tigers, a club he faced twice this spring, allowing three runs on six hits with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Skubal found success with his splitter during Sunday's 2 2/3-inning piggyback start, and his fastball velocity was up a tick as well. A win Friday at Yankee Stadium would mark the first road victory of his young career.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon has yet to find his form for the Yankees since being acquired on Jan. 24, but he has another chance here for his first win of the year.
