away_pitcher_note: Turnbull allowed three runs across six innings but took the loss his last time out against the Royals, as much a victim of the Tigers' recent RISP woes as anything else. He fanned 8 during 5 innings in his only career appearance vs. the Yankees, Sept. 12, 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber broke through for his first victory of the season on Tuesday against the Orioles, allowing only one run in 6 2/3 innings (his longest start as a Yankee) while striking out five. He’ll look to keep that momentum going against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Ureña showed serious mettle his last time out, continuing to pitch aggressively and hold his team in the game despite the defense committing five errors behind him. His reward was his first win as a Tiger. Ureña has a 2.16 ERA in two career starts (8 1/3 innings) against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta has been stellar in his last two starts, giving up two hits and two runs over 11 innings. Last time out, he outpitched the great Jacob deGrom in a 1-0 win for Boston. Pivetta is 2-0 with a 2.29 ERA in four career starts at Fenway.
away_pitcher_note: Normally this would be Matthew Boyd’s slot, but the lefty is being skipped for a turn while he deals with left knee tendinitis. Enter Fulmer, who made three starts in April -- two in a short piggyback role -- before replacing Boyd in relief last week.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty took a big step forward in his last start, allowing one earned run and striking out seven over 5 2/3 innings against the Rangers. Though he has made nine starts at Fenway for the Red Sox over the last two seasons, Pérez is still looking for his first home win.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has lost his past three starts since shutting down Houston on April 12 for his first MLB win, but he took a scoreless outing into the fifth in his last start against the White Sox before giving up two walks and two hits that resulted in a three-run rally.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi has given the Red Sox exactly what they've needed in the No. 2 spot in the rotation. Last time out, he held the Rangers to one run over six innings. Eovaldi is 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA in three starts against the Tigers, but he hasn't faced them since 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull's record doesn't reflect the quality of his pitches, but the struggle to translate that into results. He looked like a sinkerballer against the Yankees, inducing 11 groundouts, but the righty walked three batters and hit another over five-plus innings.

home_pitcher_note: The righty-heavy Yankees hit Skubal hard on Friday, when he allowed three home runs and needed 77 pitched to get through his three innings. Skubal called it a "learning lesson," but the home runs continue to be a concern.
away_pitcher_note: Shoemaker said that he's always gotten off to slow starts in his career, but his last outing against the Royals was particularly rough as he set a career high with nine runs allowed. He threw six strong innings against Detroit in his 2021 debut.

home_pitcher_note: Ureña enters Saturday with four consecutive seven-inning quality starts that show a composure not reflected in his 1-4 record. He held the Yanks to two runs on three hits and fanned seven on Monday, but he took the loss as the Tigers continued to struggle offensively.
away_pitcher_note: Berríos has still fallen victim to a problematic inning here and there, but his overall numbers are dominant, with 42 strikeouts and nine walks in 32 2/3 innings. His 2.34 FIP and 1.01 WHIP this season are both the best marks of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd missed just one turn in the rotation due to left knee tendinitis after he departed his April 29 outing after the first inning. Prior to that, he was sharp across eight innings against the Royals on April 24, allowing just three hits and one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Singer had his best start of the season when the Royals visited Detroit in April, throwing seven dazzling innings while allowing just a run on three hits, no walks and eight strikeouts. Singer gave up three runs in 5 2/3 innings on Wednesday against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Mize has tossed back-to-back quality starts without a win to show for it, including six innings of one-run ball in Boston last Wednesday. Before those quality starts, he gave up six runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Royals on April 23.
away_pitcher_note: Duffy scattered eight hits in 5 2/3 innings in last Thursday's loss to the Indians, allowing three runs with one walk and six strikeouts. It wasn't his best start of the year, but that's because he's been the Royals' most reliable starter so far.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull has battled inconsistent command in his past two starts after looking like a front-line starter upon his return from the injured list in late April. He expended 80 pitches over three innings, allowing seven hits last Thursday in Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Lynch worked to clean up some of his mechanics between starts after allowing eight runs in two-thirds of an inning against the White Sox on Saturday. He only threw 34 pitches, so the Royals were able to move him up a day to avoid facing Chicago again.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal struck out eight over five innings of two-run ball against the Twins last Friday, helped in part by turning away from the splitter he developed last winter in favor of a more traditional changeup. He has a 3.33 ERA across his six career appearances at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs are expected to activate Arrieta for the opener in Detroit. He dealt with a cut on his right thumb in his April 30 start (seven runs allowed) vs. the Reds and went on the IL. Arrieta had a 2.57 ERA in five starts before that game in Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Ureña’s sinkerball success got a test from a Twins offense that peppered him for nine hits over 4 1/3 innings of two-run ball last Saturday. He’s 2-2 with a 4.05 ERA in six career starts against the Cubs from his days in the Marlins’ rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Williams took a no-decision on May 8, when he gave up two runs over four innings against the Pirates. The righty struck out six and walked two. He is 0-2 with a 10.64 ERA in three road outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Boyd returned from left knee tendinitis by tossing six scoreless innings and changing speeds effectively for five strikeouts against the Royals on Tuesday. He’s the fifth Tigers starter since 2010 with a sub-2.00 ERA over his first seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks pitched better than his line indicated on May 9. The righty was charged with six runs (four earned) in five innings against the Pirates, but gave up a lot of soft contact. He has a 3.33 ERA in seven starts against teams other than Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi is coming off a career-high 11 strikeouts, and against the defending champion Dodgers, to boot -- a competitive game in which Seattle's bullpen blew a late lead. He’s pitched into the seventh inning in each of his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has put together three consecutive quality starts, including six innings of two-run ball in his last outing against the Royals on Wednesday. His four-seam fastball has emerged as a quality swing-and-miss pitch with an average 94.6 mph velocity.

home_pitcher_note: Dunn had decent stuff his last time out, but he hung a few breaking balls in critical sequences that wound up cutting his day short after just 3 1/3 innings at Dodger Stadium. He has the best numbers on the starting staff, but he is averaging less than five innings per outing.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull has struggled to string together solid outings since rejoining the Tigers' rotation in late April, but he looked his best all season in his last start, allowing one run over 6 1/3 innings with a walk and seven strikeouts against the Royals on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Gilbert is coming off an up-and-down MLB debut, in which he gave up four runs, including two homers, over four innings on 71 pitches. He likely would’ve gotten the chance to pitch into the fifth had it not been for a wild pitch on a called strike three that forced him to face an extra hitter.
away_pitcher_note: The former Seattle University star returns to his college city looking to get his pro career back in gear and end a skid of four consecutive losses in as many outings. He tossed a season-high six innings last start, but he gave up four runs to the Cubs on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Minor logged his best start of the season on Saturday, holding the White Sox to just one run on two hits across seven innings. He struck out seven and walked two, keeping Chicago hitters off balance with his fastball and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Ureña gets back on the mound for the first time since taking a 109 mph line drive off his right leg last Saturday against the Cubs. He left that game in the third inning with four runs allowed on five hits. He has never faced the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Singer scattered seven hits over 6 1/3 innings on Sunday against the White Sox, but the righty allowed just two runs on a homer in the fifth. He walked two and struck out seven as he pitched into the seventh inning for the second time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd faces the Royals for the third time this season, having allowed two runs (one earned) over 14 innings in their previous two meetings. His increased changeup usage has been critical in his stinginess against them compared to past seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Bubic made his case for another start after spinning six scoreless innings against the Brewers on Tuesday, allowing one hit with four strikeouts and two walks. He also extended his scoreless streak to 17 2/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has allowed four runs on nine hits over 19 2/3 innings in three starts this month, good for a 1.83 ERA to go with a 2-0 record. His work includes six innings of three-hit ball with two runs allowed against the Royals on May 12 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull makes his first start since his no-hitter on Tuesday against a Cleveland lineup that has largely struggled this season. He’s 0-6 with a 5.18 ERA in nine career appearances against the Indians, who have hit .325 and slugged .482 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Hentges' second career start didn't go quite as he would've hoped. He'll be looking to go deeper against the Tigers after allowing six runs on five hits through just 1 2/3 innings against the Angels last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal was less fastball-heavy in his last start on Wednesday, and it paid off with nine strikeouts and a win in Seattle. He’ll try to take that to the Indians, who hit him for eight runs over 9 1/3 innings in back-to-back meetings at the start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Civale outdueled Shohei Ohtani last time out, tossing seven strong frames and allowing two runs on four hits with a season-high eight K’s. He had one his longest outings of the season last time against the Tigers, giving up one run in 7 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ureña had to grind through his last three starts compared to his previous tear, but he’s continuing to attack the strike zone, which is critical for him and something he didn’t do against Cleveland in their last meeting on April 11, when he issued five walks.
away_pitcher_note: McKenzie returns to take his normal turn in the rotation after he was optioned to Triple-A on Saturday. Command has been an issue for the rookie right-hander this season: He's pitched to a 6.89 ERA and walked 30 across 31 1/3 innings in eight appearances (seven starts).

home_pitcher_note: Boyd’s first sign of a bounce-back season came with 5 2/3 scoreless innings against Cleveland on Opening Day at Comerica Park. Now comes the rematch and a test for how Boyd can mix up his arsenal a second time around against a familiar opponent.
away_pitcher_note: Terry Francona said he saw Bieber have more misfires in his last outing than he had seen in a long time. Bieber allowed three runs with a walk and six K's in 5 1/3 frames, but said he's focusing on the positives in each outing during this rough span.

home_pitcher_note: Mize will face the Yankees for the first time in his career following his one-run performance against the Royals in his last start on Sunday. Opponents are only hitting .141 with 20 strikeouts against the right-hander in four May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole tossed seven scoreless innings in his last start, limiting the White Sox to four hits. Cole's 92 strikeouts are the most by a Yankees pitcher through 10 starts of a season, surpassing Al Downing's 86 in 1963.

home_pitcher_note: Turnbull took the no-decision in his last start against Cleveland on Monday after he pitched six innings and allowed three earned runs on seven hits, three strikeouts and one walk. The right-hander set a season-high with nine strikeouts in his no-hitter against Seattle on May 18 after he recorded 11 strikeouts in two April starts.
away_pitcher_note: García last appeared in the Majors on April 26, taking a loss after allowing two runs over four innings in a road start against the Orioles. García pitched to a 4.98 ERA in six big league starts last season.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw, who has a 5.23 ERA in eight starts this season, wraps up the series against the Yankees. Skubal snapped his losing streak with his first win of the season against Seattle on May 19 and will be put to the test against a Yankees lineup that swings for the fences. Skubal has given up 13 home runs this season, and opponents are hitting .263 against him.
away_pitcher_note: King will get the start in Sunday's finale at Comerica Park. The right-hander has a 2.29 ERA in seven relief appearances this season. He last started on Sept. 21 last year.

home_pitcher_note: Burnes is one of the reasons the Brewers have one of the Majors' best rotations. He owns a 2.33 ERA with 74 strikeouts in 46 1/3 innings over eight starts this year. Burnes has allowed just one run over nine innings against Detroit in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Alexander will make his first start of the season in what amounts to a bullpen game as the Tigers fill injured Jose Urena’s rotation spot for a turn. Alexander is best known for nine consecutive strikeouts in a long relief appearance last summer.

home_pitcher_note: Lauer has dramatically improved his walk rate -- not to mention his ERA -- after shortening his arm path over the offseason to improve his command and reduce the strain on his shoulder. He has yet to face the Tigers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has lost his last three starts, allowing 13 earned runs on 20 hits over 16 innings despite 18 strikeouts. His next challenge is a Brewers lineup that hit him for two homers and seven runs over three innings last Sept. 9.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn was scheduled to work on short rest Wednesday after beating the Orioles Saturday. But a postponement in Cleveland put Lynn back on regular rest for the series and homestand opener Thursday vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Mize pitched five innings of one-run ball with seven strikeouts against the Yankees in his last outing. He leads the Tigers with 1.7 Wins Above Replacement, per Baseball Reference, this season.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel had allowed five home runs over his first 10 starts before allowing three in five innings during his last trip to the mound against Baltimore. Keuchel finished May with a 3-0 record and a 4.40 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Turnbull escaped a nobody-out, bases-loaded jam with only one run allowed against the Yankees in his last start, winning his fourth game of the season and first since his May 18 no-hitter.

home_pitcher_note: The White Sox ace had a tremendous month of May with a 4-2 record and a 2.41 ERA in six starts, striking out 45 over 37 1/3 innings. He has a 2.84 ERA over six starts this season at Guaranteed Rate Field.
away_pitcher_note: Skubal had arguably his best outing on Sunday, pitching six scoreless innings in Detroit’s victory over the Yankees. He made it look easy against a group of hitters that roughed him up for three homers in as many innings one month prior in the Bronx.

home_pitcher_note: Cease will take the bump to close out the four-game set with the Tigers. Cease has a proven track record of success against Detroit, sporting a 6-0 record with a 2.29 ERA and 37 strikeouts in 35 1/3 innings over six career starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers haven’t officially announced Ureña’s return from the IL, but manager A.J. Hinch said he remains on track for the start after throwing a side session Thursday. He hasn’t pitched since leaving his May 26 start with right forearm tightness.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 1.94 ERA over his first seven starts, Boyd has a 7.84 ERA over his past four outings, including three homers last week in Milwaukee. A home start against the struggling Mariners could give Boyd the opportunity to get rolling again.
away_pitcher_note: In his return start from the IL, Gonzales threw four innings, allowed one run and struck out six on 50 pitches. Gonzales was set to only throw three innings, but he managed to get a fourth frame completed in his efficient outing.

home_pitcher_note: Mize has been better in rematches against opponents this season, but he’ll be hard-pressed to top the 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball he tossed against the Mariners last month in Seattle. He allowed three home runs in his last start against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Flexen has struggled on the road, posting an 8.10 ERA in four starts away from T-Mobile Park compared to a 2.67 ERA in six home starts. Flexen went six innings in his last start against the A’s, but he gave up five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Alexander will step in to make his second start in as many weeks, again as part of a bullpen game. He’ll likely get a longer outing than the May 31 start in Milwaukee, where he lasted one inning before being lifted for a pinch-hitter with the bases loaded.
away_pitcher_note: Sheffield has provided some durability for Seattle, going at least five innings in each of his 10 starts this season. In his last outing against the Angels, Sheffield gave up two runs in 5 2/3 innings and allowed six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal set a career high with 11 strikeouts against the White Sox in Chicago on Saturday, and he has four consecutive outings with eight strikeouts or more. He’s just the fourth rookie since 2010 to post such a streak.
away_pitcher_note: Giolito makes his second straight start vs. the Tigers, after dropping a 4-3 home decision to Detroit on Saturday. The White Sox are 5-7 in Giolito’s 12 starts, and he has a 3.32 ERA in three career starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Ureña gets a rematch against the White Sox after giving up three runs on six hits over five innings on Sunday in Chicago in his return from the injured list. He hasn’t struck out more than two batters in an outing since May 8 against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Cease absolutely dominates the Tigers. He has a 7-0 record with a 1.91 ERA over seven career starts against Detroit, striking out 47 over 42 1/3 innings. Cease has 14 scoreless innings in two wins over the Tigers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Funkhouser, who came up in the Tigers' farm system as a starter, will make his first Major League start as part of a bullpen game. The former University of Louisville star has been a revelation in relief (2.70 ERA in 13 appearances) since being called up from Triple-A Toledo in May.
away_pitcher_note: Rodón has not received a decision in three of his last five starts, going 0-2 with a 3.45 ERA. Over that span, he had 44 strikeouts in 28 2/3 innings, a .239 opponents average and received zero runs of support in three of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Keller started well against the Angels on Wednesday with a six-pitch first inning. But things came undone late, and he wasn't able to get out of the sixth inning. Keller allowed five runs on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings, with four walks and four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd hasn’t won back-to-back starts since late 2019, but he has a chance if he can find the right pitching mix against a Royals lineup he’ll face for the fourth time this season. His changeup had been effective against them until their last meeting on May 22, in which he allowed five runs on eight hits and three walks in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Minor put together his finest start in a Royals uniform on Thursday against the A's, his former team. The veteran lefty allowed one run on three hits in seven innings, with just one walk and eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has given up as many runs in two June starts (six) as he did in five May outings, thanks in part to four home runs allowed. But he had two very strong outings against the Royals in May, including 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball at Kauffman Stadium on May 23.

home_pitcher_note: Singer was solid on Friday against the A's, with the fourth inning as the exception. He allowed back-to-back doubles and a homer to give the A's a 3-0 lead in their eventual 4-3 win. But Singer did strike out seven in six innings, with just one walk allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Skubal is unbeaten in his last three starts after racking up 25 strikeouts in 17 innings against the White Sox and Yankees. His slider has become an increasingly effective swing-and-miss pitch, coupled with more consistent command of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani had a no-decision against the D-backs in his last outing, allowing two runs over five innings with eight strikeouts. He has a 2.67 ERA over his last six starts, with 45 strikeouts in 33 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Manning will be the third of the Tigers’ highly touted pitching prospects to make his MLB debut. The former first-round Draft pick ranks 18th on MLB Pipeline’s Top 100 Prospects list, but he struggled with the home-run ball at Triple-A Toledo until his last start.

Though rotation injuries taxed the Tigers' bullpen last week, another issue was Ureña’s second-inning exit in his last start, allowing eight runs with five hits and three walks against the White Sox on Saturday. He owns a 7.46 ERA in six outings since his last quality start on May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Sandoval is coming off his first career win as a starter, allowing two runs over six innings against the D-backs. He has a 2.77 ERA in five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: The former Royals and Brewers swingman steps into Matthew Boyd’s rotation spot for his first Major League start since May 14, 2017. Peralta posted a 2.75 ERA in six starts for Triple-A Toledo this season, but he topped four innings and 60 pitches only once.

home_pitcher_note: Bundy struggled again on Monday, allowing seven runs over 2 1/3 innings against the A's. He's posted a 9.82 ERA in seven starts dating back to May 2.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has tossed three consecutive quality starts, including 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball for a win at Kansas City on Tuesday. His slider has become an increasingly effective pitch, including a .160 average allowed and 30.9 percent whiff rate.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal is 3-0 with a 2.74 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 32 batters over 23 innings. His slider has a 36.6 percent swing-and-miss rate, but he used his fastball and changeup to strike out seven Royals over six innings in a win last week.
away_pitcher_note: Still searching for his first big league win, Oviedo couldn't have done much more last time out, with seven shutout frames -- a career high in innings. Most encoraging: the 23-year-old allowed no walks, an about-face after being hampered by free passes in May.

home_pitcher_note: Injuries to fellow Tigers starters Matthew Boyd and Spencer Turnbull mean the future is now for Manning, who will make his long-awaited Comerica Park debut after holding the Angels to two runs on four hits over five innings on the road last Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Gant's last outing was a modest step in the right direction, with three earned runs across 5 1/3 frames after lasting 5 2/3 frames and allowing 12 earned runs during his two prior starts combined. The walks remain an issue, with a MLB-leading 44 offered (15.8 percent walk rate).
